## 261031.004 (r186) -- PR #194 (`set-tensor-async-ring`) re-assessed on the r186 tree and CLOSED; no delivery change

**No patch, no release, no `release.json` change** -- the delivery set stays at `v16-6050b467c-r186` (16
blocks, tip `8f9dad0be`, tree `0bd26dbe`).  Record: `archive/work/set-tensor-async-ring/`
(`RESOLUTION.md`, "Final assessment").

**Why re-open a declined PR.**  r98 declined it (-1.2 % / -2.3 % on two MoE tensor-split MTP cells) and
asked the submitter to scope the queue drain.  Nine days later the PR was still a draft with **no reply
and no new commit** (branch `325224590`), so it got one last look before closing: the patch was re-cut on
the current tree (applies cleanly to `8f9dad0be`, offsets only) and **the r98 re-entry condition was
implemented here** -- drain only where a queued upload's destination overlaps the copy, issuing only the
overlapping origins and fencing the copy on the event that issue recorded (so the rest of the queue keeps
batching), plus a fix for the ring teardown (below).

**Measured** (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, one job at a time, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, 3 interleaved pairs per
arm, seed 42, temp 0, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`, `-n 400`, all arms from the same build directory
with the `bin/` of each kept):

| config | base (r186) | PR as submitted | PR + scoped drain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flash-Next GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS + shared Q8_0 MTP, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10`, MTP n3, q8_0 K/V | **101.12** | 99.65 (**-1.5 %**) | 99.27 (**-1.8 %**) |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10`, MTP n3, q8_0 K/V | **199.66** | 199.15 (-0.3 %) | 196.95 (-1.4 %) |
| dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU, plain, 8K ctx | 30.69 | 30.66 | 30.72 |

Correctness is intact in every arm -- greedy text byte-identical on the Flash-Next cell (1775 chars
`52ccd3394a63`), the 35B-A3B cell (1401 chars `aaef5122fe19`) and a dense 4B cell (889 chars
`fbb8c4ac4d98`), no GPU faults -- so the change is numerics-neutral and r90's `set_tensor_async` snapshot
guarantee is kept, exactly as the submitter measured (and as r98 verified with the FINDINGS-2026-10-19b
self-KLD control, 100.000 % at `-ub 8` and `-ub 1`).

**The r98 attribution was wrong and is corrected here.**  The drain is the *trigger*, not the cost:
scoping it does not recover the loss, and on the 35B-A3B cell it is worse than the unconditional drain.
The cost is that these uploads leave the graph-input ring's **batched** path (r89 / PR #182) and become
one `cudaMemcpyAsync` per upload.  Isolated with the same build and only `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH=0` on
the Flash-Next cell: `base` 101.12 · `PR` 99.65 · `base + BATCH=0` (the per-copy path the PR replaces)
**96.96** · `PR + BATCH=0` 98.91.  The submitter's `+2.7 %` therefore reproduces -- against a tree whose
other host-side work drains that queue -- and it still lands *between* the per-copy and the batch path.
No delivery config drains the queue between upload and graph, so the premise of the change does not arise
here.

**Two defects in the patch itself** (found building the scoped arm; both are in the submitter's file, none
reachable in the delivery): (1) the pinned ring can be freed under an in-flight copy -- `snap_half_ev[h]`
is recorded when the ring *leaves* half `h`, so the half being filled has copies no event covers, and the
destructor synchronises the two stored events and then `cudaFreeHost`s the ring (fix: record
`snap_half_ev[snap_half]` on `stream()` before the syncs, or synchronise the stream first); (2) the
per-context ring takes no lock where the per-device ring takes `d.mtx`, and `cudaEventSynchronize` on a
half switch is a host-blocking wait inside the upload path.

**Outcome.**  PR **CLOSED as not planned** with the table above posted to the submitter, stating what
would reopen it: a measurement showing the queue is actually drained between upload and graph **on a
delivery config** (`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_DEBUG=1` / `rocprofv3` counting per-token drains that issued
queued uploads) -- and the correct fix for that is to stop whatever drains it, not to bypass the ring.
`wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` records the closure; nothing is added to `TODO.md` (a closed item is a WORKLOG entry).

## 261031.003 (r186) -- the conv fusion's single-device gate is gone (block 10): +5.7 % dense / +3.0 % MoE decode on 3 GPU `-sm tensor`, bit-identical

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r186` (16 blocks; block 10 amended).**  Canonical tip
`8f9dad0be9625542f4f1d7891dd25cbb40aa7257`, tree `0bd26dbe195185072019fe99926177d4daa7718b`,
`validate-set.sh` strict 16/16.

**What changed.**  `gdn_conv_enabled()` / `ple_conv_enabled()` no longer require
`ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count() <= 1`.  The depthwise conv1d fusion was gated to single-device graphs
on 2026-09-23 (r13) because the direct kernel produced a different greedy continuation under a 3x R9700
`-sm tensor` split while its reference path agreed byte for byte; that divergence was never root-caused
(`archive/work/closing-the-gap/2026-09-23-gfx1201-conv-fusion-tensor-split.md`).  **It no longer
reproduces**, so the gate is gone and the fusion — plus the three r183 GDN decode folds that ride it —
now runs on every split.  `GGML_CUDA_CONV_FUSION_MULTI` is **retired** (it only ever countermanded the
gate; forcing the fusion on is now the default) and `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_CONV_FUSION=1` is the A/B arm.

**Why it is safe (gfx1201).**  `test-logits-width-probe` at `P=4096`, fused vs `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_CONV_FUSION=1`,
bit-identical `W8`/row-0 on 8 arms — 27B IQ3_S 1 GPU / 2 GPU (`0,2`) tensor / 3 GPU tensor / 3 GPU layer,
35B-A3B Q3_K_M 3 GPU tensor + layer, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M 3 GPU tensor `-ncmoe 40` with and without the arena —
with the direct conv confirmed running on the shard (`C=2560` for 3 devices, `C=5120` for 2) and `snap=1`.
Greedy text identical on 4B Q8_0, 27B Q4_K_XL (tensor + layer) and 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (tensor, and `-ncmoe 40`);
MTP Protocol A identical text **and** acceptance on both split modes (tensor 0.63244 = 2445/3866, layer
0.58861 = 1850/3143); a DFlash2 draft arm identical (0.52806 = 1449/2744); prefill-logit gate on 3 GPU
tensor **0.000000 / 99.990 %**; `test-backend-ops` SSM_CONV 60/60, CONCAT 183/183, CPY 251/251 (3/3
backends); per-block build 2/2 `--fast`; no GPU faults.

**Worth (3 GPU `-sm tensor`, `llama-bench -r 5`, three interleaved rounds).**  27B IQ3_S tg128
**58.59 -> 61.92 (+5.7 %)** and pp2048 **+1.1 %**; 35B-A3B Q4_K_M tg128 **118.52 -> 122.13 (+3.0 %)**
with prefill flat; rule-5 `llama-batched-bench -npl 1,4,8` flat (+0.4 / -0.2 / -0.1 %).  Full matrix:
`benchmarks/2026-10-31-conv-fusion-multi-device.md`.

**Caveat, stated plainly.**  The 2026-09-23 divergence was never root-caused, so this is an **empirical**
result.  The likely fix is r183's rework of exactly the suspect area (the snapshot write moved into the conv
kernel, the conv-state gather deferred into it), but nothing establishes that.  Configs outside the matrix
are unproven, which is why **release gate 14 now runs a multi-device arm on every release** and
`scripts/validate-gpu.sh` step 4c runs the single-device *and* multi-device arms automatically.  A future
divergence must be gated on the config that shows it, never on a device count (that also disabled the
bit-identical `-sm layer` arms).

**Re-cut.**  Block 10 amended (`5f8b82aab` -> `f3d144a40`), blocks 11-15 re-cut on top; blocks 00-09
byte-unchanged.  Docs: `AGENTS.md` (r183 bullet), `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §73 (rule 6 + reach paragraph + index),
`ENVIRONMENT.md` (§7.1/§7.3), `MANIFESTS.md` (release gate 14 + the block-10 row), `patches/README.md`
(block 10 "r186"), `scripts/README.md`, `scripts/validate-gpu.sh` (step 4c).  Resolution appended to
`archive/work/closing-the-gap/2026-09-23-gfx1201-conv-fusion-tensor-split.md`.

## 261031.002 (docs/gates) -- PR #177 closed as superseded (it is already in r183), and the width gate it was held by is now a release gate

**No delivery change, no release, no patch re-cut** (`release.json` untouched, still `v16-6050b467c-r185`).  Docs
and CI-gate only.  Closes a four-release-old open question with a measurement instead of an assumption.

### PR #177 (`gdn-conv-snapshot-fold`, `@briansp2020`) -- CLOSED, superseded

Assessed for a last integration attempt and found **fully superseded**, three ways:

1. **It carries no code.**  Its single commit (2026-10-17, never updated) adds two files under
   `wip/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/` — one `format-patch` + a `README.md` — i.e. a `wip/` proposal, not a fork
   patch.  Both are **byte-identical** to what is already committed at
   `archive/work/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/` (sha256 `21b2337048e5…` and `65ceb2463119…`), where they went when the
   campaign closed (the no-stub rule).
2. **The change itself shipped in r183**, as block 10, through the submitter's *own* PR #256 patch `0001` —
   which is a strict **superset**: same `gdn_conv_snap_safe` byte-span check, same `gdn_conv_snap_args`, same
   `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GDN_CONV_SNAP`, plus the batched-copy run stop at a folded snapshot `CPY`
   (`cpy-batch.cu`) that #177 lacked, without which `cpy_batch` swallows one.  All 98 substantive added lines
   of #177 are present in the tree (3 in extended form, carrying the later `norm`/`state_ids`/`state_row`
   args), and `patches/0010-…-block-10-….patch` carries all of it.
3. **The blocker that held it is gone.**  #177 was declined at r81 and r100 for 35B-A3B run-to-run
   nondeterminism at P=3584, traced then to that model's prefill being sensitive to the launch sequence
   itself (TODO #75) rather than to the fold — the fold's write was proven byte-exact.  Re-run on the shipped
   r185 build (gfx1201, 1 GPU, HIP graphs on, `test-logits-width-probe`, the fold firing per
   `GDN_CONV_DIRECT … snap=1 n_snap=1`):

   | model | depth | folds on (`W8` / row-0) | vs kill switch | runs |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | P=256 | `efb1ac6b4a863719` / `aa6057acd67bd109` | identical | 3/3 |
   | 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | P=3584 | `36026b682d8aa1fc` / `23f86e866c6e5804` | identical | 3/3 |
   | 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | P=4096 | `493a0a43ad3927cd` / `bbbfff452c95a46a` | identical | 2/2 |
   | 27B UD-Q4_K_M (dense) | P=256 / P=3584 | `b43fb4ee01d6b7ab` / `cb7acb2f9013340d` | identical | 3/3 |

   `width_purity=PASS` (worst maxdiff 0) in every arm; `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  So #177's re-entry
   condition is met — by a build that already contains it.  Closed with that evidence on the PR, credited to
   the submitter and noting the one thing never used from it (the `GGML_CUDA_CONV_FUSION_MULTI=1` 2x R9700
   bit-identity data point; the direct conv's multi-device gate still stands, blocked on the 3x R9700
   `-sm tensor` divergence).  Detail appended to `archive/work/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/RESOLUTION.md`.

### The gap this exposed, and the gates that now close it

**r183 shipped these four folds with only two arms: greedy text and `gate-prefill-logits.sh --ub 1`.**  Both are
*value* instruments, and a fold is a **launch-order** change: it splits or elides launches on multi-token steps
and touches no arithmetic.  The instrument that held #177 out for four releases — `test-logits-width-probe` at
the verify widths, read **across runs** — was never run on the shipped folds.  That is the same
"that the probe ran is not that it reached the code" class as r126/r134 (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §51), one level up:
the probe was the right instrument and simply was not pointed at the fold.

* **`MANIFESTS.md` release gate 14** (new): the width probe at `P=3584` and `P>=4096` on a dense *and* a MoE
  GDN model, default vs each of the four kill switches, run-to-run stable across `>= 3` runs, bit-identical to
  every kill switch, and with `GGML_CUDA_CONV_DEBUG=1` proving the fold **fired** — a run that never logs
  `snap=1` is a vacuous pass and **fails**, not skips (the `n_snap=1` field also appears with `snap=0`, so the
  match is on the `snap=` field).
* **`MANIFESTS.md` block 10 per-block row** gained the same arm, so a block-level review sees it too.
* **`scripts/validate-gpu.sh` step 4c** runs it automatically on tier-2 CI when the applied tree touches
  `gdn-conv`/`cpy-batch`/`ggml-cuda-try-fuse`, so it is no longer a promise in a document.  Arms: `folds on`
  vs `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GDN_CONV_SNAP=1` + `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_GATHER=0` +
  `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_DECODE=0` + `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_SHEXP_GATE_SIGMOID=0`; `GDN_WIDTH_MODELS` /
  `GDN_WIDTH_P` / `GDN_WIDTH_RUNS` / `SKIP_GDN_WIDTH` are the knobs.  Cheap: **9 s** for `P=4096`, 3 s for
  `P=256` on gfx1201 (8 widths x the prefill, so ~30 s per model for both depths and 3 runs).  Exercised here
  on all four paths — pass, fold-off mismatch detection, non-GDN model (fails as vacuous), missing path (skips).
* **`AGENTS.md`** (the r183 critical-facts bullet) and **`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §73** (new rule 6 + the judgement
  paragraph + the index row) now say the fold is judged by the width probe, and why text/KLD cannot do it.

**What this does *not* change:** no kernel, no default, no env var, no block, no `release.json` value — so there
is nothing to re-gate and no new tag.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` still validates the same 16 patches (the
`release.json` hashes are byte-identical), and `bash -n scripts/validate-gpu.sh` is clean.

## 261031.001 (r185) -- the multi-slot verify WIDTH bound (block 02): +14.2 to +31.8 % on the default recommended speculator, and PR #169 closed on the measurement

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r185` (16 blocks; block 02 amended).**  Canonical tip
`5639690d2e64d4a9c9538c5c3d32a949b39a6e98`, tree `f8eaf8f005b44a11bad1a619f0c9b07b0559f64b`, `validate-set.sh`
strict 16/16.  Numbers: `benchmarks/2026-10-31-multislot-verify-width.md`; record: this entry (no `archive/work/`
campaign: the work was PR #169's assessment plus the promotion, and PR #169 is closed).

**PR #169 (`wip/spec-batch-budget`, `@briansp2020`) is CLOSED, not merged.**  Its head is byte-identical to the
copy the repo has kept at `archive/work/spec-batch-budget/` since r77, so there was nothing new to take; the third
and final assessment re-measured it on **r184** (one binary = r184 + the patch, the env var selecting the arm,
`--lazy-mode off`, 4 concurrent 300-token greedy requests, fresh server per arm, 2-4 reps, the archived probe as
the harness) and the reply on the PR carries the tables.  Two findings, and the second one is the release:

1. **The premise is not the rule.**  At a 4-slot verify width, "above ~8 rows each extra draft token costs more
   than it gains" holds only on the contributor's own shape: fixed depth 3, width 16 vs width 8, **35B-A3B 3 GPU
   432.7 vs 389.8 t/s, 2 GPU 387.2 vs 359.6, dense 27B 3 GPU 240.1 vs 211.2** (all *worse* with the cap), while
   qwen4exp Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS 2 GPU + a resident PLE table is 204.6 vs **220.8** and IQ3_S 196.7 vs **205.8**
   (better with it).  A 2-slot arm on that shape is **-22 %** at width 4 vs 8, so the knob was a per-shape gamble
   with no safe value, its structural controller defect (fed `n_accepted` against its own `n_cur`, not the capped
   depth) was never addressed, and the r79 record's "2-slot byte-identical text" no longer holds on r184 (`a59941368946`
   uncapped vs `7f8f820b9789` capped).
2. **The defect it was reaching for is real and much larger, and it is a delivery bug in the DEFAULT config.**
   `align_draft_caps()` bounded the aligned depth by the expert-cache band, and r176 made `band` answer only for a
   config with **host-resident experts** -- so on a band-0 config (all-in-VRAM, `-sm layer`, a model with no
   routed expert) a multi-slot draft was **unbounded**.  Four slots at the shipped `--spec-draft-n-max 7` present
   ~28-32 rows, past the MMVQ/MMVF -> MMQ and FA family switch, and with `draft-mtp-adaptive` (the recommended
   speculator) the *default* measured **317.1 vs 418.0 t/s on 35B-A3B 3 GPU (-31.8 %), 166.6 vs 212.4 on
   qwen4exp 2 GPU (-27.5 %), 205.7 vs 225.3 on dense 27B 3 GPU (-9.5 %)** against the same arm bounded at 16
   rows.  Per step on the 35B: 51.5 ms for 16.1 accepted (3.18 ms/accepted) vs 31.5 ms for 13.2 (2.39) -- the wide
   arm buys no acceptance for its time.  Nothing could see it: coherence, prefill-logit, the four-axis MTP
   protocol and `gate-spec-align.sh` all run one or two sequences, where `width / n_drafting - 1` is 15 or 7 and
   the bound is inert by construction.

**Delivery change (`common/speculative.cpp`, block 02, 32 lines).**  The aligned depth is bounded by
`width / n_drafting - 1`, where `width` is the arena band when one is active (unchanged) and the new
`LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN_WIDTH_BAND` (default **16**, `0`/`1` = off) otherwise.  **16 and not 8**, because at the two
widths the fixed-depth arms measure 16 rows ahead on 3 of 4 shapes (the table above); a model or shape whitelist
was rejected on purpose -- the sign flips on the same model across quant, device count, slot count and speculator,
and the variable that governs it is the verify width `n_slots x (1 + depth)`, so the rule is expressed on that and
evaluated per draft call.  A/B, one binary, band on vs off: **35B-A3B 3 GPU 4 slots adaptive 330.8 -> 434.7 t/s
(+31.4 %)**, **qwen4exp IQ3_XXS 2 GPU + PLE 175.5 -> 208.9 (+19.0 %)**, **dense 27B 3 GPU 218.5 -> 249.6
(+14.2 %)**, a fixed `draft-mtp n_max 7` arm 310.9 -> 362.8 (+16.7 %); 3 slots +16.9 %; **1 and 2 slots inert**
(16 / 2 - 1 = 7 = the default `n_max`, 2-slot text byte-identical, an `n_max 9` 2-slot arm neutral within noise),
and a host-expert config takes the arena band and runs the same code path (191.9 vs 184.5 t/s = the ±7 % noise
floor at 4 slots, measured deliberately as a control).

**Gates.**  New `scripts/gate-spec-width-band.sh` (band-0, 3 GPU, `--parallel` 1/2/4, one binary) **PASS**: the
bound fires as `aligned draft depth ... 4 -> 3 (width band 16)` and never on the knob-off arm, 4 slots 363-366 ->
425-432 t/s, 1 and 2 slots inert and text-identical (`fa36ef316479`, `e846c29f763b`/`b02d535e449d`), full token
budgets, no abort, GPU journal clean.  `gate-spec-align.sh` **PASS** with the r176 numbers unchanged (2 GPU
113.8 -> 146.7, 3 GPU 139.4 -> 178.3, host-expert 124.5 -> 151.1, splits 58+1 -> 0+1, mixed chain inert, single-slot
text `b8775233a93a`).  Coherence against a kept r184 build **byte-identical** on 5 arms (4B 3 GPU and 1 GPU
`8d89080db673`, dense 27B 3 GPU and `draft-mtp n3` `bda6ce08c7e1`, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` `265c381dbc11`).  MTP
Protocol A (27B, 3 devices, `-n 3000`, bf16 KV): layer plain 25.0 -> **61.7** t/s, tensor 50.8 -> **121.0**
(r176 at `-n 2000`: 25.0/50.9 -> 62.1/120.9); adaptive R axis at `-n 3000` 67.0 t/s and `893b1d5a3322` on **both**
builds.  Prefill-logit **0.000000 / 100.000 %**.  Per-block build `--fast` **16/16** (896 s).  `validate-set.sh`
green.

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3 (the knob + the band note), `patches/README.md` (block 02), `MANIFESTS.md` (release
gate 13 + the block 02 verification row), `AGENTS.md` (critical fact + the `scripts/` index), `scripts/README.md`
(index + detail row).

## 261030.009 (r184) -- PR #254 ships the target's speculative checkpoint in device memory (block 12): +2.1 % dense / +4.3 % MoE on n-gram rewrite requests, bit-identical, plus a `-nkvo` correction and the state-copy invariant

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r184` (16 blocks; block 12 amended).**  Contributor `@overdoingism`'s
[PR #254](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/254), filed as `wip/spec-ckpt-device/` against
r176 and applying with `git am` unchanged to r183 (one patch, `tools/server/server-context.cpp`).  Record:
`archive/work/spec-ckpt-device/`, numbers: `benchmarks/2026-10-30-spec-ckpt-device.md`.

**What shipped.**  On a recurrent or hybrid target the server saves a checkpoint of the target's recurrent state
before a verify whose draft is longer than `n_rs_seq` (`use_ckpt_tgt`) and restores it when only part of the draft
is accepted.  It went to host memory (149.6 MiB for Qwen3.8-27B).  It now carries
`LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE`, so a save and a restore are device copies into one staging buffer per slot that
the context keeps and reuses.  Decided once per slot at its first checkpoint and logged: device memory when the
target is on exactly one GPU, its state is offloaded and that GPU has the state's size plus 512 MiB free (the
buffer is allocated lazily, after the expert-cache arena sized itself); host memory otherwise, and always under
`-sm tensor` / a layer split.  `LLAMA_SERVER_SPEC_CKPT_DEVICE=0` keeps host memory always.  Context checkpoints
(the prompt cache) are untouched, and no arithmetic, kernel or KV cell moves.

**Measured (1 GPU, one binary, kill switch vs default, greedy, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`).**  27B UD-Q4_K_XL +
DFlash2 + `ngram-mod` rewrite request 310.2 -> **316.8 t/s (+2.1 %)**; 27B with `ngram-mod` alone 202.1 ->
**205.4 (+1.6 %)**; 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40` (arena on, 850 MiB free) + DFlash2 422.1 -> **440.4 (+4.3 %,
63 MiB state)**; the zh story and continuation requests 0 %; 2 slots `--kv-unified` +2.6 %.  Text, drafted and
accepted tokens identical in every arm; +150 MiB VRAM per used slot on the 27B, -150 MiB RSS.
**The PR's +10.0 %/+15.8 % does not reproduce because the win is (host save cost) x (checkpoints taken)**: a
3039-token rewrite takes 47 checkpoints (8 restores), ~6 % of steps rather than "most", and this box's host save
is 4.5 ms against the submitter's 16 ms (the r96/r151/r152 state-copy folds took the rest).  The feature is worth
as much as the host CPU is slow, which is the direction that helps weaker machines.

**Fixed on top of the submission** (both found in review, neither filed as a TODO):
* **`-nkvo` / `-ngl 0` claimed device memory for a host-resident state** (`device memory ... 13502.5 MiB free on
  ROCm0`, io class staging on the CPU buft).  The decision now requires `!no_kv_offload && n_gpu_layers != 0` and
  says so in its own log line; the `-nkvo` arm of the new gate asserts it.
* **The device arm is not a byte image** and that is now documented as an invariant (code comment,
  `patches/README.md`, `AGENTS.md`): `data_tgt` carries only the metadata, the payload is the context's per-seq
  `mem_storage` staging buffer, so a save must be restored before the next save for that sequence (the spec path
  does exactly that) and one of these must never be written to anything persistent.  A host-flagged save does not
  touch the stage.

**Gates.**  `scripts/gate-spec-ckpt-device.sh` is new and is the only gate that reaches this code: three arms
(host `=0`, device, `-nkvo`), requiring the device arm's decision and checkpoint counts, the kill switch on the
host path, `-nkvo` on the host path with its own reason, and byte-identical greedy text plus identical
drafted/accepted counts between the host and device arms - PASS (18 created / 5 restored per arm).  Also
`tests/test-llama-context` `baseline|cp_h|cp_d|cp_h_s|cp_d_s` **5/5** on the 27B (the io class the server now
uses), `gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` PASS (27B + DFlash2), `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean, coherence + prefill-logit as in
every release.  MTP Protocol A was not re-run: the change copies the same bytes from another location, MTP drafts
never take this checkpoint (`draft.size() <= n_rs_seq`), and the multi-GPU spec path is inert.

**Not covered / accepted.**  Single GPU only (multi-GPU would need a change and a run - under a split the state is
spread over devices and the r157 device io class bounces through the host anyway); +150 MiB per used slot is not
in the `--fit` estimate.

**Unrelated, observed while building** (not touched, for the maintainer): every build warns
`ggml-backend-meta.cpp:344: missing field 'moe_host_master_buft' initializer` - the meta device's positional
`ggml_backend_device_i` initializer omits the last field, so `ggml_backend_dev_moe_host_master_buft()` answers
NULL for a tensor-split (`-sm tensor`) device and `--host-experts pool` there falls back to the pinned master.
Pre-existing (the file is unchanged by this release); it needs its own assessment.

## 261030.008 (r183) -- PR #256's GDN decode folds ship (block 10): +5.9 % gfx1100 / +3.3 % gfx1201 decode, bit-identical, plus the 2-D copy guard that fixes a Flash-Next `-sm tensor` load abort

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r183` (16 blocks; block 10 amended).**  Contributor `@briansp2020`'s
[PR #256](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/256), filed as `wip/gdn-decode-folds-r176/`
against r176 and applying with `git am` unchanged to r182.  It is the follow-up that #249's review asked for
(the 1-token direct conv gated on `gdn_conv_norm_match() > 0`, `ssm_prescan` checked first, the
`return 0` -> `continue` slip fixed, measured on both gfx1100 and gfx1201), and the win arrives through the two
folds that gating enables.  All four patches are taken; the release also carries a load-abort fix found while
setting up its Flash-Next arm (**not** the PR's: it reproduces on stock r182).

**What shipped.**
* The direct GDN conv also writes the recurrent **snapshot tails** (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GDN_CONV_SNAP=1` off), so
  the `CONCAT` and the snapshot `CPY`s launch nothing wherever the direct conv runs.  Taken only when a runtime
  byte-span check shows nothing between the CONCAT and the conv writes over `state`/`x` or touches a snapshot
  destination and the destinations are disjoint; the batched-copy run stops at a folded snapshot `CPY`.
* The **conv-state gather fold** (`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_GATHER=0` off): `build_rs`'s `GET_ROWS` of the conv
  cache, feeding a CONCAT the direct conv takes, is deferred into the kernel, which reads the cache row itself
  (`row id = src[1]`) and writes it back with the three state values preloaded.  One sequence, <= 16 tokens, the
  CONCAT the gather's only reader, only folded snapshot `CPY`s writing the cache before the conv; a CONCAT over
  a deferred gather the direct conv does not take **aborts** by design.
* The **1-token direct conv** (`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_DECODE=0` off): RDNA4 / RDNA3_0, only where it also
  elides the q/k norm pair and the decode-only `ssm_prescan` would not take the conv first.  The data-dependent
  gate lives in the compute-time matchers; `graph_optimize` uses the structural
  `ggml_cuda_gdn_conv_pattern_at_concat`, a superset, so its alloc deps cover every case.
* The **shared-expert gate fold** (`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_SHEXP_GATE_SIGMOID=0` off): the gate `MUL_MAT` (one row) +
  `SIGMOID` + `MUL` + `ADD` in the `mul_mat_vec_f` launch the gate would take, reproducing `op_sigmoid` and
  `sigmoid_mul_add_f32`'s `contract(off)` expression.  BF16/F32 gate weights only, decode/verify band.
* The **2-D copy guard**: `ggml_cuda_cpy_as_memcpy_2d` keeps upstream's fast path only while the padded span
  fits the tensor's own allocation.  A 2-D copy of a view of a mirrored model weight is refused with
  `invalid argument` when the weight sits in the slab, which made `Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS -sm tensor -ncmoe 48`
  abort at load on r182 and earlier (device 1, `blk.1.ple_conv1d.weight`'s column view, the qwen4exp PLE conv;
  `-sm layer` and `GGML_CUDA_SLAB=0` both loaded).  The scalar kernels are the bit-identical fallback, and no
  other model we hold reaches the path (0 2-D copies in an instrumented run of 35B-A3B, 4B, 27B, gpt-oss).

**Worth (1 GPU, `llama-bench -r 5`, two interleaved rounds, all four on vs all four off).**  gfx1100

excepted); this is a 1-GPU decode win.  The shared-expert gate fold needs a **BF16/F32** gate weight, so no

## 261030.006 (r182) -- PR #253's 1-token router fold ships (block 10): +1.2..+3.1 % MoE decode, bit-identical

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r182` (16 blocks; block 10 amended).**  Contributor `@briansp2020`'s
[PR #253](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/253), filed as `wip/router-topk-fold/`
against r176 and applying with `git am` unchanged to r181.  A 1-token MoE decode ran the router
(`ffn_gate_inp`, an F32 `MUL_MAT` with one column) as `mul_mat_vec_f<float,float,1,256>` and then the fused
`topk_moe` as a second launch.  `topk_moe_cuda` now has a `router` mode: block `b` computes logit `b` with the
same thread map, `float2` loads, `#pragma unroll 4`, `ggml_cuda_mad` calls and warp + cross-warp butterfly as
`mul_mat_vec_f`, writes it to the logits tensor (still written, still allocated), and the block that finishes
last -- `__threadfence()`, then one atomic on a self-resetting counter in the last `moe_red_counters()` slot
-- runs the **unchanged** selection.  One launch replaces two.  The dispatcher arm reuses the topk-moe
matcher (refactored out of `ggml_cuda_try_fuse` into `ggml_cuda_topk_moe_match_at`), and
`ggml_cuda_router_topk_moe_ok` re-checks the dispatcher's route rather than trusting it: F32
weight/activation/output, contiguous, 64/128/256 experts, wave32, not MMB, `should_use_mmvf`, the same
block-size choice, one logits row, no bias, no delayed softmax, no Hadamard hint, no padded compute-buffer
`src0`.  `GGML_CUDA_ROUTER_TOPK=0` is the kill switch.

**Both patches taken, plus a 5-line hardening.**  The contributor's `0002` steps the fold aside on **RDNA4
above 128 experts**, where the one launch measured slower than the two; we reproduced the direction on our
R9700 (**-0.3 % d0 / -0.5 % d4096** with `0001` only at 256 experts; they measured -0.8/-1.0 %), so it ships
as-is.  Our amendment adds the Hadamard-hint and padded-compute-buffer refusals above (both unreachable for
a router -- the hint is only emitted by `llama_mul_mat_hadamard` and a router weight is never a
compute-buffer view -- but the predicate now mirrors `ggml_cuda_mul_mat` in its own order, the
`ggml_cuda_mul_mat_takes_mmq` discipline).

## 261030.007 -- `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` grades the save-and-clear fallback (a gate fix, no block change)

**Not a release: `patches/` and `release.json` are untouched by this commit and the block set is unchanged
(r182 is the release current at the time of writing); no re-cut and no tag.**  A scripts-only fix to the server
parking gate, plus the campaign's decisions.

**The gate HARD-failed a legitimate outcome, for two reasons.**  (1) It counted parks with
`grep -c "seq_park:"`, which also matches the **region-backed refusal warning** — logged under the `seq_park`
logger prefix — so a windowed cache read `seq_park=1 seq_unpark=0` and looked like "a park that never came
back".  (2) When the cache declines the park, the server says *"cannot park the idle slot: saving it to the
prompt cache and clearing it"* (`server-context.cpp`, `park_idle_slots_for_launch`), which is exactly the arm
the gate compares against (`lazyoff`); the gate should require `park == lazyoff` and report the fallback, not
fail on *"parking moved nothing"*.  That path already existed for any slot whose cells are not one run
(a prefix shared through `seq_cp`); the windowed KV (block 15) made it reachable.

**The fix.**  Count actual **moves** (`seq_park: seq N [lo, hi) -> [dst, bound)`), and when no move happened
but the park arm logged the fallback line, report *"parking declined -> save-and-clear fallback (N idle
transitions)"* and keep the `park == lazyoff` oracle.  A mixed arm (some parks, some fallbacks) passes with a
note; a run that neither parks nor falls back still fails.

**Verified** (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS + MTP draft, 1 GPU, `SM=layer NCMOE=48 CTX=40960`, prose prompt, 96
tokens/request, 1 R9700/gfx1201):

| arm | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `LLAMA_KV_RESIDENT_CELLS=1024` (2 windows) | **FAIL** `parking moved nothing (seq_park=1 seq_unpark=0)`; text `park == lazyoff` on A-D | **PASS** `parking declined -> save-and-clear fallback (3 idle transitions)`, `park == lazyoff` A-D, `parkoff != lazyoff` on B/C/D (the workload still reproduces #210) |
| no knob (control) | passed | **PASS** `6 park move(s), 2 unpark move(s) traced`, same oracle |

`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean on every arm's log and the kernel journal; no aborts.

**Decisions taken (the campaign's, recorded here so they do not get re-litigated):**

* **`auto` stays capacity-only** — `--fit` sizes a window only when a pinned `-c` does not fit, against
  `free - margin - everything-but-the-KV` with the arena/slab reserve in the margin.  The arena half
  (`A2-MIXED-BACKING.md` §3.7.11.4 A: +2.2..2.9 GiB, worth +3.8 % decode at the 122B's residency and ~0 at the
  35B's) needs a **numeric** `W` at or above the run depth; a policy that spills to grow the arena is not
  adopted (a percentage-of-slab form of `W` stays deferred).
* **A window across a `-sm tensor` split stays parked** — designed in
  `archive/work/kv-residency/A6-TENSOR-SPLIT-WINDOW.md` (design only; its `common/fit.cpp` cross-check lists four things
  an implementation must honour, `margins[0]` first).  It is picked up on the multi-GPU development host.
* **Goal B (a sparse attended set streamed cheaply) is next**, developed **inside `wip/` only** until it is
  promoted; `patches/` is left alone while the other delivery work is in flight.

## 261030.005 (r181) -- block 15: `--fit` + `-sm tensor` fixed properly (three asserts), plus three `auto` wiring defects

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r181` (16 blocks; block 15 amended).**  Found while gating r180's multi-GPU arms
(the PR #252 work): **default `--fit` aborted on every multi-device `-sm tensor` run in r178/r179/r180.**  The
block-15 KV-region plumbing reaches its backend entry points through `ggml_backend_dev_backend_reg(dev)`, and a
**Meta** (tensor-split) device has no backend reg (`device->reg == NULL`), so
`ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address(NULL, …)` hit `GGML_ASSERT(reg)` (`ggml-backend.cpp:1052`) at model load,
before a token.  Three separate paths asserted: the fit's KV probes (any run, model-independent), the runtime
region-buffer lookup (a numeric `W`), and the spill budget/link lookups (a numeric `W` below `-c`).  The
campaign's own box is single-GPU, which is why nothing caught it.

**The fix, and why this is the right one rather than a null guard.**  The window is one VMM region **per
device**, and a tensor split has no per-device region buffer type to hand out (its KV lives on the Meta
wrapper), so the backend genuinely has no answer there.  A reg-less device now reads as "the backend does not
provide this" (`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp`: one `llama_kv_region_dev_reg()` helper behind all five lookups), the
window is **declined** with one message naming the tensor split from the fit and one from the cache, and the KV
stays fully resident; `-sm layer` and one device keep their per-device region buffers.  In `common/fit.cpp` the
probe reg is resolved through the Meta wrapper to a **simple child** (the same walk the split accounting
already does), so the identification stays exact if a multi-device window ever exists, and a `nullptr` there
means "unknown", never an abort.

**Three wiring defects in the same code, all reproducible on ONE device:**

* **`auto`'s decision was indistinguishable from "nobody decided".**  `--fit` handed down `0` for "the KV fits
  fully resident, keep it", which the cache read as "the fit did not run" — so a run that had just been sized
  correctly still warned `LLAMA_KV_RESIDENT_CELLS=auto is sized by --fit, which did not run`.  A decided-0 flag
  (`llama_kv_region_resident_cells_decided`) makes the three states distinct: window, decided-no-window
  (silent), undecided (warns).
* **Every run without the knob logged a KV warning.**  "the windowed KV is unavailable for this cache (no
  spilled cells)" fired on the default path; it now only fires when a window was requested and declined for a
  real reason (non-uniform cell geometry, or a region-less device).
* **The pinned-RAM clamp could be taken past the VRAM budget.**  `LLAMA_KV_SPILL_RAM_PCT`'s clamp raises `W`
  so the worst-case spill fits RAM; the fit applied it unconditionally and then reported the result as
  "does not make this fit either".  It is now taken only while the wider window still meets the VRAM target;
  otherwise the fit reports that the ceiling cannot be served at this `-c` and drops the window, and the
  normal path shrinks the context.  **This is not cosmetic:** an intermediate form of the fix accepted a
  **235 GiB** pinned-spill plan for a 4B at `-c 8388608`, and creating it OOM-killed the test box (83 GB
  anon-rss, kernel OOM, session lost).  Any future change here must bound the *planned spill*, not just the
  resident window.

**Verified (gfx1201).**  `--fit on` (the default) at **2 and 3 devices**, `-sm tensor`, with no knob / a
numeric `W` / `auto`, fit on and off: no assert, tokens produced, exactly one message per requested window.
`-sm layer` 2 devices and 1 GPU still take the window per device, and `auto` still sizes the 27B Q8_0
`-c 262144 -ctk/-ctv q8_0` arm identically to r179/r180 (**123265 of 262144 cells**, 4092.8 MiB resident /
4611.2 MiB spilling).  One device with no knob: **no KV message at all**.  Purity unchanged: plain vs a
**spilling** windowed arm prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 99.990 %** (q8_0 KV) and greedy text byte-identical on
that arm; 35B-A3B (1 GPU and 2-GPU `-sm tensor`), dense 27B and the canonical 27B Q8_0 prefill-logit gate
(**0.000000 / 100.000 %**) are byte-identical to r180; MTP Protocol A unchanged (tensor acceptance **0.60816**
= 1937/3185, `plain == draft-mtp`); `validate-set.sh` green; `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from d23cd1dbe
--fast` 1/1; no GPU faults.

**Re-cut.**  Block 15 amended (`d23cd1dbe` -> `83d2c391a`), everything else byte-unchanged; `release.json`
`tip 83d2c391a` / `tree 7a139daded`.

**Left open for the campaign (not delivery work):** the window is single-device only (a tensor split declines
it, now by design and with a message), and the `auto` **policy** questions are unchanged by this fix — `auto`
still only spills a `-c` the user pinned, and it still sizes the window against the VRAM left after the
expert-cache arena reserve, so on a `-ncmoe` config the arena wins the VRAM.  Both are recorded in
`archive/work/kv-residency/A2-MIXED-BACKING.md` §3.7.12 for the campaign's resume.

## 261030.004 (r180) -- PR #252's GDN small-projection gather ships (block 10): +2.8 % decode on the quantized-GDN shape, bit-identical

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r180` (16 blocks; block 10 amended).**  Contributor PR
[#252](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/252) (`@briansp2020`) patch **0003**
(`GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_CONCAT_REORDER`).  Its siblings shipped in r177; this one was *declined, not refuted*
(`TODO` #119, now closed) because it needs a **quantized `<= 256`-row** weight and skips `Q8_0`, and every
Qwen3.6-35B GGUF we held keeps the GDN `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` at **F32** (the unsloth UD quants) or `Q8_0`
(skipped by design).  The submitter then supplied the exact file and command line, and the claim reproduced.

**What it does.**  A structural pass in `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_optimize`, right after the r177 V/K rotate,
RDNA3_0 + RDNA4: from the first quantized `MUL_MAT` of `<= 256` rows it moves up to 2 later `MUL_MAT`s with
the same `src1`, weight type, `K` and row stride directly after it (at most one of them larger than 256
rows), so the Qwen3.5/3.6 GDN `ssm_beta` + `ssm_alpha` + `attn_gate` projections run as **one** ksplit launch
via the r177 row concat.  Same nodes, one stream, every ubatch size, idempotent; `=0` is the kill switch.

**Reproduced on their exact model** (`lmstudio-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M`, sha256
`4ac6a06bce551257267f49ad2226f8671a22519ccc1a4dde9d5b433d1f2a410d` — downloaded and verified, with
`ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta`/`attn_gate` all Q4_K and 40 blocks at `full_attention_interval = 4`, i.e. 30 GDN
layers).  1 GPU gfx1201, 3 interleaved rounds, `-fa 1 -p 0 -n 128 -d 0,4096 -r 10`: tg128 **129.35 ->
132.93 (+2.8 %)**, d4096 **126.16 -> 129.65 (+2.8 %)**; `=0` returns 129.45 (≡ base).  The submitter's
+3.0 / +2.9 % reproduce (theirs on a R9700, gfx1100 +3.5 % on their 7900 XTX).  Attribution: with the row
concat itself disabled it is 130.7, i.e. the win is the concat the gather enables.  Kernel census
(`rocprofv3`): 44 808 -> 42 231 dispatches over 43 decode steps = **exactly 60 fewer launches per token**,
as claimed (30 layers x 2).

**Purity.**  Prefill-logit KLD **-0.000000 / 99.990 %** at the default ubatch and **0.000000 / 100.000 %** at
`-ub 1` and `-ub 8` (`--ab GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_CONCAT_REORDER=0`); greedy text byte-identical on 1, 2 and 3
devices for that model, and on Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M, dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, Gemma4-31B QAT UD-Q4_K_XL,
Flash-Next Q4_K_M (`-sm tensor -ncmoe 48`) and the DFlash2 draft arm.  MTP Protocol A unchanged (3 devices:
layer acceptance 0.62134 = 1951/3140 at 51.6 t/s, tensor 0.60816 = 1937/3185 at 101.5 t/s; `on == off` and
`plain == draft-mtp` byte-identical in both split modes).  Rule-5 `llama-batched-bench -npl 1,4,8` flat
(124.3 -> 127.2 / 322.5 -> 319.5 / 414.7 -> 417.3), the canonical 27B Q8_0 prefill-logit gate
**0.000000 / 100.000 %**, `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 898103305 --fast` 2/2, `validate-set.sh`
green, no GPU faults.

**Two guards in the pass are load-bearing, not tuning** (`patches/README.md`, block 10, "r180"): never move a
`MUL_MAT` whose output feeds a `CONCAT` within 8 nodes (`ggml_cuda_ssm_conv_in_try_fuse` skips those nodes,
so a node moved in would silently never run) and never move a `Q8_0` weight (`ggml_cuda_ssm_prescan_try_fuse`
matches its 16-node chain by position and only fires on `Q8_0`).  A future edit that relaxes either is a
wrong-answer bug, not a missed optimisation.

**Scope, stated plainly:** the pass cannot fire where the GDN small projections are `F32` (unsloth UD
quants, and even their "True" Q3_K_M) or `Q8_0`, so the win is real on llama.cpp-quantized files
(lmstudio-community's are) and inert on most of the GGUF set this box holds.  It is inert on a dense model
and on the qwen4exp/Flash-Next arm.

**Re-cut.**  Block 10 amended (`f71e0a024` -> `e809fb56f`), blocks 11-15 re-cut on top; `release.json`

## 261030.003 (r179) -- hotfix: `--fit` could not size the window (a probe-context bug in r178's block 15)

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r179` (16 blocks; block 15 amended).**  r178 shipped a regression that made block
15 unusable with the default `--fit on`: the fit identifies the KV's share of the device tier by the **region
buffer type**, and the r178 promotion rule "take the region buffer only when a window is active" meant the
fit's `no_alloc` **measurement context** declined a window, got the plain buffer, and so could not see the KV at
all — the fit then reported *"the requested configuration does NOT fit in device memory"* and aborted the run
**before** the window was ever created.  `LLAMA_KV_RESIDENT_CELLS=auto` and a numeric `W` were both affected, on
any `-c` that needs a window (i.e. exactly the OOM configs the block exists for).

**Fix:** the probe context takes a region buffer explicitly (`llama_kv_region_set_probe`, internal; no batch
ever runs on a probe), so the fit sees the KV and sizes/reports the window as designed.  The runtime path is
untouched: the region buffer is still taken **only** when a window is asked for, so a run without the knob is
byte-identical and keeps OOMing.

**Verified on the reported config** (27B Q8_0, `-c 262144`, q8_0 KV, `--fit on`): `auto` sizes **W = 119108 of
262144** cells (3954.8 MiB VRAM + 4749.2 MiB pinned host) and the server comes up in 4 s; a numeric
`W = 32768` reports 1088.0 MiB resident / 7616.0 MiB spilled; with no knob the fit still reports the
over-budget configuration (r177 behaviour).  Gates re-run on the amended block: default path `5ba44647188f`,
windowed `W=2048` `5ba44647188f`, spilling-arm prefill-logit **−0.000000 / 100.000 %**.

**User-facing correction for r178 users:** `LLAMA_KV_REGION=1` is **not** the window knob (the provider is on
by default and the O1 path is not shipped); the knob is `LLAMA_KV_RESIDENT_CELLS=<cells>|auto`.  On r178 the
workaround was `--fit off` + a numeric `W` (verified); r179 does not need it.

## 261030.002 (r178) -- the windowed KV ships as block 15 (Goal A of #118): an opt-in fixed-VRAM resident window with a pinned-host tail

**Released as `v16-6050b467c-r178` (16 blocks, 00-15; block 15 is new).**  Promoted from the
`archive/work/kv-residency` campaign (TODO **#118**, Goal A).  Opt-in: `LLAMA_KV_RESIDENT_CELLS=<cells>|auto`; with it
unset the KV takes the plain device buffer and a run is byte-identical to r177, **including its OOM**
(verified: `5ba44647188f`, and `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` on the 27B Q8_0 `-c 262144` baseline).

**What it does.**  The KV's VRAM cost becomes a **window** of the newest `W` cells instead of `-c` cells: one
VA reservation (a CUDA/HIP VMM region) holds the whole cache, the window's cells are VRAM and everything
below them pinned system RAM.  `set_rows`, the in-place rope shift, `state_write/read`, the kq mask and the FA
kernels keep addressing one contiguous range, so **no kernel and no op changes**; the window slides in whole
map units (once per few thousand tokens), and the apparatus itself is free (a zero-spill arm measures the same
as plain).  Payoffs: a context that OOMs today runs (27B Q8_0 `-c 262144` = 128 MiB VRAM + 8576 MiB pinned
host for the KV, 944.8 t/s prefill), and with host-resident MoE experts the VRAM the KV does not need *yet*
goes to the arena — at `-c 262144`, `-n 2000`, `-ncmoe` = the model's full layer count: **+2.2 to +2.9 GiB of
arena** (+3.9 to +6.7 points of residency) when `W` is at or above the run's depth, which is 122B-A10B
Q4_K_XL **+3.8 % decode / +4.7 % prefill** and 35B-A3B Q8_0 -0.9 % / +3 %; a `W` 35 k cells *below* the run
depth costs 11-26 %, because the spill is read over the link on every step (`(used − W) × cell_bytes /
55.7 GB/s`).

**Purity.**  A spilled KV is numerically transparent: prefill-logit **KLD −0.000000 / 100.000 %** on a
spilling 27B arm, **−0.000000 / 99.994 %** on a spilling Flash-Next (the only model with two KV caches — the
attention KV *and* the QSA indexer), and every text arm byte-identical to its plain reference (27B f16 and
q8_0, 4B, 35B-A3B, Flash-Next).  `gate-ckpt-reuse.sh`, `gate-state-pipe.sh` and the MTP verify widths pass on
arms that **provably spill** (`FLIP > 0`, `KVREGION_FREE … host=` > 0), and `test-backend-ops -o
FLASH_ATTN_QSA` is 26/26.  Two driver hazards are held: a kind flip zeroes a neighbouring live host mapping
unless the released physical is held across the create (`LLAMA_KV_REGION_QUARANTINE`, default on — `=0`
reproduces the corruption: 325 chars `fb65430049e9`), and every tensor in a windowed region is placed on the
driver's map granularity so a slide step coincides with a mapping.

**Shipped as-is from the campaign except two shape changes:** (1) the region buffer is taken **only** when a
window is active — the campaign's O1 fallback (fully resident, lazily committed) is **not** shipped, because on
a slab-armed MoE config it `GGML_ABORT`s where the plain arm completes; (2) the provider is on by default with
`LLAMA_KV_REGION=0` as the kill switch.  **A1** (the superseded two-base FA read) was stripped (6 FA files +
`ggml.h`/`ggml.c` + the graph plumbing): with one VA range the single-base read is correct, and the windowed
arms are byte-identical to plain at `W` = 1024/2048/4096 on the shipped tree.  **Goal C** (the MTP drafter
ring, `LLAMA_SPEC_DRAFT_WINDOW`) is **not** in the block.

**Re-base:** the campaign was cut against r174; block 15 is cut against r177's tip (`acbeeb840`, the r174→r177
delta in the campaign's files was only `ggml-cuda.cu` +53 lines, so the application was clean).  Patch set
regenerated: 16 patches, `release.json` `tip 38ef3a767` / `tree 92d087ef`, `validate-set.sh` green (fresh
tarball, strict `git am`, checksums, Windows path + portability scans).  Blocks 00-14 are byte-unchanged apart
from their `From` lines and the block-14 re-cut that r177 already carried.

**Owed (campaign, not delivery):** `scripts/gate-park-idle-slots.sh` still fails an arm on "parking moved
nothing" when the server legitimately saves-and-clears instead of parking — a test gap (with no window the gate
passes).  Goal B is not started.

## 261030.001 (r177) -- PR #252: its Q/K/V projection reorder and its RDNA4 row concat shipped (block 10); its GDN projection gather held off (TODO #119)

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r177` (15 blocks, 00-14; block 10 amended).**  Contributor PR
[#252](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/252) (`@briansp2020`) is three graph-ordering
patches cut against r176, applying with `git am` unchanged.  Two are folded into **block 10** (it owns
`ggml_backend_cuda_graph_optimize`'s passes and `mmvq.cu`); blocks 00-09 are byte-unchanged, 0010-0014 were
re-cut.  `benchmarks/2026-10-30-graph-order-r176.md` holds every number; the submission is preserved in
`archive/work/graph-order-r176/`.

**Taken (block 10, default-on, `=0` switch each):**

* **`GGML_CUDA_QK_ROTATE` — the V / K projections of a Q-norm attention layer move in front of the Q
  projection.**  The model graph runs Q `MUL_MAT`, `RESHAPE`, `RMS_NORM`, `MUL`, `ROPE` and *then* V and K,
  so the row concat's scan from the Q matmul stopped at the Q norm (only V+K fused) and the allocator handed
  V/K the Q chain's freed buffers, which made `ggml_cuda_qk_pair_k_at`'s overlap test refuse the Q/K
  norm+rope pair.  A structural pass (`std::rotate` of the V/K block, the r175 shared-expert pattern) fixes
  both.  Same nodes, one stream, bit-identical; every ubatch size; idempotent.
* **`GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_ROW_CONCAT_RDNA4` — the dense 1-token row concat also runs on RDNA4.**  At `ncols_dst == 1`
  a row's dot product is row-count independent there (one warp, no `small_m`; `two_rows` / the decode row
  loop / `grid_stall_pad` only move rows between blocks), so the only new condition is that every segment has
  an **even** row count (a 2-row block must not straddle a segment boundary).  RDNA3_0 keeps its own rule.

**Held off: the GDN small-projection gather (`GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_CONCAT_REORDER`).**  It needs a **quantized**
`<= 256`-row weight and skips `Q8_0`; in every Qwen3.6-35B quant we hold the GDN `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` are
**F32** (UD-Q3_K_M/Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M, Q6_K, Q8_K_XL) or **Q8_0**, and `attn_gate` is Q8_0 in the UD quants — so
the pass cannot fire.  Measured on the 35B, on vs off: gfx1201 **104.4 vs 105.1 t/s**, gfx1100 **141.1 vs
141.1** (neutral to −0.7 %).  Their +3.0 / +3.5 % needs a quant whose GDN small projections stay quantized; we
asked for the exact GGUF + command line and parked it as `TODO` #119.  It is also the only one of the three
with a positional constraint (`ssm_conv_in` skips nodes up to its `CONCAT`; the GDN prescan matches by
position), which is why the submitted guard list exists.

**Measured** (1 GPU, alternating rounds, `-sm layer -t 8`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`; stock = the r176 release
tree, kept as `build-r176/bin`): gfx1100 Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M tg128 **194.3 -> 205.8 (+5.9 %)**, d4096
170.0 -> 180.2 (+6.0 %); gfx1201 the same model **152.0 -> 160.9 (+5.9 %)**, d4096 131.2 -> 137.2 (+4.5 %) —
`QK_ROTATE=0` returns both to base, and `ROW_CONCAT_RDNA4=0` leaves 156.9 (so the reorder alone is +3.2 % and
the RDNA4 concat is +2.6 %).  2-GPU `-sm tensor` 30B: 141.2 -> 147.9 (+4.7 %).  Qwen3.6-35B-A3B +1.8 %
(gfx1201) / +0.7 % (gfx1100, noise); dense 27B flat (32.62 -> 32.72).  The submitter's +5.9 % (RDNA4 d0) and
+7.5 % (RDNA3) reproduce in shape; their 35B absolute figures are ~25 % faster than either box reads here, a
box difference rather than a patch one.

**Gates:** greedy text byte-identical to r176 on 30B-A3B (1 GPU and 2-GPU `-sm tensor`), 35B-A3B, dense 27B,
Gemma4-31B and Flash-Next (`-sm tensor -ncmoe 48`); prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %** at the default
ubatch and at `-ub 1` (the rotate runs at every ubatch size); MTP Protocol A on the dense 27B at 3 devices
unchanged — layer 25.0 -> **51.7 t/s** acceptance **0.621**, tensor 50.8 -> **101.2** acceptance **0.608**,
`plain == draft-mtp` text identical in both split modes; rule-5 band gate flat (31.91/102.11/156.90 ->
31.94/102.20/157.18); `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 19dec99a0 --fast` 2/2; `validate-set.sh` green
(tree `b7adbd1259…`); no GPU faults.

**Invariants for a future edit** (`patches/README.md`, block 10): the rotate runs in the **alloc-deps** half
of the pass, so the meta `marks_only` forward sees the unrotated order — no new mark may depend on adjacency
the rotate changes; the pass is deliberately **not** arch-gated because every fusion it enables is gated
itself; and the RDNA4 concat's even-row-count rule rests on `calc_nwarps_weight` being row-independent at
`ncols_dst == 1`, so re-check that before widening the predicate.

## 261029.008 (r176) -- TODO #117 closed: the expert-cache band is answered only for a model with HOST-RESIDENT experts (a dense single-GPU / `-sm layer` run no longer n-gram-clamps or bounds multi-slot draft widths)

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r176` (15 blocks, 00-14; blocks 09 and 12 amended).**  `TODO.md` item
**#117** (filed by the PR #244 v5 assessment, `WORKLOG.md` 261029.007) is closed.  No kernel, op or numerics
change: the whole delivery change is one predicate in `src/llama-model.cpp` (block 09) plus its contract
comments (`include/llama.h`, block 09; `common/common.cpp`, block 12).

**The defect.**  `llama_model_moe_cache_band()` documents "0 when the cache is not active, i.e. there is no
band to respect", but it considered `model->moe_host_expert_bytes` first and then **fell back to
`model->devices`**.  The CUDA device hook is `moe_cache_enabled() ? moe_cache_max_tok_dev(dev) : 0` and
`g_enabled` is **true by default** (unset `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` = AUTO), so on any non-Meta device list -- a
single GPU, or any `-sm layer` run -- a model with **no routed expert at all** answered **16** on RDNA4.  Two
consumers then acted on a band that does not exist: `common_speculative_clamp_ngram_n_max()` cut a 64-token
n-gram draft to 15 on a dense model, and `align_draft_caps()` bounded a multi-slot MTP-adaptive verify width
to `band / n_drafting - 1` rows.  Under `-sm tensor` the Meta device reports no band, which is why earlier
tensor-split checks never saw it.

**The fix.**  Only a device that actually carries host-resident experts has a band: the function now
considers `model->moe_host_expert_bytes` alone.  That account is filled by the loader for a pinned host
expert master (r97: a pageable CPU-only placement is deliberately not accounted), so it is empty exactly when
no routed expert is streamed from a host master.  The device hook's `moe_cache_enabled()` gate is kept, so a
slab-declined or arena-released host-expert config still reports 0 (the r129 / TODO #96 case), and
`moe_cache_has_tables()` is deliberately **not** used: tables register during the first compute, after
`llama_init_from_model`, which is exactly the r129 bug.  The in-tree consumers needed no change
(`verify_batch_width()`'s two call sites are already inside `!moe_host_expert_bytes.empty()` blocks).

**Measured (Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU, greedy, seed 42, `--spec-type ngram-mod
--spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64`, `-n 200`).**  `prompts/recall.txt`: r175 **142.1 / 142.4 t/s**, r176
**186.8 / 186.9 t/s (+31.4 %)** with the generated text **byte-identical** (1104 chars, sha `80309046174e`).
Control isolating the clamp from the tree: **r175 with `LLAMA_SPEC_NGRAM_MOD_BAND_CLAMP=0` = 187.9 / 188.3
t/s**, i.e. the whole delta is the clamp and nothing else moved.  `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` is neutral
(30.3/30.3 -> 30.2/30.2, text identical -- n-gram acceptance ~0 there, which is why 261029.007 read the
severity as neutral on that prompt).  This is the delivery's own record of the wide-draft win (144.7 -> 378.7
t/s) reaching a class it could not previously reach.

**The predicate's own matrix** (all `-v`, so the warning is visible): dense 27B 1 GPU **no clamp** (was
`draft length 64 -> 15`); dense 27B 2 GPU `-sm layer` **no clamp**; dense 2 GPU `-sm tensor` no clamp (as
before); 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` 1 GPU **clamps 64 -> 15**; 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40 -sm tensor` 2 GPU **clamps**;
35B-A3B `-cmoe` (all experts on the host) **clamps**; 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` with `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0`
**no clamp** (the cache is off, so there is no arena to respect -- unchanged).

**Gates run for the release.**  Coherence against a kept r175 build, byte-identical on every arm: dense 27B
1 GPU (`-n 128`, sha `980623270508`), dense 27B 2 GPU `-sm tensor` (sha `dad22c4270ab`), dense 27B
`--spec-type draft-mtp n3` (same sha as plain), 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` (sha `5d0d8db7bb9b`) and 4B Q8_0
(sha `11e3fdd3d795`).  **MTP Protocol A** (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 devices, prose, `-n 2000`, bf16 KV): layer
plain 25.0 -> `draft-mtp` **62.1** t/s, tensor plain 50.9 -> **120.9** t/s against r175's 61.9 / 120.6, text
byte-identical in all four arms (`--spec-type none` and `draft-mtp` each match their own r175 run and each
other), acceptance **identical** (layer 0.81015, tensor 0.80385) and `n_accepted` identical.  **Prefill-logit
gate**: **mean KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 100.000 %** against the recorded base.  **`gate-spec-align.sh` PASS**
(gate 9 -- this change alters `align_draft_caps`'s band input): 2 GPU diverging pair 117.4 -> 145.3 t/s
(+24 %), 3 GPU 138.9 -> 178.0 (+28 %), host-expert arm 125.3 -> 151.5 (+21 %) with split steps 58+1 -> 0+1 --
i.e. the multi-slot alignment still merges widths **with** host experts present -- the equal-length arms inert
(-0.9 / +0.6 / +1.0 %), the mixed-drafter chain inert (+1.0 %, identical draft counts), every single-slot
request byte-identical on/off and the `n_seq == 1` text byte-identical (`b8775233a93a`); `check-gpu-faults.sh`
clean on the journal and on every arm log (coherence, MTP, n-gram and spec-align runs).  **Per-block build**
`--changed-from cc1def018 --fast`: 3/3 (block 09 32 s, block 12 356 s, the tip 12 s); blocks 00-08 and 10-11,
13-14 byte-unchanged.  **`validate-set.sh`** green (fresh codeload tarball, strict `git am`, 15/15, tree
`e990c8611b715dcba923b36c91baeaf436c02d2b`, Windows-path and Windows-portability scans clean).

**Note on r176 vs the r175 band.**  Nothing changes for a config that has host experts: the band there was
already answered from `moe_host_expert_bytes`.  The dense `-sm tensor` answer was already 0.  So the change is
confined to host-expert-free models on a non-Meta device list, and no arm above moved a token.

**Also fixed (doc):** the `TODO.md` table's `#118` row had been appended after a blank line, so it rendered as
a stray paragraph instead of a table row; it is now the first row (newest first) with `#117` retired.

**Artifacts:** `release.json` = `v15-6050b467c-r176`, tip `19dec99a0`
(tree `e990c8611b715dcba923b36c91baeaf436c02d2b`); the patch set was regenerated from the canonical chain,

## 261029.007 (no release) -- PR #244 v5 (DFlash2 adaptive verify width) assessed on r175 and closed: inert on our dense payloads, still a loss on the arena arm, and a band-bound loss on a dense 3-slot server

**No delivery change, no release.**  Contributor PR
[#244](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/244) (`@overdoingism`, `wip/dflash-adaptive-width/` in the
PR branch only) was re-submitted as **v5** (patch sha256 `6d8bec95…`; steps timed per width, no width move on
unobserved positions, one width per move with a 24-draft first window / 8-draft later windows, the width carried into
the next turn of a conversation, and the measured step time proposing moves).  It was applied to the **r175 tip**
(`cc1def018`; `git apply --check` clean, builds `all`), assessed against the same arms as the v3 review, and **not
adopted; the PR is closed** with the review and an invitation to open a focused opt-in PR carrying only this feature
plus the precise config/prompt/conditions where the gain reproduces.  **`TODO #117` is filed** for the delivery bug
the assessment found (the band predicate, below).

**The default path is genuinely inert.**  With `LLAMA_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE` unset, the scratch build's text sha and
`draft_n`/`draft_n_accepted` are identical to the canonical r175 build on all four prompts.  Dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL +
DFlash2-Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, greedy, `-n 192`, two starts each: prose **80.6 / 79.4** fixed 7 vs **80.0 / 79.3** adaptive;
code **99.0 / 97.5** vs **98.1 / 97.7**; recall **142.4 / 140.6** vs **141.2 / 140.6**; reasoning **101.7 / 100.3** vs
**100.9 / 100.6** — the same drafts, i.e. the controller never leaves width 7.  At `-n 512` prose 104.0 fixed 7 /
102.2 fixed 6 / 103.3 adaptive (drafts 600/425 identical to fixed 7); reasoning 512 86.4 vs 86.3.  This is the v3
review's ask satisfied and is a real improvement on v3 (which lost 5.9 % on prose).

**The machinery is free; the decisions are the whole difference.**  `LLAMA_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE_COST=0.001` (monotone, so
the width stays at 7) lands on fixed 7 with identical drafts: **117.6** vs 116.2/117.1 on the arena arm at `-n 192`
(drafts 335/143) and **167.5** vs 168.9 at `-n 512` (drafts 656/417).

**The `-ncmoe` + arena arm is still a loss.**  35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M + DFlash2-Q8_0, 2 GPU `-sm tensor`, `-ncmoe 40`,
`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=6000`, prose: fixed 5 / 6 / 7 = 116.3 / **118.0** / 116.2-117.1 at `-n 192`, adaptive **105.6 /
105.7 (-9.4 %)**; fixed 5 / 6 / 7 = 159.8 / 168.3 / **168.9** at `-n 512`, adaptive **156.6 (-7.3 %)**.  Better than
v3 (-15.2 / -12.1 %) but still below every fixed width.  The trace is 7→6 at review 24, 6→5 at 32, then 5→6→7 at
40/48; at 512 the per-width histogram is 5:8, 6:19, 7:70.  The fixed widths are within ~1 %, so the search does not
recover the transient.

**Why a move costs more than the width it lands on (new instrument).**  `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_TRACE=1` over three sequential
192-token prose requests on the arena arm: fixed 7 `capture=1574 properties_changed=1782 direct=6838`; adaptive
**`capture=3628 properties_changed=2974 direct=8390`**, and the adaptive arm is still **-8 % on the third request**
(143.6 vs 158.1 t/s), so it is not a one-time cold cache.  Each verify width is a distinct set of captured graphs and
the repeated width changes churn that cache (replay refused, nodes run direct).  A step-time-only cost model does not
price that, which is why a marginal width change looks cheap.

**The band bound fires with no arena (the delivery bug).**  On the dense 27B, 1 GPU, `--parallel 3`, the adaptive
alignment computes `band / 3 - 1 = 4` and loses **7.5 %** wall (4.82 s vs 4.46 s; recall 152/152 vs 167/167 accepted);
`LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN=0` restores 4.42 s.  `llama_model_moe_cache_band()` answers 16 because `moe_cache_enabled()` is true
by default (AUTO) even with no registered table, and the function falls back to `model->devices` when
`moe_host_expert_bytes` is empty — against its own "0 when the cache is not active" contract.  The same mis-detection
makes v5 print `cost 0.150` on the dense 1-GPU run (README says 0.09) and clamps **our** canonical r175,
`ngram-mod --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64` on the same dense 1-GPU model, **64 -> 15** (the warning's routed-expert premise
is false there; `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0` lifts it).  Filed as `TODO #117` with the fix direction (consider only
`moe_host_expert_bytes`, keep the `moe_cache_enabled()` gate; not `moe_cache_has_tables()`, which is the r129 bug).
Measured n-gram severity on `prose` was neutral (acceptance ~0: 29.99 vs 29.61 t/s), but the clamp can only cost where
a wide n-gram draft would hit.

**No measurable gain on any arm we can run.**  Dense 1 GPU greedy: inert on all four prompts and at 512.  Dense 1 GPU,
prose 512 at T 0.7: 55.1/54.8 fixed vs **55.2/55.5** adaptive (neutral; the width walks 7→3→4→5), `COST=0.09` 55.0.
2-slot 27B `-sm tensor` concurrent pair: max wall 3.17-3.26 s fixed vs 3.09-3.21 s adaptive (neutral; the sum of the
per-slot `predicted_per_second` over-counts when the slots finish at different times).  3 slots dense 1 GPU: -7.5 % from
the band bound.  Arena: -9.4/-7.3 %.  Text matched the fixed arm in every greedy arm and slot count; all logs
`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  The contributor's +13-21 % is on Thai/zh/low-acceptance continuations we do not have;
their own added cost is a timing-driven width, so a run whose width moves is not reproducible start to start wherever
the width changes text — a property that rules out default-on for a delivery feature (the greedy gates rely on
start-to-start identity).

**Decision.**  Not adopted; closed.  The reply asks for a focused opt-in PR (only this feature), with the exact model
files, full server command, prompt (or hash + attachment), `n_predict`, sampling/slot setup and repeated baseline-vs-
adaptive starts, and says we will re-run those conditions.  Our own controller prototypes from the previous rounds
(defer the first decision to 32 reviews, raise `COST` to the measured step fit, no-repeat window) only made it inert on
our short responses, so the ask is for a payload where the gain is measurable, not another controller revision on the
same payloads.

## 261029.006 (r175) -- PR #250's seven RDNA3 decode fusions shipped (block 10); its qwen3moe graph reorder declined, its Q8_1 padding gap fixed here

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r175` (15 blocks, 00-14; block 10 amended).**  Contributor PR
[#250](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/250) (`@briansp2020`) is seven independent
decode fusions filed as `wip/decode-fusions-rdna3/`, cut against r174 and applying with `git am -3`
unchanged.  `benchmarks/2026-10-29-rdna3-decode-fusions.md` holds every number below.

**Taken (block 10, default-on, `=0` switch each):** the FA combine publishes its output's Q8_1
(`GGML_CUDA_FA_COMBINE_Q8`); the 1-token MoE gate/up+GLU publishes the down projection's Q8_1
(`GGML_CUDA_MOE_GLU_Q8`); the fused K norm+rope+SET_ROWS kernel also writes the V row
(`GGML_CUDA_ROPE_SET_ROWS_V`); MoE GEMV takes 4 rows per block on RDNA3_0 (`GGML_CUDA_MOE_RPB_WIDE`);
the 1-token MoE down writes the weighted reduction (`GGML_CUDA_MWR_FOLD`); Q and K norm+rope run as one
launch (`GGML_CUDA_ROPE_QK_PAIR`); dense V/K/Q projections run as one ksplit launch on RDNA3_0
(`GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_ROW_CONCAT`).  They are folded into **block 10** rather than appended as a new block:
block 10 owns the fusion dispatcher, the rope matcher and `mmvq-moe`, and it is the block that *creates*
`ggml-cuda-try-fuse.cu` and `mmvq-moe.cu`, so no earlier block can carry them.  Blocks 00-09 are
byte-unchanged; 0010-0014 were re-cut (block 11's `fattn-qsa.cu` call site takes the new combine
argument).

**The claims reproduce.**  gfx1100 (7900 XTX, 1 GPU, 3 alternating rounds), Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M:
tg128 **172.3 -> 206.2 (+19.6 %)** and d4096 **153.6 -> 179.6 (+17.0 %)** with the series as submitted
(they claimed +20.6 / +17.7); Qwen3.6-35B-A3B **138.2 -> 141.0 (+2.0 %)** (claimed +2.5); dense 27B
+0.5 %; prefill flat.  **The submitter could not test RDNA4 and it wins there too, with only five of the
seven patches armed** (0006/0009 are RDNA3_0-gated): gfx1201, 1 GPU, 30B-A3B **133.0 -> 142.2
(+6.9 %)**, 35B-A3B **102.0 -> 105.0 (+2.9 %)**, dense 27B +0.4 %.  Every switch was verified live by
its own switch-off delta (2.5 / 2.1 / 2.2 / 3.6 / 1.0 / 3.7 / 2.8 % on the 30B at gfx1100).

**Declined: the `src/models/qwen3moe.cpp` graph reorder** (`LLAMA_QK_ADJACENT` does not exist here).  It
expands V and the raw K projection before the Q norm so the Q and K norm+rope chains are adjacent, which
is worth 3.3 of the 30B's points (that is the whole difference between +12.2 % and +19.6 %) — but it edits
upstream model code for **every** backend to enable a CUDA fusion, for a retired arch family.  Without it
Qwen3.6 pairs anyway, qwen3moe pairs rarely, and the row concat is unaffected; the shipped 30B arm is
192.8-193.6 t/s at gfx1100 (6.7 % of the 30B's points) and 142.0-142.5 at gfx1201 (3.3 %).  This is a maintainer decision, recorded here per
the report-findings rule.

**Fixed here (the submitter flagged it):** the MoE GLU Q8_1 publish wrote the row's real blocks but not
the zero padding up to `MATRIX_ROW_PADDING`, which `quantize_q8_1` writes.  The cache arena is reused
across graphs, so any future padded-row reader would have found stale blocks; the block that completes a
row's last group now zeroes that row's tail (30B `n_ff` 768 = 8 padding blocks per row).  Text and the
prefill-logit KLD are unchanged.

**Matcher order kept as submitted** (row concat ahead of the dual-output fusion), after measuring that
the choice only matters *with* the model reorder: with the reorder dropped both orders are identical
(30B 192.8-193.6 vs 192.5-193.6; dense 27B 43.11/43.03 vs 43.06/43.03).  The dense FFN gate/up pair is
therefore still taken by the row concat rather than the r171 dual-output fusion — neutral on the 27B, and
recorded in `patches/README.md` (block 10) as the open ownership note.

`b635dc3786021fc8466ce6982e81db70ff86d673`, 15/15), `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 5bdec04ab
--fast` (blocks 10-14 rebuilt after the re-cut, plus the tip), the tip built with `all`, the
