## 261029.005 (r174) -- PR #249 assessed: its M-RoPE powf hoist shipped (block 10), its 1-token GDN direct conv declined (0 % on the submitter's own arm, -1.1 % on RDNA4 dense)

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r174` (15 blocks, 00-14).**  Contributor PR
[#249](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/249) (`@briansp2020`) is two independent
patches cut against r171 and applied to r173 unchanged, and they came out differently.
`benchmarks/2026-10-29-gdn-direct-conv-decode.md` holds the measurements.

**Patch 1 (taken, block 10): the M-RoPE section power is computed once.**  In `rope_multi` and in the
M-RoPE arm of the fused `rms_norm_mul_rope_f32`, every section arm multiplied its position index by the
same `powf(theta_scale, iw/2)`; adjacent lanes take different arms (`sector % 3`), so the divergent arms
were serialized within a wave and `powf` executed once per arm taken.  The power is now hoisted before the
branch — same input, same value, so nothing can move — and the submitter's own diagnosis is exactly what
the kernel census shows: gfx1201 `rms_norm_mul_rope_f32` **3.20 -> 2.85 µs** (`__half` dst) and
**3.06 -> 2.70 µs** (f32 dst) per launch (-11/-12 %).  Wall clock is inside the noise on RDNA4 (8 such
launches per token on a 4B is ~2.8 µs of a 9.7 ms token) and real on gfx1100: **+0.65 %** tg128 on
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M (137.6 -> 138.6, three alternating rounds), +0.25 % on 27B Q4_K_M and 9B Q8_0 —
i.e. the +0.4-0.6 % they claimed.  Greedy text is byte-identical on 4B Q8_0 / 27B UD-Q4_K_XL / 35B-A3B
Q4_K_M (gfx1201) and 9B Q8_0 (gfx1100), and the prefill-logit gate reads **0.000000 KLD / 100.000 %**
same-top-p at the default ubatch (40 chunks, against a base recorded from the r173 release build) and at
`-ub 1` (the decode-width probe, with
`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_VERIFY=0` as the fallback arm).  `test-backend-ops -o ROPE` 450/450.  The
`rope_multi` half is upstream code, so an upstream copy ships as `upstream/rope-mrope-powf-hoist/`.

**Patch 2 (declined): a GDN direct conv for 1-token decode.**  Dropping `gdn_conv_check`'s `T >= 2` gate
alone is not enough (`ssm_conv_in` still claims the concat and the direct conv then reads a matmul output
nobody wrote), so the submission also stands the `ssm_conv_in` epilogue down when the direct matcher takes
the concat.  That is the right shape, and it is numerics-neutral (ub-1 KLD 0.000000 / 100.000 %, text
identical everywhere), but it buys nothing and costs a launch:

* **It does not reproduce on the submitter's own arm.**  gfx1100 (7900 XTX), their model and flags,
  three alternating rounds: stock 137.4-137.8 tg128, `+0001` 138.5-138.6, `+0001+0002` 138.6-138.7,
  `+0001+0002` with `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_VERIFY=0` 138.7-138.9 — the conv change is **0 %**, not the
  +1.2-1.3 % claimed.  Same on 27B Q4_K_M and 9B Q8_0 (0 %).
* **Where the q/k norm fold is refused it is a regression.**  The direct kernel only repays if it also
  elides the norm pair (which it does on 35B-A3B MoE: same launch count, 0 %).  On the dense Q8_0 models
  `gdn_conv_norm_match()` returns -1 (its overlap guard refuses at T=1), so the `ssm_conv_in` epilogue —
  which wrote the whole CONCAT inside the mmvq, for free — stands down and `gdn_concat_tail` takes its
  place: **+1 launch per GDN layer per token** (1560 over 64 decode tokens, 1.44 µs each) while the fused
  conv is *not* faster than `ssm_conv_f32` (1.30 vs 1.43 µs).  Measured on gfx1201, Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0 tg256
  (3 rounds): stock **103.57**, `+0001` 103.58, `+0001+0002` **102.43 (-1.10 %)**, and the `VERIFY=0`
  control 103.56 — the loss is entirely the T=1 case.  Their "the same launch count" holds only in the
  norm-fold case.
* Two smaller points, for the record: at the SSM_CONV node the direct conv is tried before the decode-only
  `ssm_prescan` 15-node fusion, so on the archs it targets it can no longer be preempted into prescan (no
  model here reaches prescan — `ssm_conv_l2_gatebeta` appears in no trace, and
  `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_SSM_PRESCAN=1` changes nothing on stock — but a Q8_0 GDN model with matching wiring
  could); and the new call site returns 0 instead of `continue`, which abandons the remaining candidate
  CONCATs in the 8-node window.  The submitter flagged the (pre-existing) missing conv-output aliasing
  check themselves; T=1 is the least exposed shape for it (each thread reads and writes only its own
  index), so it is not the blocker.

A fix would have to gate the decode case on `gdn_conv_norm_match() > 0` (so no launch is added) and check
prescan first — and then show a measured win on both arch generations; today it has none on either.

**Gates run for the release:** `validate-set.sh` (strict fresh-tarball apply, tree `85a84972c…`),
`gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 8b4592334 --fast` (block 10 + tip rebuilt, 2/2), the prefill-logit
gate at the default and `-ub 1` ubatches, MTP Protocol A on the dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL at 3 devices (**layer
51.6 t/s, acceptance 0.621; tensor 101.1 t/s, acceptance 0.608**, both above their plain arms 25.0 / 51.0;
the layer arm is the recorded reference (51.7 t/s, acceptance 0.62) and the tensor arm reads higher than
the 90.7 / 0.60 in `AGENTS.md` at the same acceptance), the rule-5 stock-relative
band gate (`llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8`, q8_0 KV: 1.065 / 1.319 / 1.713 vs stock
1.064 / 1.313 / 1.703, no worse at B=4/B=8), and `test-backend-ops -o ROPE` 450/450.

**Artifacts:** `release.json` = `v15-6050b467c-r174`, tip `5bdec04ab`, tree
`85a84972c3f4e974ad352ad210d4500e2103226a`; the patch set was regenerated from the canonical chain and the
fork branch re-cut from it.

## 261029.004 (r173) -- PR #248 assessed: its huge-page prompt-cache buffer shipped (+331 ms off a 100K slot's new-buffer save), its banded state copies were declined (they abort on `-sm tensor`)

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r173` (15 blocks, 00-14).**  Contributor PR
[#248](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/248) (`@overdoingism`,
`archive/work/prompt-cache-save-bands/`) is two independent commits, cut on r170 and applied to r172
unchanged, and they came out differently.  `benchmarks/2026-10-29-prompt-cache-hugepage.md` holds the
measurements.

**Commit 2 (taken, block 12): a new prompt-cache state buffer is faulted in with huge pages.**
`server_prompt_cache::take()` reserves a buffer of 64 MiB or more, advises its 2 MiB-aligned part
`MADV_HUGEPAGE` and only then zero-fills it, so a multi-GiB slot state is faulted in 2 MiB pages instead of
4 KiB ones (Linux, THP in `madvise` mode; `LLAMA_SERVER_CACHE_HUGEPAGE=0` restores 4 KiB pages); a recycled
spare keeps the pages it already has.  This is the other half of r130's buffer-reuse cost, and the zero fill
— not the copy — was the dominant term: on this box (9950X3D2, THP `madvise`) 3.47 GiB alloc+zero **470 →
125 ms**, and the server's `prompt cache update took` for a 100K-token slot saving into a new 3.4 GiB buffer
**828.1 → 497.0 ms** (−40 %), with the recycled-buffer case unchanged (292.6 → 291.0 ms).  Request B's wall
clock (it waits on that save) 0.93 → 0.60 s.  Nothing copied differs, so no text or logit can move.

**Commit 1 (declined): batched state copies above `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB`, one band at a time, a piece
larger than a band being cut at a byte offset.**  Two reasons, each sufficient:

* **It aborts on a multi-device tensor split.**  A state piece is a window handed to the backend that owns
  the tensor, and under `-sm tensor` that is the meta backend, which serves only windows aligned to the
  tensor's own layout: a cut piece trips `GGML_ASSERT(size % chunk_size_full == 0)`
  (`ggml-backend-meta.cpp:2523`).  Reproduced at the **default** band — 2× R9700 `-sm tensor`, 27B
  UD-Q4_K_XL, `-ck/-cv q8_0`, `-c 266240`, a 250,000-token slot: **SIGABRT (exit 134) on the save**, where
  the same run with `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_BANDS=0` completes (save 988.8 / restore 2106.7 ms) with
  byte-identical logits; also reproducible with `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB=1` at a 4,000-token state.  A cut
  needs one piece larger than the band, and a piece is one layer's contiguous used-cell run × row bytes, so
  q8_0 (row 1088 on this model) needs > 246,723 contiguous cells — `-c 262144` with a full slot reaches it.
  f16 is *accidentally* aligned (2048 divides 256 MiB) and only cuts, which is why the PR's single-device
  arms never saw it; a 1-GPU arm cannot abort at all, which is why its "not covered: `-sm tensor`" note
  understates the result.  `llama_state_copy_staged()` (r157) already states the rule for the device-state
  class — a band is a run of **whole** pieces and an oversized piece takes a band of its own; the host path
  must obey the same one.
* **It is not a win here.**  The premise (the per-tensor path above 256 MiB is slow, ~2.4 GB/s) does not
  hold on this box: a whole-slot state's pieces are 1-27 MiB, so it already runs at **8.3-14 GiB/s** and the
  batched path's extra host copy costs more than the syncs it removes.  324 MiB state, 1 GPU: save 32.0 →
  51.9 ms, restore 23.1 → 53.9 ms (2 GPU tensor: 55.5 → 68.1 / 49.0 → 108.2); 3.47 GiB at 100K tokens:
  save 304 → 278 ms but restore 242 → 281 ms.  The server end-to-end agrees (bands-only vs release
  799.8/274.1 vs 828.1/292.6 ms).  The batched path's real shape is the opposite one — a checkpoint's ~75
  small pieces (r96) — which is what its `total <= LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB` gate encodes.

**Fixed while folding** (beyond the PR as submitted): `patches/0005-…`-`0011-…` were regenerated, so their
`From` lines now carry the **canonical** commit ids.  They had been left pointing at a wall-clock-stamped
re-cut (`git log` shows the same tree/parent with a `committer` date of the re-cut rather than the author
date), i.e. r172's artifacts and its recorded `.tip` described two different chains.  The trees are
identical, so nothing about the delivery changes; the artifact hashes do.  Block 12's `+/−` column in
`patches/README.md` was stale and is corrected.  No `TODO` item was opened: the declined half is a PR reply
plus the assessment record, not an outstanding delivery defect.

**The PR reply** asks for a re-cut of the declined half with (1) whole-piece bands, (2) a 2- and 3-device
`-sm tensor` arm whose state holds a piece above one band, and (3) a Linux measurement where the banded path
beats the per-tensor path at the sizes that occur.

## 261029.003 (r172) -- PR #247 (the derived kq mask for batches of several sequences) promoted into block 05: 1 GiB of device and 0.9 GiB of pinned host memory back on a 2-slot unified server

**Released as `v15-6050b467c-r172` (15 blocks, 00-14).**  Contributor PR
[#247](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/247) (`@overdoingism`, `wip/kq-derived-multiseq/`) extends
block 05's derived kq mask to ubatches holding several sequences, which is the r160-era hole with money in it: a
`--parallel > 1 --kv-unified` server could never derive a multi-sequence batch, and because `sched_reserve()` measures
with `n_seq_max` sequences it reserved the packed mask even when no batch ever held two.  Folded into **block 05**
(where the derived mask lives); the PR's record moved to `archive/work/kq-derived-multiseq/`.

**The change.**  Sequence `k` of the ubatch gets its own position range: its cells and its tokens' `[lo, hi]` both
shift by `k * 2^23` (`KQ_DERIVED_SEQ_STRIDE`), so the single predicate `tok_lo <= cell_pos <= tok_hi` keeps every token
inside its own sequence's window and **no kernel changes** (both FA families, and the batch-wide skip window stays
conservative).  The ranges are provably disjoint for `pos < 2^23`, and
`static_assert((int64_t) KQ_DERIVED_SEQ_STRIDE*LLAMA_MAX_SEQ - 1 <= INT32_MAX)` turns an upstream `LLAMA_MAX_SEQ` bump
into a build error rather than an overflow.  It is taken only with one KV stream, every token in exactly one sequence,
**no cell carrying two of the batch's sequences** (a prefix copied with `llama_memory_seq_cp`) and every position below
the stride; a multi-sequence batch of **at most 32 tokens** - exactly the multi-slot verify width - and every other
refused shape keep the packed mask.  `llama_kv_cells` gains an O(1) shared-cell counter, so the sharing check costs
nothing unless something was copied.  `kq_mask_packed_reachable()` loses its `n_seq_max > 1` term and `decode()` latches
`kq_mask_multiseq_seen` on the first pre-split batch the form cannot serve, then re-reserves once with the packed mask
(the r160 2-D pattern, so no batch grows the compute buffer - issue #42).

**Purity: the derived predicate *is* the packed one, verified cell by cell.**  Re-ran the contributor's diagnostic
oracle (`LLAMA_KQ_MASK_DERIVED_VERIFY=1`, which rebuilds each derived ubatch's mask with `set_input_kq_mask` and
compares visibility per (token, cell)) on gfx1201: **0 mismatches** on every derived multi-sequence ubatch of
`llama-perplexity -c 512 -b 2048 -ub 2048 --kv-unified` (4 sequences per batch) for dense 27B Q8_0 (1 GPU and 2 GPU
`-sm tensor`), Qwen3.5-4B (hybrid attention + GDN), Gemma4-12B and gpt-oss-20b (both iSWA, the latter with a live SWA
window: `visible = 229632`), 2-4 derived multi-sequence ubatches each, per-chunk PPL identical to the packed arm.  The
shared-cell counter passed its randomized check locally too (400 000 random operations over 512 cells x 6 sequences,
counter == recount after each, shared cells in 385 495 of the states).  Logit level:
`gate-prefill-logits.sh --ctx 512 --chunks 40 --ub 2048 --ab "LLAMA_KQ_MASK_DERIVED_MULTISEQ=0"` reads **0.000000 /
100.000 %** at **f16 and q8_0** KV; the release-standard gate (`--ctx 512`, single sequence) also reads 0.000000 /
100.000 %, so nothing outside the multi-sequence path moved.

**Measured (gfx1201, dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, `-c 245760 -ub 2048 -b 2048 --parallel 2 --kv-unified -fa on -ctk/-ctv
q8_0`, 1 GPU).**  After load: device **27 513 004 032 -> 26 405 838 848 B (-1.031 GiB)** and server **RSS 1 964 904 ->
982 872 kB (-0.937 GiB)** - the contributor's 1.03 / 0.94 GiB reproduce exactly.  Prefill is neutral: two concurrent
16K-token prompts 26.96 s (packed) vs 27.23 s (derived) at 1 GPU and 17.07 vs 17.09 s at 2 GPU `-sm tensor`; a
112K-resident decode beside a 16K prefill 13.97 vs 13.96 s.  That is the trade the batch-wide skip window makes (a
multi-sequence derived ubatch loses the packed path's per-tile group skip) and it is smaller than the host fill the
derived form removes.  Single-sequence greedy text is byte-identical on and off (dense 27B, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 30`, hybrid
4B) and `plain == draft-mtp` still holds (2 GPU `-sm tensor`, 400 tokens).  `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` passes (3 GPU
tensor, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS + MTP, 3 slots, park moves traced, park == lazyoff byte-identical).

**Two negatives worth recording.**  (1) It buys **nothing on qwen4exp/Flash-Next**: that graph also holds an
`allow_derived == false` builder (QSA), which creates and fills the packed mask anyway - measured RSS 30 932 856 ->
30 933 612 kB and identical VRAM, as designed (a memory `kq_mask_kvs()` does not cover keeps the packed reserve, and a
partially covered one simply gains nothing).  (2) A server that really shares prefixes through `llama_memory_seq_cp`
(the shared-system-prompt shape) will latch and then keep the packed mask: the 1 GiB is given back for the rest of the
run.  The latch could not be triggered on this box at all (this server never `seq_cp`s across slots while a slot is
busy, and prompt-split children run as single-sequence ubatches), so its firing is documented from the contributor's
`llama-parallel -pps` evidence plus code review; `-pps` here did show `n_multi = 282 (recount 282)` with the derived
form correctly withheld from the multi-sequence ubatches and identical output.

**Fixed during the fold** (beyond the PR as submitted): the block-10 comment block above
`kq_mask_packed_reachable()` still claimed multi-sequence batches always need the packed mask (rewritten with the r172
rule, including the fact that the reserve's own measure batch carries `n_seq_max` sequences); `kq_mask_kvs()` was
returning a freshly allocated `std::vector` and running 2-3 `dynamic_cast`s on **every** `decode()` batch until a latch
fires (now resolved once and cached - `memory` is immutable for a context), and `batch_needs_packed_multiseq()`'s
per-call `std::vector<bool>`/`std::vector` allocations became fixed-size arrays.  No semantic change (the gates above
were re-run on the folded build).

**A pre-existing chain defect the fold surfaced and fixed.**  Walking the per-block ladder honestly (the rebase
changes blob hashes, so `--changed-from` selects more than the touched block) failed at **block 09**, and the cause is
not this PR: r171's `TODO #115` fold removed `ggml_cuda_mmb_routed_will_take` from **block 06** while **block 08** still
called it, and only **block 10** (which moves the graph optimizer into `ggml-cuda-try-fuse.cu`) deleted that call
site — so the intermediate trees of blocks 08 and 09 have not compiled since r171, which no release noticed because
r171's own ladder used `--changed-from` and selected blocks 06, 10 and the tip.  The call site in block 08 now asks
`ggml_cuda_mmb_supported_mmid()` (r171's rule, and its four arguments are the following `MUL_MAT_ID`'s), so the ladder
is **5/5** (blocks 05, 08, 09, 10, 14) and the **tip tree is byte-identical** (`83ddc559`) because block 10 deletes the
region anyway.  `patches/README.md` (block 08) carries the note.

## 261029.002 (no release) -- PR #244 v3 (DFlash2 adaptive verify width) assessed and not promoted: on r171 it is a 1-15 % loss on every payload we have

**No delivery change, no release, nothing in `patches/`.**  Contributor PR
[#244](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/pull/244) (`@overdoingism`, `wip/dflash-adaptive-width/`) was
re-submitted as **v3** after the r164-era review: opt-in (`LLAMA_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE=1`), count-based per-position
estimates with a prior from the previous position, down two widths at a time / up one / at most once in 8 drafts, the
expert cache's band bound on the aligned width, and a cost model re-measured on the release (`COST` 0.09 per verified
row, `JUMP` 0).  It was assessed against the r171 tree (`6050b467c`, +0 the delivery) and **not promoted**; the PR is
left open with the review comment below.  This entry is the record so the next round starts from the numbers.

**What is right with it.**  `git am`s clean on r171 (the release tip, not just the r164/r167/r168/r170 the PR names)
and builds clean (`all`, 32 jobs); every new line is behind `if (adapt)`, and the hoisted `n_draft` is `params.n_max`
when `adapt` is false, so the **default path is byte-identical to the canonical r171 build** (27B + DFlash2, prose,
`-n 192`: `e350796383c675fc` on both).  The band bound is `align_draft_caps()`'s expression exactly
(`band > 1` -> `band / n_drafting - 1`, read from `llama_model_moe_cache_band(llama_get_model(ctx_tgt))` after the
context exists); `result_q` is resized with `result`; the alignment is inert with one drafting sequence.  **Text was
byte-identical between the adaptive and fixed arms in every arm and at every width** (27B 1 GPU / 2 GPU tensor, the
host-expert arm, 3 slots), no abort and `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh` clean on all 19 logs.  It is also a genuine
improvement on v2: the width now *moves* (v2 sat at `n_max` and lost 10.9 % on `code-python.txt`); on this tree
`code-python` is within 1.1 % of the best fixed width.

**Why it is still not promoted: the width decisions cost 1-15 %, and the two arms the PR's "not covered" list
skipped are the worst.**  Greedy, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, one server start per arm, raw `/completion`, `-n 192`.
27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2-Q4_K_M, `-sm tensor`:

| arm | code-python | prose | recall | reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 GPU, fixed 7 / fixed 6 / fixed 5 | 113.1 / 107.2 / 106.8 | 84.1 / **87.0** / 83.7 | 144.9 / 132.7 / 122.2 | 98.5 |
| 1 GPU, adaptive @7 | 111.9 (-1.1 %) | 79.1 (-5.9 %) | 142.6 (-1.6 %) | **101.5 (+3.1 %)** |
| 2 GPU tensor, pair aggregate | fixed 7 137.4 / adaptive 136.4 (-0.7 %) | | | |
| 1 GPU, prose `-n 512` | fixed 7 112.3 / fixed 6 110.5 / adaptive 108.7 (-3.2 %) | | | |

35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M + DFlash2-Q8_0, 2 GPU tensor, `-ncmoe 40`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=6000` (arena 11955.3 MiB,
0.90-0.94 hit, `band 16` — the production surface the review asked for):

| arm | prose `-n 192` | prose `-n 512` | recall `-n 192` | pair aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixed 7 | 128.3 | 174.6 | 202.9 | 70.67 |
| adaptive @7 | **108.8 (-15.2 %)** | **153.5 (-12.1 %)** | 201.0 (-0.9 %) | 68.15 (-3.6 %) |
| adaptive, `LLAMA_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE_COST=0.001` (width pinned at 7) | 129.7 | 174.4 | -- | -- |

**The control is what makes the finding precise.**  `COST=0.001` makes `adapt_value()` monotone in the width, so the
controller stays at 7: the arm then lands on fixed 7 (129.7 vs 128.3, 174.4 vs 174.6) with *identical* `draft_n` /
`draft_n_accepted` (300/148, 623/421).  The probe drafts, the per-draft review and the cut are free; **the whole
loss is the width decisions themselves.**

**The trace.**  Prose, 1 GPU, `LLAMA_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE=2`, deterministic (two starts, 79.07 / 79.45 t/s,
same text): `7 -> 5` on the **first** decision (8 drafts, decayed counts, a 0.5 first-position prior),
`5 -> 4` eight drafts later (a second downward move), then `4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7` one width per 8 drafts — about **24
drafts, a third of a 192-token response, at the wrong width**.  The arena arm's trace is the same shape (7->5->3).
At `-n 512` it ends on 7, i.e. it converges to the value the fixed arm starts at.

**And on this tree the optimum *is* `n_max`, so there is nothing to win.**  At `-n 512` fixed 7 wins on all three
prompts (prose 112.3 vs 110.5 for fixed 6; code and recall likewise), so a controller that converges to 7 can only
pay the transient.  The PR's headline (+18.4-18.7 % on a 30K zh continuation, widths 1-2) is the one shape it wins
on and we have no such payload; our nearest low-acceptance one (`reasoning.txt`) is +3.1 %.  Note the acceptance
profile moved under the PR's own r168 table: it measured `mean len` 3.5 at width 7 on prose/code, r171 measures
5.3-5.6 (the r170 Q6_K VDR and r171 fusion changes are decode-numerics changes that the *draft* context also runs),
so the best fixed width on the current release is 7, not 5.

**What was measured of the alignment.**  The band bound is **inert at <= 2 drafting sequences**: the DFlash2 draft
reports `dflash.block_size=8`, so `--spec-draft-n-max` is clamped to 7, and `band / 2 - 1 = 7` — the bound never
binds.  It binds at 3 (`16 / 3 - 1 = 4`); a `--parallel 3` arm exercises that path and runs clean (no abort, no
GPU fault).  So the band half of the patch is correct and, on RDNA4, almost unreachable.

**What a fix would take (measured, not asserted).**  The true fixed-width optima on the same arms, and two
controller prototypes (both throw-away edits in the scratch tree, `first decision deferred to 32 reviews` +
`no second downward move inside 16`):

| fixed-width optimum | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 35B-A3B arena, prose `-n 192` | 132.8 | **135.5** | 128.3 |
| 35B-A3B arena, prose `-n 512` | -- | 174.5 | 174.6 (flat) |
| 27B dense, prose `-n 192` | 83.7 | **87.0** | 84.1 |
| 27B dense, prose `-n 512` | -- | 110.5 | 112.3 |
| 27B dense, code / recall `-n 192` | 106.8 / 122.2 | 107.2 / 132.7 | **113.1 / 144.9** |

| arm | shipped | deferral prototype | deferral + `COST=0.15` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27B prose / code / recall / reasoning, 1 GPU | 79.1 / 111.9 / 142.6 / 101.5 | **83.8 / 112.5 / 144.6 / 99.3** | -- |
| 35B arena prose `-n 192` / `-n 512` | 108.8 / 153.5 | **130.1 / 175.0** | 127.1 / -- |

So deferring the first decision removes the whole loss (prose 79.1 -> 83.8 against fixed 84.1; arena 108.8 ->
130.1 against 128.3) and also makes the controller **inert** — `draft_n`/`draft_n_accepted` come out identical to
the fixed-7 arm (280/150, 300/148, 623/421), i.e. with only 35-45 drafts in a 192-token response it never moves.
Raising `COST` to this arm's own step-time fit (~0.15; `a + b*rows` over the fixed 5/6/7 arms) makes it move
7 -> 6 exactly once — at review 32 — which is too late to pay (127.1 against fixed 6's 135.5).  Both are needed
and neither is sufficient inside a short response, so the ranked fixes are: (1) **carry the width across requests
per slot** (`adapt_reset()` in `begin()` throws away the one thing the first response learned; a chat session is
hundreds of drafts, a response is ~40) — the transient then costs once per session; (2) **do not compare widths
whose positions are unobserved** (`adapt_value()`'s prior chain turns a 2/7 streak into p~0.3 at positions 5-7,
which is what produced 7 -> 5 -> 3); (3) one width per decision plus the no-repeat window; (4) measure the cost
rather than model it — the interval between two `draft()` calls divided by `1 + accepted` is tokens-per-ms per
width, and the accepted count is already in `n_hit`/`n_seen`, so `COST` (0.09 here, ~0.15 on the arena arm — a 2x
error worth ~5 % of width) disappears.  A perfect controller buys 0-5.6 % on our short responses and ~0 at 512;
the `zh` +18 % class is where the feature earns its keep.

**Decision.**  Not promoted; the PR keeps its `needs more info` state and the reply asks for (1) a start/seed fix so
the first decisions are not taken on 8 decayed drafts — e.g. seed from the model's observed full-block acceptance
(`draft_n_accepted / draft_n` at `n_max`), or defer the first decision until the counts are dense, and forbid a
second downward move inside one window; (2) the `-ncmoe` + arena and 2-slot `-sm tensor` arms re-measured with it,
as this entry does; (3) a self-calibrating `COST` (or a per-config default) — a 4x-wrong constant moves the width
three positions.  If it comes back with those, re-run this table plus `prompts/reasoning.txt` and the arena arm
before anything is folded into block 12 (which owns the DFlash drafter; block 02 owns `align_draft_caps()` and
`spec_align_enabled()`).  Records: this entry; the arm harness was throw-away (`/tmp`), reproducible from the table
above.

## 261029.001 (r171) -- `TODO` #115: a fusion that stands down for MMB asks the dispatch predicate, and the BF16-only activation mark can no longer be preempted

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r171`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip
`060dc264f8ad1e19dd5ff22902c7a285ce479ef6`, tree `2f5870713e94ae8532e7e616887aec27e1833673`.  Two code changes
(blocks 06 and 10), `+62 / -31` over 4 files, no kernel arithmetic touched; `TODO.md` loses #115 (row + body), the
handle is kept here and in `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §69.

**The item.**  `mul_mat_q_pair_try_fuse` stood down for MMB on a weight-*type* test
(`ggml_cuda_mmb_dense_will_take` / `_routed_will_take`) while the fused-GLU and mmq-triple matchers decide on the
*shape* (`ggml_cuda_mmb_supported_mm` / `_supported_mmid`).  The type answer is a superset, so on any shape MMB
declines (`T < mmb_min_t()`, `n_used > 64`, a `K` that is not a whole super-block count, ...) the pair had already
stood down and the **mmq triple** served the gate/up pair instead of the **pair** (one shared activation quantize).

**What it turned out to be.**  Three things, only the first of which the item named:

1. **The stand-down predicate.**  Both pair arms now ask the dispatch predicates (`supported_mmid` for the routed
   pair, `supported_mm` for the dense one), a strict superset of the fused-GLU predicate — so the priority chain is
   well defined and can never preempt an MMB claim: **MMB's fused GLU -> the mmq/mmvq triple -> the shared-quantize
   pair (the fallback) -> the two plain muls**.  `GGML_PAIR_ROUTED_OFF` is the new A/B arm for the routed half
   (`GGML_PAIR_OFF` still means both halves, `GGML_PAIR_DENSE_OFF` the dense one).
2. **A latent correctness hole in the BF16-only activation marking.**  The same shape predicates are what the
   optimizer's HC16 pass uses to decide that an activation's F32 output may be skipped; a fusion that preempts one
   of those readers reads the buffer the mark declared dead.  The marking pass now refuses to elide an activation
   with a routed `MUL_MAT_ID` consumer (it marks the bf16 *copy* instead, so the MMB reader still finds it).  Not
   reachable on the model set measured (a MoE layer's F32 router GEMM is usually a co-consumer of the same
   activation, which already forced the copy arm) — but the two decisions now hold on their own.
3. **A crash in the first cut, found only on gfx1151.**  The matcher runs on *every* graph node, so probing
   `supported_mm()` on an arbitrary `i, i+1` pair dereferenced a null `src[1]` on an op that merely preceded a
   `MUL_MAT`: Flash-Next IQ4_NL at `-ub 256` SIGSEGV'd inside `common_init_from_params`'s warm-up decode (2/2,
   GDB stack in `ggml_cuda_mmb_supported_mm` under `mul_mat_q_pair_try_fuse`), while every other arm on both boxes
   was fine.  Both nodes are now required to be the same op with every source slot present, and
   `supported_mm`/`supported_mmid` are null-safe.  A type-only predicate could not have crashed (it takes a weight).

**The item's premise did not hold, and the measurement says so.**  `TODO` #115 called LFM2 Q6_K an "MMB-declined
MoE" and read r161's fused-vs-`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_MOE_MMQ_FUSION` A/B as MMQ-vs-MMB.  On the current tree, with
gfx1151's type mask, **MMB's fused GLU accepts** it (`GGML_CUDA_MMB_LOG=1` -> `MMB_GLU fused` per MoE layer;
`M=1792 K=2048 T=512 n_used=4`), so that env was inert in both arms and the r161 pair of numbers compared two
MMB-GLU arms.  The decision is still the right one to fix; the number was not evidence about it.

**Measured.**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| gfx1151, pair vs triple (`GGML_CUDA_MMB_ROUTED=0`, `GGML_PAIR_ROUTED_OFF=1` as the triple arm; dense MMB path untouched), pp512 `-r 3`, interleaved x2 | LFM2 Q6_K **3379 / 3399** vs 3348 / 3407; 35B-A3B Q4_K_M **2304 / 2312** vs 2296 / 2313 — neutral |
| gfx1151, the shape the change moves (`GGML_CUDA_MMB_MIN_T=1024`, `-ub 512`), greedy 48 tokens | r170 == r171 == triple == unfused == `GGML_CUDA_MMB=0`: LFM2 `765 chars sha=d120b56017c2`, 35B-A3B `723 chars sha=44cbb654f6db` (the pair and the triple share the dot-product order and the `J` tile, so this is kernel *selection*, not a re-baseline) |
| gfx1151, Flash-Next IQ4_NL `-ub 256` (also exercises the routed-SWIGLU->MMQ matcher, exact stand-down now) | r170 `682 chars sha=488f8aa2f2e8` == r171; prompt 543.6 -> 546.2 t/s |
| gfx1151, `GGML_CUDA_PAIR_DEBUG=1` | `fused routed=1 T=512 type=q6_K n_experts=32` — the pair really is the arm now |
| gfx1201 (inert: `mmb_cfg().routed = 0`), r170 vs r171 same-seed 128-token text | 27B Q8_0 `da2e2d192e21`, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M `5d485275db6d` (1 GPU **and** 3 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`), LFM2 Q6_K `0b02fbdc4bd3` — all **byte-identical** |
| gfx1201 prefill `-p 2048 -r 2`, 1 GPU | 35B-A3B Q4_K_M 4856 -> 4894 t/s, LFM2 Q6_K 9177 -> 9166 (noise) |
| `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` (recorded gfx1201 bases) | 27B Q8_0 **0.000000 / 100.000 %**, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M **-0.000000 / 100.000 %** |
| MTP Protocol A (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 devices `-sm tensor`, bf16 KV, `-c 102400`, `-n 3000`, prose) | plain **50.95** t/s, `draft-mtp` **101.31** t/s, acceptance **0.608** (1937/3185) — at/above the recorded 3-device tensor reference (90.7 t/s, 0.60) |

## 261028.014 (docs) -- TODO #111 (a verify step whose slot cannot draft at all) is investigated, DECLINED and retired; the gate gains the instrument, and `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63's determinism claim is scoped

**Docs + one gate script: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change; `scripts/validate-set.sh` is
unaffected.**  `TODO.md` loses #111 (row + handle kept in this entry and in the record, never reused).  Nothing in
the delivery's runtime behaviour changed: the item was implemented as a candidate, measured, and **reverted** —
"if it isn't broken, don't fix it".

**What the item was.**  `LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN`'s cap alignment (r153) removed 58 split decode steps per 400-token
pair, but one step per response survived: a slot whose `get_n_draft_max()` is `<= 0` (its last token of the
response, or a full context) never enters the draft call, so it presents its sampled row **alone** while its
neighbour presents `n_draft + 1`, `split_equal()` stops at the shortest set, and the target runs a second pass for
that step.  Measured shape (`LLAMA_RS_ROLLBACK_DEBUG=1`, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, 2 GPU):
`prep=1/2 n_tokens=6 seq_ids=[0]` + `prep=2/2 n_tokens=1 seq_ids=[1]`, the step on which seq 1 finishes.

**Root cause is a CAP, not content** — which is why it was worth re-opening at all (the r154 rule says a
cap-caused mismatch IS worth equalizing).  The candidate fix: decide the step's verify width before any draft is
set up, and if any generating slot in that step cannot draft, let nobody draft (one row per sequence, the drafter
resuming next step).  A slot that gave up mid-draft (`--spec-draft-p-min`, default 0) or is replaying a partial
draft stays CONTENT and keeps its split.

**Why it was declined** (all measured, `benchmarks/2026-10-28-spec-align-111.md`):

* **no throughput gain.**  Unlike the depth-mismatch case, that second ubatch carries the neighbour's **genuine
  draft rows**, so both arms are two passes: split = `2 passes / ~6 tokens` in that window, suppressed = `1 pass`
  (1 token) + the next step's normal `1 pass` (~6 tokens).  A/B behind a temporary switch (6 alternating pair arms
  each): **-0.3 %**, i.e. below the floor.
* **no correctness gain.**  A verify width is a numerics/config axis (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63); nothing aborts and
  the split stays reachable anyway through content mismatches, prompt/decode mixes, the mixed-drafter chain and
  the `LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN=0` arm.
* it would add a **cross-slot coupling** (one slot's draft suppressed by a neighbour's budget) for a neutral
  result.

**What did ship (the instrument).**  `scripts/gate-spec-align.sh` now counts two kinds of split separately —
`full+tail` — where `full` (every ubatch >= 2 rows, the r153 defect) must be **0** with the knob on, and `tail`
(one ubatch of a single row, this item) is **bounded** by `TAIL_MAX` (default 2, one per response boundary) and
reported per arm.  Before this, single-row groups were excluded from the split count entirely, so a change that
*manufactured* them (a slot that stopped drafting, a slot cut to one row to dodge a mismatch) was invisible.
Measured counts with the shipped build: 27B 2 GPU `0+0`, 27B 3 GPU `0+0`, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` `0+1`,
mixed-drafter `24+0` — all <= the bound, so the gate stays green while the count is now visible.

**Finding (a real correction to the rulebook): the two-slot pair is not run-to-run deterministic.**  Two gate runs
of one build diverged on the 3-GPU pair, so four runs of one **unchanged** binary were taken: two landed on
`c05fb93d34/1237` chars at 159 t/s and two on `5bf3146c79/1232` at 174 t/s.  The basin is a property of the *run*
(the candidate build landed in the same ones), and the alignment is why — it makes one slot's verify width depend
on its neighbour's adaptive state and on which rows share its batch.  So per-config determinism is a
**single-slot** statement, the gate's INFO divergence line moves between runs by design, and a two-slot text diff
is not an instrument.  `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63 carries the correction (and the index row), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3 and
`AGENTS.md` say the same in one line each.

**Also along the way:** the gate's header still described the r153 generic cut, which r154 removed — corrected.

## 261028.013 (docs) -- TODO #112 (VRAM-resident slot snapshots) leaves the tracker and is parked as `wip/vram-resident-slots/`

**Docs only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change; `scripts/validate-set.sh` is unaffected.**
`TODO.md` loses #112 (row + scoping body).  The subject is not dropped and **#112 stays the permanent handle**
(never reused): the scoping note now lives in `wip/vram-resident-slots/README.md`, unchanged in status —
**parked, nothing implemented, not scheduled** — with `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` gaining its row.

**Why the move, and why nothing else changed.**  A parked idea is open work, so it belongs in the `wip/` index
rather than in the forward-looking TODO table (`wip/CAMPAIGNS.md`'s own rule: parked rows are *scoping notes*,
not active work).  The README fleshes the idea out instead of restating it, and the two facts worth having
written down are the ones the TODO row could not carry:

* **the device arm's shape.**  `LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE` is not a blob: the caller's host buffer holds
  only the metadata (`state_seq_get_size_ext` sizes it with `llama_io_write_dummy(skip_tensors = true)`), the
  bytes live in `llama_context::mem_storage` as one device buffer per buft, and the header says a second get
  for a seq id **invalidates the first**.  A restore is addressed by the *blob's* seq id and asserts this
  context still holds it, so a device snapshot is valid only for the live context that made it — it is a
  per-context cache, never a replacement for the host prompt cache or the slot file (which restore into a
  different slot id and after a model reload).
* **the budget arithmetic.**  `n_ctx_checkpoints` is 32 and a 27B checkpoint is 150 + 21 MiB, i.e. up to
  ~4.8 GiB **per slot**, so a device tier is a MiB-budgeted, LRU, spill-to-host cache that must decline on
  headroom — not a place to keep everything, and never something that may reach `ggml_cuda_device_malloc`'s
  OOM chain, whose last resort is the expert arena.

The four blockers from the old row are kept and expanded (plus three that only show up when the code is read:
the single `state_stage` per context, the portability/lifetime question, and the 497/355 ms first-touch stage
fault), with a phased sketch (P0 = an explicit snapshot handle API, i.e. several snapshots per seq id with a
free and a size), the gates it would owe, and an explicit "answer this first" question — a *pinned-host* tier
may capture most of the win without competing with the arena for VRAM.

**Docs.**  `TODO.md` loses #112 (row + body); `wip/vram-resident-slots/README.md` is new;
`wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` gains the row and names #112 in the parked-rows note.  Nothing in `patches/`, `release.json`,
`ENVIRONMENT.md`, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` or `patches/README.md` moves.

## 261028.012 (r170) -- block 07: dense Q6_K VDR=2 is upstream's default on every arch now, so the delivery keeps it (measured) and ships a build-time VDR=1 escape (issue #228 follow-up)

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r170`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `30855de701d623319da984f9c80f7878e49c7bef`,
tree `c6c0d8e236f7e628c36cc82df5dfb32180b92cc4`.  **Block 07 amended** — `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vecdotq.cuh`
(+18/-0: the define becomes an `#ifdef`/`#else`, plus the comment that records the measurement) and
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq-vecdot.cuh` (+3/-1: the same condition in `get_vec_dot_q_cuda()`): **comments and
one preprocessor condition only, no arithmetic**.  With the new flag off the applied tree is preprocessor-identical
for every arch, and the built gfx1151 binary reproduces the pre-change arms byte-for-byte (below).  New
build-time flag **`-DGGML_HIP_Q6K_DENSE_VDR1`** (default off).  Blocks 08-14 carry new commit ids (their
parent changed); their bodies are unchanged.

### What was reported (issue #228, comment 6483065646)

The gfx1151 consumer re-probed after the r148 HC fix: collapse gone, MTP healthy (32.7 -> 64.8 t/s), **but**
greedy text at temp 0 still moves against their r120 reference (first-token top-5 KL 0.497, top-1 0.989,
7/7 prompts diverge) and their output-identity gate (<= 0.007 across eight previous cutovers) blocks the
v15 line.  They bisected it to upstream `2744e48d1` (#30517, "faster MMVQ for low-bit types"), which sets
`VDR_Q6_K_Q8_1_MMVQ` 1 -> 2 and rewrites the q6_K `mmvq` kernel, and asked the right question: is this
intended for the v15 line, and is there a way to keep the v14 association order?  They also noted that our
own r120 stack had gated that define per arch.

### The finding is ours, not theirs

That per-arch gate **was** block 07's:

```
// Dense Q6_K keeps the upstream VDR=1 elsewhere; on RDNA4/RDNA3_0 the 16-element
// vdr2 chunk wins at the verify widths (issue #58, gfx1201) and is band-uniform.
#if defined(RDNA4) || defined(RDNA3_0)
#define VDR_Q6_K_Q8_1_MMVQ 2
#else
#define VDR_Q6_K_Q8_1_MMVQ 1
#endif
```

The `6050b467c` re-base absorbed upstream's unconditional `2`, so the macro arrives as *context*, the gate is
gone, and RDNA3_5 (gfx1151) moved 1 -> 2 as a side effect — an unverified geometry on a validated arch,
purely inherited.  The dispatch `#if defined(RDNA4) || defined(RDNA3_0)` survived but no longer distinguishes
a VDR (both arms are VDR=2: ours vs upstream's kernel).  This is the same class as the r138 `!ids` assert and
the r145 norm-order adoption: a re-base that silently re-scopes a delivery tuning decision.

### Measured before deciding (gfx1151, ROCm 10.1.0, `GGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON`, one long-lived tree, ccache)

Payload: `/llm/models/Qwen3.8/Flash-Next/Q5K` — 339 Q5_K / 199 Q8_0 / 94 IQ3_S / 44 IQ4_NL / 2 IQ4_XS /
**13 Q6_K** (the lm_head + 12 attention outputs), i.e. the same census class the report filed.  Two binaries
from the same tree differing only in the macro (interleaved, 2 reps):

| arm | tg128 | batched B=1 | B=4 | B=8 | tg128 @ d16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VDR=2 (current default) | 33.86 / 33.86 | 33.50 / 33.49 | 81.76 / 81.72 | **104.14 / 103.98** | 31.86 |
| VDR=1 (restored gate) | 33.83 / 33.81 | 33.48 / 33.47 | 81.75 / 81.55 | 102.94 / 102.60 | 31.86 |

Neutral at B=1/B=4/depth, **+1.2 % at batched B=8** -> default-on policy says keep VDR=2 (and it is
upstream's default, so keeping it is also the no-divergence choice).  Greedy text moves between the builds,
as the association-order rule says it must (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §1-§8).

**Width purity holds at VDR=2** (the invariant that matters, and the one a cross-release text gate cannot
see): Q5_K target + the shared Q8_0 MTP head, 200 greedy tokens — `plain`, `draft-mtp n_max 3` and
`draft-mtp n_max 7` all 1302 chars, sha `115141867744`.

### What shipped

* `vecdotq.cuh`: the define becomes `#ifdef GGML_HIP_Q6K_DENSE_VDR1 -> 1 #else -> 2`, with the measurement
  and the reason in the comment.  `VDR_Q6_K_Q8_1_MMVQ_MOE` unchanged (2), and the MoE path is untouched: off
  RDNA4/RDNA3_0 `GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_MOE_DENSE` already collapses it to the dense VDR.
* `mmvq-vecdot.cuh`: the dense dispatch takes the same condition, so with the flag the **generic** kernel runs
  on every arch (its VDR comes from the macro) instead of our HIP-optimised `_vdr2` one.  `get_vdr_mmvq()`
  reads the same macro, so the host K-split arithmetic and the device kernel cannot disagree.
* **No runtime knob, deliberately.**  VDR is a `constexpr` that the host's `blocks_per_iter`/`kqs`/`calc_nwarps`
  also read, so an env var means instantiating the Q6_K `mmvq` kernel family twice and adding a third
  numerics arm to gate forever — for a delta that is +1.2 % at one width.  The consumer builds their own
  binaries, so a compile-time escape serves them (`ENVIRONMENT.md` §14).

### Verification

* `scripts/validate-set.sh`: checksums, strict `git am` from a fresh tarball, tree
  `c6c0d8e2` — green; Windows portability scan 282 files, clean.
* `scripts/apply-all.sh` on a real checkout at `6050b467c`: applied tip `30855de70` == `release.json.tip`.
* Rebuilt default gfx1151 tree: 128-token greedy `d47f08557f75` (identical to the pre-change VDR=2 arm, i.e.
  flag-off is a behavioural no-op), and `draft-mtp n_max 7` still `115141867744` == plain.
* Flag-on arm compiled (`-DGGML_HIP_Q6K_DENSE_VDR1` on the `mmvq.cu` command line, object 15 189 864 B vs the
  default 15 218 536 B) and reproduces the VDR=1 binary's text `bf8ddd5271d1`.
* Docs: `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §68, `patches/README.md` (block 07), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §14, `AGENTS.md`.

### Not done (and why)

No arch gate restored and no VDR=1 default: the measurement does not support paying 1.2 % at B=8, and a
re-base inheriting an upstream default is a re-baseline, not a defect.  The reply to the reporter says exactly
that, gives them the numbers and the flag, and records their finding as ours.

## 261028.011 (r169) -- block 12: the backend-sampling compute buffers are reserved once per sequence, and again only for a WIDER chain (contributor PR #245)

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r169`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `fb7b244316d1ecdfc0e0b982e352ee3f9674452d`,
tree `a54e74175e9bb1314b5d8bf8a4efb175642aff71`.  **Block 12 amended** (`src/llama-context.cpp` +37/-11,
`src/llama-context.h` +7/-3, on top of the contributor's patch — see "the key" below for what had to change).
New kill switch **`LLAMA_BACKEND_SAMPLER_RESERVE_ONCE`** (default on).  No kernel, dispatch row or numerics
path touched: every greedy-text arm is byte-identical to r168 and `gate-prefill-logits.sh` reads
**0.000000 / 100.000 %**.

### The defect (llama.cpp's own, not the delivery's)

`llama_context::set_sampler()` set `sched_need_reserve = true` on every set of an offloadable sampler
chain **and** on every removal, and `sched_reserve()` re-creates the scheduler — freeing and re-allocating
every compute buffer again, at the same size.  `llama-server --backend-sampling` sets a new chain per
request (and clears it when a slot is released, or when a grammar request's chain cannot be offloaded), so
each request paid that before its first token.  The behaviour is upstream's, unchanged on `ggml-org` master
as of 2026-10-29, so `upstream/backend-sampler-reserve-once/` carries a copy cut against plain `6050b467c`.

### What shipped

`sched_reserve()` records what the buffers were reserved with (`sampling.reserved`) and `set_sampler()`
asks for a reserve only when that record does not cover the chain it is being given.  A chain set again, a
narrower one, or a removal needs none: the graph is rebuilt anyway (the samplers are part of the graph-reuse
check, `llm_graph_params::allow_reuse()` -> `samplers_equal()`), the output buffers are sized per decode
(`output_reserve()` runs `has_sampling` every batch), and the graph allocator grows a buffer if a chain
needs more.

**The key is the chain's node count, not the sequence id.**  `graph_max_nodes()` is recomputed *only* by a
reserve, and it is what sizes the graph's node capacity (`llm_graph_result::max_nodes` ->
`ggml_new_graph_custom`; `ggml_build_forward` asserts `cgraph->n_nodes < cgraph->size`), the scheduler's
node/leaf arrays and the compute-metadata arena.  The allocator's on-demand growth covers buffer *sizes*,
so a chain that is merely bigger in bytes is safe — a chain with **more nodes** is not, and the
contributor's seq-id-only key missed exactly that case.  `tests/test-backend-sampler.cpp`'s
`test_set_sampler` *is* that case (a 1-node `dist` chain replaced by `top_k + dist` on the same sequence):
with the seq-id key it reserved **1** time (the widening was not covered), with the node-count key **2**
(both size increases covered, the removal and the same-size set still skipped), and it PASSES in both.  The
margin on this box is large (27B: `max_nodes = 81920` against a 4076-node decode graph, so nothing was
reachable in practice) — the key was fixed because the invariant has to hold, not because it was measured
to bite.

### Measurements (gfx1201, 1x R9700)

`llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL --backend-sampling -ngl 99 -c 65536 -ub 2048 -b 2048 --parallel 2
--kv-unified -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`, a 2396-token prompt with `cache_prompt: false`, seven sampled
requests plus a grammar request and one more sampled request, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, two interleaved
starts:

| | r168 | r169 |
|---|---|---|
| median prompt time | 1963.9 ms | **1895.2 ms (-68.7 ms, -3.5 %)** |
| median client time to first token | 2750 ms | 2682 ms |
| `sched_reserve` lines over 3 requests | 4 | **2** (bring-up only) |

The contributor measured -423 ms on a 3900X; the absolute cost of the reserve is host-dependent, the
direction and the mechanism are the same.  Request text is byte-identical between the arms in all three
shapes (`f2b480f90a04abaf` for greedy and for seeded temperature 0.7, `e95291773c15cb25` for the grammar
fallback).

## 261028.010 (r168) -- TODO #70 closed: a re-arm is layer-uniform or the layer is stood down, and a starved wide-aux growth is decided once per wide pass

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r168`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `fcf00b46cff86b07100536a8174498ddd49b2d1c`,
tree `93e10130cc847e7cd9ce0f5a59c551f36f86e9d7`.  **Blocks 09 and 10 amended** (block 09
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu` +219/-9, block 10 `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda-slab.cu` +64/-3).
No new environment variable, no default changed, and no kernel, dispatch row or numerics path touched, so
`gate-prefill-logits.sh` reads **0.000000 / 100.000 %** and every greedy-text arm is byte-identical to r167.
Record: `archive/work/todo70-rearm-wideaux/`.

### What #70 was, and what shipped

r86's field fault (`WORKLOG.md` 261019.002) ended in `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` in `k_get_rows_float`
after (a) a re-arm that had to shrink one layer to a partial slot count (`layer=47 ... 344 requested, only
202 fit`) and (b) a starved wide-aux region.  r87 removed the *trigger* (a wide -> narrow compute-layout
transition always drops), so #70 was the hardening half, and its two asks are now in:

1. **A re-arm is transactional per layer (block 09).**  `moe_cache_rearm()`'s retry loop could exit with a
   **mixed-slot layer** (it set `target = min(achieved)` on its last attempt and the loop ended, leaving the
   tables it had just allocated at their own counts).  The sizing pass forbids that state -- the gate+up
   fused kernel seeds the gate lane from the **up** table's remap -- and answers it by disabling the cache,
   which a re-arm must not do (the graphs already reference the tables, and a late `g_enabled = false`
   desynchronises the MTP draft from the target).  Now `moe_cache_rearm_layer_locked()` converges a layer on
   ONE count (retrying at the largest count any table reached, halving when one cannot hold a slot) and, if
   the retries run out, stands the **whole layer** down -- never a mixed layer; a smaller-but-uniform count
   is accepted (with a warning) because that is a legal state the sizing pass also decides.  A final sweep
   re-checks the touched layers (the sizing safety net, made local).  A stood-down table makes the fusion
   guard fail and every per-table consumer decline -- the fuse-guard invariant.
2. **A starved wide-aux growth is refused once per wide pass (block 10).**  `ggml_cuda_slab_wide_aux_alloc()`
   is called on every FA op of a prefill, and a refusal used to be returned per allocation: a starved region
   became hundreds of decisions, each able to evict a band of arena tables -- or evict one and then refuse on
   a boundary move that raced the MTP draft context -- while a queued graph still held the previous placement.
   The two refusal classes are treated separately: a **VA-limit** refusal (the pinned narrow-2 region, or
   the top of the mapping) is structural -- the limit cannot grow within the pass and any later grow only
   raises the extent -- so it is latched (`wide_aux_denied_want`, cleared by a `ring_set` pass transition, a
   boundary shrink, or a slab (re-)init), and a request at least as large as the refused one returns
   immediately while a smaller one may still fit; a **snapshot-race** refusal (the boundary moved while the
   lock was dropped for the eviction) is recoverable, so it is retried -- but bounded to
   `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_WIDE_AUX_RACE_MAX` (4) attempts per pass, because every attempt costs another arena-band
   eviction.  One WARN per pass when a pass is finally refused, and the per-pass count is the new
   `aux_refused=` field of `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_STATS`.

### Two further defects found while validating (both fixed, same blocks)

* **`stand_down_table_locked()` kept a slab-backed arena pointer after handing the range back.**  A slab
  stand-down returns the range to the slab's free list (where the work pool or another table can take it) but
  kept `t.arena`/`t.arena_reserved` on the theory that "a VMM arena keeps its reserved VA" -- and
  `alloc_table_locked()` reads a non-null `t.arena` as *already allocated*.  So a **re-arm of a table that an
  allocation-OOM stand-down had dropped claimed slots in a range it no longer owned**; seen live as
  `[validate device-malloc-yield] ... layer=46 slots=0..512` right before an eviction and a re-arm of 162
  tables.  (`moe_cache_shrink_step` stands one table down on purpose, so the mixed layer itself is legal; the
  pointer reuse was not.)  Fixed by clearing both fields there, as `free_table_buffers_locked()` and
  `moe_cache_evict_slab_range()` already do.
* **The eviction hook did not invalidate captured graphs.**  `moe_cache_evict_slab_range()` frees table
  arenas through `ggml_cuda_slab_arena_free` directly, bypassing `free_arena_backing()`, which is where the
  `ggml_cuda_graph_mem_freed()` bump lives -- and a captured graph bakes a table's arena address into the MoE
  kernels' launch parameters (a raw device pointer, not a tensor source).  A wide prefill always ends in a
  boundary shrink that bumps anyway, so practice was covered; a **narrow** boundary move (a wider verify
  view, a wide-aux grow) evicts with no other bump.  The hook now bumps when it releases anything.
  `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_VALIDATE=1` also reports layer slot uniformity now (`MIXED-LAYER` = a role stood down and
  the served tables still agree, WARN; `NONUNIFORM-LAYER` = two different non-zero counts, an inconsistency).

### Gates (final build `fcf00b46c`, r167 reference `38aac1e49`, 3x gfx1201)

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| dense Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0, 1 GPU, greedy `-n 48` | output identical to r167 (only the load spinner differs) |
| Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48 -c 32768 -ub 8192`, q8_0 KV, auto cache | 288/288 resident, arena 40 925.0 MiB, 5 evictions, `re-armed 12`; identical text |
| the same + `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RESERVE_MIB=18000` | arena 14 227.8 MiB = **34.8 % residency**, 6-7 evictions (~8.6 GiB), `re-armed 162 (0 stood down)`, `validate: 288 resident, 0 down, inconsistent=0`; identical text |
| the same + MTP draft (`--spec-type draft-mtp`), `-c 16384 -ub 4096` | narrow-2 pinned (draft compute 0.50 GiB), 7 evictions, `re-armed 150`, draft acceptance **0.493**, no abort |
| MTP **Protocol A**, dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 GPU `-sm tensor`, `-n 3000` | **100.8 t/s**, acceptance **0.60816** (1937/3185), mean len 2.82 (r167 reference 90.7 / 0.60) |

Text comparisons were made with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`.  **Without it the same two builds produced
different text on the 34.8 %-residency arm** (576 vs 580 chars) at an identical arena, identical
eviction/re-arm counts and identical acceptance -- the r44/GREEDY-PURITY §44 per-process hipBLASLt solution
choice, measured on a third config.  Also note `scripts/extract-generated.py` hashes the prompt echo on a
`-v` run, so a `-v` "match" proves nothing about the generation: compare clean (non-`-v`) logs.

**Not reproducible, by design.**  The r86 shape needed the wide compute layout *never released* (the boundary
sat at the 6.9 GiB wide view); r87 forces the drop, so no config here starves the region -- `aux_refused=0` in
most prefill passes and `1-2` in a pass whose first FA op ran before the ring armed (the cheap, deliberately

above, not by a repro.

## 261028.009 (r167) -- TODO #103 closed: the "~30x VRAM collapse" is driver page migration, not a llama.cpp path, and the VRAM limit now reports itself

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r167`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `38aac1e499de319621bc6be45fba5515be266e8f`,
tree `4d971189492f6c81d29d58b0fc033e7dc50c6e21`.  **Block 10 amended** (3 hunks in
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`: +78 / -4 — the low-water sampling, two one-shot reports, and the corrected
mechanism note in block 09's `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB` comment).  One new env var (`GGML_CUDA_LOW_FREE_MIB`,
default-on diagnostic) and no default changed.  No kernel, dispatch row or numerics path changed, so the
prefill-logit gate reads **0.000000 / 100.000 %** as expected.  Record + tools:
`archive/work/vram-limit-103/`.

### What #103 was, and what it turned out to be

r135 (issue #219) recorded that on one gfx1201, dropping the free VRAM at process start from 14.46 GiB to
14.06 GiB turned a 13 s request into a 384 s one (prefill 1127 -> 35 t/s, decode 53 -> 1.5-3 t/s), and left
"is the GPU doing 30x the work or is the host stalling 30x" as the next step.  **Neither: it is the driver
moving the *other* client's memory.**  Measured on r166/r167 with the same model, flags and a 15790-token
prompt, using a holder process to set the free VRAM (64 runs; the distinct cells are below):

| free VRAM at start | holder | prefill | GTT peak |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 32 554 MiB (none) | — | **1117.9 / 1120.1 t/s** | 20 MiB |
| 15 954 MiB | one 16.4 GB BO | 626.1 t/s | **27.6 GB** |
| 15 754 MiB | one 16.4 GB BO | **577.7 t/s** | **16.7 GB** |
| 15 754 MiB | the same hold in 64 MiB BOs | **1077.3 / 1074.4 t/s** | 26 MiB |
| 15 754 MiB | 64 MiB BOs, live (touching) | 972.1 t/s, 49.2 decode | 26 MiB |
| 15 704 MiB / 15 654 / 15 604 | any | **clean abort** (`ROCm error: out of memory`) | — |

The last two rows are the finding: **at the same free VRAM** a single huge competing BO costs 48 % of
prefill and the identical hold in 64 MiB BOs costs nothing, because TTM evicts a whole BO — the holder's
16.4 GB buffer is migrated to system memory in full to free a few hundred MiB, and the migration lands
inside the measured window.  The at-the-limit cliff on this box is **~50 MiB wide** (15 754 MiB free: full
speed; 15 704 MiB free: a clean `out of memory`), i.e. the "narrow band" exists but it is *run-or-refuse*,
not *run-30x-slower*.

Three things the r135 record had assumed are now **measured** the other way:

* **HIP does not over-commit and never demotes a resident working set.**  With 1 048 MiB free,
  `hipMalloc(2048 MiB)` fails `out of memory`; a 30 GiB resident working set reads at **505-513 GB/s** with
  1 684 MiB free (versus 513 GB/s roomy).  So "the driver evicts resident weight pages to GTT" is not what
  happens to the *requester* — nothing of the run's own is moved, and `rocm-smi`'s process figure (cited in
  r135 as proof the weights stayed resident) cannot distinguish VRAM from GTT anyway.
* **It is not the FA staging stand-down.**  `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_MAX_MB=0` on a roomy card measures
  1106 t/s — the same as staging on — so the arena cannot be worth 2x, let alone 30x.  r135's *eager* hint
  (`GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_PREALLOC=2`, that tree's behaviour) turns the tight cell into an *earlier OOM*, not
  a slow run.
* **It is not graph churn.**  The graph census is identical in a 588 t/s arm and a 1117 t/s arm
  (`direct=57 replay=51 capture=3 properties_changed=1`, `graphs reused = 10`), and not clocks either (GFX
  2764-3427 MHz, `GPU use 100 %`, mem 1258 vs 1124 MHz — at most 11 %).  The workspace pool's recovery is
  `alloc … failed, flushing … and retrying` then a clean error; it has no slow path.

**Conclusion:** #103 is retired as *not reproducible as a llama.cpp path* — a 30x cell is a driver/OS
page-migration effect (on Windows it is the WDDM paging the r135 budget knob exists to avoid), and what the
delivery can do, it now does.

### The change (block 10)

1. **The free-VRAM low-water mark is tracked on every config.**  `ggml_cuda_device_malloc` sampled it only
   while the movable-boundary slab was active, and only `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_STATS` printed it — so a
   dense/plain run, the shape #103 was found on, recorded nothing about how close it came.  It is now
   sampled at every `>= 16 MiB` allocation (one `cudaMemGetInfo`; the 16 MiB gate keeps the workspace pool's
   small transient misses out of the hot path) and kept per device.
2. **`GGML_CUDA_LOW_FREE_MIB`** (default **512**, `0` = off, `=0` is the A/B arm): one WARN per device when
   an allocation leaves less than that free, naming the numbers and the knobs (`-c` / `-ub` / `-ngl`, a
   smaller quant, `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB`).  It refuses nothing and changes no behaviour.  **Diagnostic,
   default-on** per the default-on policy; skipped while the slab is armed (the slab parks nearly all free
   VRAM by design).
3. **A refused allocation reports free/total and the low-water mark** instead of only
   `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory`, so `ROCm error: out of memory` arrives with the arithmetic.
4. The `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB` comment's "30x slower because the driver evicts resident weight pages"
   sentence is replaced with the measured statement (that paragraph lives in block 09 and is edited by
   block 10, which already owns this function's tail).

### Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/validate-set.sh` | green: 15 patch files + `rdna-boosts-all.patch` verify, strict 15/15 `git am` on a fresh tarball, applied tree `4d97118949` |
| per-block build gate (`--changed-from 29219f9cb --fast`) | **2/2** (block 10, tip), 14 s; `all` (incl. `tests/`) built at the tip |
| prefill-logit gate (`scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh`) | **mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %** — bit-identical, as expected (no kernel touched) |
| coherence, 4B Q8_0 same-seed text | `111 chars sha=7e6229b260f6` — identical to the r166 binary |
| MTP smoke, 27B GSQ + `draft-mtp-adaptive`, 1 GPU, `-n 3000`, `-p prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` | prompt 5298 tok **1079 t/s**, decode **82.4 t/s**, draft 2772 / accepted 2075 (0.749) |
| neutrality A/B, interleaved, 27B GSQ + MTP, 15790-token prompt | r166 prefill **1102.9 / 1095.1** t/s, decode 61.8 / 61.5; r167 **1093.1 / 1103.3**, 61.6 / 61.8 — neutral |
| the new warning, at a tight budget | fires once: `device 0 is at its VRAM limit: 386.50 MiB free of 32624.00 MiB after a 178.50 MiB allocation` — in an arm that then completes at **1113 t/s** |
| the new refusal report | `a 178.50 MiB device allocation failed on device 0: 0.00 MiB free of 32624.00 MiB, run low-water mark 0.00 MiB` in an arm that aborts (the pool's `flushing … and retrying` line follows it) |
| `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh --since "8 hours ago"` | clean |

### Docs

`ENVIRONMENT.md` (the new `GGML_CUDA_LOW_FREE_MIB` row, and the `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB` mechanism corrected
in place), `patches/README.md` (block 09 section: the new diagnostic + the retired reading),

## 261028.008 (r166) -- TODO #102 closed: the band has its head-256 **GQA-8** arm after all (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), and the width probe can finally tokenize a corpus

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r166`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `29219f9cbfd4f3aa89bca0c75270addebbe0843f`,
tree `cbcb88080bffa9c58b43feca7236d01249841c10`.  Block 06 amended (the width probe's token buffer); docs,
one TODO retired.  Numbers: `benchmarks/2026-10-28-fa-band-gqa8-arm.md`.

**The item's premise was wrong, not the claim.**  #102 was an accepted limitation because "no head-256
GQA-8 model exists in the fleet".  `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` has been in the fleet all along and loads as
`n_head 16 / n_head_kv 2 / n_embd_head_k 256` — head 256 at **ratio 8**, i.e. the band predicate's one
unmeasured ratio (`Q->ne[0] == 256 && V->ne[0] == 256 && 4 < gqa_ratio <= 12`).  The model suggested for the
item (`gemma-4-26B-A4B`) is **not** that arm: its SWA layers are head 256 at ratio **2** and its
full-attention layers ratio 8 at head **512**, so no layer of it enters the band (same for 31B/12B/E4B).
Ratio 8 is the one ratio where the `ncols2 = 8` fold is *exact* (a whole group, no masked tail), which is
why it was worth its own arm.

**Validation.**  `test-logits-width-probe` at `P=4096` (the wide block's gate), 3x R9700, PASS with worst
maxdiff **0** on `KV=f16` and `q8_0`, `-sm layer` and `-sm tensor`, `RS=0` and `RS=from_w`, on
`prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` **and** on the model's own 25 814-token in-domain corpus; `row0_row1_hashes`
are one value across W=1..8 (no W=4/W=5 split).  Controls: `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA=0` moves every hash (so the
default arm is on the band) and `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` is bit-identical (the r134 `static_assert` seen as
a number).  A `rocprofv3` kernel census proves both band blocks are reached at GQA 8: the 64-column band
instantiation `<256,256,8,8,…fetch_ahead,band_wide=true>` dispatched 55 times next to the 32-column band's
70 and prefill's 121.  Text: `plain == draft-mtp == draft-dflash` (block-16 head) `== draft-dflash` (DFlash2
block-8 + selector) at `-n 512` on both split modes (layer 1888 chars `1c5f9e08e5e4`, tensor 2011 chars
`c5b2c23d064a`), with live drafters (acceptance 0.736 / 0.545 / 0.543; 82.9 -> 137.8 / 130.2 / 131.9 t/s).
Both DFlash heads are new files under `/llm/models/Qwen3.6/35B-A3B/{DFlash,DFlash2}/Q8_0/` (hashes in the
record).

**Block 06 amendment (found while running it).**  The probe tokenized into a fixed 8192-token vector, so the
natural prompt for a model-specific arm — its own KLD corpus, 25 814 tokens — died with `tokenize failed
(need 25814)`; it now asks the tokenizer for the required length (`llama_tokenize(..., nullptr, 0, ...)
returns -n`) and sizes the buffer from that.  Verdict logic untouched, test-only, no runtime path.

**Also found (and fixed) while publishing it: the container watcher could wedge silently.**  The release
flow tags and then moves the tag onto a trailing record commit, and the worker had already fetched the
previous position, so `git fetch --quiet --tags origin` refused the update (`would clobber existing tag`),
exited 1, and `set -e` killed `scripts/container-watch.sh` on that line **before any log write** — r166 sat
unbuilt through 40 minutes of one-second cron runs with nothing in `watch.log`.  It is now
`git fetch --tags --force` (a release tag is the source of truth) and a failed fetch is logged.  The
worker was repaired by hand and picks r166 up; `CONTAINERS.md` records the signature.

**Gates.**  `validate-set.sh` strict 15/15, tree `cbcb8808`; `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 809a27419`
**2/2** on the `all` target set (block 06 + the tip, 58 s); `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **mean KLD 0.000000 /
same-top-p 100.000 %**; same-seed coherence unchanged; Protocol A on the dense 27B UD-Q4_K_XL
(`-c 102400`, bf16 KV, `-n 3000`) `plain == draft-mtp` byte-identical on **both** split modes —
`-sm tensor` 50.9 -> 100.7 t/s (acceptance 0.608) and `-sm layer` 25.0 -> 51.6 t/s.  The width arms above were
re-run on the release binary and reproduce the same hashes.  `git diff 809a27419 29219f9cb` is
`tests/test-logits-width-probe.cpp` only, i.e. **no shipped binary links the changed TU**, so the op-test
matrices (`test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` etc.) are r165's and were not re-run.  `TODO.md` #102 removed.

## 261028.007 (r165) -- TODO #109: `hipDeviceEnablePeerAccess` is what costs a replayed decode, so the all-reduce arms were re-cut (dense -> copy engine, host experts -> RCCL's ring, peer access never enabled)

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r165`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `809a27419f0ed7201d693352f4deef3ce4ceb6b3`,
tree `6d7926b87ab6eff83da91a7c4d5e4b27c681aeef`.  Blocks 01 and 10 amended; docs, one gate extension and the
retirement of `TODO #109`.

**What #109 actually was.**  The item asked what RCCL's init leaves behind that costs a *replayed* graph 5-7 %
while the direct node loop is immune, and its own note already suspected "RCCL's presence".  It is not RCCL:
with the all-reduce path held constant, `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=internal` on 27B Q8_0 3x R9700 `-sm tensor
tg128` measures **42.25** with no peer access and **38.77** with `hipDeviceEnablePeerAccess` forced on at comm
init — the whole of the regression, from one HIP call.  It is a **host** cost: a per-token synced loop is
equal in both arms (41.39 vs 41.09), the decode window's kernel census under `rocprofv3` is identical
(24 665 per device, same kernels, the AR kernel is not slower), the AR profile accounts for only
+0.05 ms/token, and a 3-device probe (4 GiB streaming read + an FMA loop, peer access enabled before *and*
after the allocation) measures 0.0 % on bandwidth, ALU time and GPU per-dispatch cost (3.46 vs 3.51 us).
It scales with the number of enabled pairs and enable/disable costs microseconds.  And it is **not
reversible**: after `ncclCommInitAll` has built its P2P mappings, every `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess`
returns `no error` and the arm stays at 37.9 t/s — so a chain that does not want the cost must not enable it.

**Ruled out on the way** (same arm): the per-call arm choice and the hybrid routing thresholds
(`AR_SMALL_BYTES` 0/1e9, and forcing every AR to the internal pipeline with RCCL up still loses: 38.85),
RCCL's presence without peer access (`hybrid` + `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE` 42.2), proxy CPU (`NCCL_PROXY_CPUSET`),
channels (`MAX/MIN_NCHANNELS`, `MAX_P2P_NCHANNELS`), cuMem (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`), dma-buf
(`NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=0`), the graph helper/register/mixing knobs, `NCCL_PROGRESS_APPENDOP_FREQ`,
`NCCL_RUNTIME_CONNECT`, `NCCL_P2P_DIRECT_DISABLE`, `NCCL_P2P_USE_CUDA_MEMCPY`, capture churn (the
`GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_TRACE` census is identical in both arms), `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_CHUNK_SIZE`,
`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT`, `GGML_SCHED_EVENTS`.

**The change.**  The Linux/HIP default (block 01's `auto` chain) is now: internal pipeline for the
decode/verify band; RCCL brought up **eagerly** (the r34 purity rule) but with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE` set when
the user has not; the copy engine brought up too; and the **large arm chosen once, at the first large
all-reduce** by `g_comm_host_experts` — set by `ggml_cuda_slab_arm()` (block 10, which owns the slab state)
— RCCL's ring for a host-offloaded model, the copy-engine arm otherwise.  The copy-engine arm also stopped
enabling peer access (`GGML_CUDA_AR_CE_PEER=1` opts in; staged and direct peer copies measure the same).
The routing is what keeps both regimes, and it is measured at every offload depth: dense prefers the copy
engine (27B `pp2048` 2178 vs 2018, Gemma4 31B 1998 vs 1944, Flash-Next GSQ all-VRAM decode **67.2 vs
59.9** t/s) while a PCIe-saturated host-expert prefill prefers RCCL by 24-34 % (Flash-Next IQ4_NL 2 GPU
`-ncmoe 20` 809 vs 604, `-ncmoe 32` 555 vs 414, `-b/-ub 4096` `pp4096` 2901 vs 2344) and the two only
converge at `-ncmoe 8` on 3 GPUs / full residency.  Disabling RCCL's P2P globally instead (731-747) loses
8 % there, which is why it is a routing decision and not a blanket switch.  `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=hybrid`
keeps the pre-r165 P2P chain, `ce` pins the copy-engine half.

**Numbers.**  27B Q8_0 dense 3 GPU `tg128` **38.6 -> 42.3** (+9.5 %) with prefill flat (2161 vs 2177), 2 GPU
2237/33.09 vs 2210/32.68; Gemma4 31B 3 GPU 1998/34.91 vs 1944/34.40; Flash-Next GSQ IQ3_XXS all-VRAM
decode 67.15 vs 59.92; 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` 2 GPU 1252/99.14 vs 1232/99.18; Flash-Next IQ4_NL `-ncmoe 20`
2 GPU 731-747/43.8 vs 809/44.15 (the one documented residual).  Protocol A (27B Q8_0, 3 GPU `-sm tensor`,
100K ctx, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`): plain **38.3 -> 40.7 t/s**, `draft-mtp` **80.9 -> 88.5 t/s**,
acceptance **0.641** (1972/3075).

**Gates.**  The prefill-logit gate could not reach an all-reduce at all (one device, and the default split is
`layer`), so it gained `--sm` and a `--device` list; the arm switch then gates at **mean KLD 0.001448 /
same-top-p 98.676 %** against the RCCL arm on 3 devices `-sm tensor` (4B Q8_0).  `plain == draft-mtp` greedy
text holds on 27B 3 GPU `-sm tensor` and 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 40`, and same-arm repeats are identical
(the small/large crossover is unchanged, so the decode/verify band is bit-identical to r164 by
construction).  `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 6a8b807b3` **4/4** (the first attempt failed: block
01 cannot call `ggml_cuda_slab_enabled()`, which block 10 introduces — the routing therefore reads a plain
flag that block 10 sets, which is also why the arm choice is described as block 01 + block 10).
`validate-set.sh` strict 15/15, tree `6d7926b8`.

**Files.**  `ggml-cuda.cu` (block 01: the `auto` chain, the `ce` chain, the copy-engine peer opt-in),
`ggml-cuda-slab.cu` (block 10: set `g_comm_host_experts`), `ENVIRONMENT.md` (`GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE` default,
new `GGML_CUDA_AR_CE_PEER`, the r149 "known cost" note retired), `patches/README.md` (block 01),
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §67, `MANIFESTS.md` (gate options + block-01 row), `AGENTS.md` (critical facts),
`TODO.md` (#109 removed), `benchmarks/2026-10-28-allreduce-peer-access.md`.
