## 261028.006 (r164) -- PR #242: the derived kq mask input is reusable on hybrid models, so a >8-token verify step stops rebuilding its graph

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r164`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `6a8b807b39712c37292df9ca994c67cb6cc44e08`,
tree `59f6b98ebd5f7585eb33ca38a09c81e3abb8c0a7`.  One change (block 05) plus the release docs and one gate fix.

**The report.**  PR #242 (@overdoingism): `llm_graph_input_kq_derived::can_reuse()` rejects the reuse whenever
`params.mctx` is not a `llama_kv_cache_context`.  A hybrid model's memory context is a
`llama_memory_hybrid_context`, so the derived input - which was built from `get_attn()`, itself a plain kv
cache context - declined **every** single-sequence batch of more than 8 tokens, and each such step rebuilt its
graph: the verification of a long n-gram draft (9-16 rows), or an MTP verify step at
`--spec-draft-n-max >= 8`.

**Our assessment reproduced the mechanism and found the case the PR does not measure, which is the bigger
one.**  With `LLAMA_KV_N_PAD_MIN` holding `n_kv` on the 256-cell stride the derived form's own gate requires
(`n_kv % 256 == 0`), those batches really did take the derived form, so an MTP verify at a fixed depth 15
reused **0** graphs over 300 decode tokens: r163 was slower than its own `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_DERIVED=0` by
**-7.1 %** at 3 GPU `-sm tensor` (6820.18 -> 6337.97 ms / 300) and **-5.4 %** at 2 GPU (0,2) (5328.70 ->
5041.15 ms / 300).  The 2.7-4 % the PR reports for n-gram drafting on a 3900X is a real but
CPU-dependent slice: our 9950X3D pays ~1.0 ms per rebuild against its ~2.7 ms, so the same n-gram arm (n_max
15, `prompts/recall.txt`, 1 GPU) moves 127.04 -> 127.82 t/s (+0.6 %, and the r163 default was 0.7 % *below* its
own packed arm), and `draft-mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod` at its defaults moves 1331.68 -> 1308.44 ms / 400
(+1.7 %).  3 GPU prefill keeps a 26 286-token prompt at 14.28 s either way (reuse 15 -> 22, no time win).

**Fix (block 05).**  `can_reuse()` looks through a `llama_memory_hybrid_context` to `get_attn()` - exactly the
cache `build_inp_mem_hybrid()` built the input from - and then runs the existing checks unchanged (`n_kv`,
stream count, token count, `params.cparams.kq_mask_derived && kq_mask_derivable(ubatch)`).  iSWA still
rejects, and **must**: `build_inp_mem_hybrid_iswa()` creates *two* derived inputs, one bound to the base cache
and one to the SWA cache, so there is no single cache to look through and a naive look-through would validate
one against the other's state.  No maintained model here is hybrid+SWA (`qwen35` reports `n_swa = 0`), which
is why the gap is a doc note and not code.  `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_DERIVED_REUSE=0` restores the rejection (the A/B
arm); `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_DERIVED=0` remains the packed reference.

**Validation.**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| graphs reused, derived vs packed | parity on every arm: n-gram n_max 15 1 GPU **58 -> 77** (= the packed arm's 77), 3 GPU MTP depth 15 **0 -> 97** (= 97), 2 GPU MTP depth 15 **0 -> 76** (= 76), `mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod` defaults 16 -> 19 (= 19) |
| greedy text, 4 arms (r163 / r164 x derived / packed), `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` | byte-identical, `1866 chars sha=b1f1903bc51c`; the release coherence arm (4B, "The capital of France is") identical too (`111 chars sha=7e6229b260f6`) |
| draft acceptance, 300-3000-token arms | identical to 5 decimals in every arm (MTP depth 15: 0.12846 / 0.18970; adaptive,ngram: 0.97917; Flash-Next adaptive n_max 8: 0.46286) |
| Flash-Next (qwen4exp, `llama_memory_hybrid_idx_context` derives from the hybrid context) 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48` | text identical (`1033 chars sha=603ac1984270`) and reuse unchanged (35) - that model's reuse is limited by another input in both builds, so the patch is inert there rather than harmful |
| MTP Protocol A, 3 GPU, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`, `-n 3000`, bf16 KV | tensor **90.2 t/s** (reference 90.7) vs plain **48.3** (48.4), acceptance **0.604** (0.60); layer **51.8** (51.7) vs plain **25.0**, acceptance **0.621** (0.62) - every figure within noise of the recorded reference |
| prefill-logit gate | **PASS**, mean KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 100.000 % (no kernel touched) |
| per-block build | `--changed-from` r163 tip: block 05 + tip only, 2/2 build in 31 s (`--fast`) |
| `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` | PASS |
| `gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` | PASS (after the fix below) |
| `validate-set.sh` | green (15 patches, fresh-tarball strict apply, tree `59f6b98e`) |

**Gate fix.**  `scripts/gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` was the only gate calling `check-gpu-faults.sh` **without
`--since`**, so it read the whole boot's kernel journal and a stale `[gfxhub] page fault` from the previous
evening (Oct 27 18:14, an unrelated session) failed an otherwise clean run - every functional check had
passed, the keep arm's own log was clean, and the session window was clean.  It now passes
`--since "30 min ago"`, matching `gate-state-pipe.sh` and `gate-spec-align.sh`.  Nothing in the delivery
itself was at fault.

**Doc correction that matters.**  `patches/README.md` block 05 said the derived form is "only for
prefill-shaped batches (`n_tokens > 8`), so decode/verify are untouched".  That word "prefill-shaped" is what
hid this class of regression: the predicate is `n_tokens > 8`, which a verify step reaches as soon as a draft
is 8 tokens deep.  The bullet now says so, and carries the r164 fold.

The contributor's record (their README and the patch as submitted) is archived in
`archive/work/kq-derived-hybrid-reuse/` with this assessment in its `RESOLUTION.md`.

## 261028.005 (r163) -- issue #240: the DFlash layer inputs are written into F1's store from inside the target graph

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r163`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `d99fc588fa075a08f299665d29281ca2bc5057f4`,
tree `ba1e1e072f218179d9a7296483e1681311a31f38`.  One change (block 12) plus the release docs.

**The report.**  Issue #240 (Windows 11, R9700 gfx1201, TheRock ROCm 10): with a DFlash2 draft the target
marks each extracted layer's input as a graph **output** (`ggml_set_output(t_layer_inp[il])`), because
`extract_layer_inputs()` copies them after the graph has run.  An output cannot be reused by the allocator, so
by the last layer all five were live at once and the target's compute buffer grew by ~190 MiB at `-ub 2048`.
Separately, `output_reserve()` always reserved the host rows for them (`n_embd x n_batch` floats per layer,
200 MiB at `-b 2048`, pinned) which F1's device path never reads.

**Reproduced.**  27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2-Q4_K_M, 1x gfx1201, `--parallel 1 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0
-ub 2048 -b 2048 --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 5`, F1 on: target `sched_reserve`
**757.26 MiB** device compute with the draft vs **568.42 MiB** without any layer extraction (the `--fit`
probe), `ROCm_Host output buffer size = 200.95 MiB`, and `F1 device layer-input buffers: 200.0 MiB`.

**Fix (block 12).**

* **The copy is a graph node.**  `llm_graph_result::set_outputs()` emits a `GGML_OP_SET_ROWS` into the
  persistent store per extracted layer instead of marking the tensor an output.  The destination is the
  store, the source is the layer input, and the row indices are an `I32 [n_tokens]` graph **input** filled
  per ubatch (`llama_context::process_ubatch`, offset `cparams.lf_row_offset`) — a baked view offset would be
  captured into a HIP graph and replayed for the wrong ubatch (the r149 lesson), while an index tensor is
  read at runtime.
* **Placement.**  Every arch graph now records its layer inputs through `llm_graph_result::set_layer_inp()`
  (33 files, one line each) instead of assigning `t_layer_inp[il]`.  At the *next* layer's recording it
  expands that layer's nodes and then emits the pending copy, so the copy lands right after the input's last
  consumer — which is what lets the allocator free it.  An arch that does not use the hook is still correct
  (the copy lands at the end of the graph) but keeps the memory cost.
* **The store exists before the first graph that writes it.**  `llama_context::lf_layer_inp_dev_arm()` runs at
  the top of `decode()` and creates the store on the device that owns the first extracted layer (a layer input
  on another device — a `-sm layer` split boundary — is copied across by the scheduler, as the post-graph
  device copy was), then drops and re-reserves the compute buffers **once** so the run settles on the smaller
  layout.  The wait on the draft's consumed event moves before that graph (`lf_wait_features_consumed()`).
* **The host rows are lazy.**  `embd_layer_inp` is no longer part of the output buffer;
  `layer_inp_host_reserve()` allocates the pinned rows when the *host* path first runs, and the arm releases
  the rows the target's warm-up had allocated (the warm-up runs before the draft exists).  The per-ubatch
  `sync_readback()` of the layer inputs is skipped when there is no host readback to order.  **One case still
  needs the host rows:** an embedding (image/audio) ubatch has no token ids, so the draft's device injection
  cannot address its rows and reads the host rows instead.  `extract_layer_inputs()` therefore fills them as
  well when `ubatch.embd != nullptr` (reserving them on demand, so this is the only case that pays the pinned
  rows).  Before this release that path read rows the device-only extraction had left stale - the aborted
  case is now a correct host copy, and the multimodal arm below is its gate.

`GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV_GRAPH=0` restores the pre-r163 shape for A/B and bisect.  `-sm tensor` (Meta layer
inputs), a CPU-offloaded first extracted layer and an allocation failure all keep the host path and log the
reason, exactly as before.

**Validation.**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| target compute buffer (1 GPU, `-ub 2048`) | **757.26 -> 625.27 MiB** (-132 MiB); the 568.42 no-extraction probe is the floor, and the remaining 57 MiB is one layer input in flight |
| target host buffer | `ROCm_Host output buffer size` **200.95 -> 0.95 MiB**; the 200 MiB pinned layer-input rows are allocated by the warm-up and released at the arm |
| greedy text + **draft acceptance**, 27B + DFlash2, 5246-token prompt (3 target ubatches, store offsets 0/2048/4096), `-n 200` | in-graph / `GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV_GRAPH=0` / `GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV=0`: `950 chars sha=8016577f2ed8` and `0.44337 (137/309)`, `acc rate/pos = (0.806, 0.516, 0.387, 0.306, 0.194)` in **all three** arms |
| 2 GPU `-sm layer` (store on ROCm0, extracted layers 48/62 on ROCm1) | identical text (`8016577f2ed8`) in all three arms, acceptance identical to the 1-GPU arm |
| 2 GPU `-sm tensor` | arm declines (`F1: layer inputs are in a Meta buffer (tensor split), using the host path`); text identical to `GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV=0` (`832 chars sha=be945a3af397`) |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M + DFlash2, `-ncmoe 20` (movable-boundary slab armed) | identical text (`733 chars sha=dc6aecbf55b8`) in all three arms |
| 2-slot `--kv-unified` server, concurrent recall + reasoning requests | identical text (688 / 709 chars) and acceptance `0.74163 (155/209)` in all three arms |
| image (embedding) batch: 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M + mmproj-F32 + its DFlash2, `llama-server -np 4 --kv-unified`, one `/v1/chat/completions` request with a PNG | the 256-row embd ubatch takes the host fill (the reason logged: rows reserved on demand *after* the arm's release), the image is described correctly, text + acceptance `0.76271 (45/59)` identical in all three arms (`248 chars sha=80dc45f13d4a`) |
| decode throughput, `-n 1000`, four alternating arms (graph, copy, host, graph) | 106.2 / 106.7 / 106.2 / 106.7 t/s — flat; the five `SET_ROWS` per token cost nothing measurable |
| prefill, 5246-token prompt, `-n 200` | 1220.9 (graph) / 1214.4 (copy) / 1190.0 (host) t/s |
| `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` (base re-recorded from the **r162** build) | **PASS**: mean KLD **0.000000**, same-top-p **100.000 %**, base PPL 5.9325 |
| MTP Protocol A, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 devices, `-n 3000`, 4 axes x 2 split modes | text **byte-identical to r162 in all 8 arms** (e.g. prose layer `6349 chars sha=f3c9463c8d17`, tensor `6765 chars sha=a297b2564310`); decode 61.5-61.7 (prose layer) / 106.8-107.4 (prose tensor) t/s, acceptance 0.81015 (prose layer) - flat |
| `scripts/validate-set.sh` | strict 15/15, applied tree equals release.json |

**Release mechanics.**  The change is folded into block 12 (the DFlash home) with a fixup + autosquash, so
the block count stays 15; `patches/` and `rdna-boosts-all.patch` were regenerated from `6050b467c`, the set
was re-cut with `scripts/apply-all.sh`/`scripts/fork-refresh.sh` to the canonical tip recorded in
`release.json`, and the fork's `rdna-boosts` branch plus the ROCm container images are refreshed with the tag
per the pushing policy.

## 261028.004 (r162) -- issue #239: the DFlash draft reserves its noise block, not the lm_head over the whole ubatch

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r162`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `652e66694ee61d5490bac1f60c0f06b9b0a56ba3`,
tree `3a4906f1a30fd2c97279a49d88562859d0c08104`.  One change (block 12) plus the release docs.

**The report.**  Issue #239 (gfx1201, TheRock ROCm 10): a DFlash2 draft context's compute buffer was
2417.98 MiB at `-ub 2048`, of which 1940 MiB was the decoder's `result_output [n_vocab, n_ubatch]` f32.  At
runtime the draft's token batch is at most `n_seq x (n_max + 1)` rows, so no graph ever used that width.

**Reproduced.**  27B UD-Q5_K_M + DFlash2-Q4_K_M, 1x gfx1201, `-ub 2048`, q8_0 KV: the draft context's
`sched_reserve` reported **2444.41 MiB** device compute (the issue's model/vocab gives 2417.98), and
`graph_reserve` logged the pp graph at `n_tokens = 2048, n_outputs = 2048`.

**Root cause.**  A DFlash/DFlash2 draft context alternates two graph shapes by batch kind: the target-feature
KV injection (`ubatch.embd` / `lf_dev_inject`; up to `n_ubatch`, on the **main** scheduler) and the noise-block
decoder (token batch; at most `n_seq x block`, on the **alt** scheduler - `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2`, r120).
`sched_reserve()`'s generic pp measure graph is a *token* ubatch at `n_ubatch`, so it measured the decoder
branch, and that branch applies the lm_head to every row (DFlash2's selector reads every block position; it
has no `build_inp_out_ids`).  The main scheduler only ever runs the injection graph, so the buffer it was given
was sized for a decoder width it never runs.  The `#18039` encoder rule (`n_outputs_max = n_batch` for
`llama_model_has_encoder()`) is a leftover next to this, not the cause: forcing `n_outputs_max` down does not
help because the DFlash decoder ignores the output limit (the reporter measured this).

**Fix (block 12).**  `llama_batch_allocr::ubatch_reserve(..., with_embd)` can mark a measure ubatch as an
embd batch, and `llama_context::graph_reserve(..., reserve_injection)` uses it to build the injection measure
graph.  For a DFlash draft (`model.arch == LLM_ARCH_DFLASH && cparams.ctx_other != nullptr`)
`sched_reserve()` now reserves:

* the **injection** at `n_ubatch` (the main scheduler's real shape), and
* the **decoder** at `n_seq_max x max(dflash.block_size, n_outputs_max_per_seq)` (the width the noise block
  actually receives; the block covers lilicorr and the DSpark anchor layout),

then leaves the layout at the injection graph.  The buffer keeps the larger of the two, so neither shape can
grow it mid-run (issue #42), and the decoder's own (small) buffer on the alt scheduler is unchanged.  No env
knob: nothing is disabled, the reserve is simply the graph the scheduler runs.

**Validation.**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| draft `sched_reserve`, 1 GPU, `-ub 2048` | device compute **2444.41 -> 264.15 MiB (-2.18 GiB)**; host compute 40.18 -> 200.14 MiB (the injection's F32 feature input; the F1 gather's output is the same shape); free VRAM 8622 -> 10802 MiB.  `-v` logs: injection pp `n_tokens=2048`, decoder tg `n_tokens=8` (block_size 8, `n_max` 5) |
| greedy text, 27B Q5_K + DFlash2, `-n 200`, seed 42 | 1 GPU `941 chars sha=c62b6901495a`, 2 GPU `-sm tensor` `899 / 97fb92617a9b`, `LLAMA_DFLASH_DEV=0` `592 / 6e3fd559c6a8` (the host injection path), `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` `941 / c62b6901495a` - **byte-identical before/after in every arm** |
| deterministic 1-slot server (`--parallel 1 --kv-unified`, `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 5 --backend-sampling`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`) | 636 chars, **identical content** and draft counts (189 generated / 88 accepted) before vs after |
| 2-slot `--kv-unified` server (allocation/abort coverage) | both concurrent slots answer; no compute-buffer growth, no abort.  Concurrent 2-slot text is not a text oracle (per-process/concurrent nondeterminism, same shape as the documented hipBLASLt class), so it is coverage, not the gate |
| MTP Protocol A (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 devices, `-n 3000`, prose, bf16 KV) | tensor plain **48.16** / `draft-mtp` **90.78** t/s, acceptance **0.60413**; layer plain **24.96** / `draft-mtp` **51.62**, acceptance **0.62134** - the recorded 3-device reference (48.4 / 90.7 / 0.60 and 51.7 / 0.62) |
| `scripts/validate-set.sh` | strict 15/15, applied tree `3a4906f1a` equals release.json |

**Release mechanics.**  The change is folded into block 12 (the DFlash home) with a fixup + autosquash, so the
block count stays 15; the set was re-cut from `6050b467c` (canonical `apply-all.sh` tip `652e66694`, tree
`3a4906f1a`), `patches/` + `rdna-boosts-all.patch` regenerated, `release.json` rewritten.  Block 12's patch
is `+4629 / -807` over 48 files.  The fork's `rdna-boosts` branch and the ROCm container images are refreshed
with the tag, per the pushing policy.

## 261028.003 (r161) -- issue #241: the routed fused gate arm is back (block 08)

**Release `v15-6050b467c-r161`**, base `6050b467c`, 15 blocks, tip `4a156887b4918f178551993c34ded4bc4c69df48`,
tree `e379e5c3df9e4a6f5503840e2547b2fb0b578cfd`.  One code change (block 08) plus a stale gate base refresh.

**The report.**  Issue #241 (r159, gfx1151): `llama-server` aborts on the first prefill of an `lfm2moe` model
with `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu:468: GGML_ASSERT(gate && !ids && !fusion->x_bias && ...)` in
`ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q`, called from `ggml_cuda_try_fuse`.  The reporter's analysis was right in substance and
one detail was wrong, which matters for the fix:

* The firing matcher is block 08's **MoE gate/up+GLU MMQ prefill fusion** (`MUL_MAT_ID`, `ids != nullptr`,
  `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_MOE_MMQ_FUSION` as its kill switch), *not* upstream #29948's dense arm.
* Guarding the dense arm with `ids == nullptr` (the reporter's first patch hunk) is **inert**:
  `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_q` -> `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q_fusion_matches` requires
  `up->op == GGML_OP_MUL_MAT`, so it cannot match a `MUL_MAT_ID`.  What actually made their model work was the
  env kill switch, which stopped the routed arm.

**Root cause.**  `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q` serves **two** fused gate/up/GLU arms with disjoint preconditions:
upstream #29948's dense interleaved `has_fusion` arm (`ids == nullptr`, bias/scale allowed, NVIDIA-only) and
block 08's routed `has_gate` arm (`ids != nullptr`, no bias/scale, `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q_switch_type_gate`,
RDNA).  The r138 re-base merged upstream's whole `if (fusion) { GGML_ASSERT(gate && !ids && ...) }` preamble
into the function that also serves the routed arm, so the MoE fusion aborted on **every** config that reached
it, from r138 through r160.  Nothing else was wrong with the path: it is reachable and correct, and the fix is
to drop `ids` from the shared preamble (bias/scale stay dense-only).  Block 08 carries it, with the reason in
the commit's `Amended (r161)` paragraph; `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §65 is the rule, `patches/README.md` (block 08) and
an `AGENTS.md` bullet are the pointers.

**Why five releases missed it (the finding worth keeping).**  The triple matcher only runs when the *pair*
fusion (`mul_mat_q_pair`) stands down, and that is arch-dependent:

* on **RDNA4** `mmb_cfg().routed = 0` (S12: MMB's routed path is a measured loss there), so `mul_mat_q_pair`
  takes the gate/up pair before the triple is considered -> the abort is unreachable on the maintainer's daily
  arms (that is why `GGML_PAIR_OFF=1` is the gfx1201 repro);
* on **gfx1151** `routed = 1`, so the pair stands down *for MMB*, and MMB's fused GLU takes the triple on the
  Qwen-family shapes.  Only a model whose GLU shape MMB declines (this `lfm2moe`) falls through to the MMQ
  triple -> the abort.

So reproducing it needs both the arch and the model: an RDNA4 box with `GGML_PAIR_OFF=1`, or an RDNA3.5 box
with an MMB-declined MoE.  The predicate mismatch itself is filed as `TODO.md` #115 (measured neutral, so it is a
kernel-selection decision to measure, not a defect to fix here).

**Reproduced, both ways.**

* gfx1151 (`halo`, single gfx1151, the r148 tree, same assert): the reporter's own server command
  (`-c 32768 -fa on -np 1 -ub 2048 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0`, first `/v1/chat/completions`)
  aborts at `mmq.cu:468`; the r161 tree answers the same request.
* gfx1201: `llama-cli` + `GGML_PAIR_OFF=1` on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M aborts at the same assert, and passes
  after the fix (the routed kernel then runs: verified with a temporary log).

**Validation.**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| gfx1201, LFM2.5-8B-A1B-i1-Q6_K, fused vs `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_MOE_MMQ_FUSION=1` (`GGML_PAIR_OFF=1` both) | greedy text **byte-identical** (`1264 chars sha=727257c78293`); prefill **KLD -0.000000 / same-top-p 100.000 %** (llama-perplexity `--kl-divergence`, 40 chunks, `-c 512`) |
| gfx1151, the reporter's server request, 256 tokens, fused vs unfused | **byte-identical** (`965 chars sha=d55bc8a8def9`) |
