## 261028.002 (r160) -- the MTP reference figures are THREE-device numbers: r159 -> r160 has no throughput regression

**Not a release.**  No code, patch or `release.json` change; `v15-6050b467c-r160` (tip `c7adb4f2b`, tree
`1574b375e`) is unchanged.  This entry corrects a wrong attribution in 261028.001 and records the A/B that
settles it.

**What was wrong.**  261028.001 ends the gate list with "the tensor figure is below the r159 record's 90.69
with the same command; the same-binary A/B ... measures 81.3 vs 81.1 t/s, so that gap is the box (GPU pair /
host state)".  That attribution is **wrong**.  The r159 reference numbers (`benchmarks/mtp-adaptive-
methodology.md` rule 0 arm quoted in `AGENTS.md`) are **three-device** measurements, and the arm measured
here was **two devices** (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`).  Dense 27B MTP decode scales with the device count
(90.7 at 3 vs 81.4 at 2), so the comparison was never like for like.

**The A/B (interleaved, same session, same source path `~/llama.cpp`, same `GGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS` set in both
build directories, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, `-c 102400`, bf16 KV, `-n 3000`, prose prompt, `-fit off`):**
`build-r159` is the previous release's tree; `build-rocm` is r160.

| arm | r159 | r160 |
|---|---|---|
| MTP `draft-mtp`, **3 devices**, tensor | **90.8** t/s | **90.7** t/s |
| MTP plain, 3 devices, tensor | 48.2 | 48.4 |
| MTP `draft-mtp`, **2 devices (0,2 = x8+x8)**, tensor | **81.4** | **81.4** |
| MTP `draft-mtp`, 3 devices, layer | 51.7 | 51.6 |
| MTP `draft-mtp`, 2 devices, layer | 54.5 | 54.6 (acceptance 0.621) |

Acceptance, r160: 0.541 (2 devices, tensor), 0.621 (2 devices, layer).  Protocol A (draft-mtp >= plain on
both split modes, acceptance > ~0.45) is met on every arm.

**Every other axis, r159 vs r160, interleaved:**

| arm | r159 | r160 |
|---|---|---|
| dense pp2048, 2 devices tensor, `-r 5`, round 1 / 2 | 1971.10 / 1987.37 | 1962.55 / 1985.84 |
| dense tg128, 2 devices tensor, same runs | 46.32 / 46.36 | 46.36 / 46.39 |
| dense pp2048 / tg128, **1 device** | 1349.98 / 30.69 | 1353.43 / 30.75 |
| dense tg64 **@ d16384**, 2 devices tensor, 2 rounds | 44.58 / 44.58 | 44.64 / 44.63 |
| 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, pp / tg64, `-c 32768`, 2 devices tensor, 2 rounds | 1067.3 / 1058.5, 89.6 / 90.4 | 1064.2 / 1065.6, 90.1 / 91.0 |

All within each arm's own run-to-run spread; the one first-reading deviation (pp2048 1981.99 vs 1943.16,
-2.0 %) does not survive interleaving, and the same-binary reserve A/B on that arm is flat
(default 1998.86 / 1968.26 vs `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1` 1972.10 / 1966.39).  The `-ncmoe` arm's greedy
text is byte-identical (`254 chars sha=f60c8ac82d67`) and its load is unchanged apart from the intended one:
the **host (CPU) compute buffer** 48.29 -> 16.42 MiB at `-c 32768 -ub 512` (exactly the 32 MiB mask), with
the meta compute buffer (510.00 MiB), the slab (29.19 GiB), the arena (28.62 GiB) and every boundary
identical.

**The PCIe question, verified on the box.**  Root ports `00:01.1` = **x8**, `00:01.2` = **x4**,
`00:01.3` = **x8** (all max 32 GT/s; each GPU's own link is x16 @ 32 GT/s behind its switch), and
`rocm-smi --showbus` maps HIP 0 -> `03:00.0` (root x8), HIP 1 -> `06:00.0` (**x4**), HIP 2 -> `09:00.0`
(root x8), HIP 3 -> `1a:00.0` (the iGPU).  Every 2-device arm in this release used **`0,2`, the x8+x8
pair**.  The pair is not a confounder for decode (MTP tensor `draft-mtp`: 81.1-81.4 on `0,2` vs 81.2 on the
mixed `0,1`) but it is decisive for prefill, as recorded: dense pp2048 2 devices tensor **2003.36** on `0,2`
vs **1765.71** on `0,1` (**-11.9 %**, link-bound), tg128 flat (46.23 vs 46.15).

**Kept for future A/Bs:** `~/llama.cpp/build-r159` (the r159 tree at the canonical source path, so ccache
and the compiler command lines match `build-rocm`).

**Rule that follows:** quote the **device count** with every multi-GPU throughput number, and never compare
a 2-device arm against the 3-device reference.  `AGENTS.md`'s MTP bullet now carries the counts.

## 261028.001 (r160) -- a text-only M-RoPE context no longer reserves the packed kq mask it never uses (issue #238, blocks 05 + 10)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r160` (base `6050b467c`, tip **`c7adb4f2b`**, tree
**`1574b375eafa361ff2155ba075dcb5b382aff05e`** -- recorded in `release.json`, which is the source of truth;
15 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green, checksums and both Windows lints clean).  Delta against the r159 tree:
**six files, +99/-2**, `include/llama.h`, `src/llama-cparams.h`, `src/llama-context.{h,cpp}`,
`common/{common,speculative}.cpp`.  Folded into **block 05**, which owns the derived kq mask and the reserve
predicate (the reserve-reason note's 2-D bullet is block 10's text and is updated there, hence a two-block
fold).  No kernel, no numerics, no default change: every gate below is byte-identical.

**The report (issue #238, `overdoingism`, Windows 11 / R9700).**  A text-only `llama-server` on Qwen3.8-27B
(Q5_K, q8_0 KV, `-c 220160 -ub 2048`) reserved the **packed** kq mask in `sched_reserve()` although every
batch of the run took the **derived** mask (`resolve_fused_ops: derived kq mask flash attention enabled`,
and `GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2` shows the prefill reserve graph built without `attn_inp_kq_cell_pos`, i.e. with
`kq_mask_derived = false`).  The cause is the #42 fix: `kq_mask_packed_reachable()` answered "yes" for any
`n_pos_per_embd() > 1` model, and Qwen3.x is **IMROPE even for text** -- where every position is degenerate
(`x == y == pos`), so `kq_mask_derivable()` accepts every batch and the packed mask is never allocated.
Their numbers: 0.832 MiB of device compute buffer and 0.498 MiB of pinned host per ubatch token at 220160
cells, i.e. ~860 MiB + ~860 MiB at `-c 220160 -ub 2048`, which is what decides whether a bigger context or
ubatch still fits on a 32 GiB card (29.6 GiB peak on their config).

**Reproduced here** (r159 `build-rocm`, Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q5_K_M, 1x R9700 `gfx1201`, ROCm 10.1.0, q8_0 K/V,
`-fa on`, `-c 220160`, text only, `-fit` on so both contexts are visible):

| `-ub` | ROCm0 | ROCm_Host |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 357.29 MiB | 255.29 MiB |
| 1024 | 714.30 MiB | 510.31 MiB |
| 2048 | 1428.34 MiB | 1020.36 MiB |

0.697 / 0.498 MiB per ubatch token -- the host figure is the reporter's exactly (2.0 bytes per cell per
token); their device figure is 0.135 MiB/token higher because their target runs a DFlash2 draft with
backend sampling, which this arm does not.

**What shipped.**  The M-RoPE term of `kq_mask_packed_reachable()` is no longer the model's capability but
two reachability signals:
* **`llama_context_params.pos_2d`** (new, default false) -- the caller declares that 2-D (M-RoPE) positions
  can be submitted.  `common_context_params_to_llama()` sets it from `--mmproj`, and
  `common_base_params_to_speculative()` clears `mmproj.path` for the draft context (a drafter only ever sees
  the target's text positions).  A multimodal run therefore reserves the worst case **at load time**, as
  before, and never has to grow later.
* **A latch** -- `decode()` inspects the incoming batch (an embedding row, no token id, whose `pos[0..2]`
  differ) **before** `sched_reserve()` and, if the context did not declare 2-D, sets
  `kq_mask_pos_2d_seen` and forces exactly **one** re-reserve with the packed mask, logged as
  `decode: 2-D (M-RoPE) positions in this batch - re-reserving with the packed kq mask`.  This is the
  correctness half: a library that submits image chunks itself is repaired once instead of depending on a
  per-graph compute-buffer growth (which on Windows/WDDM is the failure mode that costs the most).
Multi-sequence, alibi and the `allow_derived == false` builders keep the packed reserve unchanged.
`LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1` forces the pre-r160 worst case for every M-RoPE context (the exact A/B
arm); `=0` forces the derived one and disables the latch.

**Measured after** (same arm as above, `-c 220160 -ub 2048`, text only): the `--fit` probe context reserves
**569.20 / 161.21 MiB** and the run's own context **626.12 / 161.21 MiB** instead of **1428.34 / 1020.36**
and **1571.18 / 1020.36** -- i.e. **859 MiB of VRAM and 859 MiB of pinned host memory** per context, at
exactly the mask's size.  `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1` reproduces the old numbers to the byte (so the A/B
is exact), and `-np 2` is byte-identical in both arms (multi-slot keeps the packed reserve by design).
The win scales with the context, as the mask does: at `-c 32768 -ub 2048` the same single-sequence config
goes 696.34 / 288.36 -> **568.48 / 160.50 MiB** (128 MiB, which is the mask at 32768 cells).  A **deep
context** is what the issue reports and where the numbers matter.

**The two 2-D paths were both verified.**  `--mmproj` (Qwen3.8-27B GSQ IQ3_S + its BF16 projector,
`-c 65536 -ub 2048`) logs `packed kq mask reserve = 1 (2-D positions declared, e.g. a multimodal
projector)` and reserves **2060.02 / 416.37 MiB** -- identical to `LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1`, while
`=0` drops the host side to 160.63 MiB.  A real image request (`-c 8192 -ub 512`, a 800x480 PNG -> a
375-token image chunk) runs with the declared reserve, no re-reserve, and the usual 4 same-size + 1
changed-size graph reallocs.  Then, with the declaration temporarily suppressed (a local edit, not shipped),
the same request started at 515.00 / 40.33, printed the latch line once, re-reserved to **566.50 / 48.29**
(= the declared arm exactly) and produced **byte-identical** text.

**Gates (all green).**
* Greedy coherence, 27B UD-Q5_K_M 2 GPU `-sm tensor` `-c 16384 -ub 512` q8_0, 200 tokens: the derived-reserve
  and packed-reserve arms are **823 chars, sha `e0bad2553078`** (identical), and the `-ncmoe` arm
  (35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, `-c 32768 -ub 512`, 128 tokens) is **533 chars,
  sha `1a9fe8baaa7f`** in both.
* `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` (release, against the r159-recorded base, f16 KV): **0.000000 / 100.000 %**.
  `--kv q8_0 --ab "LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1"` (base recorded from this build with the env, candidate
  default): **0.000000 / 100.000 %**, base PPL 5.9317.
* MTP Protocol A (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, `-c 102400`, bf16 KV, `-n 3000`, 2 GPU, both split modes):
  layer **54.6** vs **26.6** t/s plain, acceptance **0.621**; tensor **81.1** vs **44.8** t/s, acceptance
  **0.541**.  The tensor figure is below the r159 record's 90.69 with the same command; the same-binary A/B
  (`LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE=1` vs default) measures **81.3 vs 81.1 t/s**, so that gap is the box (GPU
  pair / host state), not this change -- the layer arm, which is the one the r159 note records as 51.66, is
  54.6 here.
* `scripts/validate-set.sh`: strict 15/15 on a fresh tarball, tree `1574b375e`, checksums, conflict-marker
  scan and the Windows portability lint all clean.

**Records:** this entry; `patches/README.md` (block 05 "the packed mask is only reserved where it is
reachable", block 10's note, the knob list), `ENVIRONMENT.md` (`LLAMA_KQ_MASK_PACKED_RESERVE`), `AGENTS.md`
(the invariant: never reserve on `n_pos_per_embd()` alone, and do not remove the latch),
`MANIFESTS.md` (block 05's verification line).  No `TODO` item was opened: the change is the issue's fix,
and the only open question it leaves -- whether a *future* `kq_mask_derivable()` rejection reason needs its
own reachability test -- is the standing rule already written into the predicate's comment.

## 261027.011 (r159) -- the FA prefill staging arena gains two OPT-IN bounds: a KV-chunked ring and an eager allocation (block 10)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r159` (base `6050b467c`, tip **`6627ed715`**, tree
**`4a02cc27b354fa4316dc5f9f4832f82f32f9b789`**, 15 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green, checksums and both
Windows lints clean).  Blocks 05/10/11-14 are unchanged in content except block 10, which gains both
changes.  **Nothing changes for a default run**: an arena allocation size and an env-gated launch path
cannot move a logit, and the default arm's prefill logits were re-measured at **0.000000 / 100.000 %**.

**Why an opt-in and not a default.**  Both bound a *transient* the default arm is happy to pay for: the
staging is worth +1.5 / +2.7 / +5.1 % pp at 8k/16k/32k (M0a) and every bound costs either the peak (eager)
or depth (chunking).  The maintainer's rule for this release is one default policy on every platform, so
both ship as choices and `ENVIRONMENT.md` documents the four-arm table (`ENVIRONMENT.md` "four documented
choices").

**1. `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_CHUNK=<rows>` -- the staging transient becomes O(chunk) (`TODO` #114, closed).**
The MMA prefill kernel's only multi-block KV split is stream-K (`kbc = blockIdx.x*total/gridDim.x`), whose
partials were published in two contracts: a tile-start block wrote a **final normalized** value and a seam
block an unnormalized partial plus meta that only the fixup folds.  A tile whose KV sat inside one block
therefore published no `(max, rowsum)` at all -- which is why the first chunked attempt (M2) produced NaNs.
r159 gives the path a **per-row partial contract**: every block publishes `(unnormalized numerator, max,
rowsum)` for its own rows (the no-seam case included, with `np > 1`'s combined max carried in the free
padding float of `tile_Q`), the two fixup kernels hand the merged value back unnormalized, and one
`kv_start` int keeps the fully-masked-group bitmap and the `KV_max` bound exact per chunk (chunks are
`lcm(nbatch_fa, FATTN_KQ_STRIDE)`-aligned).  The launcher converts + launches + folds per chunk over a
**one-slot** ring (in-order stream, so one slot suffices), merges with an online softmax and normalizes
once.  Measured (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU, q8_0 KV, `-ub 512`, `llama-bench -r 3`):

| arm | ring | pp8192 | pp16384 | pp32768 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| default | 134 MiB @32k | 1315.01 | 1245.08 | **1139.41** |
| `CHUNK=16384` | **64 MiB** | 1307.79 | 1246.99 | **1139.56 (+0.0 %)** |
| `CHUNK=8192` | 32 MiB | 1307.67 | 1245.31 | 1106.85 (-2.9 %) |
| `CHUNK=4096` | 16 MiB | 1305.53 | 1223.84 | 1089.72 (-4.4 %) |

Depth: pp65536 default 971.68 vs `CHUNK=16384` 931.90 (**-4.1 %**, 4 chunks).  The cost is per chunk
boundary (~1.5 % beyond the second), and it is **not** the merge or the fold (~0.2 % each, priced by
skipping them) nor the per-chunk conversion (~0.4 %): ~2.2 % is inside the FA kernel's short-KV execution
and is left as a documented, unbudgeted follow-up (only worth a campaign if <= 4 chunks ever becomes a
default).  Arena proof: 33k prompt -- default `FA_STAGE` climbs 16 -> 68 -> **160 MiB**, `CHUNK=16384`
prints `FA_CHUNK n_kv=33024 rows=16384 chunks=3 ring=64.0 MiB` and stays there at any depth (1024 MiB ->
64 MiB at `-c 262144`).  Gates: `gate-prefill-logits.sh --kv q8_0` re-recorded at the standard point
(`base PPL 5.9317`) -- 2 chunks **0.000995 / 99.707 %** PASS, 4 chunks 0.005264 / 98.828 % (5 % over the
limit, the expected re-baseline and the reason the recommended chunk is 16384); `FLASH_ATTN_EXT`
**6450/6450 with chunking on** (`=256` and `=128`), `FLASH_ATTN_QSA` 26/26, `W=1..8` probe PASS (maxdiff 0,
f16 and q8_0, chunk off and on), greedy text byte-identical up to ~5 chunks on 4B and 27B, and one slab
arm (35B-A3B, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`): `slab=1`, ring 16 MiB/device, pp 1241.07 -> 1237.79 --
parity, and **no benefit**, because that arena is already released at the wide-drop: documented "leave it
off on slab configs".  Three real bugs the op matrix caught and this release fixes in the mechanism: sinks
counted once per chunk (149 cases), the no-seam publish gated on an empty `stride_k` pass for small
`nbatch_combine` (7 cases, +-inf), and the unsliceable **packed** group bitmap (disabled while chunked; the
derived layout slices exactly).

**2. `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_PREALLOC=2` -- the eager allocation, validated on WDDM (block 10).**  The r156
ceiling grows the arena in <= 3 steps; on WDDM a freed allocation stays committed and a late step lands in
shared memory (issue #138 / the #237 follow-up).  Mode `2` takes the root-based hint in one allocation at
the first request.  The reporter's re-test (Windows, 1x R9700, `-c 262144`, q8_0 KV, 100607-token
`/completion`, fresh server per arm): **pp 592 -> 781** (r149: 791), one `alloc=1024.0 MiB` at 0:22 instead
of `16 -> 72 -> 296 -> 1024` at 1:48, dedicated VRAM back to r149's peak; **greedy text hash identical in
all six arms and equal to r149**, draft acceptance 44/54 everywhere, PPL identical in every arm including
per-chunk values.  The trade is the peak (1 GiB/context at `-c 262144`), which `FA_STAGE_CHUNK` or
`FA_STAGE_MAX_MB` then bound -- and the tester's own best arm was `MAX_MB=256` (pp == r149, shared == r149,
480 MiB *less* dedicated than r149).

**Dropped:** `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_DRAFT_MB` (prototyped in `beta/fa-stage-peak`, never shipped).  The
tester's arm B showed it only sets the draft arena's *starting* size -- the context kept its 1.25x ladder
(64 -> 417.5 MiB, late steps at 2:08) -- so it did not do what its name promised.  `FA_STAGE_MAX_MB` is the
knob that actually bounds a draft; a true draft ceiling is a possible future item, not a promise.

**Also clarified in `ENVIRONMENT.md`:** `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_MAX_MB` is a **per-operand** cap, so `=256`
gives a 512 MiB arena for a K+V op (the tester's "why 512?" question -- intended, not rounding).

**Records:** `archive/work/fa-stage-chunking/` (campaign: `README.md`, `FINDINGS-2026-10-27-{m0,m2,m3}.md`,
`HANDOVER-2026-10-27-114.md`, both prototypes) and `archive/work/fa-stage-peak/` (the superseded beta).
`TODO` #113 and #114 closed by this entry.

## 261027.010 (r158) -- the replay guard compares in place over a source-packed store; the graph key is built once (block 10)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r158` (base `6050b467c`, tip **`217b1c999`**, tree
**`8851bb0024e547142ec533bd76ec18912539edad`**, 15 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green).  Delta against the r157
tree: **two files, +129/-54**, `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/{ggml-cuda.cu,common.cuh}` (folded into block 10, the
block that owns the current shape of the graph-compute path).  No kernel, no numerics, no env var, no
default, no allocation size — every change is host code in the CUDA/HIP graph-replay bookkeeping.

**1. Why the guard was worth looking at.**  `ggml_cuda_graph_update_required` is the only check that a
replayed graph still points at the tensors it was captured from, and `cgraph->uid` cannot short-circuit it:
the scheduler mints a fresh uid per split per compute (upstream #21764) and the Meta rebuild mints fresh
child uids, so the walk runs on **every** `graph_compute` (verified: `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_DEBUG=1` prints zero
"CUDA Graph id … reused" lines on a decode).  Its old form built a `node_properties prop = {}` (1048 B
zero-fill) + a 328 B `memcpy` + a 1048 B `memcmp` per node, per call, on the hit path where nothing
differs.  A decode-only perf window put `__memcmp_evex_movbe` at **1.41 %** of CPU samples on the 35B-A3B
2-GPU host-expert arm.

**2. What shipped.**  (a) `ggml_cuda_graph_props_match()` compares `cgraph->nodes[i]` **in place** and
stops at the first difference, then compares only the **non-null** sources' `data`/`ne`/`nb`; a
`ggml_cuda_graph_props_store()` rewrites the store only when the guard says “changed”.  (b) The store is
packed to the sources a node has (`prop_nodes` / `prop_src_off` / `prop_srcs`) instead of a fixed
`GGML_MAX_SRC` layout: measured on the largest graph of the run, 67 nodes / 98 sources,
**70,752 -> 29,840 B (−58 %)** — ~100 MB less host state at the 4526 graph entries a 6000-token Flash-Next
session reaches.  (c) The graph key is built **once** per call and threaded into `update_required` /
`evaluate_and_capture` / `set_enabled` (it was built 2-3×), and `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_optimize` no
longer builds and discards one before its `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT` early return — dead work on every call in
the default (opt-out) configuration.  (d) `ggml_cuda_graph_check_compability` reads the device's arch once
instead of a `cudaGetDevice()` runtime call per `MUL_MAT_ID` node.  Measured after: `memcmp` 1.41 ->
0.58 %, `get_key` 0.26 -> 0.15 %.

**3. The guard is not weakened** — this is the point.  The node header is still `memcmp`'d verbatim against
the live tensor (`src[]`/`view_src`/`buffer` object identity included), and the packed source run carries
the same `data`/`ne`/`nb` values in the same source order, with the null/non-null layout already fixed by
the header compare.  PR #230's follow-up offered an identity-free compare
(`GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_PROPS_RELAXED=1`, blanking `src[]`/`view_src`/`buffer`) with a census showing 4129 -> 242
`properties_changed`; we declined it again — it treats a symptom of the r149 key collision and removes the
only check that a replay's baked arguments still point where they were captured, and its measured effect
(its own 4-pair CIs cross zero; +0.2-0.5 % on ours) does not buy that.  The *cost* of the compare was
removed instead, without changing what it compares.  Their data and the decision are recorded in
`archive/work/graph-replay-keys/README.md` §4.

**4. No throughput claim, deliberately.**  On this box the work is hidden behind the GPU: 35B-A3B 2 GPU
`-ncmoe 40` **+0.15 %** (4 pairs), Flash-Next 2 GPU `-ncmoe 48` **+0.75 %** (6 pairs, paired sd 0.63 — not
significant), 35B-A3B + DFlash2 −0.6 %, Gemma4 E4B + MTP flat, 27B 3-device dense `tg128` flat, 1-GPU
dense flat, and **+0.7 % even pinned to 2 CPU cores**.  The host enqueues ~240 `graph_compute` calls per
token in ~1-2 ms against 10-28 ms of GPU work, so it runs ahead.  The value is what a token costs a weaker
CPU (fewer instructions, less bus traffic) and the RAM it saves — which is why it ships at all, and why
no t/s figure should be quoted for r158.  Numbers: `benchmarks/2026-10-27-graph-replay-props.md`.

**5. Gates.**  Greedy text byte-identical in every pair (8/8 35B-A3B 2 GPU, 6/6 Flash-Next 2 GPU, 2/2
35B-A3B + DFlash2, 6/6 Gemma4 E4B + MTP); `replay` census **identical in every pair** (`capture`/
`properties_changed` vary run-to-run on both builds because the 10 s unused-graph sweep depends on
wall-clock load time); `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID` OK; `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **mean KLD 0.000000 /
same-top-p 100.000 %**; `validate-set.sh` green; `fork-refresh.sh --build --gates` green.

**Not taken (found while reviewing this path, its own campaign if ever):** the per-call Meta rebuild —
`ggml_backend_meta_graph_compute` re-splits every compute because the parent uid is fresh, and in the same
profile window it costs `meta_graph_compute` 1.00 % + `meta_get_split_state` 1.10 % + mutex 2.22 % +
`malloc`/`free` 1.44 % ≈ 6 % of the window's CPU; and `any_cuda_graph_enabled()`/
`_has_instance()` are O(#graphs) scans called four times per `MEAN` node (latent — no shipped arch
dispatches `MEAN`).

## 261027.009 (r157) -- TODO #110: the device-state path's cost was the pageable bounce per piece, not its views (block 12)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r157` (base `6050b467c`, tip **`c50bfdea0`**, tree
**`954548b201df410acf65e6a404cef8a23d7390ba`**, 15 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green).  Delta against the r156
tree: **one file, +169/-37**, `src/llama-context.cpp` (block 12).  No kernel, no numerics, no default and no
allocation size on any path a `llama-cli`/`llama-bench`/server run takes.

**1. What the item claimed, and what the measurement said.**  TODO #110 described
`llama_io_read_device` as creating "one simple-tensor view per KV cache chunk per layer ... where one view
per tensor plus a chunked copy would be ~24".  Instrumented, the views were **0.17 ms** for 128 of them
(plus 0.01 ms for the write side's) — the item's metadata cost was real but worthless.  The copy loop was
**2210/2269 ms** of a 2227/2269 ms pair: `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` between two meta buffers takes ggml's
fallback (a meta buffer has no `.cpy_tensor`), i.e. a **pageable `malloc` + a synchronous device read + a
synchronous device write per piece**.  Per piece, the meta read of a 2 MiB *view* cost 3.4-5.1 ms at
enqueue (V-cache tensors only; K's stayed under 2 ms) because the view's inherited split state makes the
reader splice it row by row — the same bytes handed to the backend as `(tensor, offset, size)` cost
0.15 ms.  So the device path was **58x slower than the host path it exists to beat**: 2.23 s to save and
2.28 s to restore 213.6 MiB on 2 GPUs, against 21.9/38.9 ms for the same bytes over `llama_io_write_host`/
`read_host`, and 3.0/3.2 ms on one GPU (where the copy is a true device-to-device `cpy_tensor`).

**2. The fix.**  `llama_state_copy_staged()` (`src/llama-context.cpp`) copies a list of pieces through the
context's pinned `state_stage` in **bands**: every piece of a band is queued with
`ggml_backend_tensor_get_async` on the backend that owns it, each backend is synchronized once, then every
piece is queued with `set_async` and synchronized once — so the fixed cost is paid per band, not per piece.
A band is a run of **whole** pieces (a piece is never cut: the meta backend only serves a window aligned to
the tensor's own layout — cutting one trips `size % row_stride == 0`); a single piece larger than the band
gets a band of its own and grows the stage to it.  `LLAMA_STATE_STAGE_MIB` (default 64, `0` = the old path
and the A/B arm; 8 MiB already reaches the plateau) sets the band.  Pieces are handed to the backend as
**the tensor plus an offset**, not as a fresh `ggml_view_1d` of the piece: that is the second half of the
win and the reason the fix is not just "use a pinned buffer".  Both device io classes take the context, so
the staged arm is chosen per buffer type (`llama_state_copy_bounces()`: the destination is a meta device) —
the single-device arm keeps its device-to-device copy untouched.  The read path's `same_chunking`/1:1 fast
path is gone (the byte-cursor walk it sat next to covers it: an aligned piece becomes a whole-tensor copy),
and its per-piece views are now created only in the non-meta fallback.

**3. Measured** (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL, `-c 2112`, state 213.6 MiB, 2 GPU
`-sm tensor`, best of 3):

| arm | save | restore |
|---|---|---|
| contiguous, **before** | 2227 ms | 2269 ms |
| contiguous, **after** | **14.7 ms** | **17.2 ms** |
| fragmented (49 152 pieces of ~3 KiB, the #210 lazy-idle-slot shape), before | 2237 ms | 2282 ms |
| fragmented, after | 16.1 / **14.7 ms** (rep 0 pays the stage's first fault: 497 ms) | 21.1 / **17.3 ms** (rep 0: 355 ms) |
| one GPU, before / after | 3.01 / 3.02 ms | 3.18 / 3.22 ms |

i.e. **151x / 132x** on the shape the item named, and now **faster than the host path** (21.9/38.9 ms)
instead of 58x slower.  `LLAMA_STATE_STAGE_MIB` sweep, save/restore: `0` 2231/2278, `8` 15.3/18.4, `32`
14.8/17.7, `64` 14.7/17.2, `512` 14.6/17.5.  The single-device arm is unchanged, as it must be: it never
reaches the new code.

**4. Validation.**  `tests/test-llama-context` (2 GPU `-sm tensor`, Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0): `cp_d`, `cp_d_s` (the
restored KV blob is compared byte for byte), `rt`, `ps`, `frag`, `rot`, `seq_rm`, `state_load`, `rollback`,
`replay`, `shared` **OK**.  `rf` FAILs on this build **and on the r153 build** — that case creates its own
context without flash attention, which `-sm tensor` requires; it passes on 1 GPU.  Coherence unchanged
(Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0 seed 42, 3 GPU, `1c5d32ac537d`).  `scripts/gate-state-pipe.sh` **PASS** (every host-path arm
byte-identical to `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`, pipelined -15.9 %, threaded copy -15.5 %);
`scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **0.000000 / 100.000 %**; `scripts/gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` **PASS**.
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball (tree `954548b20`).

**5. Why it stayed invisible.**  Nothing in the delivery's default paths uses this io class: the server's
prompt cache and the context checkpoints pass `LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_PARTIAL_ONLY`/`NONE` (the host path),
and only `tests/llama-context` asks for `ON_DEVICE`.  So the item was recorded as "harmless but the same
pattern", and the only thing that ever measured it was a harness written for this release.  The harness
(`archive/work/state-device-path/llama-stateio.cpp`) and the full table are in
`benchmarks/2026-10-27-state-device-path.md`; `TODO #110` is retired.

**6. Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` §4 `LLAMA_STATE_STAGE_MIB`, `patches/README.md` (block 12),
`archive/work/state-device-path/`.

## 261027.008 (tooling/baseline, post-r156) -- re-establish the baseline the IQ4_NL hc class moved: the DSV4 HC pre/post arms are reported, not hard, and the Flash-Next IQ4_NL prefill-logit point is re-recorded

**No release, no patch change.**  Nothing here touches `patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch`
or the r156 tag; this is the gate/baseline half of the r156 finding (261027.007 §6), decided by the maintainer
("we fixed a bug in IQ4_NL recently -- re-establish the baseline").

**1. What the numbers say.**  r156 measured the default fused `DSV4_HC_PRE` against its own F32 chain on
Flash-Next IQ4_NL at **mean KLD 0.027936 / 96.471 %** (a 10-chunk run); at the standard 40-chunk point it is
**0.021542 / 95.814 %**.  That is the **same order the HC combine+norm fusion has always shown** on that class
(0.0185-0.0213 / 95.6 %, 261025.014), and it is not a near-tie or a defect: the two DSV4 HC ops own the HC16
bf16 producer slots (`dsv4-hc.cu`: "a numerics change vs the F32 chain, approved as a prefill re-baseline"),
so `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_PRE=0` swaps the producer precision *as well as* the fusion.  `GGML_CUDA_MMB_HC16=0`
moves neither arm, so byte-identity was never the right criterion for that pair -- it is a numeric arm.
The r140/r141 (issue #226) fix is the one that moved this class: on a pre-#31028 / separate-tensor GGUF (which
IQ4_NL is) the fused combine+norm had been reading a *recycled* buffer as `inject`, which put that arm's PPL at
2690 against 2.45 through the chain; both arms are correct now, and the fused side is the intended behaviour.
The remaining fused-vs-chain gap is **not** from that fix -- it is inherent and pre-existing, measured at
0.021338 already on r135 (pre-r138), which is exactly why this is a re-baseline and not a regression.

**2. `scripts/gate-hc-fusions.sh`: `dsv4_pre_chain` joins `dsv4_post_op` as a REPORTED arm.**  The hard
oracle is unchanged and is the one §61 exists for -- the four `LLAMA_FUSED_HC_MIX` x `LLAMA_FUSED_HC_COMBINE`
combinations plus the CUDA-side chain fusions, byte-identical to the unfused chain.  The two DSV4 arms are
still printed with their sha and verdict, so a **change** in their divergence is visible; on the class where
they do agree (BF16-hc) they still print equal shas, so nothing was given up there.  Verified: IQ4_NL class
**PASS, 5/5 hard arms identical (444 chars `7ea23f309705`), 2 reported**; BF16-hc class (GSQ-IQ3_XXS) **PASS,
all 7 arms identical (449 chars `6a102dbc62d6`)**.

**3. Flash-Next IQ4_NL prefill-logit base re-recorded from the shipped default**, 40 chunks, f16 KV:
`base_ppl 2.7527`, `build=5bf09b93b`, `arm=<default>` -- so that class finally has a reference of its own (the
one r156 recorded was deleted: it held a *non-default* `--ab` arm and would have failed any later default run
for the wrong reason).  It is a reference, not a snapshot: the pre-r156 build (`08c471959`) reproduces it at
**0.000000 / 100.000 %**, and the shipped build against itself reads the same.  The standing check for this
class is therefore "0.000000 against the base", and the DSV4 pre/post arms are judged by their reported
KLD staying at ~0.02 / ~95.8 %.

**4. Docs.**  `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §61 (the claim, the two numbers, and *why* the pair is a numeric arm),
`MANIFESTS.md` gate 7 and `scripts/README.md` (the gate's hard/reported split), 261027.007 §6 (chunk count for
its figure and a pointer here).  The KLD bases on disk: `~/.cache/rdna-boosts/gates/`.

## 261027.007 (r156) -- issue #237: the FA prefill staging arena's size hint is a CEILING, not a target (block 10)

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r156` (block **10** amended).  `release.json`: tip **`5bf09b93b`**, tree
**`dc96d43cc294b95071a025776fbf5ccc917283ea`**; `validate-set.sh` green (fresh-tarball strict apply 15/15).
Reported by **@DanoPTT** (issue #237).

**1. What it fixes (a memory regression, not a kernel).**  Since r125 the MTP draft context's KV cache
follows the main `-ctk` (issue #216), so a `-ctk/-ctv q8_0` config *stages* its draft attention where an f16
draft cache never did.  #138's preallocation then committed the whole arena on the first prefill ubatch: the
hint is the F16 size of the K/V view **roots** (capped at 512 MiB per operand), while the first request of a
large-context prefill is a few MiB, so a `-c 262144` config allocated **1024 MiB per context** even though
the whole 5k-token prompt needs ~20 MiB.  On the reporter's 1x R9700 that is `-480 MiB` of draft KV for
`+1024 MiB` of arena, i.e. a q8_0-KV user ended up **+544 MiB** worse than the f16 default the change was
supposed to beat.  Reproduced here on 1 GPU (Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0, MTP n3, `-c 262144 -ctk/-ctv q8_0 -fa on -ub
512 -b 1024`, the 5246-token prose prompt, peak VRAM from `rocm-smi`): **12744 MiB** (default q8_0 draft) vs
**12200 MiB** (`-ctkd f16 -ctvd f16`) = **+544 MiB**, the reporter's number exactly, with
`FA_STAGE size=2.0 MiB cached=0.0` printed for both contexts (target + draft).

**2. The fix.**  `fattn_stage_try_get()` treats `size_hint` as a **ceiling on a growth step** rather than
the allocation target: a growth now aims for `min(hint, 4x the request that just arrived)` (never below the
16 MiB floor / 1.25x ladder), so a shallow prompt stays at 16-72 MiB and a deep one still reaches the hint in
<= 3 steps.  That keeps both #138 properties (a bounded number of freed-then-reallocated steps on
Windows/WDDM, where a freed allocation stays committed: the ladder's ~5x stranding becomes ~1/3 of the final
arena) and removes the 512x overshoot.  The slab path takes the same `want`, the G4 free-cap refusal and the
plain growth fallback are unchanged (an oversized hint still can never cost more than the pre-change path),
and `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_PREALLOC=0` still disables the hint entirely.  The `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_STATS`
diagnostic now prints `request=… cached=… alloc=…` **after** the allocation (the reported arena size was the
one thing the old line did not show).

**3. Measured (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, 1 GPU unless stated).**  Reproduction above, after the fix: **10840
MiB** (q8_0 draft) vs **11248 MiB** (f16 draft) = **-408 MiB**, i.e. the q8_0 draft KV now keeps most of its
480 MiB (the draft arena costs 72 MiB at this depth).  Arena allocations
(`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_STATS=1`, 2 contexts, 5246-token prompt, `-c 262144`): `request=2.0 MiB -> alloc=16.0 MiB`
then `request=18.0 -> alloc=72.0`, against 1024 MiB on the first ubatch before.  Deep prefix (`-c 131072`,
105k-token prompt): 16 -> 72 -> 296 -> **512 MiB** (the hint) in lockstep for both contexts -- the same peak
it reaches on its own today, just not from the first ubatch.  No prefill cost: the same 105k arm measures
**2960.6 t/s** against the pre-fix build's **2938.7** (+0.7 %, and the ladder measured 1108.94 vs 1108.03 on
r48), and 27B UD-Q4_K_XL `llama-bench` q8_0 KV **pp2048 1360.63 +/- 1.24 / pp16384 1248.93 +/- 0.78** vs
**1356.65 +/- 1.18 / 1247.87 +/- 0.57**.  `--fit`'s projection is deliberately unchanged (it reserves the
per-context *worst case*, `min(2*cap, F16 KV)`, which a full-context prefill really can reach).

**4. New: `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh --kv TYPE` (default `f16`).**  The gate pinned an f16 KV cache,
which **skips every quantized-cache prefill path** -- the F16 staging arena, `GGML_CUDA_FA_KV_NATIVE`'s tile
read -- so a change to either was invisible to it (this release's own change included).  `--kv q8_0` now runs
the same comparison with `-ctk/-ctv q8_0`, in its own base file (`…-kvq8_0.kld`) with the type pinned in the
meta, and its candidate log carries `FA_STAGE request=4.0 MiB alloc=16.0 MiB` (the arena is exercised).  Do
not fold it into the default: the f16 base is the recorded release reference, and a quantized cache is a
different point (its base PPL is 5.9317 vs 5.9325 at f16).  The block's five extra header lines also pushed
`--help` past `usage()`'s fixed `sed -n 2,101p` range, so it uses the repo's `2,/^set -uo pipefail/` idiom now.

**5. Gates (r156 tree).**  Coherence 4B Q8_0 3 GPU `-sm tensor` **`1c5d32ac537d`** and 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M 2 GPU
`-sm tensor -ncmoe 10` **`627b2ebd7792`** -- both == the r153/r155 build.  `gate-prefill-logits.sh`: f16
**0.000000 / 100.000 %** and the new `--kv q8_0` arm **0.000000 / 100.000 %**, both against bases recorded
from the pre-fix build (PPL 5.9325 / 5.9317).  MTP: Protocol A prose `-n 3000` `plain == draft-mtp`
byte-identical (**6168 chars, sha `c97d97802e63`**, 29.6 -> 69.9 t/s) and the four-axis adaptive arms **54.4 /
69.9 / 74.2 / 81.5 t/s** (the r155 record reads 54.4 / 70.0 / 74.1 / 81.4).  `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` PASS
(4/4, park == lazy-off), `gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` PASS, `gate-state-pipe.sh` PASS 5/5, `gate-spec-align.sh` PASS
(host-expert pair 115.9 -> 147.2 t/s, mixed chain inert, `n_seq == 1` text identical), `gate-hc-fusions.sh`
**PASS 7/7** on the BF16-hc class (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, 449 chars sha `6a102dbc62d6`); per-block build
`--fast --changed-from 0ba2387f6` **2/2** (block 10 and the tip); `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean; q8_0-KV
staging-arm text identical across `PREALLOC` on/off and `FA_STAGE_MAX_MB=1` (the native read) at `-c 32768`
and `-c 262144` (`63bb1363bbb9`).

**6. Already-known finding, re-measured (NOT changed here; now with the magnitude on record).**
`gate-hc-fusions.sh` on the **IQ4_NL hc class** (Flash-Next IQ4_NL, the `CHAIN` mixer class) fails its hard
`dsv4_pre_chain` arm: 444 chars `7ea23f309705` with `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_PRE=1` (the default) vs 453 chars
`f242246a382b` with the chain.  The r149 record already logged this as **pre-existing** (it fails identically
on an r148 build) and unrelated to the change under test; this release's tree reproduces both hashes and both
arm verdicts exactly, and the change here only alters an allocation's size.  **New here: the magnitude** --
measured at the logits with the gate's `--ab`, the default fused `DSV4_HC_PRE` reads **mean KLD 0.027936 /
same-top-p 96.471 %** against its own F32 chain at base PPL 1.7888 (a 10-chunk exploratory run over wikitext;
the standard 40-chunk cell reads **0.021542 / 95.814 %**).  `GGML_CUDA_MMB_HC16=0` does not move either arm,
so the "bf16 producer" re-baseline the kernel comments cite (`dsv4-hc.cu`: "a numerics change vs the F32
chain, approved as a prefill re-baseline") is not confirmed as the *only* route to it.  The gate's 7/7 PASS
is recorded for the class it is defined on (the BF16-hc one, as at r155); the IQ4_NL-class decision was taken
in 261027.008 below (re-baselined: reported arm + a re-recorded KLD base), and it is not a #237 item.

## 261027.006 (r155) -- PR #236: the server keeps the context checkpoint a task just restored instead of saving it again, and recycles the buffers of dropped checkpoints (block 12)

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r155` (block **12** amended).  `release.json`: tip **`0ba2387f6`** (the fork branch
tip, reproduced by `fork-refresh.sh`), tree **`5c941ec661ac1b8c0b4fd0636a495c38a9cbd981`**; `validate-set.sh`
green (fresh-tarball strict apply 15/15).  Contributed by **@overdoingism** (PR #236, one `git am` file touching
only `tools/server/server-context.cpp`).  Record: [`archive/work/server-ckpt-reuse/`](archive/work/server-ckpt-reuse/RESOLUTION.md).

**1. What it fixes (a server latency bug, not a kernel).**  On a hybrid/recurrent (or SWA) model the memory
cannot roll back, so the server saves **context checkpoints** and a prompt that resumes from a cached prefix
restores one.  It then saved the *identical* state again at the same position before its first batch (the log
line is `superseding context checkpoint`) and once more near the end of the prompt; each save allocates,
zero-fills and page-faults a fresh host buffer of the recurrent state's size (**150 MiB** on Qwen3.8-27B,
**174 MiB** with its DFlash2 draft, 50 MiB on the 4B).  A slot now remembers the `n_tokens` of the checkpoint
its task restored; when a checkpoint lands at that position nothing has been decoded since the restore, so the
checkpoint already holds the current state - it is moved to the back of the list (the ordering a re-save
produces) and **kept**, with the spec state the restore re-applied, instead of being written again.  The
buffers of erased, superseded and invalidated checkpoints are kept (4 in total, the largest kept) and an
exact-size one is taken by the next checkpoint, so a save is only the copy.  `LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_REUSE=0`
restores the eager behaviour; no arithmetic and no KV cell moves.

**2. Why the keep is valid, and why it is a hybrid fix.**  `common_prompt_checkpoint` carries the target's
`PARTIAL_ONLY` state (for a hybrid memory: the recurrent state, not the attention cells), the draft context's
state and the drafter's stashed spec state.  The restore sets exactly that payload and then `seq_rm()`s beyond
the checkpoint's extent, so a fresh save would write the same bytes back.  The guard can only match on a
**hybrid/recurrent** target: `llama_memory_hybrid::seq_pos_min()` is the max of the two caches' minima and the
recurrent cache's single cell carries the last position, so the sequence reports `pos_min == pos_max` and the
restore lands at the checkpoint's own `n_tokens`; for a dense/SWA memory `pos_next = pos_max = n_tokens - 1`, the
new checkpoint is one token short, and only the buffer recycling applies.  Upstream's restore arithmetic, not
this change, but it decides where the headline win exists.

**3. Delivery hardening on top of the PR** (both no-ops on every arm measured): `n_tokens_ckpt_restored` is
also cleared in `server_slot::reset()`, so the invariant does not rest on every task entering the
`SLOT_STATE_STARTED` branch (a TTS task already skips it); and the keep path refuses a checkpoint whose
`data_tgt` is empty, which `load_tgt()` treats as a no-op and which therefore can never stand in for the live
state.  Reported to the submitter rather than silently changed.  `data_spec` (eagle3-only, one `n_embd` row) is
not recycled - not worth a spare slot.

**4. Measured (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0; every arm's greedy text byte-identical between the two switch settings).**
Prompt time of the request that resumes from a checkpoint, ms off -> on: 4B 1 GPU **45.1 -> 31.4**, 40.0 ->
28.7, 46.4 -> 32.4; the same at 2 slots `--kv-unified` with idle-slot parking **43.4/42.2/44.6/42.2/43.9 ->
29.3/28.7/28.3/27.3/27.7**; 27B + DFlash2 2 GPU `-sm layer` **197.1 -> 163.2**, 186.9 -> 161.9, 144.1 -> 112.0,
187.6 -> 126.7 (and with 128-token generations 198.7 -> 162.3, 193.1 -> 147.2, 142.2 -> 110.7, 189.4 -> 128.3);
3 GPU `-sm tensor` **407.9 -> 373.6**, 291.2 -> 236.2, 182.4 -> 142.0, 251.7 -> 150.6.  The same logs read
`superseding` 3 times off against `keeping` 3 times on, and create **9** checkpoints off against **6** on.
**36 requests over 6 configurations are byte-identical**, including a `POST /slots/N?action=save|restore` round
trip (same saved file size, same restored text) which the PR lists as uncovered; `LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_REUSE=0` on
the r155 build reproduces the pre-r155 log transitions and text, and the r154 build reproduces the switch-off
text.  RSS +0.15 GiB (4B) / +0.45 GiB (27B) for the spares.  The win is page-fault bound, as the submitter says:
25-100 ms here (9950X3D, DDR5, THP) against their 195-223 ms (3900X, DDR4, 4 KiB pages).

**5. New gate: `scripts/gate-ckpt-reuse.sh`.**  A long prompt plus three resumptions on a hybrid model, two
arms, and it fails unless the greedy text is byte-identical, the keep arm kept a restored checkpoint and never
superseded one while the eager arm did the opposite, the keep arm created fewer checkpoints, and nothing aborts
or faults a GPU.  It **SKIPs** (rather than passing vacuously) when the config makes no usable checkpoint, or
when the keep path is unreachable (a dense/SWA target restores at `pos_max`).  **No other gate creates or
restores a context checkpoint**, and a wrong keep is a wrong answer on the *next* resume, not a crash - the same
argument that produced the parking gate and the state gate.

**6. Gates (r155 tree).**  Coherence 4B Q8_0 3 GPU **`1c5d32ac537d`** and 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 10`
**`627b2ebd7792`**, both == r154; `gate-ckpt-reuse.sh` PASS; `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` PASS (park == lazy-off
4/4); `gate-state-pipe.sh` PASS 5/5 (every restored cycle byte-identical to `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`);
`gate-spec-align.sh` PASS (2 GPU 109.4 -> 142.6 t/s, 3 GPU 87.6 -> 135.5, host experts 117.3 -> 149.1, splits
58 -> 0, mixed arm inert 100.5 -> 100.9); `gate-hc-fusions.sh` PASS 7/7 (BF16-hc class); `gate-prefill-logits.sh`
PASS **0.000000 / 100.000 %**; MTP Protocol A prose `-n 3000` `plain == draft-mtp` byte-identical (11066 chars
sha `33885f8c27bf`) and the four-axis adaptive arms 54.4 / 70.0 / 74.1 / 81.4 t/s plus mixed 56.0; a
`llama-server` four-axis acceptance check (27B, 1 GPU, `-c 32768 -fa on -ctk/-ctv bf16`, adaptive cap 3, greedy,
3000 tokens per axis, raw prompt files) **R 70.2 t/s accept 0.895 mean len 3.32 / P 80.4 / 0.990 / 3.58 /
C 73.0 / 0.934 / 3.54 / K 84.1 / 1.000 / 3.65**, i.e. healthy and in the protocol's expected order (the r154
record's acceptance numbers use a different invocation, so these are a health check, not a like-for-like
comparison; `llama-cli` does not print the speculator's statistics at all); per-block build
`--fast --changed-from 08c471959` **2/2**; `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  The r155 tree differs from r154
**only** in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` (1 file, 87 insertions), so every decode/prefill kernel and the
binary content of `libllama`/`libggml` are unchanged by construction.

## 261027.005 (r154) -- issue #234 follow-up: the verify-batch alignment stays inside the drafter whose caps it changes (r153's generic cut was a -6 % regression on the n-gram-first chain)

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r154` (block **02** amended).  What r153 shipped was correct for the case it was
measured on (`draft-mtp-adaptive`, +30..34 % at 2 GPUs, +54 % at 3, +28 % on host experts) and **wrong as a
default for the reporter's other case**.  This entry is that finding and the fix.

**1. The regression.**  r153's block 02 had two halves: `draft-mtp-adaptive` aligning its per-sequence caps UP,
and a generic "cut the finished drafts to the shortest" in `common_speculative_draft()` (the reporter's own
suggestion (a), with `draft_truncated()` feeding the cut back so acceptance counts only verified positions).
The gate only exercised `draft-mtp-adaptive`, where the align-up makes the cut a no-op, so nothing measured the
second half on its own case.  Measured afterwards on the reporter's chain (a) -- `--spec-type
ngram-mod,draft-dflash` with `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M`, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 2 GPU, `recall` + `prose`,
`-n 200`, `--spec-ngram-mod-n-max 15 --spec-ngram-mod-n-min 8`):

| arm | pair per-slot | pair agg | split steps |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN=0` (r152 behaviour) | 132.9 / 87.6 | **65.6** | 12 |
| `LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN=1` (r153, with the cut) | 122.3 / 76.2 | **61.7 (-6 %)** | 1 |

**The mechanism is the `min`.**  The two drafts are not comparable: one slot holds a long n-gram match, the
other a DFlash block, and the cut fires on every step whose n-gram match is shorter than the block, truncating
the OTHER drafter's good draft.  The `RSPREP` trace shows it: r153's verify groups collapse to 6 rows (both
slots at ~2 drafted tokens) against 6-and-16 rows in r152, the prose slot's acceptance falls 74 % -> 50 %
(231 -> 284 draft tokens for *fewer* accepts), and the removed pass costs far less than the lost proposals.

**2. The fix.**  The cut and `common_speculative_impl::draft_truncated()` are gone.  The cap alignment stays,
inside `draft-mtp-adaptive` (the one drafter whose per-sequence caps create the mismatch), and now bounds the
aligned width by the smallest **hard** cap in the call as well as by the band, so a slot nearing the end of its
response cannot split the pair either; it sets every drafting sequence's cap to that width, which is the only
case where a width shrinks and is transient by construction.  A chain of different drafters is now untouched:
measured inert, **64.6 vs 64.4 t/s** with identical draft counts.

**3. `scripts/gate-spec-align.sh` grows a mixed-drafter arm** (`ngram-mod,draft-dflash` + the DFlash2 draft,
`MIXED_ARM`/`DRAFT_MIXED`/`PROMPT_B_MIXED`, on by default) which requires that chain to stay within 2 % of its
knob-off self **with identical draft counts**, and is judged only by that: those steps keep their second ubatch,
which is the correct behaviour there, so the recovery and no-split checks do not apply to it.

**4. Gates (r154 tree, final run).**  2 GPU **106.2 -> 137.9 t/s (+30 %)**, 3 GPU **86.1 -> 133.2 (+55 %)**,
35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` **116.2 -> 148.9 (+28 %)**; the split decode steps 58 -> 0 at all three; the equal-length
arm +0.5 / -1.3 / +1.2 %; the **mixed-drafter arm inert (-0.2 %, splits 24 -> 24, identical draft counts)**;
every single-slot request and the `n_seq == 1` `llama-cli` text (`b8775233a93a`) byte-identical on/off; no abort,
`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean; the fixed `draft-mtp n3` checkpoint measures 144.4 so the aligned adaptive arm is
within 2 %.  `validate-set.sh` strict 15/15, per-block build 3/3 (blocks 02, 09, tip), coherence
`1c5d32ac537d` / `627b2ebd7792` == r153, prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %**.

**5. Recorded rule.**  A length mismatch is worth equalizing when a **cap** caused it (the band, a response
ending); when the **content** caused it the two drafts are not comparable and the second ubatch is the cheaper
arm (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63).  `TODO.md` #111 now holds only the residual: a slot that drafted *nothing* still
splits, because truncating its neighbour's good draft to nothing is the worse trade.

## 261027.004 (r153) -- issue #234: the sequences that verify in one step are aligned into one ubatch (blocks 02 + 09); +30..34 % at 2 GPUs, +54 % at 3, and the fix is device-count independent by construction

**Superseded in part by r154** (``261027.005``): the generic cut described in §2 below measured -6 % on the
n-gram-first chain and was removed; everything else here stands.

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r153` (blocks **02** and **09** amended).  `release.json`: tip **`1e992529d`**
(the fork branch tip, reproduced by `fork-refresh.sh`), tree **`672f788c9b`**, `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(fresh-tarball strict apply 15/15).  Reported by **@overdoingism** (issue #234, with a measurement, an analysis
and a patch cut on two drafters of their own); archived in
[`archive/work/spec-align-234/`](archive/work/spec-align-234/) with a `RESOLUTION.md` and an evidence log.

**1. What it fixes.**  `llama_memory_hybrid::init_batch()` splits a decode batch with
`llama_batch_allocr::split_equal()`, which takes **one token per sequence set per round and stops when the
shortest set runs out**.  A step in which two slots verify different draft lengths therefore becomes **two
ubatches** -- the shorter slot's rows in the first, the longer slot's tail in a second -- and the target model
runs a full extra pass.  A fixed `--spec-draft-n-max` never exposed it (every slot drafts `n_max`, so the
lengths match for free); the delivery exposes it because `draft-mtp-adaptive` (block 02) holds a
**per-sequence** depth, so two concurrently verifying slots routinely sit a step apart.  Reproduced on the
r152 tree, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 2 GPU `-sm tensor --parallel 2 --kv-unified -c 32768 -fa on`, greedy, `n_predict
400`: the concurrent recall+reasoning pair aggregated **108.1 t/s** against **145.6** for the same two prompts
at one fixed depth (**+35 %**), 86.9 vs 132.2 at 3 GPUs (**+52 %**).  The split is visible in the recurrent
memory's own trace: one decode step prints `RSPREP prep=1/2 n_tokens=4` (slot 0, depth 3) and
`prep=2/2 n_tokens=5` (slot 1, depth 4).

**2. The change** (`LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN`, default **on**, `0` disables; `common/speculative.cpp` only, 2 files of
delivery content across two blocks).  Block 02: `draft-mtp-adaptive` raises every drafting sequence's cap to
the deepest cap in the same `draft()` call (only ever up; each sequence keeps `--spec-draft-n-max`, the MTP
layer cap and the caller's per-slot `n_draft_max`), and `common_speculative_draft()` cuts the drafts to the
shortest one when the lengths still differ -- which covers a different speculator on each slot (an n-gram hit
has no cap at all) and a slot whose own `n_max` is smaller -- telling the implementation that its draft was cut
(`draft_truncated()`) so acceptance statistics count only verified positions.  Block 09: the aligned depth is
bounded by `band / n_drafting - 1` rows per sequence, because the expert cache's band applies to the **whole**
batch (two slots at depth 7 already fill the RDNA4 band, so a two-slot verify aligns to 7 each, not 15 each);
the bound may only widen a shallow draft, never shorten a deep one, which is what keeps a single-sequence run
bit-identical.  Both blocks are needed because `llama_model_moe_cache_band()` is block 09's API and a block may
not use a later block's symbol (`gate-per-block-build.sh`).

**3. Declined, with the reason (so they are not re-proposed).**  **Padding the shorter sequence** to equal
length advances the recurrent state in `mem_recr->prepare()`, so it corrupts the sequence it was meant to help
-- dead for this model class.  **Cutting the adaptive depth down** to the shallowest slot is the wrong
direction: adaptive depth is worth **+13 %** over a fixed depth at equal lengths (184.2 vs 163.0 on the same
pair).  `cparams.n_rs_batch` is untouched (an align-up cannot exceed the per-slot cap, which is bounded by that
same `n_max`).  The reporter's `0015-6055-spec-align-v1` does not apply -- it sits on drafters this tree does
not have -- so this is a port of the idea, plus two pieces their patch lacks (the per-implementation cut
feedback and the band bound).

**4. Measured** (`scripts/gate-spec-align.sh`, the new gate; pair aggregate of a concurrent recall + reasoning
pair, and the split decode steps from the `RSPREP` trace):

| arm | knob off | knob on | | split steps |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| 27B, 2 GPU (x8 pair) | 104.8-108.3 | **140.1-140.6** | **+30..34 %** | 58 -> 0 |
| 27B, 3 GPU | 86.5-87.0 | **133.1-133.7** | **+54 %** | 58 -> 0 |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40`, 2 GPU | 116.2 | **149.0** | **+28 %** | 59 -> 1 |

Per slot: 2 GPU 72-74/57-60 -> 112/76 t/s, 3 GPU 55/45 -> 110/72.  **The penalty scales with the devices the
duplicated pass spans, which is why the gate runs 2 and 3 GPUs**; the fix itself is device-count independent
(it edits batch composition in `common/`, before any split mode or kernel is involved, so `-sm layer` benefits
identically).  The one remaining host-expert split is a slot that drafted **nothing** that round (its sampled
row alone): cutting its neighbour's good draft to nothing would be the worse trade, so that step still splits.
The equal-length arm (two identical prompts) is unchanged (-0.4 / -1.4 / -2.1 % / +0.2 %); that arm's spread
between two identical runs is ~12 %, so the gate bounds it at 10 %.  The final gate run also measures a
`--spec-type draft-mtp -n 3` arm (equal lengths by construction, a different drafter config) as the checkpoint
the fix has to reach: pair **141.3 (aligned adaptive) vs 143.9 (fixed n3)**, i.e. within 2 %, while the aligned
adaptive arm keeps its advantage where acceptance is high (two identical prompts: 171-185 vs 161.2).

**5. Purity: the oracle is the single-sequence arm, not a two-slot text diff.**  Any fix here changes some
slot's verify width, and a verify-width change moves greedy text on its own.  Measured, in this order: (a)
**`n_seq == 1` is byte-identical** on/off (`llama-cli`, `b8775233a93a`), and so is every single-slot server
request at both device counts and on the host-expert arm; (b) cross-process text is **stable** with
`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` (two runs of one arm agreed character for character in every slot and phase); (c) the
pair's low-acceptance slot diverges at a near-tie (char 220 of 1202 at 2 GPUs, 627 of 1234 at 3), and the
**control** that attributes it to the width rather than to this change is a fixed `draft-mtp` pair at depth 5
against depth 4 -- both slots equal length in both arms, no alignment in play -- which flips the same slot at
the same kind of point (char 259, "Ada not on Monday" vs "but Ada not on Monday").  Recorded as
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63; the gate reports the divergence point and does not gate on it.

**6. Gates.**  Four-axis MTP (adaptive n3 = pinned at the floor, 1 GPU, `-n 3000`, reasoning pinned per axis,
plus the phase-switching prompt): acceptance **R 0.5425 / P 0.8091 / C 0.8722 / K 0.9920 / mixed 0.6348**;
the prose `draft-mtp n3` Protocol A arm is **bit-identical to the r152 build** (1449/1791 draft tokens, mean
accepted length 3.43, 68.7 vs 68.9 t/s), which is the inertness check for a single sequence.  Coherence 4B
Q8_0 3 GPU **`1c5d32ac537d`** and 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 10` **`627b2ebd7792`**, both == r152.  Prefill-logit
KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %**.  `gate-state-pipe.sh` **5/5** (restored text byte-identical to
`LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0` in every cycle; 3.38 ms of the pipelined copy preserved).  `gate-park-idle-slots.sh`
**PASS** (park == lazy-off on all four requests, parkoff still differs).  `gate-hc-fusions.sh` **7/7**
(449 chars `6a102dbc62d6`).  `gate-per-block-build.sh --fast --changed-from b9418b679` **3/3** (blocks 02, 09,
tip).  `validate-set.sh` strict **15/15**, Windows portability clean.

**7. Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3 (`LLAMA_SPEC_ALIGN`, with the multi-slot band note added to the verify-width
rule), `patches/README.md` (block 02 contents/knobs + the alignment paragraph, block 09's band-bound fact),
`MANIFESTS.md` (release gate 9 + the two per-block rows), `AGENTS.md` (critical fact), `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §63,
`scripts/README.md`, `TODO.md` #111 (the two corners outside the fix: a slot that drafted nothing, and the
`ngram-mod,draft-mtp` chain's cut, which has no A/B yet).

## 261027.003 (r152) -- PR #235: the state copy is streamed on two threads (block 12); -5.5 to -13 % of the server's save+load, and the streaming-store premise is a per-box property

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r152` (**block 12** amended; the only delivery content change is
`src/llama-context.cpp`, +154 / -13).  Blocks 00-11 and 13/14 differ from r151 only in their re-cut
`From`/`index`/`@@` header lines (verified per patch with those lines filtered: every one of them is byte-identical
outside block 12, so no later block's content moved).
`release.json`: tip **`b9418b679`** (the fork branch tip, reproduced by a second `apply-all.sh` re-cut), tree
**`e9993a26e`**, `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (fresh-tarball strict apply 15/15).  PR #235
(`@overdoingism`) is archived in [`archive/work/state-copy-stream/`](archive/work/state-copy-stream/) with a
`RESOLUTION.md`.

**1. What it does.**  The r151 pipeline moves a checkpoint's host side one piece (tensor range) at a time with
a plain `memcpy`.  Each piece is now copied with non-temporal (SSE2) stores over 64-byte-aligned runs, split
over `LLAMA_STATE_COPY_THREADS` (default **2**; `1` = one thread but still streamed, `0` = the pre-r152 plain
`memcpy`, the A/B arm) threads *inside one pipe group* - a worker must not cross a group boundary, because a
group's stage range may only be read after its event (a worker in the next group would read a range whose
device copy is still in flight: a torn state, not a crash).  The restore's pack takes the same copy, and
resolves each piece's stage offset once instead of re-deriving it in the queue loop (same addresses; the
`off = off_g` reset r151 kept is gone).  States below 16 MiB keep the plain copy, pieces below 64 KiB keep the
`memcpy`, the streaming store is x86-only (`__SSE2__`/`_M_X64`, MSVC x64 included) so other targets gain only
the threads, and every streamed run ends with `_mm_sfence()` before its bytes reach the caller or the device.
`LLAMA_STATE_TIMING=1` is the new per-op diagnostic (enqueue / copy+wait / GiB/s, and the restore's
pack+enqueue).

**2. Reviewed before folding** (detail in the resolution record).  The PR is cut on r150 and **does not apply
on r151** (its hunk covers the copy-out loop r151 rewrote), so this is a re-cut, not a cherry-pick.  Its
whole-state `total < 16 MiB` threshold is the wrong shape once the copy is per group, so the decision moved to
the piece (64 KiB).  Two real corrections to the submitted code: it aligned the destination to the *store*
width (16 B), which leaves two half-lines carrying partial write-combining buffers (now 64 B), and it fenced
inside the worker lambda only, so any later caller of `llama_copy_stream` would have handed a DMA stale bytes
(the fence is in the run copier, so a run is self-fencing and the thread join is the only other ordering).
Two nits went to the submitter: the save's copy-out and the restore's pack should be reported separately (they
are different paths with different destinations), and the thread count is not the 5 % afterthought their
table makes it look like (below).

**3. The mechanism had to be re-derived, and it flips the PR's emphasis.**  Measured on this box (9950X3D,
**192 MiB of L3**, DDR5) on a 164 MiB copy in a 35B-A3B checkpoint's real piece sizes (30 x 80 KiB, 30 x
2.6 MiB, 20 x 4.2 MiB): plain `memcpy` 1 thread **6.45 ms**, streaming stores 1 thread **6.47 ms**, plain 2
threads 5.17 ms, streaming 2 threads **3.56 ms**, streaming 3/4/8 threads 4.45/4.27/3.98 ms.  So the streaming
store alone is **0 % here** (the destination's lines are mostly resident in L3, so the read-for-ownership a
plain store pays hits cache) while on the submitter's 3900X + DDR4 (64 MiB of L3) it is the *whole* win
(19.4 -> 11.8 ms, one thread) - and the threads are worth ~2x on both.  Both halves ship because each is worth
most on a different box and neither costs anything on the other; the invariant recorded in `AGENTS.md` is that
neither half may be "simplified" away on the strength of one box's measurement.

**4. Measured** (`scripts/gate-state-pipe.sh`, which now carries a **`copy0`** arm gated byte-for-byte like
every other arm; prompt-cache restore of a 5246-token hybrid state, 3 cycles per arm):

| config | `copy0` (plain) | default (2 threads) | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 1 GPU `-ncmoe 10` | 38.43 ms | **33.37 ms** | **-13.2 %** |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10` | 44.15 ms | **40.49 ms** | **-8.3 %** |
| Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS + shared Q8_0 MTP head, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40` | 79.30 ms | **74.92 ms** | **-5.5 %** |

(the server's own `prompt cache update took` trace; `copy0` lands on r151's recorded 39.9 / 78.4 ms, which is
what attributes the delta to this change).  The copy itself, per size class, is -12 / -21 / -29 % for a
62.8 / 73.2 / 165.3 MiB save, -26 / -30 % for the restore's pack, and -21 / -22 / -29 % for a 112.6 / 126.6 /
250.9 MiB Flash-Next save.  The restored request's `prompt_ms` medians (INFO only; the arm-to-arm spread on
this board is 1-3 ms): 65.6 (`pipe`) vs 67.5 (`copy0`) on 1 GPU, 71.5 vs 74.1 on 2 GPU, 119.0 vs 124.2 on
Flash-Next.

**5. Gates.**  5/5 arms (pipe, copy0, pipe1, read1, sync) on all three arms above: every restored cycle
byte-identical to `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`, save side isolated by `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ=0` and restore side by
`pipe` vs `read1`, every cycle really restored (`prompt_n` 10 of 5256), no abort, `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean
on all five logs of every arm.  `test-llama-context` (15 state cases) on 1 GPU and 2 GPU tensor: PASS/FAIL set
identical between the r151 build and this one (`rf` + `rollback`, this box's slab/VRAM property).  Coherence
4B Q8_0 3 GPU `1c5d32ac537d` and 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 10` `627b2ebd7792` == the r151 build measured in the
same session (`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, `extract-generated.py`); prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %**;
`gate-park-idle-slots.sh` PASS; `gate-hc-fusions.sh` PASS (7/7 arms, BF16-hc class); per-block build
`--fast --changed-from dc6a78d5c` 2/2.

**Confirmed on the released tree** (`b9418b679`, `fork-refresh.sh --build --gates --push`): the 1 GPU
`gate-state-pipe.sh` arm reads `copy0` **39.91 ms** -> default **35.09 ms** (-12.1 %) and the restored
request's `prompt_ms` 67.97 -> 64.65 ms, with all five arms byte-identical; coherence and the prefill-logit
gate (KLD 0.000000 / 100.000 %) ran on that build as part of the fork refresh.  The fork's `rdna-boosts`
branch is `b9418b679`, i.e. the tip `release.json` records.

**6. Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `LLAMA_STATE_COPY_THREADS` and `LLAMA_STATE_TIMING`; `patches/README.md`
block 12 gains the copy bullet and its knob list; `MANIFESTS.md` gains the r152 block-12

## 261027.002 (r151) -- PR #233: the batched state copy is pipelined (block 12); -2.9 % on a 1 GPU restore, -3.6 % on Flash-Next + MTP, and a new state-path gate

**Shipped:** `v15-6050b467c-r151` (**block 12** amended; the only delivery content change is
`src/llama-context.{cpp,h}`, +135 / -16.  Blocks 00-11 and 13/14 change only in their re-cut `From`/`index`
lines and the hunk line numbers of `src/llama-context.{cpp,h}`, which block 12 owns -- no later-block code
changes; verified per patch: 0 non-metadata lines differ for blocks 00-11, and 14 changes hunk offsets only).
`release.json`: tip **`dc6a78d5c`** (the fork branch tip; the re-cut is deterministic, so a fresh
`apply-all.sh` at `6050b467c` prints the same id), tree **`e13514007`**, `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(fresh-tarball strict apply 15/15).  PR #233 (briansp2020) is archived in
[`archive/work/state-pipe/`](archive/work/state-pipe/) with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

**1. What it does.**  r96 (#189) batched the deferred state-save reads through one pinned `state_stage`;
r119 (#209) did the same for the restore's writes.  Both then ran the host memcpy and the device copies back
to back, so a checkpoint that is ~5.3 ms of memcpy plus ~6.4 ms of DMA paid them serially.  The pieces are
now cut into up to `LLAMA_STATE_PIPE_GROUPS` (default **8**, `1` = the old copy) size-balanced groups: a
restore packs a group and queues its async sets before packing the next, and a save records one event per
**(backend, group)** after that group's copies are queued and copies the group out when its event completes.
A backend without events (the CPU backend) falls back to the single `llama_state_sync_all` path.  The fold
keeps the submitter's code as-is and adds the invariant comment (disjoint stage ranges per group; one event
per group because a re-recorded event moves past the earlier one).

**2. Reviewed before folding** (detail in the resolution record): stage ranges do not overlap; the per-group
events are created before any copy is queued and fully cover the removed `llama_state_sync_all`; every
backend that exposes `event_new` also fills `event_record`, so the assert is unreachable; HIP's async
getters/setters and `event_record` share the main stream, so the event really covers the copies (a copy
stream would have been the r62 race); teardown frees the cached events after both directions have
synchronized.  Two submission nits were noted to the submitter: the format-patch carries an **empty
`wip/state-pipe/README.md`** (so `git am` of it creates a stray empty file; the fold applies the two source
files only), and `n_state_pipe_events` is a `llama_context` member although only the file-local splitter
reads it.

**3. Measured** (`scripts/gate-state-pipe.sh`, written for this release: it drives the server's in-memory
prompt cache, the only path that reaches this code.  Prompt-cache restore of a 5246-token hybrid state,
`prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` + 3 new tokens, medians of 5 cycles, `prompt_ms` of the restored request):

| config | `PIPE_GROUPS=1` | default 8 | Δ | server save+load trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S + shared Q8_0 MTP head, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40` | 134.5 | **129.7 ms** | **-3.6 %** | 81.7 -> 78.4 ms |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 1 GPU `-ncmoe 10` | 69.4 | **67.4 ms** | **-2.9 %** | 44.9 -> 39.9 ms |
| 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10` | 74.4 | 74.1 ms | within noise | - |
| Flash-Next arm with `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0` (pre-r96/r119) | 168.5 ms | | | 115.5 ms |

The 1 GPU arm lands **below** the pre-r119 synchronous path (71.3 -> 67.4 ms), so the single-device staging
cost r119 accepted as a limitation is gone.  The submitter's per-config numbers (G1 72.6 -> 66.8, G1L
79.6 -> 77.4, G2 37.7 -> 32.4, G3 41.2 -> 38.3 on r148) are their box and checkpoint sizes: the direction and
the ~5 ms Flash-Next magnitude reproduce here, their 2 GPU 35B-A3B gain is inside that arm's noise on this
box.  **Both PRs' "a few ms per turn" framing understates the relative win on the 1 GPU arm and overstates
the 2 GPU 35B-A3B one** -- quote the table, not the PR text.

**4. Gates.**  `gate-state-pipe.sh` on the 1 GPU and the Flash-Next + MTP 2 GPU arms: every restored cycle of
every arm byte-identical to `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`; the save side isolated by `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ=0`
(`read1` == `sync`) and the restore side by `pipe` == `read1`; every cycle really restored (`prompt_n` 10 of
5256); no abort; `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean on all four logs.  `test-llama-context` (all 15 state cases) on
35B-A3B 1 GPU and 2 GPU tensor: PASS/FAIL set **identical to the stock r150 build** in every arm (the
failures are this box's slab/VRAM OOMs -- `rollback` on 1 GPU, `rf` + `rollback` on 2 GPU -- and r150 shows
the same).  Coherence 4B Q8_0 3 GPU `b065f37593b3` and 35B-A3B 2 GPU `6229d4e6ce30` == r150; prefill-logit
KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %**; per-block build 2/2 (`--fast --changed-from f0060e159`: block 12, 10 s; tip,
9 s).

**5. New gate.**  `scripts/gate-state-pipe.sh`: four arms (`PIPE_GROUPS=8`, `=1`, `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ=0`,
`LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`), HARD on cycle-by-cycle text identity against the synchronous arm plus the
one-direction arms, on the run having actually restored (`prompt_n <= 32`), and on no abort / no GPU fault;
INFO on the restored-request median and the server's `prompt cache update took` trace.  It is the **only**
gate that reaches this code -- `llama-cli`/`llama-bench` never save a state, and the file-based slot
save/restore goes through `llama_io_write_file`/`read_file`, which never touch `state_stage`.  Recorded in
`MANIFESTS.md` (gate 8, and the renumbered graph-replay census to 9), `scripts/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

**Confirmed on the released tree** (the numbers above were measured on the pre-fold arm build, whose
`llama-context.{cpp,h}` code is identical; the fold added comments and re-cut the commit ids): 1 GPU
`gate-state-pipe.sh` on the release build (`dc6a78d5c`, `--fast` per-block tip build) reads
`PIPE_GROUPS=1` **70.2 ms** -> default **66.9 ms** (-4.6 %), save+load trace 45.7 -> 39.4 ms, with every
identity check green, so the shipped tree is the gated one.  The 1-2 ms run-to-run spread on this arm is
why the record quotes the direction and the range, not a single delta.

**Post-release tooling fix.**  `scripts/gate-state-pipe.sh --help` printed only the first 58 lines of its
header (fixed to `sed -n '2,/^set -uo/p'`), so `SUFFIX`, `EXTRA_ARGS` and `KEEPOUT` were missing from it.
No patch, no tag change.

**6. Docs and finding.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `LLAMA_STATE_PIPE_GROUPS`; `patches/README.md` block 12 gains
the pipelining bullet and the knob; `AGENTS.md`'s state invariant carries the disjoint-range and

file-based `--slot-save-path` save/restore still does one pageable `temp_buffer` + `llama_backend_tensor_get`
