## 261027.001 (tooling, post-r150) -- one definition for `.tip`, and a deterministic re-cut

**No release, no patch change.**  `release.json` still names `v15-6050b467c-r150` (tip `f0060e159`, tree
`dda152c10`); this is a delivery-repo tooling and documentation change only, so no new tag and no patch
regeneration.

### The problem it removes

Every release re-derived `release.json.tip` by hand, and the three SHAs in play are easy to confuse: the
working chain tip in `~/llama.cpp` (the commits a release is developed on), the re-cut tip that the
personal fork's `rdna-boosts` branch actually carries, and whatever the last edit left in `release.json`.
The chain and the re-cut have the **same tree** but different commit ids, because `git am` stamped the
*wall-clock* committer time (r150's chain tip was `3a08b6d3d`, its re-cut was `f0060e159`).

### Shipped

* **`scripts/apply-all.sh` makes the re-cut deterministic**: the committer identity is pinned to the
  patch series' author (`From:` of the first patch) and every commit's committer date is stamped from its
  own author date (`git am --committer-date-is-author-date`).  Verified: two re-cuts in one checkout, a
  second clone, and a run with `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`/`_EMAIL` overridden all produce tip **`649f03593`**
  (tree `dda152c10`, 15 commits).  The script now prints `Applied tip: <sha> (this is the value for
  release.json .tip / the fork branch tip)` instead of leaving the caller to work it out.
  **r150 and earlier predate this**, so their recorded tip is the re-cut of the day and the current
  `apply-all.sh` reproduces their tree but not that id; from the next release the two agree by construction.
* **`scripts/fork-refresh.sh`** (new) is the fork refresh from the Pushing policy as one command: clean
  check, leave the branch, delete `rdna-boosts`, re-cut, assert the tree and the commit count, print the
  tip, and optionally `--build`, `--gates` (coherence + prefill-logit, plus the MTP Protocol A command it
  cannot parameterise) and `--push` (force-with-lease, with the remote url checked against an allow-list
  so upstream is not reachable from it).  Tested end to end on a throwaway clone.
* **`scripts/validate-set.sh` prints the applied tip** and says why it cannot compare it: it builds the
  base from the commit tarball, so its commit ids differ from upstream's by construction (a commit id
  includes its parent).  The tree remains the contract there; `fork-refresh.sh` does the tip comparison
  against a real checkout.
* **Docs**: a `.tip` rule in `AGENTS.md` (what it means, the three traps, "compare trees, never SHAs"),
  the Pushing-policy checklist points at `fork-refresh.sh`, `MANIFESTS.md` records the tip print and the
  reason validate-set cannot check it, `scripts/make-release.sh`'s help states that `--tip` is the fork
  branch tip, and `scripts/README.md` indexes the new script.
* **Also cleaned up along the way**: nothing in the patch set or in `ENVIRONMENT.md` changed.

### Validation of the tooling change

`validate-set.sh` green (tree `dda152c10`); `apply-all.sh` determinism as above; `fork-refresh.sh` dry run
on a throwaway clone (tree match, tip printed, mismatch note for r150's old-style tip); `bash -n` on every
touched script.

## 261026.008 (r150) -- issue #232: the Meta backend's simple-tensor container grows instead of aborting

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r150` (base `6050b467c`, tip `f0060e159` = the fork's re-cut branch, tree
`dda152c109c2baf800271da3f9990cd9871db486`; the validated working chain tip was `3a08b6d3d`, same tree,
15 blocks, blocks 09 and 12 amended).  Delta against the r149 tree: **4 files, +154/-10** --
`ggml/src/ggml-backend-meta.cpp` + `ggml/include/ggml-backend.h` + `ggml/src/ggml.c` (block 09) and
`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp` (`park_move`, block 12).  No kernel, no numerics, no default and no
allocation-size change on the normal path.

### What was reported

`MrDrMcCoy`, 8x R9700 / 4 GPUs per server, Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Q2_0 with a DFlash2 draft, `-c 524288 -np 2
--kv-unified -ctk/-ctv bf16 --rope-scale 2`, `--fit on`, `-sm tensor`, `-sm layer`-free: after a ~258k-token
prompt the server died in `llama-server` with

```
ggml.c:1840: GGML_ASSERT(obj_new) failed
ggml_new_object: not enough space in the context's memory pool (needed 2261360, available 2260992)
```

`needed` is bigger than `available` (`mem_size`) by **exactly one `ggml_tensor` object** (368 B), so a
`ggml_context` that holds only tensor metadata was *exactly full* and one more tensor was requested.

### Diagnosis: it is the meta backend's compute container of the attention KV buffer (and `park_move` fills it)

`2260992 = 128 * 48 * 368`: the `compute_headroom * n_tensors * size(ggml_tensor)` context that
`ggml_backend_meta_buffer_type_alloc_buffer_n` builds for a buffer with 48 static tensors, at 128 views each.
A Flash-Next KV cache has exactly 48 (`12 layers * (K, V, k_stream, v_stream)`), confirmed on this box
(`GGML_META_CTX_DEBUG` in a scratch build: `n_tensors = 48, compute ctx = 2260992 B (6144 views/simple)`).

That container holds the per-device *simple tensors* of everything a "generation" registers between two graph
rebuilds: a graph's own views **plus** the views an out-of-graph operation creates.  `llama_io_read_device`
(state restore: one view per KV cache chunk per layer), `llama_kv_cache::park_move` (one per move chunk) and
every graph shape contribute.  The container was a single fixed-size context per simple device, so it had a
**cliff**: 6144 views for the attention KV buffer, then `ggml_new_object` returned NULL and the CPU-side
`GGML_ASSERT` aborted the process (the pool `WARN` is not fatal in a `NDEBUG` build).  Measured on this box
with the server: a 34,970-token context-checkpoint restore registers **432** views of the KV buffer
(18 cell ranges x 24).

**The reported trigger is KV parking, not a restore** (`MrDrMcCoy`'s follow-up, reproduced here):
`llama_kv_cache::park_move` copies a run in chunks no larger than the *gap* to its destination and
creates 2 views per (layer, K/V) per chunk, so a nearly-full unified cache (two ~258k-token prompts in
524288 cells) parks in dozens of tiny chunks — and parking runs between graphs, so nothing reclaimed
them.  Reproduced at the **default** budget with 2 slots, `-c 32768` and two ~16.3k-token prompts
(park gap ~100 cells): r149 aborts with `needed 2261360, available 2260992` inside
`llama_kv_cache::seq_park` -> `park_move`.  So the fix has two halves: stop accumulating those views,
and remove the cliff for everything else (state restores included — a 258k restore is ~3.1k views, and
two of them plus the graph's 216 also exceed 6144).

### Shipped

* `ggml_backend_meta_simple_tensor_container` keeps a **list of contexts per simple backend**
  (`ctx_for_new_tensor()`) and grows when the last one is full; a rebuild resets and **releases** every context
  in the list, so one large generation does not pin its peak.  `ctx_first()` is used where the allocator needs
  the context that holds the buffer's own tensors.  Allocation failure is a clear `GGML_ABORT` instead of a NULL
  deref.
* `GGML_META_COMPUTE_HEADROOM` (default 128) overrides the *first*-context size.  Diagnostic/testing only: a
  smaller value makes the container grow sooner and never changes an output.  A growth is logged at DEBUG,
  which is how the path was verified.
* `ggml_new_object`'s overflow warning now also logs `ctx`, `mem_size`, `n_objects` and the bytes used, so a
  report of this class is diagnosable from the log (the reporter's log could only say "needed/available").
* **Views created between graph evals go to a caller-owned scratch container**
  (`ggml_backend_meta_set_scratch_views()` / `ggml_backend_meta_reset_scratch_views()`, the reporter's patch):
  `park_move` enables it, resets it after each chunk's copies (which are synchronous — a meta buffer has no
  `.cpy_tensor`, so `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` stages through the host) and disables it, so parking no longer
  touches the per-generation container at all.  Static tensors still resolve to the static container, and the
  scratch container grows like every other one.
* Hardened in the same file while reading it: `get_node_aux()` asserts against its `nodes_aux` pool (its
  ALL_GATHER sibling already did), so an over-budget graph reports instead of writing past the pool
  (TODO #111, closed; unreachable on every recorded config).

### Validation (3x R9700 gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS)

* **The reported crash, before vs after (default budget):** 2 slots, `-c 32768`, two ~16.3k-token prompts —
  r149 aborts in `seq_park`/`park_move` with `needed 2261360, available 2260992`; the growth half alone completes
  with the attention-KV container grown 6144 -> 12288 (the indexer's 3072 -> 6144); growth + scratch completes
  with **zero** growth events.  Identical output text on all three.
* **The cliff in general:** `GGML_META_COMPUTE_HEADROOM=1` aborts the r149 build at `sched_reserve`
  (`needed 27232, available 26864`, the same `GGML_ASSERT(obj_new)`) and runs to completion on this build
  (105 growth events, `llama-cli`), with **byte-identical greedy text** in both arms and against the r149 build
  at the default headroom.
* **No numeric change:** `llama-perplexity` (wikitext-2, `-c 2048 -ub 512`, 4 chunks, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 0`)
  `PPL = 2.0901 +/- 0.05592` on both builds; same-seed greedy text identical on the 4k-context and
  server flows (e.g. the two ~240k-token prompts of the 524288-cell 2-slot flow, parking + checkpoint
  restores included).
* **Parking semantics:** `gate-park-idle-slots.sh` **PASS** — 6 park / 2 unpark moves traced, park ==
  `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0` byte for byte on all four requests, and the `parkoff` arm still differs
  (the workload still reproduces #210).
* **Set:** `validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball (15 blocks, tree `dda152c10`);
  `gate-per-block-build.sh --fast --changed-from 947fdf295` **3/3** (blocks 09, 12, tip).
* **Fork refresh (the re-cut branch, `f0060e159`, tree `dda152c10`)**: `apply-all.sh` strict `git am`,
  build green; coherence gate byte-identical to the known-good text (`ade44780`); Protocol A (`-n 3000`,
  prose prompt) on 27B UD-Q4_K_XL 1 GPU **plain 29.64 t/s / draft-mtp 58.38 t/s, acceptance 0.61660
  (1946/3156)**; `gate-prefill-logits.sh` KLD 0.000000 / 100.000 %.

### Not done (recorded, not scoped in)

The restore path still creates one view per KV cache *chunk* per layer (`llama_io_read_device` per `rinfo`),
and `park_move` one per move chunk.  Both are now harmless (the container grows), but coalescing them
(one view per tensor, chunks staged through scratch) would keep a generation's footprint at tens instead of
thousands; it is a llama-context change with its own copy-path risk, so it is left alone.  The `nodes_aux` bounds check that was
missing is added (above).

## 261026.007 (r149) -- the graph-cache key names the layer, so decode graphs replay (TODO #107 closed; PR #230 assessed and re-cut)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r149` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `947fdf295`, tree
`423a59a605a9c0532d62f1c66345dc28687fcf81`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r148 tree: **3 files, +114/-6**,
all in **block 09** -- `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh` (the key), `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu` (the
three key helpers) and `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu` (graph invalidation on a table's device
frees).  No kernel, no numerics, no default and no allocation changes.

### The defect: the key collided across every layer of a split graph

`ggml_cuda_graph_key` was `(first node data, n_tokens)`.  Under a split mode every layer's subgraph can
begin on the **same** activation buffer (the subgraphs are structurally identical and their inputs do not
overlap in lifetime), so one cache entry served all of them and each layer was compared against the
*previous layer's* properties: a source `data` pointer that had "moved" by one layer's worth of weights.
The graph was then run directly, or recaptured, on nearly every call -- which is the r144 finding
(`direct=56171 replay=3152 properties_changed=55321` over 200 tokens).  **The r144 note's stated cause order
was wrong in an instructive way**: it read the first differing byte of a collision as "the Meta rebuild
moves `src[]` object addresses" (`src[]` precedes `data` in `ggml_tensor`, so a collision always shows
there first), and the "genuine source `data` move" that appeared after canonicalising `src`/`name` was the
neighbouring layer's weights -- the same collision again.  This is `briansp2020`'s **PR #230** finding, and
it is correct.

### Shipped

1. **The key carries the weight identity** (`GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_KEY_WEIGHT`, on; `0` restores the old key).
   `first_weight_ptr` is the data of the first device-resident weight the subgraph reads (falling back to
   `nodes[0]->src[0]` when the experts are host-resident), and `shape_sig` is a cheap FNV mix of the node
   count, the first node's geometry and first source, the last node's data, and the first/last node names
   (a layer's `ffn_moe_gate-5`).  The key only *selects* an entry: a replay still requires
   `ggml_cuda_graph_update_required` to find every node unchanged, so a collision costs a recapture and
   never a mismatched replay.
2. **Freeing any of a table's device buffers invalidates the captured graphs on that device.**  The MoE
   kernels receive the arena slot table, the remap staging, the prefill routing staging and the two heat
   mirrors as **raw launch parameters**, so nothing in the property compare sees them.
   `ggml_cuda_graph_mem_freed()` is now bumped in `free_arena_backing` and `free_heat_dev_locked` (the
   helpers that return the memory) and once in `free_table_buffers_locked`, `stand_down_table_locked` and
   `moe_cache_update_host`'s device move, plus `moe_cache_release_arena`'s legacy `cudaFree` arm.  Before
   this the hole was masked: on this shape the decode graph never replayed.

**Not shipped from the PR:** its second half, an identity-free property compare that blanks
`src[]`/`view_src`/`buffer` before the memcmp.  Measured with the key fix held constant it is worth
**+0.2-0.3 %** (42.6 vs 42.8 and 112.8 vs 113.1 t/s; `properties_changed` 340/2054 vs 28/1588) and on a
3-device dense split it only moves the capture count (1161 -> 915) without changing the result, so it is
not worth weakening the replay's only safety check.  Its `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_PROPS_STRICT` knob also parsed as
presence (`=0` enabled it).  Both points are in the PR reply and in
[`archive/work/graph-replay-keys/README.md`](archive/work/graph-replay-keys/README.md).

### Numbers (2x R9700 x8; `benchmarks/2026-10-26-graph-replay-keys.md`)

| arm | r148 | r149 | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flash-Next IQ4_NL 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48`, plain, n2000 (3 pairs) | 37.7 / 37.7 / 37.6 | 42.5 / 42.9 / 42.8 | **+13.5 %** |
| Flash-Next 3 GPU `-ncmoe 48`, plain, n1000 | 37.6 | 42.1 | **+12.0 %** |
| Flash-Next 2 GPU `-ncmoe 48` + MTP n3, n2000 | 111.5 | 113.1 | +1.4 % |
| Flash-Next 3 GPU `-ncmoe 48` + MTP n3, n1000 | 107.1 | 109.2 | +2.0 % |
| 27B Q8_0 1 GPU Protocol A plain / draft-mtp | 29.6 / 70.2 | 29.7 / 70.0 | flat (acceptance identical) |
| 27B Q8_0 3 GPU tensor + MTP n3 | 42.8 | 42.9 | flat (acceptance 0.82386 both) |
| 35B-A3B 1 GPU `tg128` / Protocol A plain / draft-mtp | 101.8 / 82.0 / 174.5 | 101.7 / 81.2 / 174.1 | flat (acceptance 0.75118 both) |
| 27B Q8_0 3 GPU tensor plain `tg128` (and at d16384) | 42.0 (42.1) | 38.4 (38.3) | **-8.6 %** -- `TODO #109` |

The census on the flagship arm: `direct=549499 replay=31696 capture=149 properties_changed=452439` ->
`direct=3882 replay=574826 capture=2636 properties_changed=28`; `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` measures 37.3
t/s on both builds, so the whole delta is the replay, and both kill switches restore stock exactly
(census and t/s).  The 1-GPU arm also replays now (`properties_changed` 78215 -> 146 on 35B-A3B) but is
GPU-bound, so it is flat -- worth recording, because it means the churn was never multi-device-specific.

### The regression that is not this patch's to fix (`TODO #109`)

Now that replay works, a **3-device tensor-split dense** plain decode is slower (`-8.6 %`, above).  It is
not capture churn (one-shot per key, and the deficit survives `-n 512`), not the chunk size, not the async
input ring, not the scheduler's events; `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=internal` removes it (42.2) and `=nccl` is
worse still (35.6), while neither `GGML_CUDA_AR_SMALL_BYTES` arm moves it -- so it is the hybrid NCCL comm
layer (merely initialised) or the node-level stream overlap a captured graph cannot express.  A
`draft-mtp` draft hides it (flat at 3 devices), 3-device **MoE** is the +12 % win, and 1/2-device dense and
`-sm layer` are flat, so it is the dense plain-decode corner.  Shipped default-on with the number recorded
rather than gated away: the kill switch is `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_KEY_WEIGHT=0`.

--changed-from 29b9d1197` **3/3** (09, 12, tip); prefill-logit KLD **0.000000 / 100.000 %**; same-seed
greedy text **byte-identical in 10/10 config pairs** (27B 1 GPU, 2 GPU `-sm layer -ts 59,41`, 3 GPU
tensor; 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 40`; Flash-Next IQ4_NL 2 GPU `-ncmoe 48` + MTP; Gemma4 E4B with and without
its MTP draft) with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`; Protocol A (`-n 3000`, prose) on 27B Q4_K_XL 1 GPU and
35B-A3B 1 GPU, MTP >= plain with identical acceptance; `test-backend-ops` 9/9 oracles; the parking gate
PASS; `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  `gate-hc-fusions.sh` on Flash-Next IQ4_NL: the five hard HC arms are
identical and the `dsv4_pre_chain` arm fails **identically on the r148 stock build**, i.e. pre-existing and
untouched by this change.

assessment, the corrected diagnosis and the gates) and

## 261026.006 (r148) -- issue #228: the qwen4exp HC inject logit is the chain's 1/hc-scaled scatter logit, so the fused mixer and the fused combine agree with the model again

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r148` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `df41660ce`, tree
`80bc2009db455cc206d07126f2a4d4e8c2532697`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r147 tree: **4 files, +53/-35**
-- `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/hc-mix.cu` (the inject stores and the two combine kernels), `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp`
(the CPU references of both ops), `ggml/include/ggml.h` (the op contract) and `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`
(the oracle's own note) -- all in **block 11**.  No graph, launch count, allocation or default changes: the
same kernels run the same work with one multiply moved from the combine into the mixer.

### What issue #228 reports

`martino2k6`, Strix Halo (gfx1151, 128 GB UMA, **single device, default config**), the
`drluoto/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AgenticRequant-Q5K` GGUF (qwen4exp, PLE streamed, ctx 131072, `-fa on`, f16 KV,
true-specless): since the `v15-6050b467c` base the model **deterministically degenerates** -- greedy
repetition collapse and a logit-fingerprint drift of kl ~15 against a v14-r120 capture -- while every v14
re-cut (through r126) is clean at kl 0.0.  Their matrix localised it to a llama-level knob: on r142,
`LLAMA_FUSED_HC_MIX=0 LLAMA_FUSED_HC_COMBINE=0` restores a correct generation (kl 1.195, top1 0.986), the
CUDA-side HC fusions (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1`) change nothing, `-fa off` and the PLE load mode
(`-lzm off`) are irrelevant, and r143 was bit-identical to r142.

**Reproduced exactly on our gfx1151 box** with the model class (Flash-Next Q5_K_M trunk, 86 GiB, hc
weights Q5_K/F32/F32/Q8_0), greedy, `-c 8192 -fa on -ngl 99`:

```
default               -> "The user is asking for a short paragraph about the Eiffel Tower. The user is
                         asking for a short paragraph about the Eiffel Tower"  (a repetition loop)
LLAMA_FUSED_HC_COMBINE=0 -> a correct paragraph ("The Eiffel Tower is a famous iron lattice tower ...")
```

### Root cause: the fused op pair kept the v14 inject convention after the re-base inverted it

qwen4exp's residual stream is steered by a per-stream **scatter logit**.  `build_hc_mix` computes it and
`build_hc_combine` turns it into `w = 2*sigmoid(.)`.  Each half exists twice -- a ggml chain (upstream's
model definition) and a fused op -- and `cparams.fused_hc_mix` / `cparams.fused_hc_combine` select them
**independently** (`LLAMA_FUSED_HC_MIX` / `LLAMA_FUSED_HC_COMBINE`), so there are four arms.

* v14 (base `097cf33d9`) emitted the logit **raw** and put the `1/hc` in the combine:
  `*inject = build_lora_mm(w_inject, xn)` / `w = sigmoid(scale(inject, 1/hc))`.  The delivery's fused pair
  was written against exactly that: `GGML_OP_HC_MIX` published a raw tail and `GGML_OP_HC_COMBINE` divided
  it by `hc`.
* the `6050b467c` re-base **inverted** the convention (same final numerics, different intermediate): the
  mixer now emits `scale(mm, 1/hc)` and the combine applies `sigmoid(inject)` alone.

So the fused pair became *chain-inconsistent while staying self-consistent*.  The Q8_0/BF16-hc models take
both fused halves and never noticed -- that is the arm every dense/GSQ validation ran, which is why ten
releases passed.  The other two arms:

| mix | combine | before r148 | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| chain | chain | correct (the model's own definition) | unchanged, bit for bit |
| chain (stride: Q5_K, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, Q4_K ...) | **fused** | **`/hc` twice** -- `w` collapses toward 1 instead of sweeping `(0, 2)`; greedy repetition collapse | correct |
| **fused** (Q8_0/BF16 hc) | chain | **no scale at all** -- the BF16-hc model produced an **empty generation** with the documented kill-switch | correct |
| fused | fused | correct (self-consistent, right by accident of the pairing) | **bit-identical** |

That is issue #228 end to end: the reporter's Q5_K model is the chain-mixer class with the combine left
fused, and their rescue arm was the reference chain.  It also means **Flash-Next IQ4_NL -- the model most of
this repo's qwen4exp measurements used -- was in the broken class**, so its recorded greedy texts and any
quality judgement made on it are for a model whose HC scatter weights were wrong (throughput numbers are
unaffected: same kernels, same work).  Verified degenerate on r147 and correct after the fix, e.g.
"The user asked is a simple request. The prompt is is not encoded." -> a correct Eiffel Tower paragraph.

### Why no gate saw it

`test-backend-ops -o HC_MIX,HC_COMBINE` compares each op against a **CPU reference that encoded the same
convention**, so the set agreed with itself (the r128 oracle added for the combine does catch a wrong
`2*sigmoid` centre, an index swap or an in-place read -- not a chain-inconsistent convention).  Greedy
coherence stays plausible while the two halves match each other, and no gate ever *crossed* the arms: each
A/B compared one arm with itself.

### Shipped (block 11)

1. **The inject tail is the scaled scatter logit, in every HC_MIX path**: `hc_mix_collapse_inject` (F32
   inject), `hc_mix_down_dots` (Q8_0 inject) and `hc_mix_bf16_down_inject` (BF16) now store
   `dot * (1/hc)` -- one multiply, folded into a store that was already there.
2. **The combine does not divide**: `hc_combine_kernel` (the dispatched `GGML_OP_HC_COMBINE`) and
   `hc_mix_combine_rms_gamma` (the fused combine+mix kernel the BF16 path uses) read the logit as-is, as
   does the CPU reference `ggml_compute_forward_hc_combine_f32`; the CPU `ggml_compute_forward_hc_mix_f32`
   reference scales its inject tail the same way.  `hyperconn.cu`'s unused parameterised
   `ggml_cuda_op_hc_combine(args)` was already generic and is left alone.
3. `ggml.h` states the contract (`inject` is the chain's scatter logit; the op divides by nothing) and the
   test's comment says what the op/CPU pair can and cannot prove.
4. **New gate `scripts/gate-hc-fusions.sh`**: the four mix/combine arms (plus `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_FUSION`,
   `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_PRE=0` and the reported `DSV4_HC_POST` arm) must be **byte-identical to the unfused
   chain** on a real GGUF; `--types MODEL.gguf` prints the model's hc-down class so it is run once per
   class (Q8_0/BF16 -> fused mixer, anything else -> chain).  Wired into `MANIFESTS.md` (release gate 7 +
   the block-11 row), `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/README.md` and tier 2 (`scripts/validate-gpu.sh` step 4b, plus
   `HC_COMBINE`/`HC_COMBINE_MIX` in its op-oracle list).  Rule: `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §61; switch catalogue:
   `ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.4 (the pair is now documented as two independent arms that must agree).

### Validation (gfx1151 / halo, ROCm 10.1.0; the gfx1201 box is not this session's host)

**Also found, recorded not fixed (a gate-integrity finding, no code change):** the three CUDA-side

those matchers look for.  Measured on GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (fused-mixer class): all three produce the default

for that arm, and this is also why the reporter's `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1` probe could not have moved.

arm; `ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.4 and `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §61 rule 3 now say so.

worker builds them from the tag).

re-capture against r148: the expectation is a residual inside their own engine-to-engine floor (kl ~0.002),
and if anything above that survives we want the fingerprint, because then it is a separate finding and not
this one.

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r147` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `38507e070`, tree
`8485179335b2e0e5fa1e03f8cca1940560ec147d`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r146 tree: **1 file, +7/-3** --
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu`, all in **block 12**.  On Linux the change is a no-op
(`pool_close_file` *is* `close`), so no kernel, allocation, numerics or heap behaviour moves; the whole
point is that the file compiles with HIP on Windows again.

### What issue #231 reports

`overdoingism`, HIP on Windows, stock r144 tree: one translation unit fails, `moe-expert-cache.cu` (host
pass), at two places --

```
moe-expert-cache.cu:1395:9: error: use of undeclared identifier 'close'; did you mean 'fclose'?
moe-expert-cache.cu:4360:13: error: use of undeclared identifier 'close'; did you mean 'fclose'?
```

both added by **r143** (`pool_free_locked` and the table teardown in `moe_cache_forget_all`).  The file
includes `<unistd.h>` only under `#if !defined(_WIN32)`; every other host-pool file call in it goes
through the four portability helpers of issue #130 (`pool_open_file`, `pool_fd_align`, `pool_pread`,
`pool_aligned_alloc`), whose Windows variants do nothing -- the bounded pool never opens a file there, so
`p.fd` / `t.src_fd` stay -1 and a miss is served from the pinned master.  The two remaining direct
`close()` calls in the file are inside `#if !defined(_WIN32)` blocks and were always fine.  r131 and
earlier do not have these calls: the teardown feature brought the break, not the portability contract.

### Shipped (block 12)

A fifth helper beside the other four, exactly as the report proposed: `pool_close_file(fd)` -- empty
under `_WIN32`, `close(fd)` elsewhere -- and the two call sites route through it.  The comment above the
helper group now says "five".  Why the empty Windows arm is correct and not a stub: `pool_open_file`
returns -1 there, `pool_free_locked` and the table drop both test `fd >= 0` first, so the helper is
unreachable on Windows by construction; it exists so the *call* is compiled, which is the only thing the
Windows build needs.

### Shipped (delivery tooling, not part of `patches/`) -- the class is now linted in tier 1

A one-off fix would leave the defect class alive, and no gate on this box can reach it: there is no
Windows runner, and a Linux clang with the wrong branch is silent.  `scripts/check-windows-portability.sh`
now reports, per file, a call to an unambiguous POSIX-only identifier (`open`, `close`, `pread`,
`pwrite`, `fsync`, `fdatasync`, `unlink`, `fstat`, `access`, `opendir`/`readdir`, `posix_memalign`,
`posix_fadvise`, `fallocate`, `ftruncate`, `mkstemp`, `readlink`, `sysconf`, `getpid`, `dlopen`, `mmap`,
`munmap`, `usleep`, ...) that is **compiled on Windows**: it walks the preprocessor stack and evaluates
every condition with `_WIN32`/`_MSC_VER` pinned, three-valued for unknown macros, with the platform
macros (`__linux__`, `__unix__`, `__APPLE__`, `__HAIKU__`, ...) false, and it learns a local predicate
such as `LLAMA_LAZY_READER_POSIX` from the `#define` that is provably reached on Windows.  Comments and
string literals are stripped, and a qualified or longer name (`obj.close()`, `Klass::close()`,
`pool_close_file()`) is not a match, so the lint is reviewable rather than clever.  Scope is deliberately
the files the delivery **adds** (`git diff --diff-filter=A base..HEAD`): several upstream files it edits
have module-local names that collide with POSIX ones (hexagon's `mmap(bool)`, vulkan's member `close()`, zDNN's unguarded `sysconf` on a backend Windows never builds), so `--modified-too` exists but is a
read-the-output sweep, not a CI gate.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` runs it on the freshly applied tree
(with `--diff-from HEAD~n_blocks`), i.e. `.github/workflows/validate.yml` tier 1, ~1 s, no compiler.

**Negative control (that is the evidence, since there is no Windows compiler here):** pointed at the
r146 tree the lint reports exactly `moe-expert-cache.cu:1395 close(p.fd)` and `:4360 close(t.src_fd)` --
the two lines in the report, at the reported line numbers -- and at r147 it reports none across the 282
files the set adds.  It also has to *not* fire on the delivery's own guarded code, and it does not:
`llama-lazy-reader.cpp`'s `close`/`pread` sit under `#if LLAMA_LAZY_READER_POSIX`, which the header
defines as `0` under `#if defined(_WIN32)`.

### Validation (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0)

The change cannot move a number on Linux, so the gates are about proving it really is inert:

* **Same-seed greedy text, old vs new build** (both built in the canonical `build-rocm` at the same source
  path, one `.cu` apart): dense Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0, 3 GPU `-sm tensor`, `-c 4096`, `--seed 42 --temp 0` --
  **identical**; 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40 --host-experts pool`, 64 tokens --
  **identical** (only the t/s line differs).  That second arm is the one that matters: the pool opened
  its GGUF, prewarmed 120 tables and both teardown paths ran (`moe_cache_forget_all: dropped 120
  expert-cache table(s) (9331.0 MiB of arena)` on device 0 and device 1), so `pool_free_locked`'s
  `pool_close_file(p.fd)` and the drop's `pool_close_file(t.src_fd)` are genuinely executed, exit 0, no
  abort, no GPU fault.
* `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` against the recorded r145 base (27B Q8_0, 40 chunks): **0.000000 mean
  KLD / 100.000 % same-top-p** -- expected to the digit, and recorded because it is the release gate.
* `scripts/gate-park-idle-slots.sh` (the release gate that is the only end-to-end exercise of
  `llama_memory_seq_park`): **PASS**, 6 parks + 2 unparks traced on both caches, park == lazy-off 4/4,
  and the un-parked arm still differing on 2 of 4 (the workload still reproduces #210).
* `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --fast --changed-from 105ac9d9a`: **2/2** (block 12 + the tip; blocks
  00-11 and 13 carry byte-identical deltas, so the patch-id selection skipped them).
* `scripts/validate-set.sh`: strict 15/15 on a fresh tarball, tree equal, and the new portability scan
  green on the applied tree.

Not run, by design: MTP Protocol A (no decode/fusion change), `test-backend-ops` (no kernel change) and
the container rebuild (the worker does that from the tag; nothing in an image changes behaviourally).

### Note for the next Windows report

This lint is textual.  It cannot see a missing `#include`, an MSVC type difference, or the
`std::min<int64_t>` mangled-name clash of issue #217 -- those still need a build log.  What it does mean
is that "a POSIX call was added outside the `_WIN32` guard" can no longer reach a release.

## 261026.003 (r146) -- issue #227: parking moves a mirroring indexer cache with the attention cache (qwen4exp/glm5-next)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r146` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `105ac9d9a`, tree
`13722383a3a2988214f3faa9ab0d347ce546af9d`, 15 blocks).  The chain was cut on `5ba04fa7c` and re-applied
from the regenerated patch set at release time (the fork-branch refresh); the re-apply has its own SHAs and
the same tree, which is the identity `release.json` records.  Delta against the r145 tree: **4 files,
+98/-2** -- `llama-memory-hybrid-idx.{h,cpp}` (the park decision and the invalidation of what is derived
from the cells), `llama-memory.cpp` (the dispatch) and `llama-ext.h` (the contract), all in **block 12**.
No kernel, no allocation and no numerics change: the code is reached only through the server's idle-slot
parking, and `llama-cli`/`llama-bench`/`llama-perplexity` never call it.

### What issue #227 reports, and what reproduces here

Brian (`@briansp2020`, 2x R9700, r143 then r145, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS with an MTP draft,
default 4 slots + unified KV, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 0 -ot per_layer_token_embd.*=CPU -lm none -lzm off`):
one ~9.9k-token request completes, a short second request lands on another slot, and the server aborts

```
qwen4exp.cpp: GGML_ASSERT(mctx_idx->get_n_kv() == inp->mctx->get_attn()->get_n_kv()
                         && "the indexer cache must track the attention cache cell for cell")
```

The same on `-sm layer -ts 59,41`, and it disappears with `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0`.  Reproduced
exactly (3 GPU, GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, the same flags minus their two-GPU `-ts`), 10.6k prompt:

```
srv  park_idle_sl: idle slot parking: on
W seq_park: seq 0 [0, 10651) -> [30309, 40960)          <- the attention cache moved up
src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:979: GGML_ASSERT(... ) failed    <- the indexer cache did not
```

**Cause.**  r136's parking (PR #225) collects the caches to move in `llama_memory_attn_caches()`, which
matched `llama_memory_hybrid_idx` through its `llama_memory_hybrid` base and returned **only**
`get_mem_attn()`.  qwen4exp's and glm5-next's memory carries a **second** cache, the QSA indexer, that is
a cell-for-cell mirror of the attention cache: a batch adopts the attention cache's slot layout
(`heads_idx = heads_attn`), cell `j` is one token in both, `get_n_kv()` drives both views, and
`qwen4exp.cpp` asserts the two agree.  Parking the attention half alone moved a sequence to the top of
one cache and left the other at the bottom, so the *next* graph build saw two different `n_kv` values.
(The half-park is also why `-sm layer` was hit: the guard is arch-independent, it is the memory type that
matters.)  `llama_kv_cache_dsa` / `_iswa` (deepseek4, glm-dsa) derive from `llama_memory_i` directly and
were therefore never in the list — they report "parking not supported" and keep #210, unchanged.

### Shipped (block 12)

1. `llama_memory_hybrid_idx::can_park()`: both caches must be parkable (one stream, unshared cells, V not
   transposed, no sliding window), not just the attention one.
2. `llama_memory_hybrid_idx::seq_park(seq, park)`: moves the attention cache and then the indexer (a
   no-op when the model has no indexer, e.g. a GGUF without indexer tensors), and undoes the first if the
   second refuses.  Before moving it verifies the mirror (`attn_idx_in_step()`: the whole stream's
   `seq_pos_get()` sets, because `park_compact()` also moves the sequences parked *beside* this one) and
   **refuses with a warning** when they disagree — the server then takes its existing save-and-clear
   fallback, so a desynchronised cache can never be parked into worse shape.
3. A successful move stales the pool layout for every sequence (`mem_idx_stale_set(-1, 0)`) and drops the
   derived indexer pool's watermarks (`pool_invalidate_all()`).  Both are required, not defensive: the
   layout caches each sequence's `(position, cell)` pairs, and the derived rows are indexed by the **block
   ordinal of the cells in the decode window**, which a park changes (a parked sequence's blocks leave the
   window), so a stale derived row would be read under another block's ordinal — silently wrong, and
   invisible to the assert.  The raw key/pooled rows move with their cells, so nothing else is stale.
4. `llama_memory_can_park()` / `llama_memory_seq_park()` dispatch to the memory first; every other type
   keeps the existing path.  `llama-ext.h` documents the new half of the contract.

### Validation (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS + MTP, 4 slots, unified KV)

New gate `scripts/gate-park-idle-slots.sh` (below).  It fails on the r145 build with the reported assert
and passes on this one.  Its 4-request sequence covers the whole lifecycle: A (10.6k, slot 0) parked when
B (slot 1) launches, C back on slot 0 (**unpark** A, park B), D on slot 2 with two slots parked:

| arm | `-sm tensor` 3 GPU, all-VRAM | `-sm layer` 3 GPU |
|---|---|---|
| park (default) vs `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0` | **4/4 byte-identical** | **4/4 byte-identical** |
| `LLAMA_SERVER_PARK_IDLE_SLOTS=0` (#210) vs lazy-off | 2/4 differ | - |
| moves traced (`LLAMA_KV_PARK_DEBUG=1`) | 6 park + 2 unpark, both caches, identical ranges | 6 park + 2 unpark |
| `GGML_ASSERT` / refusal / GPU fault | none | none |

That is also the #225 promise restored for qwen4exp: a request that runs alone matches the
saved-and-cleared output, and the no-parking arm still shows the placement dependence the gate exists to
detect.  Also run: `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **0.000000 KLD / 100.000 %** against the r145 base
(build 24bfbd46c, 27B Q8_0, 40 chunks); `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --fast --changed-from
3226075a6` **2/2** (block 12 + the tip; the first attempt put the hybrid-idx edit in block 11 and the gate
caught it: block 11 does not build on its own, because the park API it calls lands in block 12); the tip's
`all` build and the prefill-logit/perplexity binaries on the canonical `build-rocm`;
`scripts/validate-set.sh` strict 15/15 on a fresh tarball.

### Not run / accepted

* **glm5-next** (the same memory, k-pool indexer variant): no GGUF on this fleet — `TODO` #108, accepted
  limitation.  The code path is shared and the k-pool layout is invalidated with everything else.
* **2-GPU arms** (at the time of this entry): the GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS tree is 71 GB and the box has 91 GB of
  RAM, so `-ncmoe 48`+2 GPU OOM-kills (85 GB of pinned host experts); the split-mode coverage was 3-GPU
  `tensor`/`layer` instead, which is where the assert fires.  **Since measured on 2 GPUs with
  `-ncmoe 44`, in both split modes, with an r145 negative control - see 261026.004.**
* The reporter's own build and their 21.6k-token production sequence were not reproduced (our 10.6k arm
  is the same code path); no Windows run.

## 261026.002 (r145) -- issue #229: the float4 rms_norm reduction becomes opt-in, the pre-#29720 strided reduction is the default again

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r145` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `24bfbd46c`, tree
`0bb571d4390cadcaebcefcda6370211d0328c2d5`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r144 tree: **3 files, +58/-16**
-- `common.cuh` (the selector + its rationale), `norm.cu` (the dispatch consults it) and `hyperconn.cu`
(`hc_combine_norm_f32` mirrors whichever grouping the chain takes).  No kernel is rewritten, nothing is
disabled and no allocation changes: the release picks which of two *existing* reductions
`rms_norm_f32` runs, and it picks the one the delivery is calibrated on.

### What issue #229 reports, and what reproduces here

Upstream [ggml-org/llama.cpp#29720](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29720) (adopted by the r127
re-base) replaced `rms_norm_f32`'s strided scalar reduction with a **float4** one: a lane owns the four
contiguous columns `4*i .. 4*i+3` of `i = tid + k*block_size`.  The reporter (1x R9700, Windows, ROCm
10.0, graphs off, Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q5_K_XL, `draft-mtp n3`) bisected **-7..-9 % tg** to that commit, with
the whole loss in draft acceptance and `GGML_CUDA_RMS_NORM_VEC=0` restoring r126 bit-for-bit.

Reproduced in kind on gfx1201/ROCm 10.1.0 (Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU, greedy, `draft-mtp n3`, one
`/completion` request per arm, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, every arm bit-reproducible):

| arm | float4 | strided |
|---|---|---|
| default fusions, 5.2k ctx, n=512 | 0.90097 (373/414) / 76.68 t/s | 0.88756 (371/418) / 75.41 t/s |
| default fusions, **94k ctx**, n=512 | 0.75855 (355/468) / 58.94 t/s | 0.75159 (354/471) / 58.51 t/s |
| **SSM decode fusions off** (the reporter's carry), 5.2k, n=512 | 0.77273 (357/462) / 68.01 t/s | 0.88756 (371/418) / 74.55 t/s |

and prefill/decode (`llama-bench`, `-r 3`): the float4 grouping is worth **+1.9/+2.7/+1.9 %** at pp512/2048/8192
(1397/1403/1341 vs 1371/1366/1316) and **~0 %** at tg128 (30.89 vs 30.87) on the 27B, +0.9-1.1 % on 3-GPU
tensor, +1.1-1.4 % on 35B-A3B.  Full tables: `benchmarks/2026-10-26-rms-norm-float4-ab.md`.

**Diagnosis.** A reduction-order change is a *numerics* change: the RMS sum's partial sums group
differently, every layer moves by ~1 ulp, and greedy draft acceptance is a discrete function of the
logits, so it moves by a **payload-dependent** amount (positive on our default arm, -18 % on the same
model with the SSM fusions disabled, -7..-9 % on the reporter's box).  It is **not** a defect and not a
draft/verify inconsistency: `--spec-type none` and `--spec-type draft-mtp` are byte-identical in every
arm above, PPL agrees to 4 dp, and the prefill-logit gate sees only a 0.0007 KLD shift.  There is
therefore no "fix that keeps float4 and repairs MTP": the grouping *is* the cause.  The choice is which
numerics is the delivery's reference.

### What else the re-base broke, and what this release restores

The re-base made three kernels that the delivery documents as **bit-identical to `rms_norm_f32`** merely
*approximate*, because they keep the strided reduction the chain no longer took: the rms_norm->Q8_1 fold
(`rms_norm_q8_1_f32`), the GDN q/k norm pair (`rms_norm_scale_pair_f32`) and `rms_norm_mul_rope_f32`.
The instrument is `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh --ab "<fusion env>" --ub 1` (decode shapes):

| fusion arm | r144 default (float4) | r145 default (strided) |
|---|---|---|
| `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_NORM_Q8_1=1` | 0.000511 / 99.216 % | **-0.000000 / 100.000 %** |
| `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_NORM_PAIR=1` | 0.000529 / 98.889 % | **-0.000000 / 100.000 %** |
| `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_RMS_NORM_MUL_ROPE=1` | 0.000441 / 99.085 % | **-0.000000 / 100.000 %** |

and end to end: under the strided reduction the whole-arm A/B is *exact* (the SSM-fusions-off arm at
n=512 is byte-identical to the default arm, same 371/418 acceptance, same text `63a2391b2208`), under
float4 it changes everything.  r141 had aligned `hc_combine_norm_f32` to the vec4 grouping for the same
reason; it now follows the selector (`vec4` only under `GGML_CUDA_RMS_NORM_VEC=1`, which is what the
r140/r141 measurement was), and the qwen4exp `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1` A/B is byte-identical again
(Flash-Next IQ4_NL, 2 GPU tensor `-ncmoe 40`).

### Shipped (block 08 + block 11)

1. `ggml_cuda_rms_norm_vec()` in `common.cuh` -- the single selector, default **off** (strided).
   `rms_norm_f32`'s dispatch consults it; so does `hc_combine_norm_f32` (as a launch argument).
2. `GGML_CUDA_RMS_NORM_VEC=1` opts into upstream's float4 grouping for a prefill-only workload or an
   A/B.  It is a **numerics selector** (`ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.5): with it on, the fused norm kernels are
   approximate (0.0005 KLD) and no MTP/acceptance number is comparable to a recorded one.
3. Rule `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §60: one reduction, the strided one by default; a new fused norm kernel owes
   the `--ub 1` KLD probe against its own disable switch; `=1` is an A/B arm, not a shipping mode; and an
   MTP acceptance report is diagnosed on the target's numerics first (if `plain == draft-mtp` holds, the
   band is consistent and the difference is the grouping).

### Validation

`scripts/validate-set.sh` strict 15/15 on a fresh tarball (tree `0bb571d4...`); per-block build gate
`--fast --changed-from 438cbb3c7` **4/4** (blocks 08, 09, 11, 14 - the trees the rebase touched; 9 s for
the unchanged block 14); coherence: a reference build of the **previous tip** rebuilt in the same build
dir gives text byte-identical to this build with `GGML_CUDA_RMS_NORM_VEC=1` (4B Q8_0 3-GPU tensor
`1c5d32ac537d`, 27B `d55055a5ec80`), and the new default reproduces the strided arm recorded during the
investigation (27B plain `ab94eb7db4d4`, MTP acceptance 0.79204); prefill-logit gate 0.000737 / 98.784 %
against the float4 base and then **re-recorded** to 0.000000 / 100.000 % (an intended numerics change, so
the base moves with it); `test-backend-ops -o RMS_NORM` OK; MTP Protocol A at `-n 3000` (27B Q4_K_XL,
1 GPU, greedy) prose 29.2 -> 68.8 t/s and code 29.5 -> 73.1 t/s with `plain == draft-mtp` byte-identical
on both axes, plus the server-harness acceptance rows above; qwen4exp `HC_COMB` A/B identical.
`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` on every fresh-process comparison.

**Not run, deliberately:** a gfx1151/gfx1100 arch sweep (the change is a compile-time-unmodified branch
selection on the same code path, and the box has no such device this session), and the full four-axis
adaptive gate (the controller is untouched; acceptance is measured on the server arms above).  The
container images are built and pushed off-host by the worker watcher on the tag.

## 261026.001 (r144) -- TODO #36 (CPU/GPU overlap for the MoE misses) is retired by measurement, and the profile it produced ships two diagnostics

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r144` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `438cbb3c7`, tree
`b8d08c5186bb5c0d74cc04d3d82ccda4d30120ee`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r143 tree: **2 files, +71/-1**, all
in block 09 -- no kernel, no numerics, no default, no allocation.  The release exists to make the
measurement reproducible: the expert cache's per-token traffic report was unusable (it divided by a
takeover count that is 0 on the identity path), and the graph state machine had no way to say *why* a
capture was not being replayed.

### #36 retired: the MoE misses are 0.1-0.4 % of a decode token

O0 was the item's own decision gate ("if the cold read is < 20 % of the token, park this").  Measured on
2x R9700 (**the PCIe 5.0 x8 root ports**, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`), Qwen3.8 Flash-Next IQ4_NL
(100.4 GB, 512 experts x 10 used, 64.8 GB of expert weights -> 85.4 % slot residency at the auto arena),
2000-token generations with a frozen heat prior so the arena is warm:

| arm | t/s | ms/token | access hit | expert H2D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `-sm tensor`, auto arena (85 % residency) | 35.53 | 28.15 | 99.74 % | 3.3 MiB/tok |
| `-sm tensor`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=8192` (25 %) | 34.04 | 29.37 | 98.71 % | -- |
| `-sm tensor`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=2048` (6 %, the floor) | 34.44 | 29.04 | 95.66 % | 55 MiB/tok |
| `-sm layer`, auto arena | 25.73 | 38.86 | 99.48 % | 6.6 MiB/tok |

Shrinking the arena **14x** (17x more miss bytes) costs **0.9 ms of a 28 ms token**: the routing is so
concentrated that 6 % of the slots still serve 95.7 % of the accesses.  3.3 MiB/token of H2D at this
link's ~28 GB/s is **0.12 ms/token**.  A CPU worker pool computing the cold experts beside the GPU would
therefore recover ~0.1 ms (2 ms in the deliberately starved 4 GiB arm) for a change that must break graph
capture at every `MUL_MAT_ID` and mix CPU numerics into the layer -- so the maintainer retired the item
outright (2026-10-26) rather than parking it, and the CPU/GPU-overlap feature is **not** implemented.
Record: `archive/work/moe-cpu-overlap/` (`RESOLUTION.md`, `FINDINGS-2026-10-26.md`).

### What the same profile found: the token is dispatch-bound, and the decode graph never replays

* `GGML_CUDA_GCDBG=1` (200 tokens): `calls=59344 nodes=2451696 host_total=2780.8ms per_node=1.1us
  per_call=46.9us` -> **297 `graph_compute` calls and 12 258 node dispatches per token, 13.5 ms of host
  dispatch** in a 28.4 ms token; `CUDAGC_BREAK ev_rest=3610.3ms` of a 5 705 ms decode.
* `rocprofv3 --hip-trace`: **~124 000 `hipLaunchKernel`/s (~4 100/token)** vs ~14 `hipGraphLaunch`/token.
* Instrumented `ggml_cuda_graph_compute`: `direct=56171 replay=3152 capture=21 properties_changed=55321`
  over 200 tokens -- 93 % of calls find the replay identity dirty, so the graph is captured and then
  never replayed.  `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` measures the same speed (35.14 vs 35.53 t/s), which is
  the corroboration.
* The first differing member (a transient probe) is, in order: the node's **`src[]` object addresses**
  (the Meta rebuild re-creates its per-device simple tensors -- the same trap the graph *key* was fixed
  for in r115), then the inline **`name`** (`hc_combine-0` -> `-4`), then a genuine source `data` move.
  Canonicalising the first two raises the replay count but is **slower** (28.29 vs 35.23 t/s) because the
  remaining moves then trigger `hipGraphExecDestroy`+`Instantiate` recaptures (~20/token).  Reverted.
* Second finding, config not code: **`-sm tensor` is +38 % over `-sm layer`** on this shape (35.5 vs
  25.7 t/s at the same hit rate) -- the per-layer cross-device split costs ~50 graph splits and their
  handoffs.  Recorded in `COMMUNITY-CONFIG.md`.

Both are scoped as the new campaign **`TODO #107`** (`wip/graph-replay-placement/README.md`: the
diagnosis, four candidate directions with their costs, the gates, the reference numbers to beat, and the
instrumentation to rebuild -- including the trap that a change which *enables* captures without removing
the churn is slower than doing nothing).

### Shipped in r144 (block 09, diagnostics only)

1. **The cache traffic report's denominator.**  `expert H2D traffic ... MiB/token` divided by
   `g_takeover / n_tables`, which is 0 whenever the hook did not take the input over (the identity fast
   path) or after r143's teardown dropped the tables -- every run printed `over ~0 tokens = 0.00
   MiB/token`, so the one number this campaign needed did not exist.  It now divides a decode-band op
   census (`g_band_ops`, counted at the single place every routed MoE op passes through) by a table count
   snapshotted **at sizing** (`g_band_n_tables`).  Measured: `over ~194 tokens = 25.38 MiB/token` on a
   200-token run (25.4 vs 3.3 MiB/token for the same config at 2000 tokens shows how much of a short
   run's traffic is warmup -- the reason the 2000-token rule exists).
2. **`GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_TRACE` graph-call census.**  The env already traced the capture state machine; at
   exit it now also prints `graph_compute calls: direct=... replay=... capture=... properties_changed=...`.
   Counters only (two increments per call); it is what made the replay finding visible and it is the
   primary instrument for #107.

## 261025.017 (r143) -- the expert cache dropped its tables at model teardown (SIGSEGV), and the reporter's IQ3_S arm closes out r142

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r143` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `5bc9720a9`, tree
`45691700837c73b8f3d6fe6ae16a2ae5ab879a15`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r142 tree: **8 files, +212**,
all in block 12 (the block that owns the moe_cache iface tail) -- no kernel, no default, no allocation size.

### The crash: a table outliving the model that registered it

Found while validating r142 (recorded there as pre-existing): Flash-Next GSQ, 2 GPU, `-sm layer -ts 59,41
-ncmoe 24` **SIGSEGV'd at the end of the run**.  Diagnosed to the exact pointer this session:

* gdb: `fill_slot_from_host -> hipMemcpyAsync -> __memmove_avx512` with `rdi`/`rsi`/`rdx` = (dst, src,
  921600) and `si_addr == rsi`, i.e. the **source** read faults; the source is `t.host + expert*hb`.
* `/proc/self/maps`: that address is in **no VMA at all** -- the host master had been freed.
* Instrumented registration: the same layer/role appeared as **two different `ggml_tensor*`** (two model
  generations), and llama-bench's own log showed the sequence `load A -> pp512 -> free A -> load B ->
  decode B -> alloc_all_locked (deferred sizing) -> fill -> SIGSEGV`.

Root cause: `g_tables` is process-global and keyed by host-master pointers the **model** owns, and nothing
told the cache when a model went away.  llama-bench reloads a model whenever a test's model params differ
(here because a `-ts` *list* makes one test per value!), a server reload and any API user that swaps models
do the same, and `llama_model_free` frees the masters out from under the registered tables.  The deferred
arena sizing fills **every** registered table, so it filled a dead one.  `--host-experts pool` was broken
identically (its master is the read-only model mapping, so a host-buffer-free hook could not have fixed it).

**Fix.**  `llama_model_free` now calls `llama_model_moe_cache_forget(model)` -> the new device iface entry
`moe_cache_forget` (appended at the very end of `ggml_backend_device_i`, the initializers are positional) ->
`moe_cache_forget_all(device)`: frees each dropped table's arena slice, remap staging, heat mirror, bounce
ring and **host pool** (that one holds pinned memory), re-points `g_key_to_id`/`g_sem_to_id`/`g_alias_to_id`
(g_heads_zeroed too, and the per-model preflight accounting) so a reused `ggml_tensor*` registers a fresh
table instead of inheriting a dead model's geometry, and **un-sizes** the cache.  Un-sizing is half the fix:
a second model used to inherit `g_sized` and stayed uncached for its whole run.

**Validation.**

| arm (this box, gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, 2 GPU, `-sm layer -ts 59,41 -ncmoe 24`, `-p 512` | **SIGSEGV** (exit 139) after test 1 | both tests complete: **572.54 / 943.73 t/s**, exit 0 |
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU, `-sm layer -ts 59,41 -ncmoe 40 --host-experts pool MOE_HOST_POOL_MIB=4096` | **SIGSEGV** after test 1 (735.78 t/s) | both tests complete: **735.92 / 766.12 t/s**, exit 0 |
| single-model cache log lines (arena, residency, identity fast path), Flash-Next `-ncmoe 24` | 76 lines | 76 identical lines + the two teardown drop lines |
| same-seed greedy text | `13406dc51399` / pool `e2dde701fc04` | identical |
| pp4096 / tg64 (`-sm layer -ts 59,41 -ncmoe 24`) | 570.20 / 40.35 t/s | 569.91 / 40.12 t/s |
| dense 27B Q4_K_XL (the forget must be a no-op) | -- | pp2048 1879.08 / tg32 47.19 t/s |

Gates: `validate-set.sh` strict 15/15 on a fresh tarball, per-block build **2/2** (`--fast`,
`--changed-from 01851831e`, 365 s), `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** 0.000531 / 98.863 % (unchanged),
`test-backend-ops` HC set 88/88 + `FLASH_ATTN_QSA` 26/26.

## 261025.016 (r142) -- issue #226 follow-up: the qwen4exp HC mixer's inject GEMM sits beside the down GEMM again, restoring +3.4 % prefill

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r142` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `01851831e`, tree
`810570cad48549af2594242cd64c9f4fad851769`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r141 tree: **1 file, +25 / -6**,
`src/models/qwen4exp.cpp` (block 11) -- no kernel, no default, no allocation size, no node added or removed.

The reporter of #226 sent a second, separate finding after r141: on their separate-tensor (pre-#31028)
Flash-Next GGUF, **r138 was ~3.4 % slower at prefill than r137** (`IQ3_XXS`, all-VRAM, `-sm tensor`,
31.5k tokens), their kernel trace showing `convert_unary_cont_vec4` 353 -> 981 ms and the new calls being
F32 -> BF16 conversions of `xn` (`[10240, 2048]`).  Their reading: r137 emitted the `hc_inject` GEMM right
behind the `hc_down` GEMM, #31028 emits it after the *gate* GEMM, and the backend's per-graph BF16 src1
cache (block 10) holds **one** converted tensor -- so the second GEMM converts all of `xn` again.  They also
sent their local fix (restore the r137 order in the fallback) with PPL identical to the last digit.

**Confirmed, root-caused and applied.**  Every claim reproduces here, and the ordering hypothesis is the
whole of it: r141 puts `hc_attn_down`/`hc_attn_inject` at graph nodes #10/#72 (`GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2 -v`), r137
had #9/#10, and the node *set* is identical (3873 nodes) -- a pure permutation, which is why no correctness
gate could see it.  `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` over one pp2048 pass counts `convert_unary_cont_vec4<float,
bf16>` on `xn` (5.24 M elements) **4560 times / 273.9 ms on r141 vs 2280 / 97.3 ms on r137**; the trailing
`if (inject && !w_down_inject)` block is what broke the adjacency (its src1 for the gate GEMM, the silu
output, is cached and evicts `xn`).

The fix is the reporter's: in `build_hc_mix`'s separate-tensor branch, build `lo`'s GEMM, **expand it**,
build the inject GEMM, expand it, and only then scale/silu `lo` -- `ggml_build_forward_expand` order, not
node creation order, is what lands a node in the graph.  The merged path is one GEMM and is untouched.

| test (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, 3 GPU `-sm tensor`, `--load-mode none --lazy-mode off`, interleaved A/B) | r141 | r142 | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pp2048 | 2287.32 | **2359.53** | **+3.2 %** |
| pp8192 | 2208.12 | **2283.70** | **+3.4 %** |
| pp31500 | 2158.08 | **2227.83** | **+3.2 %** |
| pp8192, `GGML_CUDA_BF16_SRC1_CACHE=0` (control: the mechanism) | -- | 2248.67 | (between the two: adjacency still pays ~1.5 % without reuse) |
| pp8192, 2 GPU (`0,2`, x8+x8) `-ncmoe 24` | 835.5 | 841.7 | +0.7 % |
| pp8192, `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_POST=0` | 2268.0 | 2321.6 | +2.4 % |

**Bit-identical, as a graph-order change must be:** PPL 2.4392 (default arm) and 2.4370 (`HC_POST=0`), each
the same to the last digit; **all 24 chunk PPLs** of the reporter's `--chunks 24` command identical (final
2.4202 both arms); the combine+norm fusion vs `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1` still **-0.000000 KLD /
100.000 % same-top-p** (so the r141 fusion still fires with the new emission order); and **7/7 same-seed
greedy cells byte-identical** (Flash-Next GSQ plain `487888b20ddb` and GSQ + `draft-mtp n3` the *same*hash, GSQ 2 GPU `-ncmoe 24` `13406dc51399`, IQ4_NL `9bef5c01369c`, 4B `d2ffb97ccb76`, 27B
`a7aecbf5c5c1`, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` `e2dde701fc04`).

### Found while validating (pre-existing, NOT from this change, not filed — see the release reply)

**`gemma-4-E4B-it-Q8_0` with `-sm tensor` on 3 devices aborts** --
`ggml-backend-meta.cpp:1663: GGML_ASSERT(split_state.ne[j]*split_state.nr[0] * tensor->src[i]->ne[src_ss[i].axis]
== sum * tensor->ne[split_state.axis])`.  1 and 2 devices work; the **r137 build aborts identically**, so it
is not a re-base regression.  The first failing node is `FLASH_ATTN_EXT ne=[256,8,2,1]` (head-dim 256, 8
heads, so the *result* is split on the head axis 1) whose `cache_k` view arrives split on the **cache-length**
axis with 2 used rows over 3 devices (`[1,1,0]`), i.e. the head split and the KV split cannot both be
expressed.  **Maintainer's decision: known, not important** -- E4B is an 8 GiB model and 2-GPU tensor
(`-sm tensor` on any two cards, or `-sm layer`) is the right shape for it; `-sm relaxed-tensor` would not
help either, because block 14 relaxes a *value* (the MoE amax row max), not a split-ratio inconsistency, and
the mode runs the same Meta wrapper and the same FA split derivation.  Not filed.

**Second pre-existing finding, also not this change:** on the **same box, Flash-Next GSQ, 2 GPUs (`0,2`),
`-sm layer -ts 59,41 -ncmoe 24`**, the process **SIGSEGVs at the end of the run** (the bench result is
printed, then exit 139).  gdb: `fill_slot_from_host -> hipMemcpyAsync -> __memmove_avx512` (inside HIP),
reached from `alloc_table_locked -> alloc_all_locked` via `moe_cache_update_host`, immediately after the
late-arena ramp warns *"auto arena ... MiB is below the floor (...) -- too late to disable the cache
safely (the graphs already reference the tables), so continuing with the small arena"*.  The r141 build
does it identically (2 runs each side), so it is not r142 and not a re-base regression; it also needs the
`-ts` imbalance — 2 GPU `-sm layer` without `-ts`, 3 GPU `-sm layer`, and 2 GPU `-sm tensor` are all
clean.  It does violate the r20 invariant ("a failed ramp leaves the cache disabled rather than
aborting"), so it is worth a look on its own; not touched here.

**Also recorded:** the remaining 2280 `xn` conversions (85 ms per pp2048 pass) are the one copy the first
GEMM needs; the fused combine+norm could hand it over (`ggml_cuda_hc_combine_norm_set_bf16_src1`), but on
this model the MMB path already claims the kernel's `out_xn_bf16` slot, so it would need a second slot.
Measured as the residual, not attempted -- `benchmarks/2026-10-25-qwen4exp-hc-inject-adjacency.md`.

## 261025.015 (r141) -- the combine+norm fusion becomes bit-identical to its chain, and a merged-tensor GGUF can take it

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r141` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `8701922e9`, tree
`95792b8241f5d3fabff6e385c0697fc87dde83ca`, 15 blocks).  Delta against the r140 tree: **2 files, +96 / -40**,
both in block 11 — `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/hyperconn.cu` and `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp`.  **This closes the two
items the r140 record filed as `TODO` #107 and #108; both are removed from `TODO.md` (the numbers keep
their meaning as historical handles).**

### #107: the fused combine+norm now reduces the RMS sum in the chain's own grouping

The r140 record measured the fusion 0.018523 mean KLD / 95.588 % same-top-p away from its own unfused chain
(`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1`), with the same gap on the pre-r138 r135 build (0.021338 / 95.882 %).  The
cause is the **RMS partial-sum tree**, and it is the whole of the difference: `hc_combine_norm_f32` owned
three *strided* scalar columns per lane (`col = tid + k*1024`), while the chain's `rms_norm_f32` takes its
**vec4** path for `n_embd % 4 == 0` with 16-byte-aligned operands, where a lane owns the four columns
`4*i .. 4*i+3` of `i = tid + k*block_size` (n_embd 2560 -> n4 640 -> `RMS_NORM_LAUNCH(1024, 1, true)`).
Different per-lane partials -> different `block_reduce` input -> a different `scale`.  The kernel now owns
the columns the chain's kernel owns (same `a*a + b*b + c*c + d*d` per-lane expression), and keeps the old
layout for the shapes the chain's own dispatch also sends down its *scalar* path (`n_embd % 4 != 0`, or a
misaligned destination / gamma).  The `single_block` variant (reachable only through
`LLAMA_FUSED_HC_COMBINE=0` at `n_tok == 1`) keeps the old layout, documented in place.

| pair (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS, `HC_POST=0`, 4 chunks, `--kl-divergence`) | r140 | r141 |
|---|---:|---:|
| fused vs `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1`, `-sm tensor` | 0.018523 / 95.588 % | **−0.000000 / 100.000 %** |
| fused vs chain, `-sm layer -ts 59,41` | — | **0.000000 / 100.000 %** |

End to end that is also a *text* result, not only a logit one: Flash-Next GSQ `-sm layer` greedy 32 tokens,
`HC_POST=0` fused = unfused = **182 chars sha `a99ccbd97ecb`**.  PPL moves r140 -> r141 from 2.4538 (fused)
to **2.4546** (= the chain's exact value, `-sm tensor`) and 2.4235 -> **2.4395** (`-sm layer`); the 24-chunk
reporter command reads **2.4238** in both arms.  The default `DSV4_HC_POST` arm is unchanged at 2.4409.

### #108: a merged-tensor (post-#31028) GGUF takes the fusion again

On the merged layout `inject` is a *strided* view of `lo_inject` (the `hc` rows out of `n_lo + hc`), so
`sigm->src[0]` was a VIEW and the matcher declined — merged GGUFs ran the chain unfused (the hc-wide
`REPEAT` materialises) on `-sm layer` / `HC_POST=0`.  Two changes:

* `build_hc_mix`'s merged branch emits `*inject = ggml_cont(view)` — a contiguous `[hc, nt]` copy of the
  same rows, which `build_hc_combine` already pins.  One `CONT` of `hc x nt` f32 (8 KiB at `nt = 512`)
  replaces the ~80 MB `REPEAT` materialisation on that path.
* The repeat-anchored matcher no longer requires `inject` to be a `SCALE`: it takes `sigm->src[0]` and
  requires it to be F32, contiguous, `hc*n_tok` elements, **pinned** and **`view_src == nullptr`** (a pin on
  a view does not keep the view's root alive — that is the #226 shape in another form).  Identity op params
  always; the SCALE folding it used to do is gone, so a *separate-tensor* GGUF is read exactly as r140 read
  it.  `s2`/`b2` still come from the `scale2` that follows the sigmoid.

**Validation.**  The merged-branch shape itself was exercised on a pre-#31028 GGUF with a temporary arm that
emulates it exactly (pad the inject rows into a wider tensor, take the `hc` tail back through a strided
view + `cont`, both arms of the A/B setting it): fused vs chain **−0.000000 / 100.000 %**, PPL 2.4546 =
the unmodified arm, and `LLAMA_HC_CN_DEBUG=1` shows the windows *firing* at `n_tok = 512` (20 anchors, no
`dispatch` decline) rather than declining.  The arm was removed before the cut.  The separate-tensor path
re-measured after the relax: **−0.000000 / 100.000 %** (`-sm tensor`) and **0.000000 / 100.000 %**
(`-sm layer`).  What is *not* exercised here is the merged **loader** path (`create_merged` + the converter's
row layout) — it shipped in r138, is upstream's code, and needs a post-#31028 GGUF this fleet still does not
have; a merged-IQ4_NL conversion was attempted this session and abandoned (the pre-#31028 GGUF carries an
`blk.48` MTP layer the merged writer mis-handled), so the tensor surgery is recorded here as *not* a
validated artifact.

`446e33f7ceea45c92bf306b7dc1388aef3771df0`, 15 blocks).  This is **r139 + one file**: the r139 tree was
staged, validated and never tagged (`WORKLOG.md` 261025.013), so this release carries both fixes.  The
delta against the r139 tree is **1 file, +33 / -9**, all of it in
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/hyperconn.cu` (block 11): no kernel, no dispatch order, no default and no allocation
size changed.

### The bug: a fused window read a tensor whose last graph use precedes the window

Reported by briansp2020 (issue #226) against r138: with `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_POST=0` on a **pre-#31028**
(`hc_attn_down` + `hc_attn_inject` as separate tensors) Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF, perplexity was wrong by
three orders of magnitude (their chunks 1730/3040/3412/2751, final ~3438, against 2.4131 for the default
arm).  r137 was fine; `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1` was fine; a one-line `ggml_set_output(inject->src[0])`
was fine.

The r138 semantic merge of upstream #31028 moved the `1/hc` inject scale out of `build_hc_combine` into
`build_hc_mix`, so on the separate-tensor path the tensor handed to `build_hc_combine` as `inject` became
a `GGML_OP_SCALE` node.  The repeat-anchored `hc_combine_norm` matcher then read `inject = scale1->src[0]`
— the raw GEMM output.  The fused window starts **at the REPEAT**, so `scale1`, the SIGMOID and the second
SCALE all run standalone *before* it, and the allocator reuses the buffer of the GEMM output (its last
graph use is `scale1`) for exactly the SIGMOID/SCALE of the same chain.  The fused kernel then read the
sigmoid output as `inject` and applied the whole chain to it a second time.  `build_hc_combine` pins
`inject` (`ggml_set_output`) for precisely this reason, and pre-r138 `inject` *was* the raw GEMM output, so
the pin and the read had drifted one node apart.  A merged-tensor (post-#31028) GGUF never fired the
matcher at all (`sigm->src[0]` is a strided VIEW, not a SCALE), which is why only that GGUF class broke.

### The fix: read the pinned tensor, with identity op params, and require the pin

`inject = scale1` (which the model pins and which is therefore materialized), with `s1 = 1`, `b1 = 0`
instead of descending to `scale1->src[0]`.  That is bit-identical by construction (`hc_mul_rn(1,x) = x`,
`hc_add_rn(x,0) = x`, and the SCALE kernel already stored `s1*x + b1`), and `w_ok` now requires
`inject->flags & GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_OUTPUT` — an unpinned emitter loses the fusion (correct, just unfused)
rather than reading a recycled buffer.  The **scale1-anchored A-chain** matcher is deliberately unchanged:
its window starts *at* `scale1`, so that node is elided and `scale1->src[0]` is genuinely live there (the
only window writers, `add` and `mulg`, are already alias-checked).  The alias diagnostics now name the
individual terms (`ov[add:inj=… mulg:…]`) so a declined window is not silent.

The same change is in the report as an acceptable alternative; we took it rather than pinning a second
tensor.  **Equivalence with the reporter's own patch: 24/24 chunk PPLs identical to every printed digit**
(2.4928 / 3.7799 / 2.9349 / 2.4538 / … / 2.4159).

### Reproduction and the numbers

2x R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS** (the reporter's own GGUF class:
separate `hc_*_down`/`hc_*_inject`), `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -t 8`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`:

| arm (4 chunks, `-c 512 -ub 512 -sm tensor --n-cpu-moe 0 -ot per_layer_token_embd.*=CPU`) | chunks | final |
|---|---|---:|
| r139, default (`DSV4_HC_POST` op) | 2.4661 / 3.7320 / 2.9158 / 2.4409 | 2.4409 |
| r139 + `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_POST=0` (the chain) | **1711.7 / 2932.5 / 3267.4 / 2690.4** | **2690.39** |
| r140, default | 2.4661 / 3.7320 / 2.9158 / 2.4409 | **2.4409** (identical) |
| r140, `HC_POST=0` | 2.4928 / 3.7799 / 2.9349 / 2.4538 | **2.4538** |
| r140, `HC_POST=0`, 24 chunks (the reporter's command) | — | **2.4159** (their pin 2.4209, r137 2.4202) |
| r140, `HC_POST=0`, `-sm layer -ts 59,41` | 2.4850 / 3.7629 / 2.9181 / 2.4235 | 2.4235 (theirs broken: 1781.5 / 3135.2) |

`LLAMA_HC_CN_DEBUG=1` shows the window firing for `n_tok = 512` and names the decline reason for
`n_tok = 256` (`mulg` overlaps `add` and `res` — pre-existing, unfused and correct).

### Pre-existing, NOT caused by this fix: the fused combine+norm is not logit-identical to the chain

Measured while validating (same GGUF, `HC_POST=0`, `--kl-divergence` against a base recorded from the
unfused chain, 4 chunks):

| pair | mean KLD | same top p |
|---|---:|---:|
| r140 fused vs r140 chain (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_COMB=1`) | **0.018523** | 95.588 % |
| r140 fused vs chain, `GGML_CUDA_MMB=0` | 0.019986 | 95.882 % |
| r140 fused vs chain, `GGML_CUDA_BF16_SRC1_CACHE=0` | 0.018523 | 95.588 % |
| **r135** (pre-r138) fused vs chain | **0.021338** | 95.882 % |
| r140 chain vs chain + `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_HC_MIX=1` (harness sensitivity control) | −0.000000 | 100.000 % |

The fusion has always differed from its unfused chain at that level (r135 shows the same number), so it
is **not** a regression from r138/r139/r140 and not a stale-buffer read: it is a small, broad per-token
difference (median KLD 0.0014, 90th percentile 0.044) of the same order as the r29 BF16 chunked-GDN arm
that was once flipped off.  Every elementwise expression in the fused kernel is RN-identical to the
separate kernel it replaces, so the remaining candidate is the grouped RMS reduction's summation order
(`rms_norm_f32` runs the vec4 path with one `float4` per lane; the fused kernel sums three strided scalars
per lane), which should be ~1e-6 on `scale` and does not explain the magnitude — so the cause is **open**
and tracked as `TODO` #106.  It affects the chain path only (`-sm layer`, or `HC_POST=0`); the default
`-sm tensor` arm uses the `DSV4_HC_POST` op and is unchanged.  `TODO` #107 records the companion finding
that a **merged-tensor** (post-#31028) GGUF never takes this fusion at all.
