## 261025.013 (r139) -- issue #214: the compute-buffer chunk no longer applies to a declined slab, and the r138 depth sweep

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r139` (base `6050b467c`, canonical tip `fb6e02034`, tree
`8dd11bfe094077175c826892fba20b584ab81f79`, 15 blocks).  **Staged and validated, deliberately NOT tagged or pushed yet.**
The delta against the r138 tree is **3 files, +19 / -0**: `ggml-cuda-arena.{cu,cuh}` and one accessor in
`ggml-cuda.cu`.  No kernel, no dispatch, no default and no allocation *size on a live slab's later
allocations* changed.

### The fix: the chunk is for a live slab, not an armed one

The compute-buffer chunk (`GGML_COMPUTE_BUFFER_CHUNK_MIB`, default 256 MiB) exists to keep the movable-boundary
slab's work region in whole units.  `ggml_cuda_slab_enabled()` is `env_on && g_slab_armed`, and the slab is
**armed** by the MoE preflight before it is **attempted** at the first compute-buffer allocation.  A decline
leaves the armed flag set, so a streaming config still rounded its compute buffer up to whole slab units.  On
the issue #214 reporter's 12 GiB gfx1031 card the layout is 510 MiB: the chunk made it **768 MiB**
(2 x 256 + one spare), i.e. 258 MiB the run cannot use and the declined slab cannot reclaim.  The allocation
that *creates* the slab is sized before the answer exists, so a post-decline test cannot catch it either.

The gate is now `ggml_cuda_slab_active(device)` (a new per-buft device accessor,
`ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_device`): the pre-slab percentage margin is used until a slab is live on that
device, and the chunk applies from the first allocation after it is.  A declined device never reaches that
state.  Measured (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, `-ncmoe 24`, `-c 131072`, gfx1201):

| arm | r138 | r139 |
|---|---:|---:|
| forced decline (`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB=999999`), compute buffer | 768 MiB | **561 MiB** |
| same with `GGML_COMPUTE_BUFFER_CHUNK_MIB=0` / both knobs 0 | 561 / 510 MiB | 561 / 510 MiB |
| live arena (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=4096`), compute buffer | 768 MiB | **561 MiB** |
| live arena, slab work / arena | 0.75 / 19.38 GiB | 0.56 / 19.56 GiB |

**Gates** (gfx1201, r138 build `~/llama.cpp/build-rocm`, r139 build `~/llama-scratch/build-rocm`, every
text comparison with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`):

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| 35B-A3B, streamed (forced decline) and live arena (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=4096`), greedy seed 42 | r138 == r139, **150 chars sha `4ac3a523160f`** in both arms |
| dense 4B Q8_0, 3 GPU `-sm tensor` (the standard coherence cell) | r138 == r139, **111 chars sha `7e6229b260f6`** |
| streaming `d0` / `d120000`, two interleaved reps | r138 1224.8/954.8, 1228.4/956.1 vs r139 1232.9/957.4, 1228.8/952.1 (parity) |
| live arena `pp512` / `tg128`, `-r 2` | r138 1143.71 / 63.61 vs r139 1141.11 / 64.37 (parity) |
| per-block build, `--changed-from` the r138 chain tip, `--fast` | **2/2 built, 0 failed** (block 10 and the tip) |
| `validate-set.sh` | green: checksums OK, fresh-tarball **strict 15/15** `git am`, tree == `release.json.tree` |
| prefill logits | not run: no prefill kernel, dispatch or default changed; the change is COMPUTE-buffer sizing |

### The r138 depth sweep (issue #214)

Full method, both builds and every table: [`benchmarks/2026-10-25-r138-depth-sweep.md`](benchmarks/2026-10-25-r138-depth-sweep.md).
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, one gfx1201, the reporter's `pp512` depth sweep against upstream at r138's fork
point `6050b467c`:

| regime | d0 | d32768 | d65536 | d98304 | d120000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| resident, default flags | +17.8 % | +27.2 % | +21.3 % | +19.8 % | +19.1 % |
| streaming (`-ncmoe 24`, slab declined), default flags | +18.3 % | +29.9 % | +35.8 % | +42.4 % | +44.6 % |
| streaming, `-lm none -lzm off` on both arms | -2.1 % | +9.6 % | +20.0 % | +20.6 % | +19.9 % |

**No crossover at depth on r138/gfx1201.**  The resident lead is flat; the streaming lead grows and then
plateaus.  The default shallow-depth lead is a loader difference, not a kernel one: under `auto` (mmap)
upstream leaves the `-ncmoe` host experts pageable and prints its own "consider `--load-mode none`" warning,
while the delivery pins them; pinning the mode on both arms makes d0 parity and leaves the deep lead at
+20 %.  `--lazy-mode` is inert for `qwen35moe` (no `TENSOR_READ_LAZY` tensor; that is qwen4exp/Flash-Next,
gemma4 and deepseek41).  The r138 streaming arm showed a ~10 % low cluster across runs (842-955 at 120k) while
upstream was stable (656-661); even the low cluster is +27.5 % over upstream's best deep point, and the spread
is not the load mode (it persists under `-lm none`), so it is unattributed rather than a result.

### Record correction

`archive/work/deep-prefill-depth-scaling/README.md` said the RDNA2 half was "confirmed good by the reporter"
on a 2026-10-24 relay.  His posted 2026-10-25 r126 sweep measures the opposite shape on his gfx1031 card
(lead shrinking from +36 % at d0, about even at 80k, -10 % at 120k).  The record now says RDNA4 is closed by
r126, the RDNA2 half is **not** confirmed, and the residual is `TODO.md` **#106**.  This is not a defect in
r126 (his path is the tile kernel; the r126 fix is RDNA4-only) and it is not measurable here.

### Reporter reply

Posted on issue #214: the r138 default-to-default and controlled tables, the no-crossover conclusion on
gfx1201, the caveat that gfx1030 is unmeasured here, the clamp fix already in r138, the fetch-ahead
clarification (it is RDNA4-band-only by construction, so it cannot change a gfx1030 run), and the chunk
finding with its r138 workaround (`GGML_COMPUTE_BUFFER_CHUNK_MIB=0`) and the r139 fix.

## 261025.012 (r138) -- the CI worker's GPU gate, and what it actually costs

`radiance` (a gfx1151 twin of `halo`, used as the CI/CD work-horse) now runs the repo's heavy gating tier.
Three tiers, stated explicitly in `AGENTS.md` because "CI" had been used for two different jobs:

| tier | where | trigger | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.github/workflows/validate.yml` (hosted, no GPU) | every push/PR | ~20 s |
| 2 | `scripts/validate-gpu.sh` on `radiance` (cron `*/30`) | a change in the delivery CONTENT | 0.3 s - ~12 min (below) |
| 3 | a GPU box, by hand | before a tag | hours |

Tier 1 gained a **per-block-tree scan** in `validate-set.sh`: conflict markers and block subjects in
**every** block commit, not just the tip.  That is exactly the r138 defect class — a resolution slip
committed `<<<<<<<` inside block 10's tree and a fix landed one block late in block 08 — where the tip is
clean and only the block's own tree is broken.  Proven by injecting a marker into a middle block tree: the
scan names that commit.

Tier 2 (`validate-gpu.sh`) materialises the set from scratch at `origin/main`, asserts the applied tree ==
`release.json.tree`, runs the `--fast` per-block ladder, the seven op oracles and the prefill-logit gate;
it holds its own `flock`, skips while a container build runs, caps attempts per rev, and prunes runs.

**Cost, measured rather than assumed** (the question was whether this ties the box up for hours):

* **cold ccache, whole chain: 87m37s — one time only.**  The ladder alone was 4882 s and the cost is the FA
  instantiation sets: blocks 05-12 each compile their own cold (520-610 s each) while blocks 00-04 are
  10-114 s.  ccache was empty because the box had none installed (installed rootlessly: the static 4.12.3
  release binary, `--max-size=30G`).
* **warm ladder, same chain: 89 s** (55x).
* **unchanged delivery content: 0.3 s** — idempotence is keyed on `base:tree:n_blocks`, so a docs or
  benchmarks push on `main` costs nothing (the first cut keyed on the commit sha and would have re-validated
  every push).
* **warm full run: 5m36s** (ladder 6 s with `--changed-from` the previous applied chain — only the tip
  rebuilds — plus ~5 min of op oracles).
* **prefill-logit: ~6 min**, and it now runs only when the applied tree moved a prefill path
  (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/`, `ggml/src/ggml.c`, `src/llama-graph.cpp`, `src/models/`, `src/llama-kv-cache*`)
  or the base moved; `KLD_ALWAYS=1` forces it.

So a release-shaped push costs ~6 min (~12 min if it moves a prefill kernel) and a docs push costs 0.3 s.
Two self-inflicted bugs were caught by measuring: a legitimate prefill skip fell through into the failure
branch, and a skip was being treated as a partial run (which withheld the up-to-date marker).

## 261025.011 (r138) -- container watcher: bounded retries, a checked checkout, bounded logs

Inspected the off-host release pipeline on `radiance` (the watcher is the only automated piece there; there is
no self-hosted Actions runner).  The r138 handover itself was healthy — the watcher saw `v15-6050b467c-r138` at
15:50, built and pushed both ROCm lines (`latest` moved, `-6050b467c` immutable tags, GHCR prune ran), and the
50-odd `error`/`failed` lines in its build log are Ubuntu package-install noise.  ccache is working there too
(**95.71 % direct hits** on the 10.1 line), so the ~30 min is the re-base's genuine content delta, not a cold
cache.  Three real defects in the unattended path, all fixed in `scripts/container-watch.sh`:

* **An unfixed release was retried forever.**  A failed build did not record the tag, so cron (every 10 min)
  re-ran a 10-40 minute build indefinitely, pinning the worker.  There is now a per-tag attempt counter
  (`failed-<tag>`) and `MAX_ATTEMPTS` (**default 3**), after which the watcher logs
  `ERROR: <tag> has failed N times; not retrying` and stops until the file is removed (or `FORCE_TAG` is
  used).  A successful build deletes the counter; a *new* tag is always attempted.
* **A failed tag checkout could have published the wrong image.**  `git checkout --force --detach "$tag"`
  was unchecked, so on failure the build would have run against whatever tree was left checked out — the
  previous release — and then recorded the **new** tag as built.  The checkout is now checked, and `HEAD` is
  verified to be that tag's commit before anything is built.
* **Build logs grew without bound** — 66 logs / 768 MB on `radiance`.  `KEEP_LOGS` (**default 10**, one log is
  ~8 MB) prunes them after a successful build; pruned to 10 logs / 84 MB by hand there as well.

Verified without burning a 30-minute rebuild: a stubbed-builder harness (throwaway git origin + repo + stub
`build-containers.sh`) proves the success path end-to-end (builder invoked as
`--rocm "7.14.1 10.1" --push --prune --force`, `last-built` written, counter cleared, logs 16 -> 10) and the
failure path (2 attempts, then the give-up line with the file to remove); a bogus `FORCE_TAG` proves the
checkout guard aborts before building.  The deployed `~/bin/rdna-container-watch.sh` on `radiance` is the new
script, and an ordinary run there reports `up to date (v15-6050b467c-r138)`.  No delivery artifact changes (the
watcher is not in `patches/`), so no re-tag.

## 261025.009 (r138) -- throughput A/B of the re-base against r137 (post-tag)

The r138 re-base was gated for **correctness** (per-block build 15/15, prefill-logit KLD 0.000531 / top-p
98.863 %, op families, `plain == draft-mtp` on three arms, MTP Protocol A) but **no throughput measurement
was taken for the changes it makes** — including the two adoptions (upstream #31028's one-GEMM qwen4exp HC
path, #29948's `has_fusion` plumbing), the hand-merged MMQ tiling geometry in block 00 and a restructured
`rope.cu`.  That gap was flagged and then closed with an interleaved r137-vs-r138 A/B; full method, builds
and both reps are in [`benchmarks/2026-10-25-r138-rebase-ab.md`](benchmarks/2026-10-25-r138-rebase-ab.md).

**Result: no regression on any arm; dense prefill is 1.4-2.3 % faster.  No follow-up release.**  r137 was
rebuilt from `e8bd52069` with the *same* configure and the same pinned `GGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS` set as the
shipped build (its binaries are kept in `~/llama-scratch/build-b137/bin` for the next A/B).

* Band gate (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 3 GPU tensor, 512/128): pp **+2.3 % / +1.5 % / +1.2 %** at npl 1/4/8, tg
  **+1.2 % / +1.7 % / 0.0 %**.
* Dense prefill: pp2048 **+1.4 %**, pp8192 **+1.8 %** — the row that covers the hand-merged tiling (upstream's
  column-innermost grid, which is there for L2 weight-tile reuse).
* The fused prefill arm is still live on r138: pp2048 **1883.92** (default) vs **1778.46**
  (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1`), i.e. the gate+up+GLU MMQ arm is worth **+5.9 %** and repeatable to ±2 t/s.

## 261025.008 (r138) -- re-base onto `6050b467c` (upstream 2026-10-25; 21 commits)

**Release:** `v15-6050b467c-r138`.  Base **`6050b467c`** (base tree `cb3251e177`), canonical tip
`abb8f76b2b13c324760795c38eebe24f569a51e4`, tree `35090ba36cbe2aae9bde9de47bb4a8c14286bada`, **15 blocks**,
numbering unchanged (no block merged, split or renumbered; block 14 is still the temporary
`-sm relaxed-tensor` block).  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums, fresh-tarball **strict 15/15**
`git am`, applied tree == recorded tree); per-block build gate **15/15**; prefill-logit gate **PASS**
(KLD **0.000531** / same-top-p **98.863 %** against the r137-recorded base — no re-record needed);
op tests `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` **6450/6450**, `GATED_DELTA_NET` 55/55, `MUL_MAT`, `MUL_MAT_ID`,
`FLASH_ATTN_QSA`, `TOP_K_MASK`, `HC_MIX` all pass; `plain == draft-mtp` **byte-identical** on dense
Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0 3 GPU tensor, 35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M 2 GPU `-ncmoe 40` (the host-expert/slab arm) and
Qwen3.8 Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS 3 GPU `-ncmoe 48` with the MTP head; MTP Protocol A (27B UD-Q4_K_XL,
1 GPU, `-n 2000`) R **1.81x** / P **2.34x** / C **2.47x** / K **2.71x** (r137: 1.81 / 2.41 / 2.47 / 2.70).

### Why (the gap is one day, but dense)

21 upstream commits, 98 files.  Two of them duplicate delivery work, so this was a **semantic** re-base,
not a mechanical `git am`:

* **#29948 fused FFN gate/up + GLU in MMQ** is the same feature as block 08's prefill gate fusion — but
  NVIDIA-only by construction (its predicate ends in `turing_mma_available()`; its write-back relies on the
  MMA accumulator layout).  **Both paths now ship, arch-disjoint, on one dispatch**: upstream's machinery
  is adopted verbatim (`has_fusion`, `x_gate`/`glu_op`/`glu_limit` as leading kernel args, the interleaved
  loader rows, `I_dst = I/2`, `mul_mat_q_switch_fusion`), the delivery's two-pass arm rides as a second
  template parameter `has_gate`, and `static_assert(!(has_fusion && has_gate))` makes "one fused path at a
  time" a build error.  RDNA keeps the arm it validated; NVIDIA keeps upstream's.
* **#31028 qwen merge tensors on convert** subsumes block 11's two-GEMM `hc_*_down`/`hc_*_inject`: adopted
  (one GEMM for both products, converter-compatible, with the loader's separate-tensor fallback kept).
  The MTP branch stays the delivery's own (QSA top-k + derived visibility) — protected, and re-gated.

Also: upstream factored the MMQ J-tile selection into `ggml_cuda_mmq_get_J_best()`; the delivery's
`ggml_cuda_mmq_select_J()` is a strict superset (routed-compact bands, `GGML_Q6_COMPACT_J`, the fused-gate
register cap, `GGML_CUDA_MMQ_J_MAX`), so upstream's helper is now a delegate to it and the J cap moved
inside the selector (both call sites honour it).  Block 10's moved dispatcher needed the documented
**pre-move** 3-way merge (`git merge-file` against the old chain's block 09) — using the rebased block-09
tree instead looks "unchanged" and silently drops upstream's new arm.  Full per-collision table, the
gate numbers and the process lessons (a fix must be committed by the block that owns the code, and
`git add -A` during a conflicted rebase stages unresolved files) are in
`archive/work/rebase-2026-10b/` (`README.md`, `DECISIONS.md`).

Shipped unchanged from r137: every block's feature set and numbering.  Greedy text differs from the r137
build on every arm — expected on a base move (upstream changed rope and MMQ), and decided by the
prefill-logit gate, not a cross-build text diff.

## 261025.007 (r137) -- block 14: `-sm relaxed-tensor` (a TEMPORARY local relaxation; flint/mellum/mistral4 can tensor-split)

**Release:** `v15-3f03b1772-r137`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `e8bd52069`,
tree `5d6a19af59bc36a3442bbb5c7b368450c29a1a1e`, **15 blocks**.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(checksums, fresh-tarball **strict 15/15** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree); per-block build gate
**1/1** with `--changed-from` the r136 tip (only block 14's delta, 8 s at the long-lived path); coherence
**byte-identical to the r136 build** on four arms (dense 4B 1 GPU; dense 4B 3 GPU `-sm tensor`; 35B-A3B
UD-Q4_K_M 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, the host-expert arm; flint Q8_0 2 GPU `-sm layer`); prefill-logit
gate **KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 99.980 %**; adaptive-MTP four axes (Protocol A, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU,
`-n 3000`, `--spec-draft-n-max 3`, reasoning pinned) acceptance **R 0.54420 / P 0.83041 / C 0.87435 /
K 0.99200**, MTP vs plain **1.81x / 2.41x / 2.47x / 2.70x**, and the P/C decode text **byte-identical
r136 vs r137** (5975 chars sha `2928e6d6ea55`; 13151 chars sha `4187f8fae610`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`);
`scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  **No existing block renumbered, merged or split**; block 14 is a new
commit on top of block 13, and deleting its patch returns the r136 tree.

### What it is, and why it is separate

Upstream #30861 gives the MoE down projection a per-`[expert, token]` amax rescale: it pools the whole
matmul row (`ggml_pool_1d(abs(cur), POOL_MAX, k = s = n_ff_exp)`) and divides/undoes `cur` by a power of
two derived from it.  Under `--split-mode tensor` the MoE intermediate is split on axis 0, so **no device
holds a complete row**; #31081 removed the Meta `POOL_1D` case (it claimed `MIRRORED`, which is false) and
denied `-sm tensor` for `flint`, `mellum` and `mistral4`.  Flint Q8_0 (39.39 GiB, 95.1 % in the split expert
tables) therefore could not run tensor-split at all.

Block 14 adds a split mode instead of a blanket deny.  `-sm relaxed-tensor` places the weights exactly as
`-sm tensor` places them (zero extra VRAM: 20.66 GiB/device at 2 GPUs, 14.42 at 3) and admits one new split
state, `GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_PER_DEVICE` — same shape on every device, **its own values** on each.
`handle_pool_1d` produces it for a whole-row `POOL_MAX` over an axis-0 split; `handle_bin_bcast` lets it be
consumed elementwise/broadcast; every copy/gather/reconcile/read-back path aborts with a message.  The
delayed-reduce MUL-chain in `ggml_backend_meta_graph_compute` accepts it **so the all-reduce stays after
each device's own undo** — that ordering is what makes the per-device value cancel (an `e` that is a power
of two commutes with the sum, and `e_local <= e_global` keeps at least the reference's f16 headroom).  With
the undo on the wrong side of the reduce the result would be wrong **and silent**, because the shipped
divisor (1024) leaves `e = 1` unless a row max exceeds 1024.

**It is deliberately temporary.**  The maintainer's read of the upstream PRs is that this will be replaced
by a better implementation, so the block is kept separate, is **not** a supported feature of the delivery,
has **no `upstream/` candidate**, and is tracked as `TODO` #104 with an explicit "drop the block when
upstream fixes it" instruction.  Deleting `patches/0014-*.patch` restores the r136 tree exactly.

### Validation of the mechanism (why `e = 1` is not enough)

Greedy text alone cannot prove this path: at the shipped divisor `e` is 1 nearly everywhere, so a wrong and
a right ordering agree.  With the amax divisor forced to 1 (temporary local change, not shipped) an
instrumented `POOL_1D` shows each device pooling its **own 256-wide slice** (`iw=256`, not 512) and the
per-device maxima differing on ~half of the ~185 calls per run, and with `e` differing on ~half the layers
the text still matches `-sm layer` exactly (prose 0.0836/2.0/1.0/8.0 style splits).  Flint 2 GPU
`-sm relaxed-tensor`: **77.9 t/s** generation vs **59.5** for `-sm layer` (short decode-only run — not a
depth-16384 measurement, which is not claimed).  A non-amax arch (Qwen3.5-4B) is byte-identical under
`tensor` and `relaxed-tensor`, i.e. the mode is a no-op without the amax node.

### Limitations (recorded, not fixed)

Exact on RDNA/HIP; **not** equivalent on a backend whose in-kernel `src1` rescale is non-linear (Vulkan's
clamp-into-fp16-range, #30656), which is why it is an opt-in mode and not part of `-sm tensor`.  No
`-ncmoe`/expert-cache arm (the arena still refuses tensor-like modes, as for `tensor`).  `mellum` and
`mistral4` are enabled by the same change but **unvalidated** (no model on hand; `mistral4` was denied
before the amax rescale, so it may still hit an unrelated path).  No draft/MTP run against these arches.
`-sm tensor` keeps upstream's strict behaviour; its error message now names the new mode.

### Gates not re-run, and why

The stock-relative `llama-batched-bench -npl 1,4,8` arm was **not** re-run: no decode, verify, mmvq or FA
kernel changed (the r136 result stands), and block 14's only new code path requires a Meta device, which a
single-GPU arm never creates.  The four-axis acceptance values differ from the r136 entry within the
per-start hipBLASLt spread (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44 — the source of every file the draft uses is
byte-identical between the two builds; K matches to the last digit); the bit-level check for this release
is the pinned cross-release **text** comparison above.

### Docs

`patches/README.md` (block 14 section + index row, temporary-status banner), `README.md` (block table +
count), `MANIFESTS.md` (15 blocks, apply order), `BASELINE.md`, `TODO.md` #104, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §58.
`ENVIRONMENT.md` unchanged (no environment variable: the mode is a CLI/split-mode value).

## 261025.006 (r136) -- PR #225: park the resident idle slots at the top of a unified KV cache

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r136`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `43505eac8`,
tree `0c372dd2316a8c988086a0236b4664cb03a1adc2`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree); per-block build gate **2/2** with
`--changed-from pre-r136` (block 12's delta changed, the tip is always rebuilt); prefill-logit gate
**KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 99.980 %**; adaptive-MTP four axes (Protocol A, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU,
`-n 3000`, `--spec-draft-n-max 3`, reasoning pinned) acceptance **R 0.53158 / P 0.78686 / C 0.86744 /
K 0.99200**, MTP vs plain **1.79x / 2.31x / 2.46x / 2.70x**, and P/C text byte-identical (`6450` chars
sha `5fee404b9957`; `13145` chars sha `13a522e90425`); coherence vs the r135 build byte-identical on
dense 4B 1 GPU and 3 GPU `-sm tensor` (the timing line filtered).  **No block renumbered, merged or split.**  The whole change
is a fold inside **block 12** (8 files: `common/common.cpp|h`, `src/llama-ext.h`, `src/llama-kv-cache.cpp|h`,
`src/llama-kv-cells.h`, `src/llama-memory.cpp`, `tools/server/server-context.cpp`); block 13's patch is
regenerated because its parent tree changed, not because its content did.  Two new env vars
(`LLAMA_SERVER_PARK_IDLE_SLOTS`, on; `LLAMA_KV_PARK_DEBUG`, diagnostic) and no kernel or dispatch change.

Reported by **@overdoingism** (PR #225, `wip/server-park-idle-slots`; the PR text says it was written with
Claude).  This entry records the promotion and the delivery's own gates, not a re-statement of the PR.

### What it fixes, and the change

#210 (r130) keeps an idle slot's KV resident in a unified cache.  A request that then runs alone no longer
starts in an empty cache: its cells land after the resident ones and its attention range (`n_kv`) covers
them.  Flash attention's KV tiling and split depend on the cell indices and on `n_kv`, so near-ties can
resolve the other way (the reporter's 4/16 repeat test; our own 13/32 with the same-slot schedule).

Block 12 now has a staging API, `llama_memory_seq_park()` / `llama_memory_can_park()` (`llama-ext.h`):
`seq_park` moves a sequence's cells to the top of a unified cache, below the sequences parked before it,
copying the K/V rows on the device and moving the cell state (`llama_kv_cells::mv`, including `seq_pos` and
the extension).  New cells are taken only below the lowest parked cell (`find_slot`) and `get_n_kv()` stops
there too, so a sequence in the low cells attends over the same range, at the same cell indices, as when
the idle slots are saved and cleared.  `seq_unpark` moves a parked sequence back to the lowest free run, and
`park_compact` keeps the parked stack together.  Parking is refused unless the cache has one stream,
unshared cells, a non-transposed V and no sliding window.  The server parks idle slots when a task starts
and unparks the slots that run (`LLAMA_SERVER_PARK_IDLE_SLOTS`, on unless `0`, together with the lazy idle
slots and `--kv-unified`); a cache that cannot park keeps #210 unchanged and says so once.

A slot whose cells are not one run of its own (shared through `seq_cp`, for example a cached prompt-prefix
restore) cannot be parked.  It is saved and cleared by default, which is the lazy-off output.  **Delivery
fix on top of the PR:** with `--no-cache-idle-slots` there is no saved copy to restore and the lazy idle
slots are meant to stay resident, so such a slot is now left resident instead of being cleared.  The
fallback still logs at INFO; the `--no-cache-idle-slots` case logs at DBG.

### Accuracy of the PR's claims (our measurements)

Gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2-Q4_K_M, 4 slots, `-c 131072 --kv-unified -fa on -ctk/ctv q8_0`,
16 varied prompts, two rounds, `cache_prompt: false`:

| arm | rounds identical | parking == lazy-off |
|---|---|---|
| parking (default) | **16/16** | **32/32** |
| `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0` | 16/16 | -- |
| `LLAMA_SERVER_PARK_IDLE_SLOTS=0` (#210) | 13/16 | 13/32 |

With `cache_prompt: true` and a shared prompt prefix (the prefix restore creates cells shared through
`seq_cp`), both parking and lazy-off measure 12/16 across rounds and still agree **32/32**; the fallback is
by design, not a defect, and it is why the reporter's "no fallback fired" is workload-specific.  The
reporter's 16/16 is likewise their request set: the round-to-round disagreement that remains with
`cache_prompt: true` is present in the lazy-off arm too, so it is not introduced by parking.

Other arms: `-fa off` (V transposed) and Gemma-4 E4B (sliding window) report parking as unsupported and
are text-identical with the switch on and off; dense Qwen3.5-4B (hybrid attention/recurrent) has
parking on == lazy-off 16/16; 2 GPU `-sm tensor` on the 4B works with no parking failure.  The reporter did
not cover multi-GPU, MoE with the expert cache, vision or more than 4 slots; the 2-GPU tensor smoke is the
extent of our coverage there.  We did **not** independently re-measure the PR's switch-time table
(0.85 s #210 / 0.90 s parking / 2.01 s lazy at 40K); the correctness comparison above is the gate.  The
adaptive-MTP four-axis numbers above are the release gate, not a parking measurement (llama-cli never
calls `seq_park`).

### Records

`patches/README.md` (block 12), `MANIFESTS.md` (row 12), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §15, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §57 (and
the §38 note), `archive/work/server-park-idle-slots/` (the PR as submitted plus our evidence).  The
`rdna-boosts` fork branch is refreshed to the canonical tip and force-pushed to the personal fork; the
container worker picks the tag up as usual.

## 261025.005 (r135) -- issue #219: a device VRAM budget, and an over-budget `--fit` that says so

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r135`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `d43d6634c`,
tree `84dae2bec130cf7a46ccad1e2d2835d3fc3e8683`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree); per-block build gate green for
**block 09** (the only block whose delta moved; blocks 10-13 are SHA-only rewrites) plus the tip.  **No
block renumbered, merged or split**; all three changes are folds inside **block 09** (3 files,
`ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu` + `ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu` + `common/fit.cpp`).  One new env var
(`GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB`, opt-in/off) and no default changed.  No kernel, dispatch row or default-on
path changed, so the prefill-logit gate does not apply; the coherence gate and a 27B MTP arm were run.

Reported by **@xxyygt** (issue #219; the original budget report is #216).

### What the report actually is

A 16 GiB RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, HIP 7.1.1 on Windows 11) running the 11.29 GiB
`Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-mtp` + `mmproj-BF16` + adaptive MTP at
`-c 65536 -b 4096 -ub 1024 --flash-attn on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ngl 99`.  A `/v1/chat/completions`
request carrying `tools` and a 24 005-character system prompt (nothing else: filler text, `你好`, two trivial
tool schemas) faults at the **second 4096-token prefill batch** (`progress = 0.28`), either as
`ROCm error: unspecified launch failure` in `ggml_backend_cuda_synchronize` or as a **bugcheck 0x7E inside
`dxgkrnl.sys`** (minidump + the exact request body: `github.com/xxyygt/crash-219-minidump`).  After the fault
the GPU is dead for the rest of the Windows session, so every bisect step costs a reboot.

### What we measured (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, one R9700 at 32 GiB)

The reporter's **exact model, exact flags and exact request body**, with a `hipMalloc` holder process
pinning part of the card so the free VRAM matches a 16 GiB card:

| arm (same request, `14765` prompt tokens) | free VRAM at start | result |
|---|---|---|
| 16 GiB-class card, comfortable | 15.46 GiB | **clean**, prefill 1127 t/s, decode 53 t/s, 3/3 requests |
| true requirement, no pressure (sampled `mem_info_vram_used`) | 18.5 GiB | **peak 15.07 GiB** of device memory |
| 0.6 GiB below that | 14.46 GiB | clean but zero headroom (peak == the whole budget) |
| 1.0 GiB below that | 14.06 GiB | 384 s instead of 13 s (35 t/s prefill, 1.5-3 t/s decode) and then `ROCm error: out of memory` on the next larger prompt |

So the config needs **~15.1 GiB**, i.e. 94-100 % of a 16 GiB card before the Windows desktop takes its
share.  This is a budget failure, not a tool-call defect: the tool path adds no device work (a plain
`/completion` of the same body peaks higher), and the "69.5 K tokens at 563 t/s" control the reporter
quoted runs at `-c 131072` on the legacy endpoint, i.e. a different cell.

**On Linux the same state does not fault**, which is why this is a delivery *guard* and not a kernel fix:
the allocation fails (a clean `ROCm error: out of memory` abort, no driver fault) or, in a narrow band,
the driver evicts resident weight pages and the run silently collapses to ~1/30 speed.  On Windows/WDDM
an over-committing allocation is **not** refused at all, so the process keeps running until a GPU access
reaches a paged allocation, and that is the bugcheck.  `--list-devices` still reporting ~16 GiB free after
the fault is the same mechanism seen from userspace.

### The change

1. **`GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB`** (block 09, default `0` = off): a free-VRAM floor at
   `ggml_cuda_device_malloc`, the single choke point.  A refused allocation returns
   `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation`, so the existing fail-soft chain runs unchanged and the run fails with a
   message that names the budget.  It is **skipped while the movable-boundary slab is armed** (the slab
   parks nearly all free VRAM by design, so a floor there would refuse legitimate outside-the-slab
   allocations).  Verified at the 16 GiB emulation: `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB=1024` turns the silent
   30x-or-abort band into a deterministic `refusing a 453.54 MiB device allocation ... it would leave
   1330.00 MiB free, below the budget of 1024 MiB` at context creation, and an unlimited-budget run of
   the same config is byte-for-byte unaffected.
2. **`--fit` says the numbers when it cannot help** (block 09, `common/fit.cpp`).  When the free-memory
   target cannot be met and the context is pinned by the user, the fit used to end with one
   `W ... failed to fit params ...: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort` line after the INFO
   breakdown.  It now prints an ERROR block: projected vs. free vs. target margin, the shortfall, the
   context's size and MiB per 1024 tokens, and either "about N fewer context tokens would fit" or "even
   the smallest context cannot make this fit: lower `-ngl`".  On the reporter's shape the fit already
   knew the answer (`need to reduce device memory by 3124 MiB`) and nothing acted on it.  Nothing is
   changed automatically and nothing is refused: `--fit` still only adjusts arguments the user did not pin.
3. **`moe_cache_release_arena()` only reports a release when it freed something** (block 09).  On a dense
   model it logged `released the MoE expert cache arena (0.0 MiB) ... experts come from the host` and
   returned true, which reads as "the slab/arena was involved" in a failure that has no arena at all.
   Same class as the r125 gated flat draft reserve (issue #216).

### Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/validate-set.sh` | green: 14 patch files + `rdna-boosts-all.patch` verify, strict 14/14 `git am`, tree `84dae2bec1` |
| per-block build gate (`--changed-from 58120d4e3`) | block 09 + the tip build the `all` target (the other 12 blocks' deltas are unchanged) |
| coherence, 4B Q8_0 same-seed text (1 GPU), repeated | stable across repeats; no kernel, dispatch row or default changed, and the new floor has no live code path unless `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB` is set |
| 27B GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S + adaptive MTP n3, 2 GPU `-sm tensor`, q4_0 KV | coherent, generation 86.4 t/s |
| the reporter's exact request + flags + model, 16 GiB emulation, **release binary** | 3/3 clean, prompt eval **1140 t/s** (14765 tokens), decode 80 t/s, peak **15.07 GiB** on the unconstrained arm |
| `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB=1024` at the same emulation | refuses at context creation with the budget message (no 30x, no abort) |
| the same arm with the budget unset | unchanged (`13.1 s` for the same request, same output) |
| `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh --since "4 hours ago"` | clean (no GPU fault in any of the edge runs) |

### Open, recorded rather than fixed

* The ~30x collapse in the narrow band where the model + KV leave only a few MiB free (14.06 GiB here)
  has no root cause yet: the weights stay in VRAM (`rocm-smi --showpids` confirms 15.08 GiB), the FA
  staging fallback is *not* it (forcing `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_MAX_MB=0` on a roomy card is 13.3 s), and the
  workspace-pool flush + graph invalidation explain a fraction of it, not 30x.  It is harmless on Linux
  and unreachable with a budget set, but it is not understood - `TODO.md` #103.
* The Windows fault itself cannot be reproduced off Windows.  The reporter has one distinguishing test to
  run (issue #219): the same request at `-c 32768` **and** `GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB=1536` in a fresh
  process.  A clean start (or a clean OOM) confirms the budget mechanism; a fault there means something
  else on the chat path and needs `-lv 4` from them.

### Docs

`patches/README.md` (block 09), `ENVIRONMENT.md` (`GGML_CUDA_MIN_FREE_MIB`), `README.md`/`BASELINE.md`/
`TODO.md` (current-release pointer), `TODO.md` #103 (`wip`-free, no stub), this entry.

**4/4** (blocks 05, 06, 10, 13 — the blocks whose delta moved).  **No block renumbered, merged or split**;
the change is a fold inside **block 05** (the FA band) plus one inside **block 06** (the width probe).  The
delta against the r132 tree is **6 files, +214 / -119** (`ggml-cuda/{fattn-mma-f16.cuh,fattn.cu}`,
`template-instances/fattn-mma-f16-band-wide-*.cu` x2, `template-instances/generate_cu_files.py`,
`tests/test-logits-width-probe.cpp`).  No new env var, no default changed.  Record:
`benchmarks/2026-10-25-fa-band-width-purity.md`.

Reported by **@overdoingism** (issue #224, with the r126 bisection and the `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` control).

### The defect: r126's deletion was load-bearing for width purity

A band block splits each Q column's KV rows `np = nwarps*cols_per_warp/ncols` ways, with `cols_per_warp` 16
for the RDNA4 256-dim WMMA tiles.  The 32-column block (widths 1..4, 8 warps) is `np = 4`; the deleted
`ncols == 64` row was 512 threads (16 warps) and therefore also `np = 4`.  r126 left widths 5..8 on prefill's
8-warp table row, `np = 2` -- a different reduction over the same KV cells.  On the reporter's shape (dense
head-256 GQA-6, Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2 `n_max 5`) greedy text with the draft therefore differed
from plain decode (their first difference: token 325 at 8K, token 142 at 110K), identical with
`GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` and on r123.  Reproduced here on the first sentence at 8K (1506 chars
`7181badffbcc` plain and two-tile vs 1619 `7a3819b47df4` with the draft), so the near-tie is not required to
see it.

Every gate between r126 and r133 passed because **none of them could see it**: same-seed text only fails on a
near-tie, the CPU-referenced `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` op cases have a tolerance, and `test-logits-width-probe` never
reached the block at all (below).

### The fix: TODO #99's instantiation, now required

`ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_rdna` returns `fattn_mma_config(512, 1, 64, 64, 64, 32, 1, true)` for
`(256, 256, ncols 64, ncols2 8)` when a new compile-time `band_wide` flag is set, threaded through the config
getters (host getters require the flag, so a device-style call cannot bind to one inside `__launch_bounds__`),
the `case` function and the kernel.  `fattn.cu`'s band branch calls `..._case<DKQ, DV, 8, 8, true>`; prefill
keeps `(256, 2, 64, 128, 128, 64, 1, true)` and its `__launch_bounds__`.  The band's 64-column case and its
q8_0 fetch-ahead variant are new translation units, emitted by `generate_cu_files.py`, so neither shares a TU
with prefill's kernel.  `nbatch_combine` stays 32: 16 warps with combine 64 needs 68 KiB of LDS.  The
fetch-ahead depth's 16-warp/8-warp comment is once again true for the rows it was tuned on.

**The guard is a build error.**  A `static_assert` next to the band rows checks that both split each column
the same way and share `nbatch_fa/K2/V2`, `nstages_target` and `Q_in_reg`.  Re-selecting the r126 row for the
band fails to compile (verified by doing exactly that).

**The probe was blind, not absent (block 06).**  `test-logits-width-probe` reported `width_purity=PASS` on
every r126..r133 arm because the wide launch's gate is `K->ne[1] >= 4096`, `K->ne[1]` is the context's
**used** length, and the probe prefilled 256 tokens into a fixed `n_ctx = 4096`.  Its `n_ctx` is now
`P + W + 8` and a purity run must pass `P >= 4096`: at that point the r126 geometry fails (worst maxdiff
0.199764 on q8_0 K/V; the row-0 hash splits between W=4 and W=5) and the shipped geometry passes with
maxdiff 0 on q8_0/f16/bf16.  `MANIFESTS.md` blocks 05/06 now name the requirement.

### Gates (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm` on the release tree; `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`)

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| width purity, `plain` vs `draft-dflash`, `-n 512`, `-c 12288` | **identical in all 9 arms** (`KV` f16/bf16/q8_0 x `n_max` 3/5/7): f16 `2416d85188b1`, bf16 `bb0612faf7f5`, q8_0 `7181badffbcc` |
| the same at a 131072-cell FA range (2 GPU `-sm layer`) | plain == draft == wide == two-tile (`664 chars 63b6b7cf6fdf`) |
| `test-logits-width-probe`, `P=4096`, `KV=q8_0/f16/bf16` | **PASS, worst maxdiff 0** (the r126 row: FAIL 0.199764 / 0.206944) |
| the same probe on a **GQA-12** head-256 model (Flash-Next, `RS=from_w`, 2 GPU `-sm layer`, `-ncmoe 40`, q8_0) | **PASS, worst maxdiff 0** (GQA 8 has no model here: `TODO.md` #102) |
| `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` | **6414/6414** |
| `plain == draft-dflash` cost, wide vs `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` | parity: 8K 75.2/74.6 vs 75.0/74.9 t/s; 131072-cell 61.0/60.6 vs 60.9/60.8; W=8 MoE arm 164.5/166.6 vs 166.3/164.9, text byte-identical (`80309046174e`) |
| kernel level (`test-backend-ops perf`, kv 16384, q8_0, head 256 GQA 6) | `n_q` 5: 163.3 (wide) vs 167.3 us; `n_q` 8: 174.0 vs 170.0 — +-2.5 % |
| prefill (35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, `llama-bench -p 512`) | d0 **4764** t/s, d98304 **1641** t/s (r126: 4624 / 1632) — r126's win intact, the row is untouched |
| prefill logits | not run: no prefill kernel, dispatch row or default changed (same row, same throughput) |

The single pass is kept even though it measures at parity here rather than the reporter's 2.2-2.5 % at 110K:
it is the only geometry that is both pure and one pass over the KV cache, and the reporter's box/config
measures it faster.

### Docs

`patches/README.md` (block 05: the deleted-row bullet now describes the band-only row, the TUs and the
`static_assert`), `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §51 (the `np` split as part of the width contract, and "a probe must
reach the block it probes"), `MANIFESTS.md` (blocks 05/06 gate rows), `ENVIRONMENT.md` (`GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE`
now states the geometry and that the two-tile arm is at parity), `archive/work/rdna4-fa-band-wide/README.md`
(dated addendum superseding its "Declined" verdict), this entry, the benchmark record, and the release strings
in `README.md`/`BASELINE.md`/`TODO.md`/`AGENTS.md`.

## 261025.003 (r133) -- PR #223: the decode/verify band skips fully masked KV groups (block 05)

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r133`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `368496e40`,
tree `972701d20366ef817cc941ce8146241260bbb825`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree), per-block build gate 2/2 (block 05
and the tip; every other block's delta is byte-identical to the r132 chain).  **No block renumbered, merged
or split**; the change is a fold inside **block 05**, every patch re-cut.  The delta against the r132 tree is
**3 files, +50 / -5** (`ggml-cuda/{fattn-common.cuh,fattn-mma-f16.cuh}`, `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`).  One
new default-on kill switch, `GGML_CUDA_FA_BAND_SKIP`.

Contributor PR: **#223** by **@overdoingism** (the author of the issue-#45 report the band itself came from),
filed as one `git am` file plus a WIP note against r131; it applies to r132 unchanged.  Promoted with a
`Co-authored-by` trailer on the block-05 commit and an entry in `README.md` -> *Community Acknowledgements*.
Campaign record: `archive/work/fa-band-skip/` (the submitted patch is kept verbatim there).

### The change and the claim

The fully-masked KV-group skip (issue #48, upstream #28495) was **prefill only**: the packed bitmap was
built under `Q->ne[1] > 8`, so the decode/verify band (the RDNA4 WMMA band, `n_q <= 8`, round-robin KV
split) read every cell in the shared range, including the other slots' `-INF` cells.  The PR builds the
packed per-(stream, query tile, 256-cell group) bitmap for the band too and hands its tile row to the band
entry.  The band's skip loops already existed in block 05 and had **never been reached**; block i keeps
owning iterations `i, i+P, ...` and only omits the fully masked ones, so the claim is bit-identity, not
equivalence.

The claim reproduces, and it is larger here than reported (reporter: -16.9 %, gfx1201 / ROCm 10.0.0):

| arm (gfx1201, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, `q8_0` K/V, 2 slots `--kv-unified`, 384 greedy tokens) | skip off | skip on | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~105K conversation resident, active 9.8K one, plain decode | 50.84 ms/step | **41.69** | **-18.0 %**, token ids identical |
| the same with the reporter's DFlash2 draft (`--spec-draft-n-max 5`) | 18.62 ms/step | **14.83** | **-20.3 %**, ids identical |
| single slot 9.8K, nothing to skip | 41.62 / 41.53 | 41.30 / 41.34 | -0.6 % |
| single slot at 105K, nothing to skip | 25.1 t/s | 25.1 t/s | neutral |

**Why this is not the 2026-09-26 "break-even, close it" verdict.**  `archive/work/unified-cache-decode/`
implemented the same option (b) and measured it on a 2-slot `llama-batched-bench` cell whose foreign-cell
fraction was small, where the per-layer prepass (~0.6-1 %) cancelled the saving (~1 %).  r130's
`LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS` changed the workload: a resident long conversation in front of an active one
makes ~92 % of the FA range fully masked, and the saving is an order of magnitude larger than the prepass.
The old record got a dated addendum pointing here rather than being rewritten.

### Added on top of the PR

* **Decode-width packed-hole op cases** (`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`, 12 cases: `nb` 1/2/3/8 x
  f16/bf16/q8_0 x the band's hole).  The suite had `mask_hole` cases only at `nb` 9..32, i.e. the paths that
  were already covered, so the band skip had **no oracle at all**.  Verified as real coverage: mutating
  `fattn_kq_group_masked` to skip one *visible* group fails **all 14** hole cases (12 new + the 2 existing
  head-256 ones), while 6414/6414 pass unmutated.  Also run with `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` and
  `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_FETCH_AHEAD=0`, so all four band kernel variants (fetch-ahead on/off x wide on/off) are
  covered, plus `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA=0` / `GGML_CUDA_FA_WMMA_256=0` / `GGML_CUDA_FA_MASK_SKIP=0`.
* **The band predicate is evaluated once** in `launch_fattn` (`band_wmma`), and both the group-skip gate and
  the 2-D launch read it, so the two cannot disagree if the predicate changes again.
* The stale `// prefill only: the decode/verify band keeps its tuned round-robin KV split untouched` comment
  is replaced by what the code now does.

### Gates (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm` on the folded tree; `GGML_CUDA_FA_BAND_SKIP=0/1` A/B)

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` (full matrix + the 12 new hole cases) | **6414/6414** |
| coverage probe (group test mutated to skip one visible group) | **0/14** hole cases pass -> the cases exercise the skip |
| `test-logits-width-probe` (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, prose, `P=256`), `KV=q8_0/f16/bf16` | **PASS, worst maxdiff 0**; row-0 hashes identical between the arms (`710641958f1aa46e` / `b12bd89b74c301f6` / `26bbb7aab7ee2010`) |
| `plain == draft-mtp` prose `-n 3000`, 1 GPU and 2 GPU `-sm tensor` | text identical in all four arms (`778154646e23` / `e4d32ce80614`), MTP 69.3 vs 69.0 t/s (1 GPU), 101.4 vs 102.1 (2 GPU) |
| four-axis MTP acceptance (`-n 3000`, draft-mtp n3, `-lv 4`, prose/code/reasoning/recall) | **identical to the last digit** on every axis (R 0.52697, P 0.80144, C 0.86491, K 0.99200; 1837/3486, 1332/1662, 2164/2502, 372/375) |
| `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` (27B Q8_0) | **PASS, mean KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 99.980 %** |
| `llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8`, 27B `q8_0` KV | within noise (30.32/99.09/152.29 vs 30.41/98.28/152.17 t/s; the band is off for `B > 1`) |
| 2-slot `--kv-unified` server cell, plain and DFlash2 | the table above; token ids identical (`a14854397efa688c`) in every pair |
| per-block build (`--changed-from 6950f7ad1`) | **2/2 built, 0 failed** (block 05 362 s, tip 4 s) |
| `check-gpu-faults.sh` (journal + every gate log of this release) | clean |
| `validate-set.sh` | green -- strict 14/14 on a fresh tarball, tree == `release.json.tree` |

**The off arm IS the r132 A/B.**  With `GGML_CUDA_FA_BAND_SKIP=0` the launcher computes
`kq_block_skip_packed` from the r132 expression and the band receives a null bitmap, so every pair in the
tables above is r132-behaviour vs r133-behaviour on one binary (no cross-build hipBLASLt confound), and the
width probe's identical row-0 hashes are a logits-level statement rather than a text hash.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not done

The gate is the **band's** predicate, so this applies on RDNA4 + head 256 + GQA 5..12 + `n_q <= 8` only.
The tile-kernel decode every other model uses (head != 256, GQA <= 4, RDNA3/RDNA3_5, or
`GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA=0`) keeps the pre-r133 behaviour: extending option (b) to that family needs its own
decode-width hole cases and a measurement at the r130 shape, and the 2026-09-26 campaign measured it
break-even at a small foreign fraction.  Not done here, and not filed as a TODO.  The per-layer prepass
(option (a)'s target: caching per-slot group visibility in `llama_kv_cache`) stays unimplemented: the
measurements above say it is not needed, because the padded tail group it also skips already pays for it.

Docs: `patches/README.md` (block index + the skip entry + the knob list), `ENVIRONMENT.md`
(`GGML_CUDA_FA_BAND_SKIP`), `GREEDY-PURITY.md` **§37** (the band is covered now; the exact-no-op argument,
the oracle and the numbers), `MANIFESTS.md` (the block-05 verification row), `AGENTS.md` (critical fact),
`README.md` (credit), `archive/work/fa-band-skip/` (record), `archive/work/unified-cache-decode/README.md`
(dated addendum), `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` (promoted line).  No `TODO.md` item.

**Not validated:** gfx1100 / gfx1151 (a no-op there by construction -- the predicate is false, so
`kq_block_skip_packed` is computed exactly as before), and any concurrent-server text comparison (that is
not a purity gate, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §38; every measurement above is a sequential, fixed schedule).

## 261025.002 (no release) -- build cost: a release arm must not get its own source path (ccache keys on it), plus `scripts/scratch-tree.sh` and per-block build timing

**No delivery change**: `patches/`, `release.json` and the release tag are untouched (`release.json` still
names `v14-3f03b1772-r132`).  Tooling and docs only, recorded because it changes how a release is built.

### The measurement

The r132 release (two PRs assessed, folded, gated) spent roughly 60-90 minutes compiling for ~20 minutes of
actual work.  It was not the per-block gate that was expensive, and it was not the build-dir wipe:

| what | wall | ccache |
|---|---|---|
| same r132 content, **new source path** (`/tmp/pt-same`, and again at `~/ccache-test`, both at tip `6950f7ad1`) | **5m56s / 85 CPU-min** | 722 **misses**, everything recompiled |
| same r132 content, **same source path**, **fresh build dir** (`/tmp/mb-all`) | **8.6s** | 343 TUs, all direct **hits** |
| one `.cu` delta at an established path | 15-30s | the one TU + link |
| `common.cuh` (or any widely included header) delta | 3-5 min | ~100 dependents |
| per-block gate, 7 block states at an established path | 640s total (block 06 alone: **34s**) | the per-block deltas |

**ccache's key includes the absolute source paths in the compiler command line**, so a worktree at a new
path is a full cold build no matter how identical the tree is.  r132 used four paths (a per-PR worktree for
each PR, the folded tree, and the canonical checkout), i.e. four cold builds.  `CCACHE_BASEDIR=$HOME` does
**not** fix it here (tested: still 5m55s / 724 misses).

### What changed

* **`scripts/scratch-tree.sh`** (new): one long-lived worktree + build dir, switched between states inside
  it — `init`, `state REV`, `blocks [BASE]` (apply-all), `arm PATCH...` (`git am -3` on the release tip, the
  PR/beta flow), `tip`, `keep TAG` (copy `build/bin` aside so a later state can be A/B'd against it),
  `gate [args]` (runs the per-block gate with `--repo` pointing here), `show`.  It configures with the same
  flags `~/bin/build-llama-rocm` and the gate use (so the three share cache entries) and prints every
  build's wall time.  `--fast` builds the five binaries + `test-backend-ops` for a tight edit loop (`all`
  costs ~0 extra on a warm cache, so it is not the default).
* **`scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh`**: prints each commit's build time and the run's total, and its header
  now records the cost model above (why `--repo` must be the long-lived path, and that a first block taking
  minutes on an unchanged tree means the path was new).  The per-block method itself is unchanged and
  deliberately still a **wiped build dir + `all` build** per commit: the wipe is free (8.6s measured) and
  `all` is what the r2 lesson requires.
* **Docs**: `AGENTS.md` (*Build the fork*: the rule with the numbers, and the honest per-delta budget),
  `scripts/README.md` (a "Release work" flow block + the script's row), `MANIFESTS.md` (release gate 4: run
  it against the long-lived checkout, and read the timing output).

### r132 gate cost, measured at the canonical path

Re-running the gate at `~/llama.cpp` for blocks 00-06 (7 states, all of them content that path had never
built) took **640s**; block 06 by itself, whose tree is r131 content plus its own two amended files, took
**34s**.  By contrast the same 14-block walk at a fresh path costs ~6 min per block.  The r132 release gate
(5 selected blocks) at the canonical path is therefore a few minutes, and the fixed cost of a future release
is one build of the new tree plus the per-block deltas, not N full builds.

## 261025.001 (r132) -- PR #218 (MMB per-device arch dispatch, Q8_1 cache view-offset + range guard) and PR #213 (split-state hit copy) promoted into blocks 06/08/09/10

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r132`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `6950f7ad1`,
tree `7368926758ba53bb505b63ffffd7408122656665`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  **No block renumbered, merged or
split**; the changes are folds inside **block 06**, **block 08**, **block 09** and **block 10**, every patch
re-cut (the `From <sha>` lines change on any rebuild).  The delta against the r131 tree is **6 files,
+155 / -36** (`ggml-backend-meta.cpp`, `ggml-cuda/{common.cuh,ggml-cuda.cu,mmb.cu,mmvq.cu,unary.cu}`).  No
kernel's arithmetic changed, no default changed, no new environment variable.

Two contributor PRs, both filed as add-on patch sets against r120/r126 and both re-cut onto r131 and
reviewed claim by claim.  **The headline of each one does not reproduce on this tree, and the record below
says why** — the changes were taken because they are correct and cheap, not because they measured here.
Evidence, probes and commands: `archive/work/pr213-pr218-r132/` (`README.md`, `EVIDENCE.md`).

### #218 part 1 -- MMB's per-arch dispatch keyed on the primary (block 06)

Every per-arch decision in `mmb.cu` (`mmb_enabled`, `mmb_cfg`, `mmb_cfg_dump_once`, `mmb_dense_flag`,
`mmb_wtype_mask`, `mmb_dense_tmask`) read `ggml_cuda_info().devices[0].cc`.  MMB is designed off on RDNA2
(no WMMA), so on a **mixed-arch** box (gfx1100 primary + gfx1030 secondary) the policy froze at the
primary's and the RDNA2 card ran RDNA3-tuned MMB kernels: the reporter's V620 produced byte-exact zero
output-projection logits (PPL == vocab, 248320) or garbled tail-layer GEMMs (PPL ~917), depending on which
device held the output projection.  All six sites now read the **running** device's cc — the idiom
`mmq`/`mmvq`/`fattn` already use — and `mmb_cfg()` takes one magic static per architecture **class**, which
is exactly per-arch because `mmb_arch_defaults()` discriminates only RDNA4 and RDNA3_0 (documented in the
code so a future RDNA3_5 row does not silently share the fallback).

**Added on top of the PR:** `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_optimize()` now calls
`ggml_cuda_set_device(cuda_ctx->device)` first.  The MMB *marking* half consults the same predicates, and
under the Meta backend that pass is forwarded per child from meta `graph_compute`, where the current device
is still the previously computed one — without the line, `get_device()` would be truthful for launches and
stale for marks, and `GGML_CUDA_MMB_DOWN16`/blk16/res16 marks can elide an F32 output.  It is a no-op when
the device already matches, so a single-device run is unchanged.

**Not reproduced here (no RDNA2 hardware).**  On a uniform box the current device's cc *is* `devices[0].cc`,
so the change is bit-for-bit by construction, and that is what was validated: 12/12 same-seed configs
byte-identical, prefill-logit KLD 0.000000 on both recorded points, no GPU faults.  The reporter's
mixed-arch matrix is the only mixed-arch measurement.

### #218 part 2 -- the Q8_1 quantize cache's identity and its source guard (blocks 08 and 10)

The cache is keyed by the **root** tensor's identity but its arena is filled from the caller's (possibly
offset) **view** pointer (and the entry records the key's `data`), so an offset view that walked to the root
stored its quantized rows under the root's identity; a later op with the same root and canonical row layout
could take them, and after a compute-buffer reuse the stored pointer was stale — the reporter's V620 decode
faulted with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION`.  Every key walk that reaches the cache now stops
at the **first pointer change** (`while (key->view_src && src->data == key->data)`), so offset-free views
keep the shared root entry and an offset view gets its own; `q8_1_src_range_ok()` additionally validates the
source read extent against the root buffer's allocation before every `quantize_row_q8_1_cuda` / fused
gated-Q8_1 launch and **aborts with the layout logged** instead of launching into a stale pointer.

**Placed where the sites are:** block 08 owns the cache, `common.cuh`'s guard, the four `mmvq` sites and the
unary `mul_q8_1` site; block 10 owns the fused GLU -> Q8_1 site and its two launch arms, which the PR (cut
against an older tree) could not have patched.  The PR's one cosmetic slip (two statements on one line in
`ggml_cuda_op_shexp_down_gate`, our own block-08 code) is fixed while the line is touched.

**Not reachable here.**  A temporary probe at the four `mmvq` sites counted **0 offset-view keys** in
14336-60416 walks per config across seven configs (dense 4B 1/3 GPU tensor, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL 3 GPU tensor,
27B UD-IQ3_S 3 GPU tensor, 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40` and `-ncmoe 10`, Flash-Next GSQ 2 GPU tensor with MTP,
Flash-Next `-sm layer`, Ling IQ4_NL), so no arm of ours could have hit either defect and the identity arms
are the whole validation: 12/12 configs byte-identical, four-axis MTP acceptance identical, prefill-logit
KLD 0.000000.  The guard itself never fired in any run (grep for `q8_1 source out of range` is empty).

### #213 -- the split-state cache hit returns instead of copying (block 09)

`ggml_backend_meta_get_split_state()`'s hit path built the ~2 KiB state in a named local
(`split_state_entry::get()`) and copied it into the return slot; it now returns `entry.get()` so the state is
built once in the caller's object.  Same values, same assertions.  The PR measured that copy as ~half of the
function's self time on its build (2 `rep movsq` -> 1).

**It is codegen-neutral on this tree, and that is the finding.**  With both ROCm trees in use here (clang 24
in 10.1.0, clang 23 in 7.14.1) at `-O3`, the function is the *same size* before and after (one instruction's
worth of difference in the whole 1272-instruction body; no `rep movs` in either), i.e. the NRVO elision the
PR makes explicit is already happening.  `perf record` over short follow-up turns puts the function at
1.63-1.92 % of all process samples before and 1.56-1.60 % after — noise — and wall-clock prompt/turn times
are identical within noise on three alternating server pairs.  Taken anyway (it states the intent at the
source level and removes a dependency on an optional elision, provably value-identical) and recorded in the
block-09 body **as neutral**, so nobody re-reads it as a speedup.

## 261024.012 (r131) -- PR #222: the three kq-mask fills that lacked their sibling's buffer guard (block 05)

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r131`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `8a449543b`,
tree `5946a27a53697d2a8ed5154d4b64ed459c1e7f44`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  **No block renumbered, merged or
split**; the change is a fold inside **block 05**, every patch re-cut (the `From <sha>` lines change on any
rebuild).  The delta against the r130 tree is **1 file, +15 / -3**, all of it in `src/llama-graph.cpp`.  No
kernel, no dispatch, no GGML numerics, no default changed.

Contributor PR: **#222** (issue **#221**) by **@RikshaDriver** (Asim Siddiqui), a first-time contributor —
reviewed, reproduced independently here, and promoted with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the release commit
and an entry in `README.md` -> *Community Acknowledgements*.

### The defect

A **single-sequence** context on a hybrid-memory model died before the first token:

```
GGML_ASSERT(buffer) failed at ggml-backend.cpp:579        (571 on the reporter's r128 build)
  ggml_backend_buffer_is_host()      -> llama_kv_cache::set_input_kq_mask     src/llama-kv-cache.cpp
  llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_k::set_input                                     src/llama-graph.cpp:1302
  llm_graph_result::set_inputs      -> llama_context::process_ubatch -> decode
```

Reproduced here on gfx1201 with the reporter's model and prompt (`bailingmoe3` /
`Ling-3.0-tiny-IQ4_NL`, `-ngl 999 -c 32768 -np 1`, r130 tree): rc 134, 2/2 runs, at `-c 8192` / `32768`
(their 4096 / 131072 also abort).  `-np 2` and `-np 4` are unaffected in both builds.

### The cause

Block 05's derived kq form is registered by `build_attn_inp_kq_mask(..., allow_derived = true)`, and the
runtime gate `multi_stream = n_seqs > 1 && (!cparams.kv_unified || arch == LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4)` keeps it
**enabled only at one slot**.  With the derived form on, the packed `n_kv x n_q` mask has no consumer, and
the allocator gives an unconsumed input tensor **no buffer** — the documented behaviour the sibling classes
rely on.  `llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_k::set_input` then filled it unconditionally, and
`llama_kv_cache::set_input_kq_mask` opens with `GGML_ASSERT(ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(dst->buffer))`.

**Ten of the thirteen** `set_input_kq_mask` sites in `src/llama-graph.cpp` already guarded the fill with
`if (tensor && tensor->buffer)` — the idiom the `attn-k-null-mask-guard` upstream candidate introduced
(`llm_graph_input_attn_kv` is the origin, and `llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid` guards the *identical* call two
hundred lines above the broken one).  Three did not: `llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_k` and
`llm_graph_input_attn_k_dsa`'s `mla` and `lid` masks.

* `mem_hybrid_k` was **reachable**: its input is built by `build_attn_inp_k_impl()`, which passes
  `allow_derived = true`.
* the `attn_k_dsa` pair is **hardening**: `build_attn_inp_kq_mask(mctx_cur->get_mla()/get_lid(), ..., false)`
  passes `false`, so no delivery path leaves those two masks unallocated today.  The reporter's own note was
  "the gate is a property of the gate, not of the mask" — accurate, and the guard costs nothing.

`can_reuse` needs nothing: `can_reuse_kq_mask()` reads `ne[]` only, never `buffer`.

### What changed

Three guarded fills, in the file's existing idiom; the contributor's patch is taken as-is apart from
dropping the one stray blank line each hunk left behind (cosmetic).  Block 05's commit body carries the
report and the credit.

**Other unguarded fills of the same class were surveyed and deliberately left alone.**  `set_input_k_idxs`
(`attn_k`, `attn_k_dsa`, `mem_hybrid{,_k}`) and the pointer-only `s_copy` / `k_rot` checks are unguarded in
upstream master too, and none is reachable: a `k_idxs` / `s_copy` / `k_rot` tensor is always consumed by the
node that needed it, so it always has a buffer.  Guarding them would be dead code on a path nothing tests;
the invariant is recorded in `AGENTS.md` instead so a new fill site (or a new `allow_derived = true`
builder) carries the guard.

tree `c4f9659fc120487a01a136a52cc0377aa385c72e`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  **No block renumbered, merged or
split**: both changes are folds inside **block 12**, whose subject now names the server prompt cache.  The
delta against the r128/r129 tree is **7 files, +254 / -23** across `common/speculative.cpp`,
`src/llama-ext.h`, `src/llama-model.cpp`, `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, `tools/server/server-task.{cpp,h}`
and the server unit test.  No kernel, no dispatch, no GGML numerics.

Two contributor PRs (`overdoingism`), both filed as `wip/` patches against `v14-097cf33d9-r120`, reviewed,
re-cut onto r129 and promoted after their own gates.  Both are **default-on with a kill switch**, per the
default-on policy (`LLAMA_DFLASH_INGEST_TAIL=0`, `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0`,
`LLAMA_SERVER_CACHE_REUSE=0`).

### #212 -- a windowed DFlash draft ingests only the prompt tail

Every layer of the Qwen3.8-27B DFlash2 draft attends over a 2048-position sliding window and its KV cache is
sized for it, but `process()` fed it every prompt row: a 110K prompt was encoded row by row, all but the last
~2048 dropped again unread, and every prompt batch waited on the target before the draft started, which also
broke the queue of the target's prompt ubatches.  When **every** draft layer has a window the impl now takes
the prompt end from the block-02 `set_prompt_end()` hook and skips the rows before `prompt_end - n_swa`; a
batch left with no rows returns before the target wait, and the first generation row resets the threshold as
the MTP impl does.  Exact because DFlash sets `LLAMA_SWA_TYPE_STANDARD` unconditionally, so the mask is
`p1 - p0 >= n_swa` and a draft query can attend exactly a prompt's last `n_swa` positions
(`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §53).  The window test needs the per-layer pattern, which `llama_model_meta_val_str()`
cannot return, so a new staging query `llama_model_n_layer_swa()` sits in `src/llama-ext.h`.  The patch is
**delivery-only** (it needs the block-02 hook), so there is no `upstream/` copy.

**The reported gain is understated on r129.**  The PR measured -0.9..-2.7 % prefill on r120; on r129 (faster
prefill, and the F1 device path turns each prompt batch's `llama_synchronize(ctx_tgt)` into a real stall) the
same switch is **+8-12 %**: 6.1K 1556 -> 1683 t/s, 26.5K 1591 -> 1787, 88.6K **1271 -> 1395** (no-draft
1415), i.e. the draft's share of the prefill falls from **10.2 % to 1.4 %**; 35B-A3B Q4_K_M + its DFlash2
**+14.6 %** at 6.1K.  One PR claim does not hold for our model files: it says the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B draft has
"5 of 6 layers windowed" so the tail stays off there, but our `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash2-Q8_0.gguf` reports all
six windowed and the tail **does** engage -- that arm was validated here (text and acceptance identical)
rather than taken from the PR.  The re-cut also had to cover the F1 device path and the DFlash2/LiLiCorr
members added since r120.

### #210 -- idle slots stay resident, the KV-full path saves before it clears, a failed restore makes room

With a unified KV cache and `--cache-idle-slots` (default on), every new task saved each idle slot to the
host prompt cache and cleared it, so two conversations taking turns on two slots copied their whole state
out and back on every switch.  An idle slot now keeps its context; `try_clear_idle_slots` saves the least
recently used idle slot before clearing it; a restore that fails for want of cells held by another idle slot
moves idle slots out one at a time (with the entry being restored held out of that eviction) and retries; the
slot-selection save holds the entry the task is about to restore out of its own eviction
(`server_prompt_cache::find()` split out of `load()`); and buffers of restored/evicted states are reused for
the next save, counted against `--cache-ram` with the cached states.

**The headline numbers reproduce** (2 slots, unified, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL, no draft, `--cache-ram 8192`): a
conversation switch at 11.5K tokens **0.5 -> 0.2-0.3 s** with byte-identical text, and the PR's overflow
case (the second conversation fills a 16K unified cache while the first idles) **8.3 s recompute -> 0.5 s
restore with 4 tokens evaluated**, the restored text equal to the original.  MTP and DFlash2 drafts behave
the same (0.4-0.5 -> 0.2 s per switch).  The output caveat is correct and already ours: a different cache
history places a sequence's KV in other cells, which is the `--kv-unified` non-determinism of
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §38; every *sequential* arm measured byte-identical.

**Two things were added on top of the PR.**  (1) `find()` now skips a cache entry whose main state buffer
was already consumed: `load()` transfers the main buffer before the draft buffer, so a failed *draft* restore
leaves an entry that re-matches, compares against zero bytes, has `llama_state_seq_set_data_ext(..., 0)`
report success and leaves the slot's tokens on top of a failed/cleared KV.  That was a pre-existing upstream
hazard on a later task; the new retry loop made it immediately reachable.  (2)
`tools/server/tests/unit/test_kv_keep_only_active.py` asserted the old eager save-and-clear and failed 1/3;
it is updated for the new default and keeps the old assertions under `LLAMA_SERVER_LAZY_IDLE_SLOTS=0`
(3/3 green).  The change is **pure upstream code**, so it is also staged as
`upstream/pr210-server-prompt-cache-lazy/` (cut against `3f03b1772`, with the `find()` fix).

A 4-slot unified concurrent storm (12 concurrent + 1 replay, DFlash2) was 13/13 green with no asserts; a
restore that cannot be satisfied because every other slot is *busy* correctly falls back to a recompute.
`--no-kv-unified`, `--cache-ram 0` and a cache too small for the state are unchanged (the last recomputes).
Peak RSS with reuse on is bounded by `--cache-ram` (6938 MiB vs 6898 with reuse off, six 13.4K saves at
`--cache-ram 4096`).

## 261024.010 (r129) -- TODO #96 fixed (the band clamp runs on the live arena), #97 and #99 retired

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r129`.  Base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip `99a2736fb`,
tree `de1edae72cae8505ddbc6882acf8d2e11f891f41`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums,
fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  **No block renumbered, merged or
split**; the change is amendments inside blocks 09/10/12 plus a re-cut of every patch (the `From <sha>`
lines change on any rebuild).  The delta against the r128 tree is **5 files, +76 / -30**: `common/common.cpp`
(block 09), `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda{,-slab}.*` (block 10), `src/llama-context.{cpp,h}` (block 12).
No kernel, no dispatch, no default changed.

### #96 -- the n-gram band clamp ran on the model-load *armed* flag, not on the arena

`common` clamped an enabled n-gram speculator to `band - 1` **before** `llama_init_from_model`, but the
movable-boundary slab is only *armed* at model load: it is created or it declines at the first compute-buffer
allocation, which is **inside** the context's widest reserve, and a decline there calls
`moe_cache_disable_streaming()`.  So a host-expert config whose slab is armed and then declines was clamped
to 15 while it streamed with no arena — issue #214's reporter class — and lost the wide draft that is the win
on that path.  Reproduced on gfx1201 at r128 (35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M `-ngl 99 -ncmoe 40 --spec-type ngram-mod
GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB=999999 --fit off`, `-lv 3`): `ngram-mod: draft length 64 -> 15` in the same
second as the slab decline — i.e. *before* it.

**The fix is the TODO's option 1 (split the two widths), implemented without a new public knob.**  The clamp
moves to **after** `llama_init_from_model`, where `llama_model_moe_cache_band()` answers from the arena's real
state (a declined slab or a released arena reports 0, and the wide draft is kept).  The deferral is free --
the speculator is built from `params.speculative` long after this -- but it means the clamp can no longer
lower `cparams.n_rs_batch`, because that context already exists.  That field now stays the **unclamped
safety bound** (`common_speculative_n_max() + 1`, i.e. 65 for `ngram-mod`'s default 64), which is the
*correctness* quantity (the widest per-seq batch a partial rollback can land in) and the value floored into
the chunked-GDN threshold, so a 64-row verify can never take the chunked path.  What it no longer does is
size the slab's narrow (decode/verify) reserve: that takes the band-limited width instead, through a new
`llama_context::verify_batch_width()` (the live band, falling back to `n_rs_batch` when there is none) at the
three reserve probes.  A live arena therefore reserves byte-for-byte what it did before.

**The decline messages now name every knob.**  `ggml_cuda_slab_init_locked` prints the H2D-ring term
explicitly (it only said "plus the H2D-ring hole" before) and lists `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` /
`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB` (floor), `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB` (ring hole) and
`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RESERVE_MIB` (reserve); the `moe_cache_disable_streaming` companion and the #136
could-not-be-created message name the same set.  In the #214 report 768 + 2048 = 2816 fit in 3072 MiB
available and the auto-sized ~1.6 GiB ring hole was the binding term, which the old message named nothing for.

**Gates (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`; every fresh-process text comparison with
`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`).**

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| 35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, 1 GPU `-ncmoe 40`, ngram-mod, **slab declined** (`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB=999999`) | **no clamp line**, `llama_context: n_rs_batch = 65`; greedy text identical to `--spec-type none` (plain) and to the pre-fix workaround arm |
| 35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, 3 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, ngram-mod, **live arena** | clamp still fires (`draft length 64 -> 15`), `n_rs_batch = 65`; slab narrow floor **1024/1280 MiB** and `identity fast path ON` **142/142**, identical to the same run with `--spec-type none` (arena unchanged) |

The one accepted trade, documented in `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3 and `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §50: a GDN model with an
enabled ngram speculator now floors the chunked-GDN threshold at the **unclamped** draft width for the whole
run, so a prefill **tail** ubatch below it takes the sequential (bit-identical) kernel -- measured <= 1 % on
the 16k-prompt arm above.  And a decline that happens *after* the context exists (an OOM-yield arena release
inside `ggml_cuda_device_malloc`) still leaves the draft clamped; `LLAMA_SPEC_NGRAM_MOD_BAND_CLAMP=0` is the
escape in both cases.

### #97 -- retired: the RDNA2 half closed on the reporter's own sweep

r126 fixed the RDNA4 half (the `ncols == 64` MMA band row was also the prefill instantiation).  The RDNA2
half was never measurable here -- the box has **no gfx1030/gfx1031**, and its only RDNA2 silicon is a
**gfx1036 iGPU with a 2 GiB BAR and ~1.8 GiB already taken by the desktop**, i.e. no room for a model, a KV
cache or an FA staging arena (checked with `rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram` before discarding the arm).  The
reporter ran the depth sweep on their 12 GiB gfx1031 card against the current build and **reported it works
well** (maintainer relay), so neither block 05's RDNA2 tile table nor the `prefill_stages = !RDNA3_5` staging
gate shows issue #214's shape on RDNA2.  No code changed for it; record
`archive/work/deep-prefill-depth-scaling/README.md` ("Resolution").

### #99 -- retired: the premise was measured and does not hold

`TODO.md` #99 kept "restore the W=5..8 band geometry via a compile-time band instantiation, only if a
decode-bound workload shows it pays".  There is no decode-bound head-256/GQA-8 workload in the fleet (the
only models that reach the band are MoE and are measured with host experts, where FA is a minority of the
step), and r129 measured the two geometries that already exist end to end: on the arm that reaches W=8 every
step (3 GPU `-sm tensor`, Flash-Next IQ4_NL + shared MTP head, `-ncmoe 48`, `--spec-draft-n-max 7`, 2 reps)
**default 110.1 / 110.2 t/s vs `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WIDE=0` 108.9 / 107.6 t/s** -- the shipping 256-thread row
is the faster of the two, and greedy text is byte-identical across all four runs (`883f4c55ece2`).  So the
16-warp geometry's kernel-level ~17 % still does not reach the wall clock, and the instantiation would ship
an unvalidated FA variant (a new template parameter + a fresh `template-instances/*.cu` set on the build-time
hot spot + the prefill purity gate) for no measured gain.  Declined; record
`archive/work/rdna4-fa-band-wide/README.md` ("Status after r126/r129"), which also keeps the two-tile arm as
the starting point if a decode-bound head-256/GQA-8 model ever appears.

`From <sha>` lines change on any rebuild).

Small release by design: the delta against the r127 tree is **4 files** — `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`
(+109), `src/llama-model.cpp` (115 lines renamed back), `src/CMakeLists.txt` (comment), `src/llama-context.cpp`
(1 line).  No kernel, no dispatch, no default changed.

### #100 — `HC_COMBINE` had no oracle (block 11)

`test-backend-ops -o HC_COMBINE` ran **0/0**: the op had no test case in any tree, while its sibling
`HC_MIX` had 30.  A wrong fused residual combine (`out[e,c,t] = residual[e,c,t] + block_out[e,t] *
2*sigmoid(inject[c,t]/hc)`) is a *uniform* corruption of the residual stream, so same-seed text, MTP
acceptance and the width probe all agree with themselves and no gate could see it.  `HC_MIX`'s cases cannot
see it either: their `x` is a random tensor, so a broken combine only feeds a different random input.

Two cases, both in block 11:

* `test_hc_combine` — the op against its CPU reference (the unfused `SCALE/SIGMOID/SCALE/REPEAT/MUL/ADD`
  chain): `n_embd` 512/2560, `hc` 2/4/8 (the CUDA kernel's `w[8]` bound), `nt` 1/2/3/5/8/16 (16 is
  `HC_BF16_MAX_TOKENS`, the widest the op accepts), and both `block_out`/`inject` shapes (broadcast
  `ne[1] == 1` and per-token).  **20/20.**
* `test_hc_combine_mix` — a *whole graph* `HC_COMBINE -> BF16 HC_MIX` at the Flash-Next shapes (n_embd 2560,
  hc 4, low rank 320), `nt` 1/2/3/5/8 plus the `w_inject`-less head call.  A single-op case cannot reach
  `ggml_cuda_hc_combine_mix_try_fuse`, which is **default-on**; `run_whole_graph()` can.  **6/6 with the
  fusion on, 6/6 with `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_HC_COMBINE_MIX=0`** (the unfused control), and a temporary
  instrument confirmed the matcher fires on the default arm and not on the control.  Perf cases added too
  (`test-backend-ops perf -o HC_COMBINE`).

`-o "HC_MIX,HC_COMBINE,HC_COMBINE_MIX"` → **56/56**; `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` all 3 backends green
(GPU NMSE 4.42e-14, mixed batch 2.07e-14).  New rule: `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §52; per-block row 11 in
`MANIFESTS.md`.

### #101 — the `ml`→`ml_l` rename is gone (block 00, propagated through 09/12)

The loader parameter rename was introduced by block 00's `-Wshadow` sweep and cost 115 lines of divergence
in `src/llama-model.cpp` — every re-base conflict in that file was re-skinned for nothing.  It is reverted
across the **whole chain** (block 00 renames nothing, blocks 09/12's added lines use `ml`), so the delivered
file now matches upstream's identifiers exactly.

**Why the parameter and not the member.**  The first attempt renamed the *member* (`ml` → `ml_ptr`, 3 lines)
instead; that is a trap: upstream's own arch files read the member **by name** in
`load_arch_tensors(llama_model_loader &)` (unnamed parameter) — `src/models/eagle3.cpp` and
`src/models/dflash.cpp` do `ml->get_tensor_meta(...)` / `ml->get_key(...)` (7 sites, all upstream text).  A
member rename breaks with every upstream addition of that pattern, so the member keeps its upstream name.

**The cost, accepted and documented.**  clang has no `-Wshadow=local` (GCC does, and the CMake comment
already says the delivery does not police declaration-shadows-a-member), so clang reports upstream's idiom:
**9 standing warnings** — 8 in `llama-model.cpp` (`ml` parameter vs `ml` member) and 1 in `llama-graph.cpp`
(`build_amax_src1_f16()`'s `n_embd` local).  They are enumerated in `src/CMakeLists.txt` with the
instruction that a `-Wshadow` hit anywhere else is the class the flag exists for.  Verified: the full
`llama` target rebuilt from scratch reports exactly those 9 and nothing else.

### Drive-by (block 12)

`llama_io_read_host`'s constructor initialised `buf_size` before `lctx` against the declaration order
(`-Wreorder-ctor`, new in this tree from the r119 async restore).  Reordered; the warning is gone.
