## 261024.008 (r127) -- re-base onto `3f03b1772` (261 upstream commits): 14 blocks replayed, no block renumbered, gfx1151 validated

**Release:** `v14-3f03b1772-r127`.  `release.json` base `3f03b1772` (base tree `14370bd49a`), canonical tip
`0c28ef86c`, tree `f46264b1fe565a016940e6fc7858cf50e3b11a9d`, 14 blocks.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(checksums, fresh-tarball **strict 14/14** `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree); a strict `git am` of
the regenerated set onto a clean `3f03b1772` reproduces the tree exactly.  **No block was renumbered,
merged or split**; the changes are amendments inside the owning blocks plus a re-cut of every patch.

**Why.**  The old fork point (`097cf33d9`, 2026-10-12) was 12 days and **261 commits / 868 files
(+96 173 / −48 196)** behind the maintainer's fork master.  Upstream had meanwhile implemented several of
the same things differently — a chunked GDN prefill kernel, the MoE cache rewritten to a 50/50 SLRU, a
4 GiB pinned-host cap, chunked CUDA graphs, a fused QSA mask op, QSA selection without the kq_mask, MMQ /
MMVQ retunes, `hc_stream_mean` for the DFlash layer-input tap — so this was a **semantic** re-base: every
collision was decided (SUBSUMES / CORDON / INTEGRATE) with a measurement or a bit-identity argument, not
mechanically unioned.  The campaign record, per-rung conflict tables and the halo recipes are in
[`archive/work/rebase-2026-10/`](archive/work/rebase-2026-10/README.md) (`STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`,
`GOTCHAS.md`).

**What landed, by block** (the full per-block detail is `patches/README.md`):

* **03** — upstream's RDNA3.5 MMA chunked kernel is eligible at `n_tokens >= 2048` on gfx1151 but stays
  **behind** ours: it runs only where our chunked path stands down.  **One chunked kernel per device
  class** is the rule; measured below.
* **08** — upstream's hadamard-folded weight split (`cur_mm` for the weight, the primal `cur` for the LoRA
  delta) adopted; the top-k MoE A/B helper is now defined where the matcher lives.
* **10** — the moved fusion dispatcher takes upstream's chunked-graph shape: our WIP AR-stage hook runs
  before the **last chunk's** capture, the HIP `hipGraphExecUpdate` leak workaround lives inside upstream's
  new `ggml_cuda_graph_update_executable(cudaGraphExec_t &, cudaGraph_t)`, and the recapture condition is
  `instances.empty() || mem_gen` moved.
* **11** — **CORDON, twice**: upstream's fused QSA mask op (`GGML_OP_TOP_K_MASK`, #30640) and its
  "selection without kq_mask" rework (#30965) both leave qwen4exp on the delivery's derived-visibility
  selection (`additive` + `run_top_k`, no mask tensor) — the -800 MiB win and the QSA oracle are intact.
  Upstream's `hc_stream_mean()` **subsumes** our `graph::build_hc_mean()` for qwen4exp (identical node
  list), so our copy is gone; deepseek4/glm5-next keep theirs.
* **12** — the op-count `static_assert`s were recomputed with both sides' ops (**108** after block 11,
  **109** after block 12; the old chain's "107…!= 108" message typo is fixed).
* **00/07/08/09/10** — the campaign's four *fixup* commits were **folded into the blocks that own them**
  and dropped, so the chain is exactly 14 commits again.  `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh` then found
  three defects a tip-only build cannot see and they are fixed in their blocks: block 08 used
  `ggml_cuda_topk_moe_fusion_disabled()` that only block 10 defined; block 09 carried a stray `}`; and
  every block tree carried `ml.` where the delivery renamed the loader parameter to `ml_l` (two of those
  were hard build errors).

## 261024.007 (r126) -- the RDNA4 MMA band row is no longer also the prefill row: deep-context prefill recovers (block 05, TODO #98 closed)

**Change:** **block 05**.  `release.json` tip `760ac6aaf`, tree `6abcc1a92`;
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums OK, fresh-tarball strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree ==
recorded tree).  One config row in `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh`; no new block, no new env, no
allocation change.

**The bug** (`WORKLOG.md` 261024.006, `TODO.md` #97/#98).  `ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_rdna` began
with two RDNA4 GQA-8/head-256 **band** rows keyed on `ncols` alone.  The 64-column one
(`fattn_mma_config(512, 1, 64, 64, 64, 32, 1, true)`) was reached by **both** the W=5..8 verify band and
every wide prefill, because the query-width dispatch gives `ncols1 = 8, ncols2 = 8` (ncols 64) to both, and
`nthreads`/`occupancy` feed `__launch_bounds__` -- so prefill was compiled with the band geometry (16 warps,
occupancy 1) while upstream's `(256,256,64)` row is 256 threads / occupancy 2.  Traced at
`pp512 @ d98304` (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M, q8_0 K/V, 1 GPU): the FA kernel took **28.74 s vs upstream's
19.63 s** for the same 980 dispatches, -10 % end to end at depth.  This is issue #214's shape (short prefill
fast, deep prefill slow) on gfx1201.

**The fix.**  The `ncols == 64` band row is **deleted**; prefill falls through to the table row
`(256, 2, 64, 128, 128, 64, 1, true)`, which is the same row upstream and the non-RDNA4 arches already use.
The `ncols == 32` band row stays and the comment now states why it is band-only (`ncols1 = 32/ncols2` is
dispatched only for `n_q <= 32/ncols2`).  A separate W=5..8 band instantiation was considered
(`TODO.md` #99) and deliberately not cut: the measured `-ncmoe 40`, 32k-context, q8_0-KV, n_max 7 arm
(verify width 5..8) is **unchanged within noise** -- r125 248.8 / 239.6 t/s vs r126 241.2 / 249.7 (and the
n_max 3 arm, which never used the row: 197.4 / 196.5 vs 196.8 / 197.2), so the 16-warp row's kernel-level
~17 % was not reaching the wall clock on a MoE-bound decode.  Restoring it later needs a compile-time band
flag, not a row (GREEDY-PURITY.md §51).

**Measured** (gfx1201, 1 GPU, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, fully resident, `-fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`,
`-p 512 -n 0`, `llama-bench`):

| build | d0 | d32768 | d65536 | d98304 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| r125 | 4541 | 2488 | 1620 | 1210 |
| **r126** | **4624** | **2957** | **2023** | **1632** |
| upstream @ master | 3600 | 2273 | 1661 | 1366 |

So the delivery goes from -10 % below upstream at d98304 to **+20 % above it**, with the short-context lead
intact (+28 % over upstream at d0).  The reporter's streaming regime (`-ncmoe 24`, cache off) was already
faster than upstream at every depth and is unchanged by this row (it is prefill-only).

**Gates** (the build is the tree re-cut from `patches/`, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`):

* `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` (gfx1201, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0): **6391/6391**, 2/2 backends.
* `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh`: **PASS** at the standard point (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %).
* **The head-256 changed shape is a family switch, and it was judged as one.**  The standard gate model
  (dense 27B, head 128) does not exercise the row, so a base was recorded from the r125 build on
  Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (head 256) and the r126 build compared: mean KLD **0.005073**, same-top-p **97.118 %** --
  over the absolute limits, so `--family-switch` measured a same-kernel reordering control on the spot
  (r126, `-ub 512` vs `-ub 256`) at the same point (base PPL 5.82, inside the calibrated domain):
  **0.007251 / 96.912 %**.  The candidate is no worse than the control on both metrics, which is the §46
  calibration -> **PASS**.  (Raw logs: `~/.cache/rdna-boosts/gates/prefill-logit-gfx1201-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-*`.)
* **Same-seed greedy text, `plain == draft-mtp`:** 35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M 1 GPU `-ncmoe 40` q8_0 KV

## 261024.006 (no release) -- issue #214: the reporter's box was never on the arena (r123 is not their fix), the band clamp fires on a slab-declined config, and their real regression is deep-context prefill

**Docs only so far: no patch, `release.json` or tree change; `scripts/validate-set.sh` is unaffected.**  The
maintainer re-opened issue #214 on this record.  The r123 fix stands and the campaign record stays
`archive/work/ngram-mod-host-experts/`; the two new items are `TODO.md` **#96** (the clamp gating) and
**#97** (deep-prefill depth scaling).

**What the reporter's update says** (comment 6383029106, 2026-10-24T10:19:55Z -- posted seven minutes before
the r123 ship note, so our reply raced it).  All three r120 server runs and the llama-bench runs log the
movable-boundary slab refusing to be created and `moe_cache_disable_streaming` (stock `-ncmoe` streaming);
there is no `moe_cache_report`, `h=` or `expert traffic per token` line in any of them.  On that 12 GiB card
(128k context plus the MTP draft context leaves ~540 MiB) the 2048 MiB arena floor is out of reach, so the
expert cache never ran.  Their r120 numbers are therefore the **no-arena / streaming** regime, not the arena
regime the r123 clamp is for.  Their decode was already at parity or better than upstream (write 29.0 vs
28.2, rewrite 172/183 vs 173/183, fresh 47.1/43.3 vs 44.1/43.9 t/s), consistent with the clamp being inert
for the arena there and with the wide draft being the win off the arena.

**The regression that is left is not the band, and was never diagnosed.**  Their own table holds the query
count constant and grows only the KV depth: `pp512` at d0 **+63 %** vs upstream (922 vs 566 t/s), d32k +17 %
(559 vs 479), d100k **-6 %** (274 vs 290); `read 3.8k` -6 % (920 vs 979), `read 117k` **-19 %** (360 vs 443).
A per-token cost (host experts, MoE, the arena) is constant at a fixed token count, so this localises to the
**attention / KV-read path scaling worse with depth on RDNA2**, which at 117k (quadratic attention)
compounds into the reported -19 %.  Short-context prefill is much faster and decode is fine, so "our code is
slower than upstream" is specifically "our deep-context prefill is".  That is `TODO.md` #97.  RDNA2-only
candidates, all block 05: the wide-tile `GGML_CUDA_FATTN_TILE_Q_GLOBAL` reads Q from global once per KV tile
(the +30 % figure was a shallow measurement), the per-DKQ RDNA2 tile table / launch caps / WGP occupancy,
the checked tail for the last tile -- and the `prefill_stages = !RDNA3_5` FA staging arch gate (RDNA3_5 was
measured native-better at every depth; RDNA2 was never depth-swept).  A near-full card adds one more: the
FA prefill staging arena can be refused (their peak is 12204 of 12272 MiB), which falls back to native K/V
reads.

**Upstream drift is a live alternative and it is larger than the patch set.**  Our fork point `097cf33d9`
is 2026-10-12; upstream `master` on 2026-10-24 is `71255fefc` (257 commits).  The window holds
`62df1815b` *cuda, hip: GDN chunked kernel (#29353)* -- the GDN prefill path block 03 owns -- plus
`5aeac37a3` / `99db719bd` FA fixes, `280141e6d` *CUDA: chunk graphs*, `4c1004c49` MMQ Stream-K cap,
`1a24df163` DP4A MMQ tile height and `2744e48d1` faster MMVQ.  The reporter's upstream is b11804, which
already contains all of them.  So the re-base is the first experiment, not a patch hunt; the A/B below is
what separates them.

**r123 defect this exposed: the band clamp fires on a config whose slab declines.**  `common` queries
`llama_model_moe_cache_band()` in `common_init_from_params` (before `llama_init_from_model`), when the slab
is only *armed*; the slab is created (or declines) at the first compute-buffer allocation
(`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu` -> `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`), and only then calls
`moe_cache_disable_streaming()`.  So a config exactly like the reporter's -- preflight passes, slab armed,
slab cannot be created, run streams -- is clamped anyway while its arena does not exist.  Repro (gfx1201,
35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M, `-ngl 99 -ncmoe 40 -t 8`, `--spec-type ngram-mod`, forced decline with
`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB=999999`): `ngram-mod: draft length 64 -> 15` at 0.03.631 s, then
`the movable-boundary slab does NOT fit` + `moe_cache_disable_streaming` at 0.03.652 s.  Safe (a narrower
verify is always valid) but wrong: it takes the copy-heavy win the wide draft gives off the arena (2x R9700
control: 67.6 wide vs 52.2 capped t/s).  `LLAMA_SPEC_NGRAM_MOD_BAND_CLAMP=0` is the workaround.  A correct
fix has to decide **before** context creation, because the clamp also sets the GDN `n_rs_batch` bound and the
slab's narrow verify floor; `TODO.md` #96 records the three options (defer the clamp and give the floor its
own width; a conservative preflight feasibility test; or accept the clamp and document it).

**The decline message names the wrong knob for a small card.**  Their log says the slab needs the work
buffer (768 MiB) + a 2048 MiB arena floor + the H2D-ring hole, and only 3072 MiB was available after the
1024 MiB reserve: 768 + 2048 = 2816 would fit, so the auto-sized ~1.6 GiB ring hole is what tipped it.  The
message names `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RESERVE_MIB`; `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_MIN_ARENA_MIB` (lower the floor) or
`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB` (leave the ring outside the slab) are the knobs that can make it fit there, and
the message should name them.

**The A/B reproduced the shape on gfx1201 and found one cause -- our own FA config, not upstream drift.**
Three builds, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`: our r125, upstream at the fork point `097cf33d9` (`~/llama-up-base`)
and upstream `master` `71255fefc` (`~/llama-up-head`).  Cell: 1 GPU, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M (21.1 GiB,
fully resident), `-fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -t 8 -b 2048 -ub 1024 -p 512 -n 0 -r 1`, the reporter's
constant-query depth sweep.  `pp512` t/s:

| build | d0 | d32768 | d65536 | d98304 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| r125 | **4541** | 2488 | 1620 | 1210 |
| upstream @ fork point | 2522 | 2248 | 1651 | **1345** |
| upstream @ master | 3600 | 2273 | 1661 | **1366** |
| r125 + the prototype row below | **4694** | **2954** | **2058** | **1645** |

The same ordering holds with `-ncmoe 24 MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0` (the reporter's streaming regime, our path):
r125 1223 / 1106 / 997 / 892 vs upstream 983 / 884 / 775 / 694 (base) and 991 / 884 / 780 / 707 (master) --
i.e. our host-expert path is *faster* at every depth there, so their -19 % is not that path.

**Root cause (gfx1201): the RDNA4 *band* MMA row is baked into the prefill kernel.**
`ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_rdna` (`fattn-mma-f16.cuh`) starts with two RDNA4 GQA band rows keyed on
`ncols` alone; the 64-column one returns `fattn_mma_config(512, 1, 64, 64, 64, 32, 1, true)` (16 warps,
occupancy 1).  `__launch_bounds__` is compiled per instantiation, and the query-width dispatch gives
`ncols1 = 8, ncols2 = 8` (ncols 64) to **both** the W=5..8 band and every wide prefill (`Q->ne[1] > 4`).  So
prefill runs the band geometry; upstream's row for (256,256,64) is 256 threads / occupancy 2.  Kernel trace
at `pp512 @ d98304` (`rocprofv3 --kernel-trace`, r125 vs master): total kernel 45.0 s vs 40.1 s, and the
only large component is `flash_attn_ext_f16<256,256,8,8,...>` at **28.74 s vs 19.63 s** for the same 980
dispatches -- ours `workgroup (32,16)` / LDS 36864 / private 112, upstream `workgroup (32,8)` / LDS 34944 /
private 404.  Everything else is ours (MMB, routed-compact, GDN), which is the +63..+80 % at d0.

Prototype (the row replaced by upstream's `(256, 2, 64, 128, 128, 64, 1, true)`, one line, rebuilt):
**+36 % at d98304 (1210 -> 1645), +36 % at d65536, +19 % at d32768, +3 % at d0**, and 20 % above upstream
master at d98304.  So the delivery is *not* slower than upstream at depth once the band row stops applying to
prefill; the reporter's own bias (short-context fast, deep slower) is the same shape at a smaller magnitude
on RDNA2.  The plain revert is **not** the fix: it also gives up the W=5..8 band geometry (the source row's
comment measures ~17 % for q8_0 at that band, and MTP-adaptive/ngram verifies live there).  The fix is a
query-width-keyed instantiation split (band row only when `n_q <= 8`), which changes prefill FA's KV-row
split/combine order and therefore owes `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` plus coherence -- `TODO.md` #98.

**The reporter's RDNA2 case is not this bug** (gfx1030 has no WMMA: its prefill takes the tile kernel and the
`get_config_rdna` table, which is 256 threads for ncols 64 in both trees), so #97 keeps an open RDNA2 half:
block 05's RDNA2 tile table from PR #165/r76 at depth, and their 117k per-token costs.  Their sweep is the
measurement that separates those.

**Docs:** `README.md` (the "no active arena" note gains the slab-declined class and the clamp caveat),
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §50 (same, plus the reporter's confirmation), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3
(`LLAMA_SPEC_NGRAM_MOD_BAND_CLAMP`), `patches/README.md` (blocks 05/09), `TODO.md` (#96, #97, #98).

## 261024.005 (r125) -- issue #216: the MTP draft's KV cache type follows the main `-ctk`/`-ctv`, and the draft-reserve log only fires where it is used

**Change:** **blocks 02 and 09**.  `release.json` tip `55d421582`, tree `a3379b6d0` (unchanged from
r124's block content otherwise; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green -- fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`,
applied tree == recorded tree).  One user-facing default (the draft context's KV cache type) plus one
log gating; no kernel, no allocation and no prefill change.

**The report (issue #216, gfx1201 / Windows 11 / HIP SDK 7.1.1 / 16 GiB RX 9070 XT).**  A dense Qwen3.8-27B
IQ3_S with `-c 131072 -b 4096 -ub 1024 --flash-attn on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive
--spec-draft-n-max 3` loads and answers short prompts, and aborts on the first prompt over ~1 K tokens with
`rocBLAS error: Could not initialize Tensile host: No devices found` and exit `0xC0000409` (the alternate
signature: `unspecified launch failure` in `ggml_backend_cuda_synchronize`).  The report also carried the
load-time line `keeping the flat 3584 MiB draft reserve`, which reads as if the slab or the expert-cache
arena were involved in a **dense** model.

**What the investigation established** (measurements on 1x R9700, gfx1201, headless, 10.5 K-token prompt,
the reporter's flags, no mmproj):

* **The config does not fit a 16 GiB card.**  Static device memory is **14.80 GiB** (10 951.6 MiB weights,
  2 304 target KV + 598.5 recurrent state, 512 draft KV, 788 compute, ~2 output) and the first-prefill peak
  measured **16.03-16.17 GiB**; `mmc` unaccounted (Tensile code objects, workspace pool, FA staging arena)
  is ~1.4 GiB of that.  For scale: `-c 81920` 14.74 GiB, `-c 32768` 13.37 GiB, no MTP 14.41 GiB.
* **The reporter's `-ngl` controls were no-ops.**  `-ngl` is a **layer count** and this model has
  `n_layer_all = 65` (64 trunk + the NextN block), so `-ngl 85` / `-ngl 97` offload exactly what `-ngl 99`
  does: measured `-ngl 85` peak **16.17 GiB**, byte-identical to `-ngl 99`.  `-ngl 51` (15 layers really on
  the CPU) drops the peak to **13.70 GiB**.  So "freeing 2.5 GB does not help" was not evidence against a
  memory cause.
* **The rocBLAS message is a symptom, not an OOM inside rocBLAS.**  `TensileHost::GetDeviceCount()`
  (`library/src/tensile_host.cpp`) prints it when **`hipGetDeviceCount()` returns non-success**, then aborts;
  that path allocates nothing.  It is the process's *first* rocBLAS touch, so the device was already gone --
  on WDDM an allocation set larger than the card pages into system memory and the loss surfaces later.  Our
  tree makes **zero** rocBLAS calls for this config (an `LD_PRELOAD` probe counted 0 `hipblasCreate`, 0
  `hipblasGemmEx` at 300- and 1800-token prompts, and 0 with `GGML_CUDA_MMF32=0`), so on r124 nothing in the
  target prefill can be that first touch.
* **`--fit` could not have helped either** as invoked: it declines outright when `-ngl` is set, and it only
  resizes `n_ctx` when `-c` was left at `0`.

**Change 1 (block 02): the draft context's KV type follows the main one.**  Upstream gives the speculative
draft its own KV type pair (`-ctkd` / `-ctvd`, default **f16**) and applies it unconditionally, so
`-ctk q4_0` still built an f16 draft cache.  For MTP that is invisible waste -- the draft *is* the target
model and its context only carries the NextN layer: at `-c 131072` the single draft layer held **512 MiB**
of f16 KV against **144 MiB** at q4_0, i.e. **368 MiB** a 16 GiB card cannot spare.  `common_base_params_to_speculative()`
now takes the main type unless the draft type was set explicitly (`common_params_speculative_draft::cache_type_k_set` /
`_v_set`, set by the two arg handlers), so `-ctkd` / `-ctvd` still pin anything, f16 included.  It cannot
change a generated token (the draft only proposes; the target verifies).

**Change 2 (block 09): the draft reserve is only computed and logged for a model that has host-resident
experts.**  `llama_model_moe_cache_preflight()` walks `model->moe_host_expert_bytes` and is a no-op when the
map is empty, so a dense model printed a reserve nothing consumed.  `common_init_result` now gates the
whole block on `llama_model_moe_host_expert_dev_count(model) > 0`.  No behaviour change where the reserve
is used (derived value, flat fallback and `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_AUX_RESERVE_MIB` override are identical), and
the MoE arm still prints the line.

**Gates** (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`, r124 binaries kept as the reference):

* **Same-seed greedy text, r124 vs r125, all identical:** dense 27B IQ3_S MTP n3 (q4_0 KV) and plain
  (`2bce65443284`); 35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40` MTP n3 (190.4 -> 190.8 t/s, `c502088e87e0`); 4B Q8_0
  3 GPU `-sm tensor` MTP n3 and plain (`9ec2b0fc2de4`).
* **Protocol A, four axes, `-n 3000`, bf16 KV, 1 GPU, dense 27B** -- r124 -> r125 MTP t/s: **R 65.2 ->
  65.4, P 82.3 -> 82.4, C 88.2 -> 88.2, K 98.9 -> 98.8**, plain 35.4 / 34.7 / 35.3 / 35.6, and the generated
  text identical across all three arms on every axis (`04a575ad230a` / `d2a1dae74474` / `ba9ab0795f58` /
  `a87c4318b649`).
* **The change's cost, measured rather than assumed.**  At `-ctk q4_0 -c 102400 -n 3000` three alternating
  reps gave **80.8-80.9 (r124) vs 80.6-80.7 t/s (r125)** and at `-c 8192 -n 400` **56.4-56.6 vs 56.4-56.5**,
  i.e. neutral; an earlier 3-rep A/B that showed "-2 %" was run-order drift (the f16 arm always ran first),
  which the repeat caught.  The cost is real but confined to **one arm shape**: a *fast small model under
  `-sm tensor`*.  4B Q8_0, 3 GPU tensor, `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`, MTP n3: **-1.5 %** (same binary, alternating
  A/B: 237.7 / 236.1 / 240.0 t/s with `-ctkd f16 -ctvd f16` vs 232.0 / 237.2 / 233.7 with the q8_0 draft),
  **-1.9 %** (r124 vs r125, three ordered pairs) and **-2.9 %** (the first three ordered pairs) -- call it
  **1.5-3 %, mean ~2 %** -- with identical text and acceptance.  It is **not** "the FA kernel is slower": a
  rocprofv3 kernel trace of both arms is identical in kernel names, counts and total GPU time (771.28 vs
  771.00 ms over a 60-token run, delta -0.28 ms = -0.04 %), and `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` (-1.6 %) and
  `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` do not change it.  What does change is the *graph composition*: the CUDA backend
  evaluates **1536 more `MUL_MAT` nodes** and **390 fewer `SET_ROWS`** over 200 tokens (`GGML_CUDA_GCDBG`),
  i.e. ~4 `MUL_MAT` per draft KV row write replaces 1 `SET_ROWS`, and that is per-step host work, which is
  where a 4 ms/token model notices it.  Writing a quantized KV row needs an F32 `src0`
  (`ggml-cuda.cu`'s `SET_ROWS` support list) while the f16 cache accepts f16, so the quantized draft pays
  the conversion; the **target** pays it in both arms.  `-ctkd f16 -ctvd f16` restores the old behaviour,
  and 1 GPU and `-sm layer` are neutral (-0.2 % / +0.1 %), so it is a tensor-split + fast-model tail.  A
  small model is fast enough, and a 4B spread over three cards is not a VRAM-constrained user, so this
  ships documented rather than fixed.
* `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %);
  `build-rocm/bin/test-arg-parser` OK.

**Shipped.**  `v14-097cf33d9-r125` tagged and pushed (`main` = `ef955745` code + `bcaf9b69` docs, both CI
workflows green: **Validate delivery set** 23 s, **Release patch set** 16 s); the fork branch `rdna-boosts`
was force-pushed `355417a72...55d421582` to the personal fork after a **strict re-apply verification** of the
shipped patches in a clean clone at `097cf33d9` (14/14 `git am`, applied tree `a3379b6d0` ==
`release.json.tree`; the gated build is that same tree).  Container images are built/pushed off-host by the
`radiance` watcher.  A follow-up docs commit sharpened this entry's cost measurement after the same-binary
A/B and the kernel trace (see the cost bullet above).

**Docs:** `patches/README.md` (block 02 paragraph + the two block 09 bullets), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §3
(`LLAMA_ARG_SPEC_DRAFT_CACHE_TYPE_K` / `_V`), `README.md` (block table row `0002` + a "on a card that is
close to full" note carrying the #216 budget numbers and the `-ngl` gotcha), `wiki/MTP-Quick-Reference.md`

## 261024.004 (r124) -- the Windows HIP build: int64_t `std::min`/`std::max` in the expert cache collide on one mangled name (blocks 09 + 10)

**Change:** **blocks 09 and 10**.  `release.json` tip `355417a72`, tree `221bc7dda4`;
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  No
kernel, no allocation and no default change: a build fix for a toolchain this box does not run.

**The report (issue #217).**  On Windows with HIP (clang 23 from TheRock + MSVC STL 14.51.36231 / VS 18),
r123 fails to compile `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu` in the host pass with `definition with same
mangled name '??$min@_J@std@@YAAEB_JAEB_J0@Z'`.  `_J` is `__int64`, so *both* clang's force-included
`cuda_wrappers/algorithm` (a `__host__ __device__` template selected by `enable_if(true, "")`) and the MSVC
STL `<utility>` define an inline `std::min<long long>`, and the MSVC ABI does not encode the `enable_if`:
a TU that instantiates both carries two definitions under one name.  The calls here (`std::min<int64_t>`
since r112; r92 has none) pick clang's version, the STL's own templates use theirs, and the linker/CodeGen
rejects the second definition.  Other CUDA TUs that use `std::min`/`std::max` compile on that toolchain --
the collision only fires where the STL's own instantiation is also emitted -- but ~10 of them still carry
the int64_t pattern (argmax, cpy-batch, fattn, mmvf, fattn-common, gated_delta_net, top-k, ssm-scan,
ggml-cuda, hc-mix), so the same failure can reappear in another TU (TODO #95, accepted limitation).

**The fix.**  Two `static inline` helpers at the top of `moe-expert-cache.cu` (`moe_cache_min_i64` /
`moe_cache_max_i64`, plain ternaries -- behaviour identical to `std::min`/`std::max` for `int64_t`) and the
three int64_t sites converted: the auto-arena floor in `alloc_all_locked` and the heat-coverage bound in
`moe_cache_report` (block 09, which owns the file and the helpers) and the tables-registration slack guard
in `moe_cache_tables_complete_locked` (block 10, which introduced it).  `std::min`/`std::max` stay where the
type is `int`/`size_t`.  Nothing else changed; the reporter's tested diff is what ships.

**Gates** (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`, the tree re-cut as `rdna-boosts` at
`release.json.tip`, so the release build is the one measured).  Semantics-identical by construction, and
measured: same-seed greedy text is byte-identical to r123 on the dense 4B (`-sm tensor`, 3 GPU,
`1c5d32ac537d`) and on the host-expert arm (35B-A3B UD Q4_K_M `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, `627b2ebd7792`), both
with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`; `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %); Protocol A MTP on the MoE 35B-A3B (UD Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, prose, `--reasoning off`, `-n 3000`):
plain **81.0 t/s**, `draft-mtp` **171.2 t/s** (2.11x), acceptance **0.73881**, mean len 3.22 -- identical to
r123.  Only the Linux build was run here; the Windows compile is the reporter's, against the diff that
ships.

**Shipped.**  `v14-097cf33d9-r124` tagged and pushed (tag message references issue #217); the fork branch
`rdna-boosts` was refreshed from the amended chain at `release.json.base` (strict 14/14, tree
`221bc7dda4`, tip `355417a72`, built and gated there) and force-pushed `ef13b805d...355417a72` to the
personal fork.  CI on the tag: **Validate delivery set** green (21 s) and **Release patch set** green
(14 s), GitHub Release assets `patches.tar.gz` / `rdna-boosts-all.patch` / `release.json` /
`SHA256SUMS` published.  Container images are built/pushed off-host by the `radiance` watcher.  Docs:
`patches/README.md` (block 09 bullet + the "any new int64_t min/max must use the helpers" rule),
`MANIFESTS.md` (block 09 verification gains the grep), `AGENTS.md` (critical fact), TODO **#95** (the other
HIP TUs, accepted limitation).

## 261024.003 (no release) -- TODO #80 retired: the Meta split-state lookup-count headroom sits below the delivery's re-allocation rate

**No source change, no release.**  `TODO.md` **#80** ("Meta split-state cache: 30+ lookups per node per
re-allocation", parked) moved out of the open list into **Documented, deliberately NOT fixed** (accepted
limitation): the investigation found the item is no longer an active concern.

**Why.**  The defect that opened the thread -- the reported r80 -> r82 3.5 % 4-stream regression -- was not
reproducible here (`261018.010`), and the cost the reporter then measured at the right place was the
pre-warm walk's **heap churn**, fixed in r100 (`261020.014`, block 09, `GGML_META_SS_SCRATCH`, default on).
Issue #184 was closed 2026-10-21 with his confirmation that r100 is in his production build (+1.6 %
4-stream decode, identical greedy output).  The remaining record is his ~165k cache hits per re-allocation
(30+ per node) with the note that hashing the cached 336-byte `ggml_tensor` copy to skip the `memcmp` is a
wash -- so the only lever is the lookup **count**, a recursion/pruning redesign of `calculate_split_state`
and the pre-warm walk.

**Measured on the current tree (`r123`, 3x R9700, new `archive/work/issue-184-meta-r80r82/probe-reallocs.py`).**
The reporter's own shape (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS + the shared Q8_0 MTP head, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 47`,
`-fa auto`, q8_0 KV, `-c 131072`, `-np 4`, `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 3`, four
concurrent pre-warmed greedy 192-token completions) reports **3 graph reallocations** for the whole 4.24 s
window (2 same-size + 1 changed size) with **63 graph reuses** per stream; dense 4B Q8_0, 2 GPU tensor,
4 x 128 tokens: 12 reallocations / 126 reuses.  His workload re-allocates **~230** times per run, which is
why the walk matters there and not here: at his own post-r100 16.0 ms per re-allocation (the whole
`ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph`, not just the walk) our 3 reallocations are at most ~1 % of the window, and the
lookup-count share of that is below this box's noise floor -- r100's removal of the *entire* heap churn
measured +0.29 % on this shape.

**Why not queue it anyway.**  The split-state machine is `GGML_ASSERT`-heavy and its cache feeds every Meta
split decision, so a pruning/recursion change owes the full r100 proof set (identical states under
`GGML_META_SS_VERIFY=1`, identical greedy text and prefill-logit KLD, same-binary A/B via
`GGML_META_SS_SCRATCH=0`) for a win that cannot be demonstrated on any config the delivery validates.  The
code is unchanged since r100 (`git log -L` over the walk: block 09 is the last commit that touches it), and
both knobs are already documented (`ENVIRONMENT.md` §2, `patches/README.md` block 09).

**Docs.**  `TODO.md` (table row and section removed, accepted-limitation entry added with the numbers),
`archive/work/issue-184-meta-r80r82/RESOLUTION.md` (+ addendum and a repro line) +
`probe-reallocs.py` (the probe).  `WORKLOG.md` 261020.014 stays as the r100 record.

## 261024.002 (r123) -- a draft length is a verify width: clamp the draftless n-gram speculators to the MoE expert cache's band (block 09, TODO #59 closed)

**Change:** **block 09**.  `release.json` tip `ee842ded4`, tree `e91b266d4`; `scripts/validate-set.sh`
green (fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  No kernel, no allocation and
no default change outside a config whose host experts are served by the expert-cache arena.

**The bug (TODO #59).**  `ngram-mod` + `draft-mtp-adaptive` "halves decode with host-resident experts".
Root cause: the expert cache serves a routed `MUL_MAT_ID` from its VRAM arena only up to its decode/verify
band (`moe_cache_max_tok_dev()`; **16 tokens on RDNA4**, 8 on RDNA3/NVIDIA).  Above it
`moe_cache_update_host()` returns false and the routed experts are streamed from the pinned host master on
**every** verify step.  A verify batch is `n_draft + 1` rows: `--spec-draft-n-max` is already bounded to 15
(a 16-row verify) by `LLAMA_SPEC_DRAFT_N_MAX_CLAMP`, but the **draftless** n-gram speculators had no width
bound at all — `ngram_mod.n_max` defaults to **64** with `n_min 48`, and the ngram-map family's `size_m` to
48 — so the README's own recommended combo put every ngram step outside the band.  It is a cliff, not a
slope: on 2x R9700 / Flash-Next IQ4_NL `-sm tensor -ncmoe 36` (`prompts/recall.txt`, `-n 2000 --temp 0
--seed 42`) 159.2 t/s at a 16-row verify, **55.0 t/s at 17** (repeat 55.2), 48.1 at 33; the arena hit rate
drops 0.978 -> 0.898 and the cache's counted `reaches` collapse 1086540 -> 129660 (wide steps never reach
the arena).  A deep draft also cost ~5 GiB of arena (the slab's narrow verify floor is measured at
`n_rs_batch`): 32938 -> 27814 MiB.  Measured on the documented pick: `draft-mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod
--spec-draft-n-max 9 --spec-ngram-mod-n-match 45` **73.9 t/s** uncapped vs **168.3 t/s** clamped (+128 %);
`draft-mtp,ngram-mod` 74.1 -> 160.2.

**The fix.**  A new `moe_cache_band` device query (appended to `ggml_backend_device_i`; CUDA answers
`moe_cache_enabled() ? moe_cache_max_tok_dev(device) : 0`), `llama_model_moe_cache_band()` (the smallest band
over the model's host-expert devices), and `common_speculative_clamp_ngram_n_max()`:
`common_init_from_params` clamps an **enabled** n-gram speculator to `band - 1` after the model load (where
the cache preflight's decision is known), lowers `n_min` with it (ngram-mod discards a draft shorter than
`n_min`, so a naked `n_max` clamp would silently disable it) and refreshes `cparams.n_rs_batch`.  Kill
switch `LLAMA_SPEC_NGRAM_MOD_BAND_CLAMP=0` (reproduces 74.1 t/s exactly).  A `draft.n_max` above the band
warns instead of clamping — the 15 bound is a correctness one (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §27) and equals the RDNA4
band.

**Why not global.**  Device-resident (3 GPU, `-ncmoe 0`): MTP n3 144.7 -> ngram default **378.7** t/s vs
244.6 clamped — the wide draft is the product.  CPU-compute experts (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0`): 38.5 ->
67.6 (wide) vs 52.2 capped — the weights are local, so extra rows buy amortisation; that is upstream's
shape and why the issue-#214 reporter (12 GB card, `-ncmoe 24`) sees `ngram-mod` win on a rewrite.  Both
report band 0 and are never clamped (verified: 380.2 and 68.1 t/s, no clamp line).

**Gates.**  Text purity with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44, and the reason the first
cross-run comparison looked like a text change): on the host-expert cell `plain` / `draft-mtp n3` /
ngram hand-capped at 15 / ngram **auto**-clamped all hash **`9d914f47aebb`** (1793 chars), identical to the
pre-amend build; the arm without the env var differs run-to-run as documented.  The same three hashes are
reproduced by the release build re-cut from `patches/`.  No prefill kernel or default-on approximate path is
touched (the gate was still run for the release: PASS, KLD 0.000000); the MTP controller path is untouched by
construction (the clamp only fires for an enabled n-gram type, and the MTP-only arms log no clamp).  `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §50 added; `README.md` recommended-configuration rewritten;
`ENVIRONMENT.md` §3 catalogues the kill switch; `patches/README.md` (block 09) updated.

**Campaign.**  `archive/work/ngram-mod-host-experts/` (README, evidence tables, the `run-arm.sh` harness and
its logs).  TODO **#59 closed**.  Upstream (CPU-compute host experts) has no such cliff, so no `upstream/`
candidate.

**Shipped.**  `v14-097cf33d9-r123` tagged and pushed (tag message references issue #214); the fork branch
`rdna-boosts` was refreshed from the set in a clean `~/llama.cpp` (strict 14/14 `git am`, tree
`e91b266d4`, tip `ef13b805d`, built and coherence-checked there) and force-pushed
`960c1ddc6...ef13b805d` to the personal fork.  CI on the tag: **Validate delivery set** green (21 s) and
**Release patch set** green (13 s), GitHub Release assets `patches.tar.gz` / `rdna-boosts-all.patch` /
`release.json` / `SHA256SUMS` published.  Container images are built/pushed off-host by the `radiance`
watcher.  Protocol A MTP on the MoE 35B-A3B (UD Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, prose, `--reasoning off`, `-n 3000`):
plain **81.9 t/s**, `draft-mtp` **170.8-171.3 t/s** (2.09x), acceptance **0.73881**, mean len 3.22 —
identical acceptance to r122.  `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %).


## 261024.001 (r122) -- the loader honours `--lazy-mode off` under `--load-mode mmap`, and the `-sm tensor` load uses the chunked async ring (block 00); 4 MiB staging slots

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r122` (**block 00**; the Meta uploader edits the block-09 Meta path but is
owned by block 00).  `release.json` tip `3a16b4305`, tree `cb3648871`.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree).  The fork branch `rdna-boosts` was
refreshed from the set (strict 14/14, tree `cb3648871`) and force-pushed to the personal fork at
`960c1ddc6`; tag `v14-097cf33d9-r122` was pushed (Validate delivery set + Release patch set green; GitHub
Release assets published).  `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` PASS (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %); MTP Protocol A on the MoE 35B-A3B (UD Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, `-n 3000`, prose, `--reasoning off`):
plain **77.1 t/s**, `draft-mtp` **162.8 t/s** (2.11x), acceptance **0.739** (0.867/0.739/0.610).  Container
images are built/pushed off-host by the `radiance` watcher.  No kernel change; same-seed greedy text is
byte-identical on Gemma4-E4B and Flash-Next.  Upstream candidate:
[`upstream/lazy-mode-off-resident/`](upstream/lazy-mode-off-resident/README.md).

**1. `--lazy-mode off` was defeated by `--load-mode mmap`.**  `lazy_read::add()` returns false for OFF,
so the tensor is created like any other; with `use_mmap`, `load_tensors()` gives its context a host-pointer
buffer over the model mapping and `load_data()` takes `from_mapping = use_mmap || lazy.has(cur)` — so the
PLE/engram table stayed file-backed and was faulted in on access.  The tooltip said "always keep them
resident"; the mapping won.  Measured on Gemma4-E4B (2,856 MiB `per_layer_token_embd`): max RSS 5.90 GB
with `mmap` + `auto` vs 10.03 GB with `none` + `off`; `mmap` + `off` was also 5.90 GB.

**The fix (block 00).**  Explicit `off` + `TENSOR_READ_LAZY` + `use_mmap` records the tensor in
`lazy_read::add_resident()` and gives it a dedicated `ctx_key{buft, lazy=false, resident=true}` context;
`load_tensors()` does **not** turn that context into a host-pointer buffer, and `load_data()` reads it with
the direct `read_raw` path (the `ranges` set is deliberately not used — that set gets `MADV_RANDOM`, which
measured 0.22 GB/s for a fault-in + copy).  Only the explicit OFF does this: `auto` below its 4 GiB
threshold and `on` are unchanged, so default loads do not change.  Log:
`add_resident: tensor per_layer_token_embd.weight (size = 27465 MiB) kept resident (--lazy-mode off, not mapped)`.

**2. `--load-mode none` under `-sm tensor` paid a whole-tensor pageable read.**  The loader's
`upload_backend` bailed on the Meta device (`ggml_backend_dev_is_meta(dev) -> nullptr`), so the chunked
pinned async ring was never used: the fallback allocated a whole-tensor `no_init` buffer, `read_raw`'d it,
then called `set_tensor` — no overlap (the verbose log said `device Meta() is a Meta device; using
whole-tensor uploads`).  That bail predated the Meta async setter's partial-row arm; the setter already
serves a mid-row chunk with `write_partial_row` and falls back to the sync setter for a segmented/PARTIAL
table, and the event proxy was added to fan the ring's backpressure out to the simple devices.  Removed the
bail.  Cold Flash-Next `-sm tensor` load: `none` + `off` **32.2 s -> 13.6 s**; log
`using async uploads for device Meta(), buffer type Meta(), backend Meta(ROCm0,ROCm1,ROCm2)`.

**3. Staging slots 1 MiB -> 4 MiB** (`LLAMA_LOAD_STAGE_MB`, default 4; 4 slots, so 16 MiB pinned).  Cold
curve on the Flash-Next load: **1 MiB 15.7 s, 2 MiB 13.7, 4 MiB 13.7**, 8 MiB 14.8, 16 MiB 15.2, 32 MiB
16.3, 64 MiB 16.8.  4 MiB is the plateau and scales better on a faster disk; DIO keeps its 64 MiB buffer.

**4. Load measurements** (cold page cache, load-only probe, 3x R9700, no `-ncmoe`):

| arm | load | host RSS | PLE resident |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `--load-mode none --lazy-mode off` | **13.6 s** | 29.8 GB | yes |
| `--load-mode mmap --lazy-mode off` | 23.8 s | 29.1 GB | yes |
| `--load-mode mmap --lazy-mode auto` (old) | 18.9 s | 1.6 GB | no |

Host-read-only (`-ngl 0`): `mmap` + `off` 15.7 s vs `none` + `off` 18.3 s.  On this box `none` + `off` is now
the fastest resident option; the point of the fix is that `mmap` + `off` also keeps the PLE resident, so
either load mode can be chosen for the bulk.

**5. Correctness.**  Gemma4-E4B (single GPU): `mmap`+`off`, `none`+`off` and `mmap`+`auto` all emit
`363188840c…` (67 chars).  Flash-Next 3-GPU `-sm tensor`, both with and without `-ncmoe 48`: `none`+`off`
and `mmap`+`off` both emit `d13cf4cf…`, identical to the pre-change sync path.  `test-lazy-reader` passes.
No kernel change, so the prefill-logit gate does not apply.

**6. Docs/knobs.**  `LLAMA_LOAD_STAGE_MB` in `ENVIRONMENT.md`; the `--lazy-mode` help text and the
`LLAMA_LAZY_MODE_OFF` comment now state the precedence; `patches/README.md` block 00/09; `AGENTS.md`
critical fact.  The tag, fork `rdna-boosts` refresh and container images are the normal release steps;
`release.json` names `r122` and the off-host `radiance` watcher builds the images from the pushed tag.

## 261023.006 (r121) -- TODO #94: DFlash2 drafting on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp exports the HC-averaged layer input, block 11); a slab peer copy into an ungranted range aborted `-sm layer` + `-ncmoe` (block 10)

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r121` (**block 11** for the qwen4exp layer-input export, **block 10** for the
slab peer-access grants + the staged copy).  `release.json` tip `9f353b22a`, tree `bad14d63e`.
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree == recorded tree);
`gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from aa67b58ab` **4/4** (blocks 10-13 rebuilt); `gate-prefill-logits.sh`
PASS (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %); `check-gpu-faults.sh` clean (kernel window + the arm logs).
Records: [`archive/work/qwen4exp-dflash2/`](archive/work/qwen4exp-dflash2/RESOLUTION.md).

**1. TODO #94: the reported blocker is a shape, not an algorithm.**  A DFlash2 head for Flash-Next exists
(`incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2`, Q4_K_M 362 MB) and every shape lines up with the target except one:
`src/models/qwen4exp.cpp` published `t_layer_inp[il] = res_hc`, the **wide** hyper-connection residual
(`hc * n_embd` = 10240), while `llama_context::extract_layer_inp()` requires `n_embd` per row — so the run
aborted at `GGML_ASSERT(row_floats == model.hparams.n_embd)` (llama-context.cpp:3437).  Reproduced on the
r120 base.  The head wants the **mean over the hc streams** (5 x 2560 = 12800), which is what its own sglang
capture patch does (`hidden_states.unflatten(-1, (hc, hidden)).mean(dim=-2)`), and what `deepseek4`/
`glm5-next` already export for their own DFlash paths.

**2. The fix (block 11, `qwen4exp.cpp` + `models.h`, 28 lines, no new env var).**  `graph::build_hc_mean()`
(the same 8 lines as deepseek4) and the export gated on `cparams.embeddings_layer_inp[il]` exactly like
deepseek4's — the old line was an unconditional pointer store, so an ungated collapse would have added
`hc-1` adds + a scale to every qwen4exp graph (plain decode, MTP, QSA) for a tensor nobody reads.  Capture
point settled from the reference source rather than by search: the patch inserts the capture **after** the
layer call, so `completed i` = llama.cpp's `t_layer_inp[i+1]` = the GGUF's `target_layers`, no shift.

**3. Evidence.**  `plain == draft-dflash` greedy text **body-identical on six arm pairs** (3 GPU tensor
`-ncmoe 48` on code and on recall, 2 GPU tensor, `-sm layer`, `GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV=0` host injection, and
fully device-resident experts), and pre-fix vs post-fix **plain** text identical, so the non-DFlash paths
are untouched.  Flash-Next GSQ prefill logits pre/post: PPL 1.9404 both, mean KLD −0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %.  The reduction is the right one: an env-gated stream-0-only export (removed before shipping)
measured recall acceptance length **2.41 vs 4.32**.  Acceptance is healthy, not the "broken encoder ~0.3"
the campaign's heuristic suggested — the ratio falls with the block size while mean length is the metric
(FN DFlash2 n7: code 0.293 / len 3.04, recall 0.478 / len 4.32, against the head card's own block-4
reference of 2.83-3.26).

**4. Decode (3 GPU tensor, `-ncmoe 48`, `-c 16384`, q8_0 K/V, greedy 256 tokens, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`).**
Flash-Next GSQ + the head: **code 97.2 t/s (len 3.04) vs plain 69.4 (+40 %)**, **recall 133.0 (len 4.32) vs
69.6 (+91 %)**.  Not a win on every arm: 2 GPU tensor 67.9 vs 68.8 (parity), `-sm tensor` with all experts
resident 66.2 vs 76.9, `-sm layer` (no `-ncmoe`) 57.7 vs 54.0.  `-spec-draft-n-max 3` (the head card's own
block-4 shape) is 92.1 / 115.7.

**5. A pre-existing slab defect (found while validating #94, fixed here): `-sm layer` + `-ncmoe` aborted at warm-up.**  The
slab grant fix and the staged copy are block 10; the full analysis, the driver experiments and the numbers
are in the block-10 note in `patches/README.md`.  Reproduced on the r120 base with **no drafter attached**,
so it was never a DFlash2 defect.  After the fix: Flash-Next GSQ `-sm layer` + `-ncmoe 48` runs (265 t/s
prefill, 48.4 t/s decode) with greedy text identical to its `GGML_CUDA_SLAB=0` arm, and the configs whose
grants complete are unchanged (tensor-split DFlash2 97.19 → 97.20 t/s, 27B acceptance 0.34556 / len 3.39
identical).

**6. Known limit (documented, not fixed):** qwen4exp does not export layer-input index `n_layer` (the
"output of the last layer", which deepseek4 supports) — after the loop `res_hc` may be row-gathered, so it
needs the pre-gather residual.  No DFlash2 head taps the final layer.

## 261023.005 (r120) -- issue #208: a DFlash2 draft block never reached the second draft scheduler (block 09); reuse 0 -> 97.8 %, decode +1.5 % (27B 2 GPU) to +3.7 % (35B-A3B host experts)

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r120` (**block 09** amended; **block 12** amended only to move one call site's
ownership so block 09 builds on its own -- the merged tree is unchanged).  `release.json` tip
`aa67b58ab`, tree `0fd9827d7`.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`,
applied tree == recorded tree); `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 5efc1e9f1` **3/3**;
`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean.  Record and harnesses:
[`archive/work/dflash2-draft-sched2/`](archive/work/dflash2-draft-sched2/).

**1. The report.**  [issue #208](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/issues/208)
(`@overdoingism`, r112, 1x gfx1201): the second draft scheduler (r65, `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2`) is selected
with `sched_alt_select(n_outputs > 0)` and the graph result with `gf_res_prev[n_outputs > 0]`.  That fits
MTP -- a no-output ingest graph and a 1-token draft step with an output -- but a DFlash2 draft block has
**no outputs either**: `common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash::draft()` adds the noise-block tokens with
`output = !is_dflash2`, because the selector lattice is read from the nextn embeddings, not from logits.
So both of a DFlash2 draft's graphs had `n_outputs == 0`, shared one scheduler **and** one `gf_res_prev`
slot, overwrote each other's graph every cycle, and the draft context rebuilt and re-allocated both on
every verify step.  r84's #183 fix (the allocator layout fingerprint) is unrelated and does not help;
the reporter also confirmed `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` made no difference for DFlash2, which is exactly the
symptom.

**2. Reproduction.**  Pre-fix r119 tree, temporary env-gated trace in `process_ubatch`
(`LLAMA_DRAFT_GRAPH_DEBUG`, not delivered): **0 of 362** draft ubatches reused, the injection
(`n_tokens=6 embd=1`) and the draft step (`n_tokens=6 embd=0`) both on `slot_alt=0`, matching the
reporter's "reused 0 of 100 graphs" and 0.27-0.30 ms of build + allocate per draft decode.

**3. The fix (block 09, `src/llama-context.{cpp,h}`).**  The decision moves into a new
`llama_context::sched_alt_for(const llama_ubatch &)`, and `get_gf_res_prev(bool alt)` takes it as a
parameter so the scheduler and the graph slot cannot disagree:

* `LLM_ARCH_DFLASH`: the **batch kind** decides -- the injection is the batch that carries the target
  features (host `embd` rows, or the F1 device injection with `cparams.lf_dev_inject`), so the draft step
  is `ubatch.embd == nullptr && !cparams.lf_dev_inject`.  The partition is total and exclusive for a
  DFlash draft context and behaviour-preserving for a DFlash (non-2) / DSpark draft, whose step graph has
  outputs and already took the second scheduler.
* everything else: `n_outputs > 0`, unchanged.  The batch kind must **not** be used for MTP: its ingest is
  also a token batch, so the two MTP graphs would be *merged* instead of separated (the reporter's own
  caveat, and why their experiment was not a fix as written).
* No new environment variable: the r65 `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` kill switch covers this path and now
  reproduces the pre-fix behaviour exactly (measured 94.25 vs 94.20 t/s).  Default stays on.

**4. Measurements** (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0; 27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2-Q4_K_M or 35B-A3B
UD-Q4_K_M + DFlash2-Q8_0, `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 5`, `-c 16384 -ub 2048 -b 2048
-fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -t 8`, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`, 512 greedy tokens, seed 42; clean base
vs clean fix build, only `libllama.so` differs, arms interleaved):

| arm | base | fix | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 27B, 2 GPU `-sm tensor` | 94.07 | 95.50 | **+1.5 %** |
| 27B, 3 GPU `-sm tensor` | 110.20 | 112.13 | **+1.8 %** |
| 27B, 1 GPU | 66.05 | 66.15 | +0.2 % |
| 27B, 2 GPU `-sm layer` | 60.35 | 60.70 | +0.6 % |
| 27B, host injection (`GGML_LF_DFLASH_DEV=0`) | 94.30 | 95.75 | +1.5 % |
| 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, 2 GPU | 203.23 | 210.83 | **+3.7 %** |
| 27B, 2 GPU `-np 2` | 94.20 | 95.60 | +1.5 % |
| 2-slot unified server, 2 concurrent requests | 52.50 / 97.21 | 53.05 / 99.05 | +1.0 / +1.9 % |

Draft graph reuse over the last 400 draft ubatches: 0 % -> **97.8 %** (27B 2 GPU: 177 injection + 177
draft-step of 362) and 0 % -> **97.9 %** (35B-A3B); the 2-slot server goes 29.9 % -> 86.4 / 95.0 %.  The
win is a per-verify-step host cost, so it scales with target decode speed (largest on the MoE host-expert
arm, smallest on one GPU).

**5. Gates.**  Generated text byte-identical base vs fix in every arm; dense `Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0` 3-GPU
coherence hash `1c5d32ac537d` unchanged; the **adaptive-MTP four-axis gate** (27B embedded MTP head,
`-n 3000`, reasoning pinned per axis) identical on all four axes -- 59.3/59.4, 75.2/75.3, 81.1/81.1,
87.5/87.6 t/s, acceptance 0.57070 / 0.82903 / 0.90119 / 0.99200 and text `89b8dc5d4c70` /

## 261023.004 (r119) -- PR #209: the state restore batches its device writes through the save path's pinned stage (block 12); ~15-18 % faster on 2 GPU tensor, ~2 ms slower on one GPU

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r119` (**block 12** amended; the only delivery content change is
`src/llama-context.cpp` (+54 / -9).  Blocks 00-11 and 13 are otherwise unchanged; the later blocks differ
only in their re-cut `From`/`index` lines and hunk offsets.  `scripts/validate-set.sh`: green (fresh-tarball
strict apply -> tree `64a7d1492`).  PR #209 (briansp2020) is archived in
[`archive/work/state-restore-batch/`](archive/work/state-restore-batch/) with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

**1. What the restore still paid.**  r96 (#189) batched the save side: `llama_io_write_host` queues the
deferred state reads as `ggml_backend_tensor_get_async` into one pinned stage, syncs each backend once,
then copies to the caller's buffer.  The restore side still issued one synchronous
`ggml_backend_tensor_set` per tensor piece.  A hybrid model's checkpoint is ~75 pieces; under `-sm tensor`
each one bounces through a pinned chunk and synchronizes every device.  The r96 comment said restores
measured no faster batched, but that was the r91 measurement; on r115/r118 the batched restore is faster on
more than one device.

**2. The change (PR #209).**  `llama_io_read_host` now takes the context (all three construction sites pass
`this`).  On destruction it packs the deferred pieces into the same pinned `state_stage` the save side
keeps, queues each with `ggml_backend_tensor_set_async` on the backend that owns it, and synchronizes each
backend once.  The per-tensor synchronous path stays when there is no context, a tensor's backend cannot be
resolved, the state exceeds `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB`, or with `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ=0` (or
`LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0`).  The stage is one buffer per context, so saves and restores on one context must not
run concurrently; the comment now says so.

**3. Measured (server prompt-cache restore, 1571-token checkpoint, q8_0 KV, 4 new tokens after the restore,
`prompt_ms`; 2x R9700 gfx1201, same build dir, stock r118 vs r118 + the patch; medians of the timing
samples):**

| config | stock | + patch | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flash-Next GSQ, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10` | 88.6 ms | **75.5 ms** | **-14.8 %** |
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10` | 48.8 ms | **39.9 ms** | **-18.2 %** |
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M + DFlash2 draft, 2 GPU | 68.5 ms | **58.2 ms** | **-15.0 %** |
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 1 GPU | 39.1 ms | 40.9 ms | +4.6 % (about 2 ms; one 45.4 ms sample) |

The 2 GPU tensor restores drop 15-18 %; the 1 GPU arm pays about 2 ms for the extra staging copy, which is
the cost the submitter disclosed (their 1.5 ms).  The win is the multi-device sync saving; a single device
has no sync to save.  Absolute times differ from the PR's G1 row because we do not have the shared Q8_0
Flash-Next MTP head; the no-draft Flash-Next arm and a DFlash2 draft on 35B-A3B exercise the same
target/draft `llama_state_seq_set_data_ext` path.

**4. Correctness and gates.**
* A restored checkpoint's **48 greedy tokens equal a fresh `cache_prompt:false` run** on all three 2 GPU
  configs (35B-A3B plain, 35B-A3B + DFlash2, Flash-Next GSQ).
* **Four-axis MTP A/B** (35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU tensor, `-n 3000`, `draft-mtp n3`): the generated text is
  identical stock vs patched on R/P/C/K, and so is acceptance: R 0.77335 (2095/2709), P 0.75685
  (1326/1752), C 0.88240 (2176/2466), K 0.98148 (371/378); generation 242.4/235.3/266.5/284.1 vs
  242.7/235.1/266.3/283.7 t/s.  The change is state-only, so this is the expected result.
* **Same-seed coherence** (Qwen3.5 4B Q8_0, 3 GPU tensor, 20 tokens): text identical.
* **Prefill-logit gate**: mean KLD **0.000000**, same-top-p **100.000 %** (no compute change).
* `test-save-load-state` and `test-state-restore-fragmented` PASS (the fragmented test restores a 52.4 MiB
  state through the new path).
* `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh` over the server logs and the kernel journal: clean.
* `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from b0d8e4bf8`: block 12 and block 13 build the `all` target.

**5. Docs and archive.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ` and the save/restore wording;
`patches/README.md` block 12, `MANIFESTS.md` and `AGENTS.md` record the shared stage and the verification;
the campaign moved from `wip/state-restore-batch/` to `archive/work/state-restore-batch/`.  The single-GPU
cost is an accepted limitation, not a gate failure; `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_READ=0` is the A/B arm.

## 261023.003 (r118) -- PR #206: the MTP prompt tail no longer forces a whole-path `synchronize()` (or the target's nextn readback) after every prompt batch (block 02); +1.24 % prefill with `LLAMA_MTP_INGEST_TAIL`, nothing without it

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r118` (**block 02** amended; the deliverable changes are `common/speculative.cpp`,
`src/llama-context.{h,cpp}` and `src/llama-ext.h`; blocks 03-13 change only in their re-cut `From`/`index`
lines and the hunk line numbers of `common/speculative.cpp` / `src/llama-context.cpp`, which block 02
already touches -- no later-block code changes).  Records: `archive/work/mtp-tail-readback/` (decision +
purity argument), `benchmarks/2026-10-23-pr206-mtp-tail-readback-promotion.md` (measurements).

**1. What the tail was still paying for.**  `LLAMA_MTP_INGEST_TAIL` (block 02, #143) already made the MTP
draft ingest only the last N prompt positions, but every prompt ubatch still cost two target-side things:
the target copied its nextn hidden state to the host (`~21 MB` per 2048-row ubatch on Flash-Next, and
`decode()` waited for it when another ubatch followed), and the MTP hook called
`llama_get_embeddings_nextn()` after every prompt batch -- **and that C wrapper calls
`ctx->synchronize()`**, so the host waited for both backends to go idle before it could build the next
ubatch.  (That getter-side drain is the real cost; the per-ubatch `sync_readback` in `decode()` only runs
when another ubatch follows, because `if (!mctx->next()) break;` comes before it -- recorded as a side
finding because the block-00 comment reads as if that wait always applies.)

**2. The change (PR #206, @briansp2020, plus two of ours).**  New staging API
`llama_set_embeddings_nextn_from(ctx, seq, pos)` (default `0` = every row is needed, so no other caller
changes).  The MTP impl sets it to `ingest_from - 1` and returns from `process()` before any getter for a
prompt batch that lies entirely below it; `decode()` skips that ubatch's nextn `get_async`.  Why nothing
the draft reads is skipped: an ingested row `p` reads `h(p - 1)`, and any ubatch holding a row at
`pos >= ingest_from - 1` is never skipped, which is why the threshold is `ingest_from - 1` and not
`ingest_from`.  Vision rows are always read (M-RoPE jumps the text position after an image).  Ours: the
per-row scan is gated on `cparams.embeddings_nextn` (as submitted it ran on every decode of every model,
over an all-zero array), and `LLAMA_MTP_TAIL_READBACK=0` disables **both halves**, i.e. restores the
pre-r118 behaviour with the tail still set.

**3. Measured (31,476-token prompt = prose x6, 2x R9700 gfx1201, Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS + shared Q8_0 MTP
head, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10 -c 32768 -b 2048 -ub 2048`, MTP n3, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, 2 alternating
pairs, both arms from the same build directory):**

| arm | prefill t/s | vs r117 |
|---|---:|---:|
| r117 | 1488.3 | - |
| r118 | **1506.8** | **+1.24 %** |
| r118, `LLAMA_MTP_TAIL_READBACK=0` | 1490.0 | +0.11 % (the switch restores r117) |

An earlier 3-pair series measured +1.42 % (95 % CI +0.9..+1.9); the submitter's +1.9 % (CI +0.6..+3.2)
sits inside it.  No tail: 1424.6 -> 1423.3 t/s (-0.1 %, i.e. noise; with every threshold 0 the skip cannot
trigger).  The tail's own gain goes from +4.5 % to **+6.1 %**.  A 2x2 on a diagnostic build splits the win:
the hook half (no `synchronize()`) is ~+0.6 % and the readback half ~+0.1 %, so it is the *drain*, not the
21 MB copy, on this box.

**4. Correctness.**  300 greedy tokens after the 31.5k prompt, tail 4096, 2 loads per arm: text
`98c4f67d6ed9` and **177 accepted / 364 generated** with acc/pos (0.754, 0.426, 0.270) in *every* arm
(base, r118, and the kill-switch arm) -- identical draft counts mean the draft saw exactly the same data.
Decode flat (98.31 vs 98.22 / 98.13 t/s).  Mechanism wiring checked with per-ubatch debug logging on a
15,738-token prompt: skip on -> 5 ubatches skipped / 10 read, `=0` -> 0 / 15 (the debug logging was not
shipped).  Dense 4B coherence `ba301f021e66` unchanged; prefill-logit gate mean KLD **0.000000** /
same-top-p **100.000 %** (no compute change).  No new env var on the default path; the tail itself stays
opt-in (it is still a prefill/decode trade, this only improves its prefill side).
EOF

## 261023.002 (r117) -- TODO #93: the expert cache prefers whole-table identity, so a marginal arena keeps the decode fast path (block 09); +27.6 % decode on the arm that exposed it

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r117` (**block 09** amended; the only content change in the set is +157 lines in
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-expert-cache.cu`, plus the `@@` line numbers of the later blocks' hunks in that one
file — blocks 00-08 and 10-13 apply to byte-identical files).  `scripts/validate-set.sh`: green
(fresh-tarball strict apply → tree `8cb64b69`).

**1. The cliff.**  A cache table is on the decode band's **identity fast path** only at its FULL slot count
(`t.slots == t.n_experts`); one slot short is not "almost" — it takes the remap path and pays the per-token
routing readback exactly like a table with no arena at all.  Each table's arena is rounded up to the slab
arena unit, so a budget that is "just enough" in aggregate lands **one unit per table short** and *every*
table drops off the path.  Measured (`archive/work/three-gpu-performance/`, GSQ-IQ3_XXS, `-ncmoe 48
-sm tensor`, mix30k 32358 tok, plain decode, `-n 300`, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`):

| 3 devices, plain decode | arena | identity tables | decode t/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=13800` (pre-r117) | 40845.1 of 40925.0 MiB | 0 / 432 | 46.7 |
| `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=15000` | 40925.0 | 432 / 432 | 65.0 |
| auto, `-c 40000` | 40925.0 | 432 / 432 | 65.1 |

The same cliff cost the **2-device** field arm 46.3 vs 66.4 t/s at `-c 204800` (92.4 % residency, 0 identity).

**2. The fix.**  `alloc_all_locked` now prefers **whole-table identity**: when at least 96 % of the layers
can hold their full slot count, those layers get full residency and the coldest few are dropped to **0
slots** — an existing, supported state (a layer that cannot be uniform above 0 already runs through the
scheduler's host copy) — instead of spreading the shortfall over every layer.  Selection is in the same
heat order the allocation uses (allocation order IS the eviction policy), the cost estimate accounts for the
per-table arena rounding exactly, and the placement never exceeds `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` (so it cannot
surprise a user's VRAM budget).  **The drop is capped at ~4 % of the layers**, because a dropped layer is
not free: 1 of 48 dropped is **+27.6 %**, 6 of 48 dropped is **−30 %** (that case — 2 devices, auto,
`-c 204800` with the draft — therefore reverts to the uniform plan unchanged, 93.1 t/s vs 93.4 before).
`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_IDENTITY_PREF=0` restores the pre-r117 uniform placement (A/B and bisect only).

**3. Measured (one binary, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, `-t 8`, same-seed greedy).**

| arm | pre-r117 | r117 | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 dev, `-ncmoe 48 -sm tensor`, cache 13800, plain, `-c 40000` | 46.7 | **59.5** | **+27.4 %** |
| 3 dev, same + `draft-mtp-adaptive`, `-n 1000` | 103.2 | **107.0** | +3.7 % |
| 3 dev, same + `draft-mtp-adaptive`, `-n 3000` | 101.8 | **106.8** | +4.9 % |
| 2 dev, auto, `-c 204800`, plain | 66.4 (`-c 40000`) | 66.4 | unchanged |
| 2 dev, auto, `-c 204800` + draft (6-layer drop, capped out) | 93.4 | 93.1 | unchanged (±0.3 % noise) |
| 3 dev, auto, `-c 40000`, plain | 65.1 | 65.0 | unchanged |

The arms where the change is inert (the arena already reaches identity, or the drop would exceed the cap)
are unchanged within run-to-run noise (≤0.3 %).

**4. Gates.**
* **Coherence (same-seed greedy text identity, within each device count):** dense 27B Q8_0 at depth 15746
  `-sm tensor` = `d56f08cfbcf8` at **both** 2 and 3 GPUs (identical to r116); Flash-Next GSQ `-ncmoe 48`
  `-sm tensor` plain = `40d493bbb5ac` (2 dev) / `ecf8a32bae77` (3 dev) — identical to r116.
* **Adaptive-MTP gate at `-n 3000`** on the arm the change touches (GSQ `-ncmoe 48`, 3 dev, cache 13800,
  `draft-mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod`): acceptance **0.74517 (193 accepted / 259 generated), mean len 4.06** —
  **bit-identical** with `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_IDENTITY_PREF` 1 and 0, and the same text hash.  The dense 27B
  four-axis gate is inert for this change (a dense model registers no host-expert tables, so the sizing path
  never runs); it was smoke-run on the patched binary at both device counts (8 arms, sane acceptance,
  no faults) but is not a discriminator here.
* `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh --since "60 min ago"` over the run logs and the kernel journal: **clean**.
* No prefill kernel is touched (`scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` not applicable), and the change cannot move
  a value: it only chooses which tables are resident (the dropped layer is served the same bytes through the
  scheduler's copy) — confirmed by the identical text/acceptance above.

**5. Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_IDENTITY_PREF`), `patches/README.md` block 09,
`AGENTS.md` (the identity-cliff invariant now records the fix, the 4 % cap and the kill switch),
`TODO.md` #93 **closed** (the trim-admission *warning* was not shipped — the block-13
`N · n_devices < n_vocab` rule stays a documented operator rule), and the campaign record
(`archive/work/three-gpu-performance/RESOLUTION.md` §3/§11, `evidence/identity-cliff.md`).
