## 261022.012 (r116) -- TODO #90: the `-sm tensor` model-load staging buffer is reused instead of allocated per tensor (block 08); 27B Q8_0 3-GPU load 12.7 s -> 9.5 s

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r116` (**block 08** amended; blocks 00-07 and 09-13 apply to byte-identical
files — the only content change in the whole set is 50 added / 4 removed lines in
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, plus the `@@` line numbers of the later blocks' hunks in that one
file).  Record: [`archive/work/decode-warmup-stall/`](archive/work/decode-warmup-stall/README.md) §7 (the
finding, the numbers, the tooling); code notes: `patches/README.md` block 08, `ENVIRONMENT.md`
(`GGML_CUDA_STAGE_PIN`).

**1. The cost.**  A `-sm tensor` model load uploads one tensor at a time through
`ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor_2d`'s pinned gather buffer, and that buffer was
`cudaMallocHost`'d and `cudaFreeHost`'d **per tensor**.  Measured with an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer that
attributes a HIP call to its caller (`archive/work/decode-warmup-stall/tools/hip-api-probe.c`): a 27B
Q8_0 load at 3 devices makes **678 pairs** — 2.2 s of `hipHostMalloc` + 1.1 s of `hipHostFree` of a
~10.7 s load, i.e. ~30 % of the load.  (The same interposer showed the run's `hipFuncGetAttributes`
calls are all librccl's, not ours — see the r116 sibling entry, `WORKLOG.md` 261022.011.)

**2. The fix.**  One **grow-only pinned buffer per device**, reused across the tensors of a load, kept in
a per-device slot behind the same `std::unique_lock` pattern `ggml_cuda_pin_chunk` already uses.  Retained
footprint is bounded at **64 MiB per device** (a larger tensor falls back to the one-shot allocation), the
copy is the same bytes on the same stream with a stream sync before the buffer can be reused, and
`GGML_CUDA_STAGE_PIN=0` restores the per-call allocation.

**3. Measured (same binary, `GGML_CUDA_STAGE_PIN` 0/1 alternating, 27B Q8_0, `-sm tensor`, 3 GPUs).**

| arm | wall |
|---|---:|
| `=0` (pre-r116) | 11.15 / 12.94 s |
| default (staging cached) | **9.70 / 10.22 s** |

Pinned allocations per load **678 -> 5**.  Release-build A/B in the r115-vs-r116 gate also measures the
load arm at 12.56 s (r115) vs 10.18 s (r116).  On the Flash-Next GSQ `-ncmoe 48` load the win is inside
that arm's run-to-run spread (49.4-54.3 s both ways) — claim it only for the dense/resident load.

**4. Gates.**  Same-seed greedy text **byte-identical to r115** with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` on eight
arms: 27B Q8_0 3 GPU and 2 GPU (`draft-mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod`, 200 tokens), Flash-Next GSQ
`-ncmoe 48` + MTP head 3 GPU and 2 GPU (80 tokens), and the four adaptive-MTP axes at `-n 3000`
(R reasoning on; P/C/K off) — the only differing line in any pair is the `build :` commit line.
Acceptance is bit-identical where it can be read (`llama-server`, the only instrument that prints it):
K axis 0.98214 (2694/2743, mean len 9.83) and R axis 0.47695 (2431/5097, mean len 5.29) on both builds.
No prefill kernel is touched, so the prefill-logit gate does not apply.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree `39c7614ee31b664021cd3b19e4494a465a6c1c1f`),
`scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh --since "90 min ago"` clean over the gate logs and the kernel journal.

**5. The first cut was wrong, and the gate caught it — worth recording.**  The candidate that had been
measured guarded the allocation but still freed the buffer unconditionally, so the cached buffer was
freed on first use and the next call memcpy'd into released memory: `SIGSEGV` in
`__memmove_avx512_unaligned_erms` under `set_tensor_2d` on **every** gate arm within 6 s of a load (the
earlier measurements were clean because the record patch had been split out of a larger working-tree diff
and the `if (one_shot)` free hunk landed in the *probe* patch, so the tested tree was not the saved
patch).  Folded corrected into block 08; the whole matrix above was re-run on the release build.  Lesson
recorded in the campaign README: apply the patch you will ship to a clean tree and re-measure it.

## 261022.011 (docs) -- TODO #89 closed: the "residual per-device decode stall" is a one-time lazy code-object load (0 % of decode); the load-path pinned churn is staged as #90

**Nothing in `patches/` changed; no release.**  Record:
[`archive/work/decode-warmup-stall/`](archive/work/decode-warmup-stall/README.md) (probe patch, the HIP
call-site interposer, the numbers, reproducer).  `wip/decode-warmup-stall/` is deleted (no stub) and the
`TODO` item is retired.

**1. The premise did not survive measurement.**  `#89` was opened as a *periodic* ~70 ms per-device
decode stall, ~300 ms of a ~3050 ms decode (10 % of the wall clock), with the strong suspicion of lazy
kernel module loading.  The lazy-loading half is right and the "periodic / 10 % of decode" half is not:
with the r115 probe extended by a per-`(device, op)` first-use counter (the instrument the handover asked
for), a 300-token decode on 27B Q8_0 at 3 devices shows **12** `CUDAGC_SLOW` entries summing 311 ms, all
of them inside **four launches**: the main context's 2-token warm-up (i=0: `MUL_MAT` 57/56/55 ms,
`GET_ROWS` 5, `CONCAT` 1.7, fused `UNARY` 6 per device; i=6: `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` 5.2), the MTP draft's
warm-up (`ADD` 13/12/12) and the first decode-width subgraph (`MUL_MAT` 7.3/6.5/6.4).  Every single one
coincides with a `FIRSTUSE` of that op family on that device.  **The identical 12 entries (same totals to
3 %: 301 ms) appear in a `-n 1500` run** — 5x the tokens, zero extra stalls — and the only later first-uses are
3-8 us (`ROPE`).  The 300 ms is spent *before* the prompt prefill, i.e. it is cold start, not decode:
`--no-warmup` moves the same ~320 ms onto the user's first steps, which is proof that the existing
`common_init_from_params` warm-up is what keeps it off the request path today.

**2. Mechanism, pinned.**  The time is inside a single `hipLaunchKernel` (`rocprofv3 --hip-trace`: longest
launches 117-122 ms under the profiler; the audit kernel trace shows the GPU dispatching nothing), the
first `MUL_MAT` costs the same 55 ms on a Q8_0 dense 27B and an IQ3_XXS MoE (`mul_mat_q` is one code
object holding mmq *and* mmvq — which is also why the first prefill `MUL_MAT` after a decode-only warm-up
is cheap), and ops that are *not* first uses are inflated in the same window (`RMS_NORM` 4.7-5.1 ms right
after the FA load) because further enqueues block behind a load.  `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` reproduces
the same 12 entries with the same totals, so the graph path is irrelevant; 1 GPU shows one 81 ms warm-up
stall instead of three ~110 ms ones, so it is per device.

**3. Both old leads resolved, one of them to a real win.**  An `LD_PRELOAD` interposer that attributes a
HIP call to its caller shows **every** `hipFuncGetAttributes` in the run coming from **librccl** (288
calls / 878 ms — NCCL module loads at init), not from this tree, so that lead was never about ggml.  The
`hipHostMalloc`/`hipHostFree` churn (678 pairs, 2.2 s + 1.1 s) is
`ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor_2d`'s **per-tensor** pinned staging during **model load**.  A
grow-only per-device staging buffer (<= 64 MiB retained, `GGML_CUDA_STAGE_PIN=0` kill switch) takes a 27B
Q8_0 3-GPU **load from 12.7 s to 9.5 s** (678 -> 5 pinned allocations) with byte-identical greedy text
under `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` on 27B 3 GPU (MTP+ngram, 200 tokens), 27B 2 GPU and Flash-Next GSQ
`-ncmoe 48` + MTP 3 GPU.  It is **prepared, measured and deliberately not applied** — `TODO #90`, awaiting
the maintainer's go/no-go.

**4. What was declined.**  A warm-up that covers more cannot help (the prefill-only code objects are
shape/depth dependent: at depth 16 K the 3rd prefill ubatch loads a new FA prefill variant mid-prefill,
65 ms on one device, once).  Running the warm-up per device from separate host threads would overlap the
three ~110 ms loads and save ~200 ms of a ~10 s startup — declined unmeasured as a Meta-scheduler change
for a cold-start number below the maintenance threshold; re-open only if cold start becomes a product
requirement.  Also noted for the next reader: `CUDAGC_SLOW`'s threshold is an absolute 5 ms per
child-graph launch, so on 1 GPU ordinary 4 000-node steps report 5-8 ms and the counter reads "stallier"
the fewer devices there are — normalise per node or by `FIRSTUSE`.

## 261022.010 (r115) -- TODO #51: the 3-GPU stutter is HIP graph-capture churn under the `-sm tensor` Meta backend (graph key is a data pointer now)

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r115` (**block 09** amended; blocks 00-08 and 13 byte-identical, 10-12 differ
only in `index` lines and hunk offsets because block 10's big hunk carries the key function as context).
Record: [`archive/work/graph-key-churn/`](archive/work/graph-key-churn/README.md) (diagnosis,
elimination table, numbers, reproducer, the probe patch).

**1. The symptom.**  The field 27B server (`-sm tensor`, `--parallel 3`, bf16 KV, `draft-mtp-adaptive` +
`ngram-mod`) stutters: 2494 streamed tokens at 86 t/s with ~20 gaps of **475-485 ms** per 30 s, and the
whole gap sits inside `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async`.  The all-reduce is **not** involved
(`GGML_CUDA_AR_PROFILE=1`: max 2 ms per call, spin p99 243 us — the user's `ce`-vs-`hybrid` theory is
disproved), nor memory (zero reclaim/PSI), nor power (55 W at a stall against a 250 W cap), nor PCIe
runtime PM (`active` in every sample).  Stack sampling during stalls lands in `hipGraphInstantiate` /
`hipGraphExecDestroy`; the kernel timeline shows the GPU dispatching **nothing** for the gap.

**2. The cause.**  `ggml_cuda_graph_get_key()` was `{ nodes[0], n_tokens }` — the first node's *tensor
object* address.  The Meta (tensor-split) backend re-creates its per-device *simple tensors* on every
rebuild, so that address changes on every scheduler reallocation even when the graph is identical and
points at the same device buffer, and the graph cache never warms.  Measured (same binary, 300-token
decode): 3 GPU tensor **3954 keys / 1206 captures / 484 ms instantiate** vs 67 keys / 9 ms for
`-sm layer` on the same three devices — the meta backend is the whole of it, and it is why 3 GPUs
decoded slower than 2 (3947 ms at 2 devices vs 4315 at 3).

**3. The fix.**  Key on `nodes[0]->data`, the per-device buffer address the captured graph actually
bakes in: **144 keys / 45 captures / 15 ms** and **+41 % decode at 3 devices** (+6 % at 2, unchanged at
1).  Safe by construction: the per-call `update_required` node-property check (forced by the meta's
fresh `cgraph_uid` per rebuild) recaptures on any difference, so a key collision costs a recapture, not
a mismatched replay.  This is *not* the dropped r25 PR #106 patch 0002 — that one **added** data
pointers to the object key and fragmented a warm cache; this **replaces** the unstable object address.
Kill switch `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_KEY_DATA=0`.

**4. Validation.**  Same-seed text **byte-identical** to r114 at 2 and 3 GPUs (dense 27B and Flash-Next
GSQ, resident and `-ncmoe 46`).  Adaptive-MTP 4-axis gate (`-n 3000`, R `--reasoning on`, P/C/K off):
R 83.1 → 90.9, P 97.1 → 109.7, C 105.9 → 119.0, K 99.7 → 128.1 (**aggregate 96.5 → 111.9, +16.0 %**)
with acceptance, accepted/generated counts and mean accepted length **bit-identical on every axis**.
Flash-Next GSQ 3 GPU: 91.7 → 128.3 t/s (**+40 %**), `-ncmoe 46`: 79.4 → 119.5 (**+50 %**).
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green (strict 14/14 `git am`, tree == `release.json.tree`).

**5. Left open (TODO #51 stays open, narrower).**  A residual ~70 ms per-device stall remains (~3 times
per 2500 tokens, first subgraph of a step, every op in the window inflated, unchanged by
`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`, ~2-3 % of wall time); its signature says lazy kernel module load, not
scheduling.  The deeper cache fix (stable simple tensors, or a stable child-cgraph uid so the
`uid == uid` fast path applies) is recorded in the campaign README §6.

## 261022.009 (r114) -- TODO #87 closed (DIO auto, one-launch pool staging, adaptation declined), #86 closed (foreknowledge, not churn), #88 implemented (band-split heat prior); `MOE_HOST_POOL_RAM_PCT` 85

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r114` (**block 12** amended; blocks 00-11 byte-identical to r113, block 13 re-cut
with a new `From` line and an unchanged body).  Two campaign records closed:
`archive/work/host-pool-swap-and-prefill/RESOLUTION.md` and
`archive/work/moe-admission-quality/RESOLUTION.md`.  Both campaigns left `wip/` (no stubs).

**1. `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO` is now `auto` (`#87.1`).**  The r113 default (`1`, O_DIRECT) was a hand-set guess
whose optimum *inverts* between boxes: on a RAM-rich box it throws away a page cache that could hold the whole
host expert set.  `pool_decide_dio_locked()` decides once, at the first pool build, from the numbers
`MOE_HOST_POOL_RAM_PCT` already reads — buffered iff `planned pool + host expert set <= MemAvailable`, else
O_DIRECT — and logs all three.  `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=0|1` still forces either arm.  Measured (2x R9700, 35B-A3B
Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40 --host-experts pool`, 70K prompt, `-ub 2048`): `auto` → buffered, **2103 prefill / 46.6
decode t/s**, against 2088/**22.7** for a forced `DIO=1` and 2099/49.3 for `pinned`.

**2. The pool-backed prefill staging is ONE kernel launch (`#87.2`).**  It issued one `cudaMemcpyAsync` per
expert (~200 per table per ubatch) where the pinned-master path has always staged a whole table with a single
`moe_cache_stage_kernel`.  That kernel now takes a pool source: the per-expert snapshot encodes `>= 0` arena
slot, `<= -2` pool slot (`-v-2`, read from the pool's UVA alias), `-1` in neither tier (the host copies those,
each being a separate mapping/disk read).  **2103 vs 1564 t/s prefill** (`MOE_HOST_POOL_STAGE_BATCH=0`) = +34 %,
decode flat — this is the rest of the gap to `pinned`, and it is larger than r113's estimate because that
estimate was taken on a config where the staging was not crossed.  The pool now stages within 0.3 % of `pinned`.

**3. Long-session adaptation: measured and declined (`#87.3`).**  On a real long, topic-shifting trace the
oracle-layout ceiling is 7.45 MiB/token of L3 reads, a layout built for the *new* topic is 7.55, and one built
for the *previous* topic (the delivered case) is 8.05 — so the whole prize is ~6 % of the L3 traffic per shift,
while every churning policy costs several times that (`pool-retire` 24.6 MiB/token; re-admitting the arena
victim trades 32.8 GiB of copies for 8.7 GiB of L3).  The only candidate left is a periodic bulk re-rank,
bounded by that 6 %; not implemented, and the numbers are the bar.

**4. `MOE_HOST_POOL_RAM_PCT` 80 → 85** (maintainer's call): the FRAC wants more than the ceiling allows on the
30 GiB field box (32.6 GiB host set), and 85 % of `MemAvailable` pins ~2 GiB more of it while staying clear of
swap.  This is the ceiling that turns an oversized pool into a *trim* instead of a silently failed
`cudaHostAlloc` per table.  It binds only on a tight box (inert on the 184 GiB primary box: 147 GiB of ceiling
against a 14.9 GiB pool), and the reference point is that box's own FRAC sweep, which pinned **26.0 GiB** with
0.3 GiB of swap — 85 % of its `MemAvailable` allows ~24.6 GiB, below what it already tolerated.  **Not
re-measured on the tight box with the r114 binary** (the box's checkout predates r113, so an A/B there needs a
fresh build); the soak command is in `ENVIRONMENT.md`.

**5. TODO #86 closed: the gap is FOREKNOWLEDGE, not admission or churn.**  Step 0 landed in the replayer:
`--seed none|heat|probe:N|sidecar:<path>` (mirrors `apply_heat_seed_locked`, including `count=ghost=last=0`),
`--churn on|off` (a miss may take an EMPTY slot but never evicts) and `--score-band all|decode`.  The 2x2 on
two real 35B-A3B traces, 43.8 % residency: eviction is worth **+2.6 pts** unseeded and **+11.9** with a real
prior — i.e. churn is refuted as the problem — while the same policy with an oracle prior gains **+13.2 pts**
(0.8139 → 0.9461).  The delivered configuration (heat map on, its default) measures **`h=0.8718` on the GPU**
and sits on the whole-trace `static` line (0.8765); the campaign's 11-pt gap was measured with
`MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0`, which is not a shipped configuration.  What is left is prior *quality*: the persisted
map's top-112/table covers 71.8-80.1 % of the decode mass against a same-workload map's 92.2-80.3 % and an
oracle's 95.4 %, and the prior's largest defect is **band mixing** — one counter for both bands means a
5256-token prefill outweighs a 128-token decode by 41x, and restricting that same map to its decode component
takes its coverage to **95.3 %** (the oracle's).  #86 itself shipped no C++: that lever is item 6 below, done in
the same release.

**6. TODO #88 — the heat prior is split by band, and it is worth real disk time.**  `t.heat` was ONE counter
fed by both bands, and its consumers want opposite rankings: the **arena** serves the decode/verify band, the
**host pool** stages whole tables *for a prefill*.  A prefill ubatch routes ~`n_tok` experts, so on a
5256-token prompt the prefill outweighed the decode **41x** and the arena was seeded from a nearly uniform
distribution.  Shipped: a `heat_dec` counter (decode host tally + the sampled identity decode device tally,
through its own `heat_dec_dev` mirror), `heat_rank_vec()` for every heat-driven ARENA decision (the seed and
the heat-ordered layer placement), the combined vector kept for the pool's bulk layout, and sidecar format
**MHT2** (`all` + `dec` per table).  **MHT1 still loads with `dec = all`** (the pre-r114 behaviour), so no map
is invalidated and nothing aborts; the split simply re-learns as the map is rewritten.

Measured on the GPU with the **same** map in both arms — the decode band zeroed in one copy, everything else
identical (35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU tensor `-ncmoe 40`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=4096` = 43.8 % residency):

| prompt | ranked by combined | ranked by DECODE | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 284-token (`code-reasoning-mixed`) | `h=0.8747` | **`h=0.8862`** | +1.15 pt |
| 5256-token (`prose-rdna-boosts`) | `h=0.8698`, 18798 evictions | **`h=0.8948`**, 12402 evictions | +2.50 pt |

Offline (decode band, the band the arena lives in; the runtime's `h=` also counts the prefill, which dilutes
it): 0.9047 → **0.9400** and 0.8347 → **0.9397**, covered mass 91.7 % → 95.0 % — i.e. at the static oracle's
line (0.9535) rather than 4-10 pts below it.  **In disk time** (this box's SSD peaks at **~1.8 GB/s**, so
1 MiB/token ≈ 0.55 ms/token is the L3 floor): the long-prompt arm goes from **48.1 → 17.6 MiB/token**, i.e.
from **~26 ms/token of unavoidable disk read (~38 t/s ceiling) to ~9.5 ms/token (~105 t/s)** — the prior was
spending more time on the SSD than the whole decode was getting.  Short prompt: 27.7 → 17.5 MiB/token
(~15.0 → ~9.5 ms/token).  Purity: greedy text byte-identical across the r114 build, a decode-ranked v2 map and
a combined-ranked one (735 chars, one hash), `MOE_HOST_POOL_VERIFY` clean, `gate-prefill-logits.sh` KLD
0.000000 / same-top-p 100.000 %.  Landed in **block 12** (its r111/r113 amendments already own the seed and
pool-ranking functions; see `patches/README.md`, "Facts that span blocks").

**Two instrument defects fixed (both had produced published numbers).**  (a) `load_heat_sidecar` did not
normalise the role name (sidecar `blk.0.ffn_gate_exps.weight` vs trace `ffn_gate_exps.weight`), so every lookup
missed and `--pool-init sidecar-complement` silently fell back to the **oracle** — the arm r113 quotes as "a
real `.moe-heatmap` prior = 237 MiB, the same as the oracle" was the oracle twice, so **that r113 claim is not
established** and must be re-measured before it is quoted again.  A sidecar matching no table is now a hard
error and a missing table degrades to expert-id order, never to the oracle.  (b) `--mass-band` was not applied
to the pass loop, so the arena policies were scored on all bands while `covered%` came from the decode band
(which made `static` look *worse* than `shipped` on a long prompt: 0.7553 vs 0.8498) — now `--score-band`.

**Purity.**  Greedy text byte-identical across `pinned` / pool / `DIO` 0 and 1 / staging on and off (one hash
at `-n 32` and at `-n 200`), `MOE_HOST_POOL_VERIFY=1` clean (0 mismatches), `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh`
green (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p 100.000 %).  A pool fill serves byte-identical bytes, so placement cannot
move a value.  `patches/` + `release.json` regenerated; `validate-set.sh` green.

## 261022.008 (r113) -- the host pool is a LAYOUT, not a churning cache; TODO #65 retired

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r113` (**block 12** amended; blocks 00-11 byte-identical to r112, block 13 re-cut
with a new `From` line and an unchanged body).  Canonical tip `74d6310a0`, net tree `186cf7019…`.
Campaign record, the offline model and the measured-and-dropped candidates:
`archive/work/host-pool-layout/` (`README.md`, `RESOLUTION.md`, the harness and the logs).  This closes
**TODO #87**'s disk-I/O half and **retires TODO #65**.

**What was wrong.**  `--host-experts pool` was making the disk serve bytes that were already in pinned RAM.
Two independent causes.  (1) The pool's **content** was expert-id order: it was prewarmed before any tally
existed, then re-ranked by the *prefill* tally — which is nearly uniform, because a prefill routes every
expert.  (2) The **whole-table prefill staging bypassed the pool** entirely (so every ubatch re-read the
entire host expert set from the file) and the demand path evicted a pool resident on every arena fill and
re-read the evicted arena expert back into the pool.

**The one instrument that decided it.**  `scripts/moe-trace-replay.py` grew a **two-tier** model (arena +
pinned pool + mapping/disk, `--pool-frac`, five pool policies, and `--pool-init sidecar:<file>` which reads a
real `MHT1` `.moe-heatmap` prior — the `#86` step-0 instrument).  Replaying a real `MOE_EXPERT_TRACE` of the
field config (10.5K prompt, 512-token decode, 144 tables) at the run's own geometry (arena 369 and pool 409
slots per table) put a **15x** difference on the pool's content — expert-id 3571 MiB of L3 reads over 451
decode tokens, heat-ranked arena-complement **237 MiB**, oracle 237 MiB — and only **0-246 MiB** across
every eviction/hand-over policy.  That is why the fix is a layout, not a policy.

**What shipped (block 12, `moe-expert-cache.cu`).**

1. **Layout**: `pool_rank_experts_locked` (heat prior > prefill tally > expert id) and
   `pool_rerank_from_heat_locked` place the pool as the **arena's complement**, in bulk, at sizing (after the
   heat/prefill seeds) and at the first decode-band pass.  The old flat tally re-rank
   (`pool_rerank_from_tally_locked`) is gone.
2. **No churn on the demand path**: `pool_peek_locked` + `pool_fill_empty_locked` — a resident expert is the
   source, a miss takes an EMPTY slot, otherwise the per-table pinned bounce serves it.  The arena victim is
   never copied into the pool, so the background eviction-prefetch worker and `MOE_HOST_POOL_BGFETCH` are
   gone.
3. **The prefill staging reads the pool** and fills empty slots, so later ubatches find them there.
4. **`MOE_HOST_POOL_RAM_PCT`** (new, default **80**): the pool is a percentage of the model's HOST EXPERT SET,
   which says nothing about what the box can pin — an oversized pool fails every table's `cudaHostAlloc`
   silently and falls back to the bounce path.  This caps the whole pinned pool at 80 % of `MemAvailable`
   (measured once at the first pool build), trimming per table with one WARN; `0` disables.

**Measured (gfx1201, 2x R9700, IQ4_NL Flash-Next field config `-ncmoe 48`, MTP n7, `--cache-ram 16384`,
70K-token prompt, 128-token decode, one build).**

| arm | prefill t/s | decode t/s | pool h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pre-change, `DIO=1` (the default) | 39 (still prefill at 27 min) | -- | 0.2609 |
| pre-change, `DIO=0` (128 tok, HEAD) | 447 (10.5K) / 581 (70K) | 46.6 (10.5K) / 30.6 (70K) | -- |
| **post-change, `DIO=1` (default)** | **218 (10.5K) / 287 (70K)** | **22.7 / 23.1** | 0.9183 / 0.9044 |
| **post-change, `DIO=0`** | **579 / 733** | **53.7 / 53.7** | 0.9183 / 0.9044 |
| `pinned` (reference, unaffected) | 853 (10.5K) / 836 (70K) | n/a / 57.5 | -- |

Pool evictions 4600 -> **0**.  The `DIO=1` remainder is the fraction of each table no tier holds (FRAC 80
leaves 20 %), which a prefill ubatch re-reads; `DIO=0` (page cache) or FRAC 100 removes it.

**Dropped after measuring (kept in the campaign record).**  `pool-swap-slot` — the literal "the victim takes
the pool slot the incoming left" — was implemented and cost **2x decode** (25.9 vs 52.8 t/s, identical text
and acceptance, 6259 swaps x 2 extra strided copies) for 0 MiB of L3.  Write-over-the-weakest-candidate (the
maintainer's proposal) is the cheapest moving policy (1 copy, 105 MiB of L3 saved in the model) and is still
a copy per arena eviction for a gain the layout makes irrelevant.

**TODO #65 retired.**  The r67 residual ("IQ4_NL field (MTP) + `--host-experts pool` decode collapses", 2.1
t/s, never re-picked-up) does not reproduce: the config decodes at 30.6 t/s (70K, 32-token arm) with buffered
fills on r112 and 53.7 t/s after this change, against `pinned` 34.9 then 57.5.  What it was reading as a
pool memory shortfall is the layout + `DIO` interaction above.

**Gates.**  `validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 14/14 `git am`, applied tree `186cf701…`);
`gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from c9b12e988` (blocks 12/13); `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS**
(0.000000 / 100.000 %); 96-token greedy continuation **byte-identical** between the pre- and post-change
binaries on 35B-A3B Q8_0 `-ncmoe 20 --host-experts pool` with `MOE_HOST_POOL_VERIFY=1` clean; the RAM clamp
verified by forcing `MOE_HOST_POOL_RAM_PCT=5`.

**Known follow-ups (TODO #87 keeps them separate from the closed disk-I/O half).**  `DIO` auto-selection from
`MemAvailable`; a pool-aware prefill staging kernel (one launch instead of one copy per expert — the rest of
the prefill gap to `pinned`); long-session pool adaptation.

**Docs with it:** `ENVIRONMENT.md` §1.2.1 + the variable table, `patches/README.md` block 12,
`archive/work/host-pool-layout/`, `TODO.md` (#65 removed, #87 updated and the list re-ordered).

## 261022.007 (r112) -- POOL-mode defaults: `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC=80`, `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=1`

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r112`, **block 12** amended (blocks 00-11 byte-identical to r111; block 13
re-cut with a new `From` line and an unchanged body).  Two default values only -- no code-path change, and
the `pinned` default mode is untouched.

`--host-experts pool` exists for one case: the host expert set does **not** fit in RAM.  Its r111 defaults
(25 % pool, buffered fills) were inherited from the r35 era, when the pool sat *next to* a pinned master and
the page cache was the real tier.  On a memory-tight box that shape is wrong twice over: the pool only holds
a quarter of the working set, and the page cache tries to hold a second copy of the same bytes, which is what
pushes the box into swap.  r112 sets `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC=80` and `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=1` (O_DIRECT, no page
cache), measured on the field case (gfx1100, 24 GB VRAM, **30 GiB RAM**, 35B-A3B **Q8_0** = 37.8 GB,
`-ncmoe 40` = 31.9 GiB of host experts, 2000-token greedy runs):

| config | pool | swap | decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| r112 defaults (`-ncmoe 40`) | 26.0 GiB | 0.3 GiB | **78.3 t/s** |
| r112 defaults (`-ncmoe 36`) | 23.4 GiB | 0.3 GiB | 75.2 t/s |
| r111 defaults, 25 % buffered (`-ncmoe 40`) | 8.2 GiB | 0 | 48.6 t/s |
| `pinned` (`-ncmoe 40`, same box) | 0.8 GiB (the pinned allocation FAILS) | 15.9 GiB | 2-3 t/s |

80 % is the knee (90 % measured 71.8 t/s *and* started swapping), and gfx1201 is unaffected (184 GiB RAM,
`-ncmoe 40`, 2-GPU tensor: 115.8 t/s vs 115.2 for `pinned` -- the arena is fully resident, so nothing fills).
Texts stay identical across every arm and every FRAC/ncmoe combination tested (2000-token runs at
`-ncmoe` 36 and 40 byte-identical to each other and 200-char-prefix-identical to the r111 arms).

**Known follow-ups (unchanged, `TODO.md` #87 / `archive/work/host-pool-swap-and-prefill/`):** the buffered fill
(`MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=0`) still SIGSEGVs in the background pool worker at high FRAC on a memory-tight box --
now opt-in only; a prefill-band access must not fill/evict pool slots (the first prefill is inherently a full
O_DIRECT read: ~10 s on that box, which is why a short prompt shows ~0.6 "prompt t/s" while a 1400-token
prompt measures 49 t/s); and the arena-evict ⟷ pool-admit LRUs are still independent.

**Docs with it:** `ENVIRONMENT.md` §1.2.1 (defaults, rationale, the knee, the defect note), `AGENTS.md`
pool critical fact, `patches/README.md` block 12, the campaign README, TODO #87.

## 261022.006 (r111) -- `--host-experts pool` drops the full pinned master (TODO #55, phase 3)

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r111`, **block 12** amended (blocks 00-11 are byte-identical to r110; block 13
is re-cut with a new `From` line and an unchanged body).  Canonical tip `0349d6b4af5ff2bbcf88d1c4631599a625df0d53`,
tree `e51b1023a42b1183c3fca8b93be677ffa4cb194b`.  The fold went into **12** rather than 09 for the reason
recorded in `patches/README.md` ("A block owns its code"): it depends on block 11's fused / `-sm tensor`
slice geometry (`table_t::n_slices`), so a block-09 fold would have needed a second, pre-fused pool path
that block 11 then had to re-amend.  Campaign record, measurements, gates and trade-offs:
`archive/work/host-expert-master-drop/` (`README.md`, `RESOLUTION.md`); the diff is also there as
`master-drop.patch`.  Gates at promotion: `validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict `git am`, tree
`e51b1023…`), `gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 8bb85cc82` → blocks 12/13 built clean, 0 failed.

**What the mode does now.**  `--host-experts pool` keeps its bounded pinned budget and gives up the
master: host expert tensors are placed in the **read-only model mapping** through a new per-device host
buffer type (`ROCm_HostMap`, host + device, so the scheduler still puts the `MUL_MAT_ID` on the owning
GPU), and every GPU read is served through the pinned pool -- or a per-table pinned **bounce ring** when
the pool declines (a slot held by the background worker, a geometry that does not fit a slot).  The
cold-UVA serve and the device-side gather stand down for a pageable master (they read the master in
place, issue #116), and `moe_cache_gather_host` already declined on `host_dev == nullptr`.  The reader
inventory that had to become pool-aware: the eager fill, the fused/sliced fill, the identity fill, the
prefill/heat seeds, the whole-table staging (`moe_cache_stage_table`, which now serves the pre-sizing
prefill too) and the scheduler's used-expert copies (`moe_cache_upload_pageable`, wired into
`set_tensor_async`/`stage_upload`/`stage_gather`).  `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC` stays 25 %; `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=1`
is the disk-only tier; a non-mapped load (`--load-mode none/dio`) keeps the pinned master and warns.

**Result.**  `RssShmem` 18.6 -> **6.8 GiB** (35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, `-ncmoe 40`, 18 662 MiB of host experts,
1x R9700) and 40.8 -> **11.2 GiB** on the 100 GB Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS (2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48`),
the difference sitting in reclaimable page cache (18.5 / 26.0 GiB).  FRAC 50 pins 10.2 GiB and FRAC 100
reproduces the old footprint, so **the pinning is a knob**.  Under a 12 GiB or 8 GiB cgroup (MemoryMax,
no swap) the `pinned` arm is OOM-killed (rc 137) and the `pool` arm runs at 93.3 / 93.4 t/s; at 6 GiB the
pool arm needs `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC=10` and then also runs (93.6 t/s).  That is the "host expert set larger
than RAM" case the TODO asked for.

**Gates (all green, ROCm 10.1.0, gfx1201, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`).**  Generated text identical to the
`pinned` arm on: 1 GPU `-ncmoe 40`; 2 GPU `-sm tensor` plain and `--spec-type draft-mtp`; 3 GPU tensor;
gemma4 26B-A4B Q8_0 (the fused `ffn_gate_up_exps` tables); Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS.  Prefill-logit KLD
(2 GPU tensor, 35B-A3B, wikitext `-c 512 --chunks 8`, base recorded on `pinned`): **mean KLD -0.000000,
mean Δp 0.000 %, RMS Δp 0.001 %, same-top-p 100.000 %**, recorded PPL 6.2080.  `none == draft-mtp`
holds on both arms.  `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID` 947/947 (3/3 backends).  Throughput: decode parity
everywhere (97.9/97.6; 111.0/111.2; 216.2/216.4 MTP; 18.5/18.7 at 3 GPU; 73.0/73.2 gemma4; 56.5/55.7
Flash-Next), prefill -1..-6 % except **B=1 pp512 on the 2 GPU tensor config -34 %** (165.7 -> 109.0 t/s): a
single 512-token ubatch stages the whole expert set once and dropping the master adds one host memcpy of
it.  Decode never pays it (the band is served by the arena/pool).

**Disk tier, measured** (1 GPU, arena forced to 4096 MiB so the pool misses): buffered `pool` 41.8 t/s
with 18.0 GiB of page cache; `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=1` (nothing cached, every miss a disk read) **7.5 t/s**.
That is the honest shape of a third cache level -- and the reason the fraction knob exists.

**Three PRE-EXISTING bugs fixed en route** (all reachable only once the pool became the sole host source):
(1) `pool_dio_read` used a shared `static` bounce buffer while the background prefetch worker reads the
GGUF without `g_mutex`, corrupting the tail of an expert (~520 KiB into 576 KiB, variably) -- found with
a new `MOE_HOST_POOL_VERIFY=1` byte-compare against the mapping, fixed by `thread_local`; (2) `g_host_pools`
was a static `std::map` touched by the DETACHED worker, so at exit the map was destroyed under a worker
still inside a slow (DIO) read -> `double free or corruption` in `pool_reap_locked`, fixed by leaking it
like the worker's mutex/cv/queue; (3) the AUTO pool budget was a running `+=` over every preflight call
(`--fit` probe + real load + draft = 3x) AND divided by the host tensors registered SO FAR (pools are
created lazily during sizing), so FRAC 25 pinned 75 % of the host set -- fixed by deriving the total from
the per-device MAX and giving each pool `frac %` of its own experts.  Bugs (1) and (2) are independent of
this campaign and should be kept even if the master-drop is not promoted.

**Known limitation found after the tag (gfx1100 field session, 2026-10-22).**  On a box whose RAM is smaller
than the model (fingon: 7900 XTX, 24 GB VRAM, **30 GiB RAM**, 35B-A3B **Q8_0** 37.8 GB) the mode works and
produces byte-identical text in every configuration tested (`-ncmoe` 28/32/36/40, pool/pinned, FRAC
10/25/50/75/90, DIO on/off) — but **the buffered pool at `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC=75` SIGSEGVs in
`pool_bg_worker`** (2/2, `memcpy` from the model mapping, `error 4`), while `MOE_HOST_POOL_DIO=1` at the same
FRAC and the low-FRAC configurations are clean.  That is a defect to fix (r11x), not a tuning item: tracked
as **TODO #87** with the campaign `archive/work/host-pool-swap-and-prefill/` (which also carries the two design
questions: prefill must not evict pool entries, and the arena eviction ⟷ pool admit swap).  Field numbers
for the record: `-ncmoe 32 pinned` 83.7 t/s decode / 492 t/s prefill (host set fits in RAM, pool is pure
cost, as the default-on policy intends); `-ncmoe 36 pool FRAC 75 + DIO` 74.4 t/s decode with **zero swap**
and 49 t/s prefill on a 1400-token prompt (the stable disk tier); `-ncmoe 40 pool FRAC 25` 48.6 t/s;
`-ncmoe 40 pinned` degenerates (the pinned allocation fails, 15.9 GiB of swap, 2-3 t/s).

**Docs with it:** `ENVIRONMENT.md` §1.2.1 rewritten (the "it does not reduce host RSS yet" paragraph is
gone; `MOE_HOST_POOL_VERIFY` and `LLAMA_HOST_MASTER_PINNED` are documented), `AGENTS.md` gains a
`--host-experts pool` critical fact and its pinning fact is qualified, `patches/README.md` gets the block-12
entry, and `TODO.md` #55 is closed.  `MOE_HOST_POOL_FRAC` stays **25 %** by decision (frees page cache to
back the reads so the disk is hit less often); tuning it and the prefill staging cost is a follow-up
session.

## 261022.005 (r110) -- the expert cache gets a policy instrument, and its two host-tally gaps close (TODO #61, #64)

**Shipped:** `v14-097cf33d9-r110`, block **09** amended (blocks 10-13 are re-cut with a new `From` line
and the same bodies; blocks 00-08 are byte-identical).  **No behaviour/throughput claim on the default
path and no new default-on feature**: the changes are one opt-in diagnostic, two host-tally fixes, a
reporting addition and one dead function removed.  Tree `5abfa8e4…`, ROCm 10.1.0, 2x R9700 gfx1201.
Record: `archive/work/moe-cache-coverage/RESOLUTION.md`.

**TODO #61 P1 -- the offline routing-trace replayer (the campaign's missing instrument).**  The campaign
had only an aggregate heat vector, which cannot answer thrash/prefetch/window questions.  Now
`MOE_EXPERT_TRACE=<path>` dumps every `mul_mat_id`'s raw routing and `scripts/moe-trace-replay.py`
(stdlib, no model, no GPU) scores policies against it.  Two bands, two sources, neither able to disturb a
captured graph: DECODE from the scheduler hook (the ids are already on the host -- no readback, no sync),
PREFILL from the device entry (the staged prefill never brings the ids to the host; prefill is never
captured, so one readback per op is legal).  A fully-resident (identity) table's decode band is not
traced -- it cannot miss.  Opt-in only; `MOE_EXPERT_TRACE_MIB` (default 1024) caps the file.

**TODO #61 P2 -- the per-layer capacity quota is measured and NOT shipped.**  On a real trace
(Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=4096` = 43.8 % residency,
296-token prompt, 128 decode tokens, `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` so the replayer's unseeded model is
comparable): shipped `h` **0.8505** modelled vs **0.8248** logged (the model has no persisted prior, no
seed and no arena shortfall -- judge deltas), quota **+0.0025 h / -1.6 % traffic**, oracle static top-f
0.8765, static bound 96.14 % of the routed mass.  Per-layer routed mass is flat in the decode band, so
the water-filled slot counts are uniform (113/table) except where the UD quant promotes a layer's
`down_exps` to Q6_K (106).  That is the campaign's own 0.3-0.5 pt prediction, inside the trace-to-trace
spread, for a sizing change that must preserve the layer-uniform re-size, the re-arm slot table and the
`slots >= n_used*n_tok` decline bound.  Closed unshipped; the replayer's useful finding is elsewhere:
the shipped policy sits **~11 pts of hit rate below an oracle static placement**, which is an
admission-quality question (a history-driven prefetcher), not a slot-allocation one.

**TODO #61 P3 -- metric parity.**  `moe_cache_report` now prints the resident set's **covered mass**
against *this session's* routing (the `heat_delta` basis -- the persisted prior is a month-long aggregate
and hides the session's own distribution), the **global-top-f static bound** at the same slot count, and
the resident/expert slot counts, beside the existing `h` and expert MiB/token.  Field example
(35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, `MIB=4096`, 296-token prompt): resident 77.8 % of the session's routed mass vs a
98.2 % static bound.

**TODO #64.1 -- the host pool's warm order.**  `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_PREFILL_SEED`'s in-run tally only
accumulates on the *eager* prefill path, and the default staged prefill intercepts the upload, so
`pool_prepopulate_locked` warmed the `--host-experts pool` pinned tier in **expert-id order** and
`pool_rerank_from_tally_locked` was an uncalled function.  A new `pool_rank_from_prefill_locked()` folds
the **device** prefill tally in once, at the first decode-band pass after a prefill (gated on a
prefill-op counter so a pre-warmup pass cannot consume the one-shot), and feeds both consumers.  Verified
on 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40 --host-experts pool`: pools created early are re-ranked ("pool re-ranked from
prompt tally ... 144/207 slots") and later ones prewarm with the new log's `ranked by the prompt tally`
instead of `ranked by expert id (no tally)`.  With `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` the historical id order remains.

**TODO #64.2 -- a fully-resident table's decode routing is now tallied, sampled.**  An identity table
takes the fast path that never reads the routing back, so its decode traffic contributed nothing to the
heat prior.  It is now tallied at the device entry, one op in `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DECODE_SAMPLE`
(default 64, `0` off), **weighted by the period** so the counts match the exact tallies; every other
table is still tallied exactly on the host (never double counted).  **The heat mirror is now
pre-allocated at sizing**, because the decode band is a captured graph and a `cudaMalloc` there aborted
with `operation failed due to a previous error during capture` (found and fixed in this session).  A/B on
fully-resident gemma4-26B-A4B Q8_0 `-ncmoe 99`: sampled 942 092 150 vs 942 063 478 unsampled heat total
= the 28 672 counts the decode band now contributes (was 0).

**TODO #64.3 -- `moe_cache_observe` removed** (dead since `moe_cache_heat_observe` superseded it); the
stale header comment that claimed the dispatch called it is corrected.

**The new default-on knob is measurement-side only, and its overhead is measured at zero.**  It is
explicitly **not** a new default-on performance feature (nothing in this amendment claims throughput):
*Benefit* — an identity table's decode routing was previously invisible to the heat prior (prefill-only),
so the prior a *later, partially-resident* run of the same model starts from was skewed to prefill.  When
every table is fully resident the tally changes nothing in that run by construction (everything is
resident); it warms the sidecar for the next run.  *Overhead* — one relaxed atomic increment per decode
op (per layer x role, i.e. ~120-144 per token) and, for one op in 64, one mutex + a small map lookup +
one 128-thread kernel launch (~1.9 sampled ops/token): fully-resident gemma4-26B-A4B Q8_0
(`-ncmoe 99`, 2 GPU, 400 tokens, `--temp 0`) measured **75.8 / 75.7 t/s** at sample=64 and
**75.7 / 75.8** at sample=0, i.e. inside the +/-0.13 % run-to-run noise.  `0` disables it.

**TODO #86 opened (scoping) — the campaign's follow-on.**  The replayer's real number is the ~11 pt gap
between the shipped policy and an oracle static placement, which the slot-quota question was never about.
New `archive/work/moe-admission-quality/` (TODO #86, closed in r114), offline-first: step 0 adds a `--seed heat|trace` model to the
replayer so the gap decomposes into *foreknowledge* (the persisted prior) and *churn* (eviction); only a
candidate that wins there is written in C++.  Its first measured warning is already in hand: pass-start
pre-admission *lowers* `h` (0.7846) while cutting traffic 25 %, so prefetch is not automatically a win.

**Gates.**  Same-seed coherence A/B on the cache-on config (35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU `-sm tensor
-ncmoe 40`, `MIB=4096`, `-n 48 --seed 42 --temp 0`): **byte-identical**, `206 chars sha=cf7f8b23f404`
before and after.  `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh`: **PASS**, mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %.  Decode purity smoke (35B-A3B Q8_0, 2 GPU, `-ncmoe 40`, 296-token prompt, `-n 800
--ignore-eos`): `--spec-type none` == `draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 3`, `4262 chars
sha=801a9fa3ebc0` (MTP active: 174.8 vs 112.7 t/s).  `scripts/validate-set.sh`: green (14/14 strict
apply on a fresh tarball, tree `5abfa8e4…`).

## 261022.004 (r109) -- the MTP draft-vocab validation arms closed (3 GPU is NEGATIVE, depth flat, MoE neutral)

> **Numbering note — this item is `TODO` #85.**  #83 was already used once before: the gemma-4 bf16 K/V
> `rope.cu` item was *filed and closed* as #83 in r103 (`WORKLOG.md` 261021.007 item 1, `patches/README.md`
> block 05), and #84 is the async-input-per-origin ring (closed r105).  The r107 campaign reused #83 for this
> block-13 item, breaking the "numbers are never reused" rule; the maintainer resolved it as **#85** on
> 2026-10-22.  #83 keeps its r103 meaning, #84 keeps the ring, and the r107 entry below now carries an inline
> pointer.  The item is **closed** (validation complete) and therefore removed from `TODO.md` per the
> closed-item rule.

**No shipped code, default, knob or `release.json` field changes** -- this is a validation record for block 13
(`--spec-draft-mtp-vocab N`) plus one guidance caveat the 3-GPU arm forced.  Tree `8e67f977…` (r109),
ROCm 10.1.0, 3x R9700 gfx1201, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` for every run (determinism, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44).
Record: `archive/work/spec-draft-mtp-vocab/VALIDATION-2026-10-22.md`; raw runs + harness:
`archive/work/three-gpu-performance/tools/arms-2026-10-22/` (`summary.csv` = the 36 runs used, `invalidated.csv` =
the two setup mistakes kept for the record).

**The 3-GPU arm is a loss, and the mechanism is the block's own allocation.**  Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0,
`-sm tensor`, four axes at `-n 3000`, trim 0 -> 98304 at `--spec-draft-n-max 7`: **+1.4 % aggregate at
2 GPU** (r107 recorded +1.6 %; table reproduced within 0.4 %/axis) but **-2.2 % aggregate at 3 GPU**
(R -1.7, P -2.3, C -2.6, K -2.1).  The subset head is allocated from the LM head's buffer type, so under a
tensor split it is **mirrored on every device** while the untrimmed head is **split**: the per-device draft
matmul is `N` columns vs `n_vocab / n_devices`.  At 2 GPUs `98337 < 124160` (win); at 3 GPUs
`98337 > 82773` (loss).  The width sweep is the control -- 98304 and 131072 have *identical* acceptance
(0.67337 / mean len 4.67 at 2 GPU; 0.68827 / 4.83 at 3 GPU), so only the matmul width differs:
2 GPU 94.3 (trim 0) / 95.8 (98304) / 93.1 (131072); 3 GPU **98.3 / 96.0 / 93.3**.  At 3 GPUs the width
threshold (82773) sits below the acceptance floor: 64000 measures 89.1 t/s (-9.4 %, acceptance
0.68878 -> 0.67260), so **no N is profitable there** -- the advice for a 248320-vocab model on 3 GPUs is
leave the trim off.  The r107 record's "still 2.5x smaller at 98304" compares against the whole vocabulary;
on a tensor split the live comparison is the per-device share.

**Depth 16384 is flat for the trim** (prompt `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` x3 = 15746 tok,
`sha256 6fec9806b375…`, `-c 20480`): 2 GPU 92.2 -> 92.3, 3 GPU 84.4 -> 83.2.  **MoE + `-ncmoe` is neutral**
(35B-A3B Q8_0 -- the UD-Q4_K_M on this box has no nextn block -- 2 GPU `-ncmoe 40`, expert cache 100 %
residency, 32640 MiB `ROCm_Host`: P 196.1 -> 197.9, K 64.1 -> 63.7 with identical acceptance).

**Purity holds everywhere tested** (trim only loses proposals): 3-GPU shallow `none` / trim 0 / trim 98304
all `c5421068b4e0`; 3-GPU at depth all `12048e399854`.  `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh --since "90 min ago"`
(kernel journal + run logs): clean.

**Docs bug found and fixed in the record.**  The campaign README wrote the invocation as
`--spec-draft-n-max <N> --spec-draft-n-start <N>`; `-n-start` is the *initial* adaptive depth (default 3),
not a ceiling, and pinning it at 7 changes the trajectory (2-GPU P 94.3 -> 87.6 t/s, acceptance
0.670 -> 0.627).  The validated config is `--spec-draft-n-max 7` with `-n-start` default.

**Dense 2-vs-3-GPU data for `TODO.md` #51** (same runs, trim off): aggregate 109.4 -> **113.1 (+3.4 %)**,
per axis R +9.2 %, P +4.2 %, C +0.3 %, **K -14.4 %** -- and K's acceptance, counts (480/488) and mean
length (29.24) are *bit-identical* across widths, so that -14.4 % is a clean device-count effect at verify
width ~30.  At depth 16384 the 3rd GPU costs 8.5 % (84.4 vs 92.2) and the shallow->deep penalty is -14.1 %
at 3 GPU vs -2.2 % at 2 GPU.  So 3-GPU decode is *width*-dependent on a dense model (it wins at 2-5-token
verify widths, loses at ~30 and at depth), which is the discriminator §5 of the campaign predicts: on 3
devices the small-message path is the host-staged chunked ring (both 2-device fast paths need exactly 2
devices) and its cost grows with the message.  Written up in
`archive/work/three-gpu-performance/FINDING-2026-10-22-dense-27b-and-mirrored-draft-subset.md`; it does **not** close
#51 (the MoE/field-config arm is still the campaign's target).

## 261022.003 (r109) -- block 10 split in two: the infrastructure stays 10, qwen4exp becomes block 11

**Release `v14-097cf33d9-r109`**, **14 blocks**, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `933b964c7`, tree
`8e67f977c02faee882ce2966cdc9bd79db9134d3` -- **the tree is unchanged from r108**.  This is a
delivery-structure change only: no shipped code, default or knob moved, so every r108 gate result still
describes the same tree.  Old blocks 00-09 are byte-identical commits; the old block 10 is split into
**block 10 (infrastructure)** and **block 11 (qwen4exp)**, and the old blocks 11/12 are re-cut as blocks
**12/13** with unchanged trees (only the subject line and the `[PATCH NN/13]` series counter differ).

**Why.**  Old block 10 was 33.8 k patch lines across 110 files, and it owned four unrelated things: the
qwen4exp model graph, the movable-boundary slab, the `ggml_cuda_try_fuse` dispatcher TU and the async
graph-input ring (plus the GDN/MMB/rope fusion work).  A change to any one of them re-cut a block that
touches all four, which is why every r94-r108 amendment "block 10" needed a whole-file conflict review, and
why the qwen4exp-only concerns could not be reviewed or reverted on their own.  QSA moved with qwen4exp by
the maintainer's decision (it was added along with the model).

**How it was cut (tree-identical).**  New block 10 = the old block-10 tree with the qwen4exp/QSA/HC
surface reverted to its block-09 state; new block 11 = the old block-10 tree exactly
(`0d79622d9c94930a30254e1c3bf9b79b49883889`, verified equal).  Old blocks 11/12 were then replayed on top;
the tip tree is `8e67f977...` as before, and `rdna-boosts-all.patch` is **byte-identical**
(`sha256 79ed963b...`).  Both new blocks build the `all` target on their own.

**Boundary (the rule to apply to a future fix).**  Block 10 keeps the general infrastructure: the slab /
arena / VMM TUs, the fusion dispatcher and every fusion arm implemented inside a pre-existing kernel TU,
the async input ring, the rope/FWHT and GDN/MMB fusions.  **Block 11 owns everything that exists only
because of qwen4exp**: `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp`, `llama-memory-hybrid-idx`, the QSA + indexer ops and
kernels (`fattn-qsa*`, `indexer-*`, the 4-head WMMA scorer in `lightning-indexer.cu`), the HC ops
(`hc-mix`, `hyperconn`), the managed lazy reader, the keys-only indexer cache (`llama_kv_cache::v_enabled`),
the qwen4exp arch gate, and **the fusion arms whose matchers live in those files** (the HC combine-mix /
mix / combine-norm / gate-mix arms, the indexer relu-sum and its alloc dep, the HC_BLK16/RES16 marking

## 261022.002 (r108) -- block 10 amendment: the gate/beta BF16 fusion was wrong for every sequence but the first (issue #204)

**Release `v13-097cf33d9-r108`**, 13 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `70815f407`, tree
`8e67f977c02faee882ce2966cdc9bd79db9134d3`.  One block amendment (**10**, which owns `mmvf.cu` and the
PR #200 fusions per the r102 fold rule); blocks 00-09 are byte-identical commits, 11-12 re-cut with the same
trees.  Reported by @briansp2020 with the fix; the campaign record (probe harness, the sweep, all raw logs)
is in `archive/work/issue-204-gate-beta-multiseq/`, doctrine in `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §49.

**What was broken.**  `ggml_cuda_gate_beta_bf16_try_fuse` (r102) collapses the GDN alpha/beta chain into one
`mul_mat_vec_f` launch, and it passed the chain's gate `MUL` as the launch `dst`.  The launch takes its column
count from `dst->ne[1]` and its channel count from `dst->ne[2]`; with one sequence the gate MUL is
`[nr, n_tokens, 1]` and matches the projection, but in a multi-sequence ubatch it is
`[nr, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs]` against `y = [ne10, n_tokens]` with one channel.  Every channel past the first
therefore re-ran the beta rows and wrote the gate/beta values computed from `y`'s **first `n_seq_tokens`
columns**: each sequence but the first silently took sequence 0's alpha/beta gates (and `n_seqs`x redundant
beta work).  **Correction to the report's mechanism, same bug and same fix:** `y`'s channel index is
`fastmodulo(channel, nchannels_y=1)`, so the kernel does not read `y` past its end and its writes stay inside
`gate_mul`/`beta_w` (both have `n_seqs x n_seq_tokens` columns) - the defect is wrong values for sequences
1..n-1, not an overrun.

**Why the gates missed it.**  Single-sequence decode/verify is unaffected (identical shapes), the text stays
coherent, and it needs a BF16 `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` (a BF16-tensor GGUF - our Q8_0 set takes the separate,
correct `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GATE_BETA_VERIFY` arm, and F32 tensors take neither).  It was caught only with
multi-sequence serving.  **New finding - the exposure band is per projection:** the fusion runs only where the
plain matmul would be an MMVF, and `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf` returns `ne11 <= 3` for BF16 once
`should_use_mmf` is applicable.  A 48-row projection (Qwen3.8-27B, Flash-Next) keeps the whole 8-token band on
gfx1201 - so 4 concurrent requests x 2 tokens *is* exposed on our box - while a 32-row one (Qwen3.5-4B) only
reaches 3.

**The fix.**  Launch with the projection's own shape: `ggml_tensor dst_flat = *alpha_w;
dst_flat.data = gate_mul->data;`.  Both tensors are contiguous with the same element count (the matcher already
checks it), so it is the same memory written flat.  A single-sequence launch is byte-for-byte identical
(ne/nb/data/op_params), so single-stream numerics cannot move; multi-sequence now matches the unfused chain
exactly.

**New regression gate (`tests/test-fusion-gate-beta-multiseq.cpp`, shipped, built by default, ctest-registered).**
No model needed.  For `(n_seq_tokens, n_seqs)` = (1,1) (2,1) (3,1) (4,1) (1,2) (1,3) (1,4) (2,2) (3,2) (2,3)
(2,4) it builds the chain on the GPU backend and compares the fused launch with the same graph made ineligible
for fusion (one extra consumer of the `ADD` output makes `ggml_can_fuse_subgraph` reject the window), requiring
**bit-identical** gate and beta values.  The fusion's fire is proven directly: the fused launch skips
ADD/UNARY/MUL, so the `SOFTPLUS` output is left at a NaN sentinel - a change that made the matcher stop firing
fails the test instead of passing it vacuously.  On the r107 build it exits **2 with 7 failing rows** (all
multi-sequence rows, `maxdiff` 0.75-1.58); on r108 **PASS, 11/11 fused, 0 failed**.

**Evidence (gfx1201, 2026-10-22, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`).**  A lockstep probe (one token per sequence in one
batch, distinct prompts) gives bit-identical logits for two runs of the same arm, so arms compare exactly:
`n_seqs = 1` pre-fix == post-fix == fusion-off; `n_seqs = 2, 3` pre-fix **differ at every step** (sequence 0
unaffected, sequences >= 1 wrong and equal to each other); post-fix all arms identical and equal to the pre-fix
**unfused** reference.  Reproduced and fixed on Qwen3.8-27B-BF16 (3 GPU `-sm layer` **and** `-sm tensor`) and on
Flash-Next GSQ IQ3_XXS (qwen4exp, 3 GPU - the reporter's model class, which does carry BF16 gate weights).
Single-stream is unchanged: 4B/27B/35B-A3B greedy text identical between the r107 and r108 builds, and the
prefill-logit A/B against the pre-fix build is mean KLD **0.000000** (same-top-p 100.000 %) at `-ub 8` and
`-ub 512` on 27B Q8_0 - mmvf is the decode/verify band only, so the prefill gate is not applicable and this
A/B is the stronger form of "prefill did not move".

**Full fusion-family sweep (the report asked for the siblings).**  Seven switches x the models that fire each
arm, switch on vs off, multi-sequence logits compared bit-exactly, and the fusion-skip signature compared to
prove each arm fired: `GATE_BETA_BF16` (4B BF16, Flash-Next) - **was the only broken one**; `GATE_BETA_VERIFY`
(27B Q8_0), `GDN_GATE` (all), `GDN_BETA_SIGMOID` (all), `GDN_CONV_NORM` (dummy qwen4exp), `CONT_GATE_Q8_1`
(27B Q8_0, Flash-Next) and the GDN snapshot-copy fusion (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GDN_CPY`) are all identical
post-fix, and identical *pre-fix* too (so no second defect).  `GDN_NORM_GATE` never fired in any multi-sequence
run - its guard bails on `xn->ne[3] != 1`, an explicit sequence dimension - and its kernel is
`ggml_nelements`-based anyway.

**Throughput.**  4B BF16 1 GPU, np = concurrent slots, 2 runs each: **64.2 / 114.6 / 165.6 t/s** pre-fix vs
**64.2 / 114.4 / 165.5 t/s** post-fix at np = 1/2/3 - unchanged.  On our box the false gates cost no
throughput at 2-3 streams; the reporter's 4-stream -3.5 % was mostly the draft-acceptance loss (0.85 -> 0.82
with MTP), which is why the correctness fix is the whole of it.

**Validation.**  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (13/13 strict `git am` from a fresh tarball, applied tree ==
`release.json.tree`); `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from f2ee094df` **2/2** (block 10 and the tip,
the other 11 patch-identical); the new test PASS on the release tree and exit 2 on the r107 library.  Not run:
`test-backend-ops` (no op, op instantiation or dispatch predicate changed - the diff is one launch argument in
one fusion and a new test file) and `gate-per-block-build` for the untouched blocks (patch-identical).

**Release tooling fixed while publishing (post-tag commit, patches unaffected).**  The off-host container
watcher (`scripts/container-watch.sh`, cron on `radiance`) selected its release tag with a hardcoded
`git tag -l 'v12-*'`, so it kept reporting "up to date (v12-097cf33d9-r106)" and **never built r107 or r108** -
the tag prefix moved to `v13-` with the 13-block set and the glob was never updated.  It now filters
`^v<blocks>-<base>-r<N>$` without pinning the block count (creation-date sort unchanged, so re-bases still
order correctly); `scripts/README.md` and `CONTAINERS.md` say so as well.  Nothing in `patches/` or
`release.json` changes, so the tag's delivery content and hashes stand; the image build was re-run with
`FORCE_TAG=v13-097cf33d9-r108`.

## 261022.001 (r107) -- block 12: the MTP draft vocabulary subset (`--spec-draft-mtp-vocab N`, opt-in)

**Release `v13-097cf33d9-r107`**, 13 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `25bec484e`, tree
`91bcefc49ef42220ba97a937821fb5e1d4fda6a8`.  One new block: **12**.  Campaign record:
`archive/work/spec-draft-mtp-vocab/` (`README.md` = the gate record, `RESOLUTION.md` = the promotion); the
contributor's PR is archived verbatim in `archive/work/pr205-spec-draft-mtp-vocab/` (merged for authorship).
`TODO.md` #83 tracks the remaining validation arms.  *(Handle corrected 2026-10-22: #83 is the r103 bf16
`rope.cu` item — this block-13 item is **#85**; see 261022.004.  The quoted text is otherwise unchanged.)*

**What ships.**  `--spec-draft-mtp-vocab N` makes the MTP draft head score only the LM-head rows for token ids
`< N` plus every control/user-defined id, and scatter the result into a full-vocabulary row of `-inf`.  The
speculator still sees a full-vocab logit row and **the target's verification is untouched**, so the trim can
only lose proposals, never change an accepted token.  Opt-in and default off: `0` builds no subset and adds no
graph node (measured byte-identical to r106 on plain decode and on `draft-mtp` at n-max 1 / 9 / adaptive-9).
Scope: `qwen35`, `qwen35moe`, `qwen4exp`, `gemma4-assistant` (the last one wired up, not beneficial -- below).

**The bug the campaign had to fix first.**  The subset is copied out of the LM head, and under `-sm tensor`
that head is **vocabulary-split**; `ggml_backend_meta_get_tensor_impl` could only serve a *whole-tensor* read of
a 2-D axis-1-split tensor (its splice chunk is `nb[axis + 1]`, which for a 2-D tensor is the whole tensor), so
`-sm tensor` + the flag aborted with `GGML_ASSERT(size % chunk_size_full == 0)`.  The block adds a
row-granular splice (segment -> repeat -> device, per-device byte offsets advanced exactly as the setter does).
Verified 18/18 on a standalone Meta-device check (uneven and even splits, a range straddling the split, a
repeated `nr = 2` split and a range crossing a repeat, whole tensor, last row) and by the product path itself.

**Gate (gfx1201, 2x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0).**  Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0, 2 GPU `-sm tensor`,
`--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive,ngram-mod --spec-ngram-mod-n-match 45`, `-n 3000` per axis, delivery prompt
files, flag off vs on:

| configuration | R | P | C | K | aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--spec-draft-n-max 9`, `--spec-draft-mtp-vocab 64000` | 69.7 | **89.4** | 113.4 | 413.7 | 109.0 (-0.4 %) |
| `--spec-draft-n-max 9`, `--spec-draft-mtp-vocab 98304` | 67.9 | 95.2 | 118.3 | 408.2 | 110.7 (+1.5 %) |
| baseline (flag 0), n-max 7 | 68.1 | 93.8 | 120.6 | 368.2 | 110.1 |
| **`--spec-draft-n-max 7`, `--spec-draft-mtp-vocab 98304` (shipped recommendation)** | **69.0** | **95.4** | **123.5** | **371.2** | **111.8 (+1.6 %)** |

The 64000 row is why the cut is payload-specific: it is the reporter's gfx1151 value and it *loses* acceptance on
our 27B (prose -3.6 %).  At 98304 acceptance is unchanged (0.61925 -> 0.61941, mean accepted length 4.77 ->
4.86).  n-max 7 is the recommendation because per-position acceptance is already 0.011/0.007 at positions 8-9, so
the higher ceiling buys nothing and sits outside the purity promise.

**Purity.**  `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §48 (new doctrine).  With the trim on, `--spec-type none` == `draft-mtp`
n-max 7 at trim 0 / 64000 / 98304 on prose (`-n 3000`, all `fa4867aa074e`) and on code (trim 98304,
`f7256a7b1380`).  The campaign's first apparent divergence was **outside** the documented band (adaptive n-max
9): with **no campaign code applied** the r106 build already produces three different greedy texts on
`prompts/code-reasoning-mixed.txt` for `draft-mtp` n3 / n9 / adaptive-n9, because verify-width numerics flip a
near-tie.  The item filed for that was withdrawn (it was against a known non-promise, methodology rule 4 /
§11) and the rule is now written down instead.

**Regression pass.**  `test-backend-ops` **21179/21179** (2/2 backends); `test-logits-width-probe SPLIT=tensor`
**PASS** (`W=1..8`, `maxdiff_vs_W8=0`); `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD 0.000000, same-top-p
100.000 %) against a base recorded from the r106 build; plain 27B `-sm tensor` decode text- and t/s-identical
to r106.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (13/13, strict `git am`, applied tree = `release.json.tree`).

**gemma4 (supported, not beneficial).**  `gemma4-assistant` + `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0-MTP` (layer split only:
the assistant arch rejects `-sm tensor` at load): full vocab 150.3 t/s, 64000 -> 104.5 (acceptance 0.669 ->
0.339), 196608 -> 106.9, 245760 -> 150.5 (a no-op).  Its draft top-1 ids split across ids < 64000 and the
229376+ "space piece" band, so any lossless cut saves nothing.  A two-band subset (98368 rows, 0.610
acceptance) measured 0.4 % *slower* and was not shipped (the two-band item, item 4 of the validation list; handle **#85**, see 261022.004).

**Cost.**  A second copy of `N/n_vocab` of the LM head, per device under `-sm tensor`: 510 MiB at 98304 on the
27B (332 MiB at 64000), allocated when the MTP context is created -- i.e. **not** in the `--fit` estimate.

**Not run (open at the time; the item is #85):** 3 GPU `-sm tensor`, depth-16384 decode, and MoE with `-ncmoe` / expert cache
active.  The MoE arm that *was* run (35B-A3B Q8_0, 2 GPU tensor) is neutral: 233.5 -> 233.4 t/s.

## 261021.016 (r106) -- DFlash2 under `-sm tensor`: the Meta `ALL_GATHER` collective (TODO #78 closed)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r106`**, 12 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `2e258d3b1`, tree
`d3c1e6c53ab60b027a51474eaca3a12fbff2ea7b`.  One block amendment: **11** (the whole fold -- see below for why
it did not go to 09/10).  Campaign record: `archive/work/dflash-meta-split-impl/` (`FINDINGS-2026-10-21.md`,
`RESOLUTION.md`, `all-gather.patch`, the as-validated change).

**What was broken.** A DFlash2 drafter with a selector (`dflash.selector_rank > 0`) aborted under
`-sm tensor` and was cleanly rejected since r54: its selector reduces along the vocabulary axis
(`ggml_top_k` picks the candidates, `ggml_get_rows` reads their values), and the draft logits come from the
**target's** `output.weight` projection, which the target's policy places vocabulary-split.  Two obvious
routes were refuted first, with evidence: **mirroring the drafter** changes nothing (the offending tensor is
the target's, resolved through the *buffer's* buft device, and it stayed `SPLIT_AXIS_0` with extents
`[124160, 124160]`), and **demoting only the drafter to `-sm layer`** aborts at load (a layer-split draft
context cannot read the target's shared embedding/lm-head out of the target's `Meta()` buffers).

**The fix.** The campaign's route (b): a **split→mirrored gather**, as a new general ggml collective
`GGML_OP_ALL_GATHER` (`ggml_all_gather()`), used in `build_dflash2_selector()` whenever the draft is a
≥ 2-device tensor split.  On the Meta backend the result is `MIRRORED`, the op is its own subgraph boundary,
the node is dropped from every per-device child graph, and the collective copies each device's slice into
every device's copy **one row at a time** (the slice is contiguous in its own copy but strided in the full
tensor; the destination offsets are the canonical cumulative extents of
`ggml_backend_meta_get_tensor_impl`).  Only a plain axis-0 split is implemented -- anything else aborts by
design.  CPU/CUDA execute the op as a copy, `RPC_PROTO_PATCH_VERSION` goes 7 → 8 (the op enum is on the wire),
and the r54 rejection is removed.  The gather was verified **byte-exact** against the canonical host
assembly for `[248320,2]` and `[248320,4]` tensors while it was instrumented.

**Two defects the work surfaced, both fixed here.**  (1) `extract_layer_inputs()`'s F1 "device" copy is one
pointer range, which a Meta buffer cannot express: under `-sm tensor` it aborted in
`ggml_backend_tensor_set(NULL)` (via `ggml_backend_meta_buffer_set_tensor`).  **Pre-existing for any** DFlash
drafter that requests `dflash.target_layers` -- the r54 guard only covered selector models.  It now takes the
host path (byte-identical output; the escape hatch the allocation failure already used).  (2) The slab's
**narrow-2** region only accepted the VA the creation reservation left unmapped, i.e. the *draft-context
estimate* whose `compute` term is a measured 512 MiB tier; a tensor-split drafter runs the whole draft graph
on every device, so its per-device compute buffer measured **1280 MiB** and did not fit, and the fallback
`cudaMalloc` could not fit either with the slab holding the VRAM (`graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute
buffers` for `-sm tensor` + a draft + `-ncmoe`).  The pin is now two-phase -- decide under the lock, evict
the arena tables in `[off, mapped)` **outside** it (`moe_cache_evict_slab_range` re-enters through
`arena_free`), then commit by capping the arena at the new top when the region is below `mapped` -- so the
arena yields (r20) instead of the run aborting.

**Measured** (`Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL` + `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M`, `-c 16384`, q8_0 K/V, 5258-token
prompt, `-n 128 --seed 42 --temp 0`):

| config | 2 GPU decode | 3 GPU decode |
|---|---|---|
| plain, `-sm tensor` | 44.7 t/s | 40.8 t/s |
| DFlash2, `-sm layer` (the only config that worked before) | 63.4 t/s | 60.8 t/s |
| **DFlash2, `-sm tensor` (r106)** | **84.5 t/s** | **61.1 t/s** |

Draft acceptance is **identical to `-sm layer`** (0.67742, per-position rates `0.857/0.714/0.429`), the text is
deterministic across runs, `--parallel 2` is coherent on both slots, and `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q8_0` + its DFlash2
goes 161.9 → **191.0 t/s**.  The slab fix, no override env anywhere: 35B-A3B-Q8_0 + DFlash2 `-ncmoe 20
-c 8192` **2 GPU abort → 138.6 t/s** and **3 GPU abort → 87.4 t/s** (acceptance 0.849), while the
fits-in-the-spare arm is unchanged (1 GPU `-ncmoe 40`: 0.75 GiB from the *unmapped VA spare*, 98.5 t/s).

**Gates.**  `test-backend-ops` **3/3**; `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` against the r105 base (Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0)
**mean KLD 0.000000 / same-top-p 100.000 %**; the 4B/9B dense greedy text **byte-identical to the r105 build**;
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green (12/12 strict `git am`, applied tree == `release.json.tree`);
`gate-per-block-build.sh` not re-run: blocks 00-10 are **byte-identical commits** to r105 and only block 11
changed, so their per-block builds are the ones r105 already validated.

**Why block 11 and not 09/10** (recorded because it bends the "a fix goes into the block that owns it" rule):
`ggml-cuda-slab.cu` does not exist before block 10, and amending blocks 09/10 would have re-cut the entire
chain (conflicts in `ggml.h`/`ggml.c`/`ggml-rpc.h`/`ggml-backend-meta.cpp`, all of which block 10 edits) for an
entirely additive change that applies last.  The delivery content is identical either way; blocks 00-10 stay
untouched and the r105 validation of them still holds.

**States.**  `-sm tensor` + DFlash2 is a supported configuration; `-sm layer` remains the escape hatch (no new
environment variable, by the maintainer's decision).  A true Meta *distributed* top-k (gathering
`top_k × n_devices` candidates instead of the whole row) stays available as a later optimisation -- the gather
measured inside the draft step's noise.  `TODO` #78 is closed and its campaign is archived.

## 261021.015 (r105) -- issue #201 fixed (the async-input ring is actually per-origin) + `mmf32` default-on for RDNA3_5

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r105`**, 12 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `dfb7fe80d`, tree
`60f5017c72d8f990ff22bc45b7a246f4a8f14aaa`.  Two block amendments: **10** (the ring, issue #201 / `TODO` #84)
and **06** (`mmf32` predicate: RDNA3_5 joins RDNA4).  Campaign record:
`archive/work/async-input-per-origin/` (`RESOLUTION.md`, `repro/`); the record correction this release owed is
its own entry, **261021.014** below.

**Block 10 — the ring's ordering state is now per host thread.**  r101 keyed the per-origin map on
`cudaStreamPerThread`, which is the sentinel `((hipStream_t)2)` — the same value in every thread — so there was
exactly one origin per device and "per-origin ordering" did not exist.  Now keyed on
`std::this_thread::get_id()`; uploads are still *issued* on `cudaStreamPerThread` (ordering is carried by the
per-copy `ev` / batched `flush_ev`, never by a stream handle), and the r101 comment's "a stream is a
`llama_context`" model is replaced (an origin is a host thread).  Fixed with it: only the **owning** thread
consumes an origin's `pending`/`has_flush` (a foreign wait may still *issue* a foreign queue — the loader
uploads from another thread — but no longer steals the owner's wait), the `flush_ev` wait happens **before**
the `o.q.empty()` early-out, and the ring head wraps only after every origin's queue is issued and the device
has drained (a foreign origin's *queued* uploads would otherwise be overwritten before they were ever issued —
a fourth gap that only a correct key exposes).  `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_DEBUG=1` logs the origin count and
thread id (`ENVIRONMENT.md` §7.4).

**Proven, not assumed.**  `repro/ain_origin_repro.cpp`: two host threads, two CUDA backends, **one device**.
r104 semantics → **1 origin**, and the second thread's first wait finds `issued=0 ev=0 flush=0` (its copy was
issued on the *other* thread's stream: the foreign-thread drain).  The fix → **2 origins** (`key == thread`),
and the owner still consumes its flush after a foreign drain.  Re-verified on gfx1201, gfx1151 and gfx1100.

**Gates (gfx1201 unless stated, one GPU job at a time).**  `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0` vs default through the
prefill-logit gate with hipBLASLt pinned on both arms: **0.000000 / 100.000 %** — the ring is byte-identical
to the old path.  `test-backend-ops` SET/SET_ROWS/CPY **422/422**, MUL_MAT **2444/2444** (seeded NMSE).
Determinism (dump hashes): 35B-A3B **12/12** one class at 1 GPU (`d598fa841cff`, r104's class) and **4/4** at
2 GPU `-sm tensor` (`e5179311f6d2`), dense 27B 4/4.  Coherence 4B 3 GPU `1c5d32ac537d` (== r93…r99).
Perf, 3 interleaved visits, ring on vs off: 35B-A3B 2 GPU `-ncmoe 40` → pp512 **+2.7 %**, pp2048 **+1.6 %**,
tg128 **+4.3 %**; Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS 2 GPU `-ncmoe 48 -ub 2048 --load-mode mmap --lazy-mode off` → pp2048
flat, tg128 **+4.9 %**.  No regression; r90's decode win survives.

**Block 06 — `mmf32` default-on for RDNA3_5** (`GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA4 || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3_5`), the
r104 admission legs re-run on `halo` (gfx1151) with the kernel as the *default*: `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT`
2444/2444; **12/12** fresh starts one logits class (`3f86d992a67f`, the class the r104 campaign recorded for

**Release gates.**  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums, strict 12/12 from a fresh tarball, tree

## 261021.014 (docs) -- record correction: the r101 gemma4 MTP "0 -> 8/10" step was the hipBLASLt lottery, not the async-input ring

**Correction only -- no patch, no `release.json` change.**  `WORKLOG.md` 261021.003 (r101) and
`archive/work/fix-gemma-4/` credit block 10's **per-origin async-input ring** with taking the gemma4 26B-A4B MTP
arm from *unstable in every sample* to **8/10** "by removing a genuine cross-context ordering defect".  That
attribution is withdrawn: the ring's origin map was keyed on the `cudaStreamPerThread` sentinel and could hold
only **one** origin per device (issue #201, fixed in r105 — see 261021.015), so it cannot have changed the
single-context ordering it was credited with, and the residual had already been re-attributed to the hipBLASLt
solution lottery (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44) without explaining the 0 -> 8/10 step.

**Re-derived on the r105 tree** (gemma4 26B-A4B Q8_0 + `mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B`, `-ngl 99 -ncmoe 40 -sm layer
--fit false -c 16384 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -n 300 -t 8 --seed 42 --temp 0 --ignore-eos`,
2 devices, draft-candidate fingerprint classes via `archive/work/fix-gemma-4/tools/fp.sh`):

| arm | 10 x `-n 300` | 3 x `-n 3000` |
|---|---|---|
| hipBLASLt **on** (default) | **10/10** `05e32c4dee` | 3/3 `867a09a093` |
| `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` | **10/10** `05e32c4dee` | 3/3 `867a09a093` |
| **`GGML_CUDA_MMF32=0`**, hipBLASLt on | **2 classes in 6**: `6f6923ef36` x4, `51274cb0f2` x2 | — |

So the r101 "unstable" arm was the **hipBLASLt per-start solution lottery** on the F32 MoE-router GEMM
(`m=128 n=375 k=2816`, inside `mmf32`'s window): `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` pinned it at r101 (8/10, not
10/10), and **r104's `mmf32` removed it by construction** — which is why both arms are 10/10 today.  The two
unstable fingerprints are exactly the two classes §44 recorded for this config, which is the independent
cross-check that the attribution is right.

`archive/work/fix-gemma-4/RESOLUTION.md` gains a "Correction" section pointing here; the r101 entry itself is
not edited (a dated record is never rewritten).  `TODO` #84 and the ring remain as recorded in 261021.015.

## 261021.013 (docs) -- session close: RDNA3_5 `mmf32` default + issue #201 bundled into r105; campaign seeded with a handover

**Docs only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no default flipped yet.**  Records the two decisions this
session ends on and the work that now owns them.

**1. `mmf32` default for RDNA3_5 — decided, deliberately NOT shipped alone.**  The gfx1151 validation
(261021.012) qualifies on the same four legs RDNA4 was admitted on: `test-backend-ops` 2444/2444 with NMSE
**6.11e-14 vs rocBLAS 6.83e-13** on the intercepted cases, **12/12** fresh starts one logits class,
**+1.0 % pp512 / +1.6 % pp2048** with decode flat, and a `--family-switch` **PASS** at the shipped confident
point (**0.013016 / 98.673 %** against a same-kernel control of 0.019125 / 97.975 %).  The change is one
predicate (`IS_RDNA4 || IS_RDNA3_5` in `ggml_cuda_mmf32_enabled`).  The maintainer's decision is to **bundle it
with issue #201 into one release** rather than cut a release for a single line — so it is staged in the campaign
handover, not applied.  RDNA3 (gfx1100) stays opt-in: −1.3…−2.2 % at `pp2048`, one visit a tie.

**2. New campaign: `wip/async-input-per-origin/` (issue #201, `TODO` #84).**  The finding, re-verified against
the r104 tree rather than quoted: the async-input ring keys its per-origin map on `cudaStreamPerThread`, which is
the sentinel `((hipStream_t)2)` in every thread (`hip_runtime_api.h:1160`), so there is exactly one origin per
device and r101's per-origin ordering does not exist.  Still open in r104: a foreign-thread drain issues another
thread's queued uploads on the caller's stream while the owner's graph has nothing left to wait on; the wrap
path's "every OTHER origin" sync loop is empty; `o.stream` means "the calling thread's stream", not the origin's
(the r101 comment's *"a stream is a `llama_context`"* is the wrong model — an origin is a host thread).  A
secondary gap survives a correct key: `if (o.q.empty()) continue;` skips the `has_flush` wait, so a queue drained
by another thread leaves the owner unordered behind that flush.  The campaign README carries the fix design (key
on `std::this_thread::get_id()`, keep issuing on `cudaStreamPerThread`, consume `flush_ev` on the empty-queue
path, `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_DEBUG` proving >1 origin), the full gate list, and the release shape (r105 = block
**10** for the ring + block **06** for the RDNA3_5 predicate).  `NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md` is the cold-start prompt.

**Record correction to carry, not to inherit:** r101 (261021.003) and `archive/work/fix-gemma-4/` credit this
patch with taking the gemma4 MTP arm from *unstable in every sample* to 8/10 "by removing a genuine
cross-context ordering defect".  A patch that cannot produce more than one origin cannot have done that, and the
residual was subsequently attributed to the hipBLASLt lottery (§44, which already says the ring is not the
residual) — so the 0 → 8/10 step is **unexplained**.  The campaign re-derives it after the fix and, if it does
not reproduce, adds a correcting `WORKLOG` entry and points the fix-gemma-4 resolution at it.  The old entry is
not edited.

**Also corrected this session:** `fingon` is **single-RDNA3** (its second `rocm-smi` entry is a gfx1036 iGPU),
so it does **not** provide the 2-card box `TODO` #79 needs; `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` lost the stale
`fa-rdna3-head512-purity` row (closed at r103, directory archived) and gained the new campaign row.
