## 261021.011 (r104) -- `mmf32` promoted into block 06: the F32 prefill GEMM is ours, so 35B-A3B/gemma4 prefill is deterministic and 4 % faster

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r104`**, 12 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `f38bfa9dd`.  One block amendment
(06).  Closes `TODO` #82 and the `hipblaslt-bypass` campaign.

**What shipped.**  A non-quantized (F32) weight with more than 16 token columns could not take `mmf` (there is
no F32 MMA form on RDNA — `amd_mfma_available` is CDNA-only, `amd_wmma_available` is f16/bf16), so it fell
through `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas()` to rocBLAS, i.e. to **hipBLASLt**, which picks its solution *per process
start* from a heap-ordered container.  That is the residual run-to-run nondeterminism of `TODO` #75 (3 logit
classes in 8 starts on 35B-A3B), and the solution the heuristic lands on is the slowest in the pool.  Block 06
now owns the path: `mmf32.cu`, a plain SIMT tiled GEMM for exactly those shapes (32 output rows per block, a
4×8 thread sub-tile, `BN=256`/`64`, the k range split into contiguous chunks summed in increasing z — a fixed
reduction tree, no atomics, **no approximation**).  F32 only, `m <= 256`, `17 <= n <= 65536`,
`256 <= k <= 8192`, `ldc == m`; everything else keeps the rocBLAS call.  Default-on for **RDNA4**
(`GGML_CUDA_MMF32=0` disables; opt-in `=1` on RDNA3/RDNA3_5 until those boxes run the same pair) —
`ENVIRONMENT.md` §10.1.

**Measured (gfx1201, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, one GPU unless stated; r103 tree during the campaign, re-run on the
r104 tree for the release gates).**  Determinism: **one logits class in 12/12** fresh starts
(`llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 1`), **6/6** at 2 GPU `-sm tensor`, `--chunks 8` dumps byte-identical.
Throughput, 3 interleaved `llama-bench` visits: **pp512 +4.2 %** (5068 vs 4862), **pp2048 +4.1 %** (5013 vs
4818), tg128 flat; the kernel is 0.032 ms vs 0.046 ms for the best hipBLASLt class on `32×512×2048`.
Correctness: 16-shape standalone oracle NMSE ~1e-13 (odd `k=2051`, odd `m`/`ldc`, `n<m`, `n>m`, `n=17`);
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` 2444/2444, and with r103's `LLAMA_TEST_OP_NMSE`/`LLAMA_TEST_SEED` instrument the
intercepted cases are **11x closer to the CPU reference than rocBLAS** (6.1e-14 vs 6.9e-13, threshold 5e-4).
Purity: `--family-switch` at the new confident point (`prompts/kld-corpus-35b-in-domain.txt`, base PPL 1.43)
gives **0.014646 / 98.045 %** against a same-kernel control of **0.018100 / 97.808 %** — no worse on both
metrics; at the wikitext point (PPL 5.82) it is 0.005787 / 96.480 % against a control of 0.006017 / 96.588 %
and `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` at 0.005969 / 96.667 %.  `GREEDY-PURITY.md` **§47** is the new rule.

**What was measured and deliberately not shipped.**  Pinning the hipBLASLt solution in our own code
(a direct `hipblasLtMatmul` with a validated index) is deterministic and +5.2 %/+4.8 %, i.e. ~1 % faster than
the kernel, but it owes a **per-ROCm-release solution table** (10.1.0: `m <= 64 -> 140219`, else `140232`;
7.14.1 has only four solutions from `140723`, so it falls back) and a `hipblaslt` link.  The kernel buys
almost all of the win with none of that obligation, so **the kernel shipped and the pin did not** (maintainer
decision).  The campaign also refuted `TENSILE_SOLUTION_INDEX` / `HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE` (arm A) and
raising `mmf`'s 16-column cap (arm B, a kernel limit).

**A false lead worth keeping.**  The prefill-logit gate's **self-KLD control is not exact**: the base file
stores **uint16-quantised** log-probs (`scale = (max-min)/65535` over a ≤16-nat window ⇒ step ≈ 2.4e-4 nats),
so the same arm compared against its own base reads `mean KLD -0.000000` but `same-top-p 99.951 %` *while the
dumps are byte-identical* — and the stock arm carries the same RMS Δp floor.  Determinism is judged on the
**dump hash**, not on the self-KLD top-p.  (Found on 35B-A3B; it cost a session's detour.)

**Not done / accepted limitations.**  BF16 prefill (Flash-Next, 2790 hipBLASLt dispatches) is untouched: it
keeps hipBLASLt's +51 % **and** its own per-start lottery — a BF16 counterpart is a separate job, not a gap
in this one.  A full-F32 model's FFN GEMMs (`m` ≫ 256) still reach hipBLASLt (recorded in
`patches/README.md`, block 06).  **Cross-arch:** validated on gfx1201 only; gfx1151/gfx1100 are opt-in until
the maintainer's boxes run the determinism + bench pair, which is why the default is arch-keyed rather than
global.

**Docs.**  `patches/README.md` (block 06: MMB **and** mmf32, scope + limitation), `MANIFESTS.md` (a block-06
verification row), `ENVIRONMENT.md` §10.1, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §47 (+ index), `prompts/README.md` +
`prompts/kld-corpus-35b-in-domain.txt` (the confident gate point, with the reproduction recipe),
`README.md`/`TODO.md` (release id; #82 closed), `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` (campaign closed), and the campaign record
moved to `archive/work/hipblaslt-bypass/`.

**Release gates on the r104 tree (gfx1201).**  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (checksums, strict 12/12 from a
fresh tarball, tree `a1317584…` matches `release.json`); `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from
<r103 tip>` **3/3** (blocks 06, 08, 11 — 08's delta changes only because its `ggml-cuda.cu` context moves);
fresh-start determinism on the release build **12/12 one class** at 1 GPU and **4/4** at 2 GPU `-sm tensor`;
`llama-bench`, 3 interleaved visits against the kill switch: **pp512 5114 vs 4862 (+5.2 %), pp2048 5033 vs
4812 (+4.6 %)**, tg128 flat; prefill-logit gate, standard model (dense 27B Q8_0, untouched — 0 intercepts)
**0.000000 / 100.000 % PASS**; family-switch gate at the shipped corpus point (base arm = the kill switch, base
PPL 1.4345) **0.014646 / 98.045 %** against a same-kernel control of **0.020671 / 97.808 %** → PASS with
`--allow-control-pass`; `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` 2444/2444; `check-windows-paths.sh` clean.  Coherence:
Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0 and Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 see **0 intercepts** (bit-identical by construction), gemma4 sees 1 (its
router) and measures 1209.848 → 1209.880 PPL.

**ROCm 7.14.1 is default-on too (arch-gated, not runtime-gated), and was checked before publication:** the
r104 tree built against `/opt/rocm-7.14.1-gfx120X` engages the kernel and gives **4/4 the same logits class**
(`d598fa841cff`, the same class as the 10.1 build — the arithmetic is runtime-independent), with

## 261021.010 (wip) -- P3(ii): our own F32 GEMM for the hipBLASLt shapes -- deterministic, +4.2 %, no external dependency

**WIP only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change** (prototype in
`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/tools/experiments/mmf32-splitk-WIP.patch`, applied to a working `~/llama.cpp`, measured
on the **r103 tree**, reverted).  Record: `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/evidence/p4-mmf32-kernel-implemented.txt`;
campaign status in `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/README.md` §2 arm C / P3(ii).

**Why it exists.**  Arm G (261021.008) pins the hipBLASLt solution and wins 5.2 %, but it owes a per-ROCm
solution table that must be re-established on every runtime.  A GEMM of our own removes that obligation
entirely: RDNA has no F32 MMA (arm B), so this is a SIMT kernel — a 32-output-row block tile, a 4×8 thread
sub-tile, `BN=256`/`64`, and the k range split into contiguous chunks summed in increasing z (a fixed reduction
tree, no atomics).  The split is the whole win: 0.266 → 0.032 ms on `32×512×2048` (2.07 TFLOP/s vs the best
hipBLASLt class 0.046 ms).

**Correctness.**  16-shape standalone oracle vs a double reference: **NMSE ~1e-13** (odd `k=2051`, odd
`m`/`ldc`, `n<m`, `n>m`, `n=17`, `m=1..256`).  `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` **2444/2444**; with r103's new
`LLAMA_TEST_OP_NMSE`/`LLAMA_TEST_SEED` instrument the two intercepted cases are **11x closer to the CPU
reference than the rocBLAS path** (6.1e-14 vs 6.9e-13, threshold 5e-4), and a case the kernel does not take is
bit-identical.  Gemma4 PPL 1209.848 (default) vs 1209.880.

**Determinism.**  1 GPU: **1 logits class 12/12** (`-c 512 --chunks 1`) and **4/4 byte-identical dumps**
(`--chunks 8`).  2 GPU `-sm tensor`: **1 class 6/6**.

**The session's open "99.951 % self-KLD" question is closed, and it was the instrument.**  A run compared
against a base recorded by the same arm reads mean KLD −0.000000 but same-top-p 99.951 % *while both dumps are
byte-identical*: `tools/perplexity/perplexity.cpp` stores the base as **uint16-quantised log-probs**
(`scale=(max−min)/65535` over a ≤16-nat window ⇒ step ≈ 2.4e-4 nats) and the top-1 comparison mixes exact F32
candidate logits with quantised base values, so a sub-step near-tie can be scored as a disagreement.  The stock
arm carries the same RMS Δp floor (0.001 %).  **Determinism is judged on the dump hash, not on the self-KLD
top-p** — worth knowing for every gate read of this tool.

**Throughput** (35B-A3B, 1 GPU, 3 interleaved visits): **pp512 +4.2 %** (5068 vs 4862), **pp2048 +4.1 %**
(5013 vs 4818), tg128 flat.  Against `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` (4890/4820) the kernel is +3.6 % prefill: it
buys determinism *and* speed, because the heuristic's bit-class is the slow one.

**Purity, with the r103 family-switch mode** (candidate `GGML_CUDA_MMF32=1` vs the default base, same-kernel
control measured on the spot): wikitext `-c 512 --chunks 40` (base PPL 5.82) candidate **0.005787 / 96.480 %**
vs control 0.006017 / 96.588 % and `=0` 0.005969 / 96.667 %; in-domain `-c 2048 --chunks 7` (new corpus
`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/tools/kld-corpus-35b-in-domain.txt`, base PPL **1.43**) candidate **0.014646 /
98.045 %** vs control **0.018100 / 97.808 %** — no worse on both metrics, so `--allow-control-pass` PASSes
(§46 calibration).  The absolute limits fail at both points for the control and the `=0` arm too, i.e. the
point is what the limit measures, not the switch.  This is an **exact** F32 GEMM reordering: no quantisation,
no approximation.

**Scope / not covered.**  F32 only, `m <= 256`, `17 <= n <= 65536`, `256 <= k <= 8192`; outside that window the
rocBLAS call is unchanged.  Flash-Next (BF16) and dense 27B see **zero intercepts**.  A full-F32 model's FFN
GEMMs (`m` ≫ 256) still reach hipBLASLt — recorded as an accepted limitation.  P3(i) BF16 untouched.
Promotion would need default-on with `GGML_CUDA_MMF32=0` as the kill switch, an `ENVIRONMENT.md` entry, a block
note in `patches/README.md`, the prefill base re-recorded on this arm (§5b) and the corpus shipped under
`prompts/`.  Maintainer decision, not taken.

## 261021.009 (docs) -- hipBLASLt-bypass promotion decisions: bases are arm-scoped, solution indices are a per-ROCm-release table

**Docs only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change.**  Records the maintainer's answers to the
two open questions from 261021.007, so a future session does not re-litigate them.

**Q1 -- the prefill-logit base (answer: re-record it).**  A default change that moves the prefill arithmetic
into a different kernel family does not get scored against the old family's base: the base is **re-recorded
from the arm that ships**, and the old-vs-new KLD is logged as the **family-switch magnitude**.  For the
hipBLASLt pin on 35B-A3B that number is **0.007279 mean KLD / 96.618 % same-top-p** (and `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`
measures **0.007271 / 96.618 %** from the same base, which is why the old comparison was reading the lottery).
The general rule is now written into `benchmarks/prefill-logit-methodology.md` **§5b**: *a base is only valid for
the arm it was recorded on*, with the 2026-10-21 measurement as its evidence and the pinned-vs-pinned control
(0.000000 / 100.000 %) as the interpretability requirement.  This extends §5's existing "a noisy self-KLD is a
measurement result, not a gate result" with the two obligations: find the cause (here: the library's per-start
solution pick), and re-baseline deliberately rather than tune the threshold.

**Q2 -- solution-index portability (answer: a per-ROCm-release table, re-established per release).**  The
patched code keeps a small validated `(ROCm version, arch) -> index` table (10.1.0/gfx1201: `m <= 64 -> 140219`,
else `140232`) and the fallback that is already measured: an unadvertised index -> the smallest advertised one
(still deterministic), a failed launch -> refuse the shape and use rocBLAS.  **The table is a measured artefact:**
each ROCm release we ship gets it established and validated (probe + determinism gate, ~10 min) instead of
inheriting it, and the versions that were measured are listed with the block.  ROCm 7.14.1 is the worked example
of the fallback (4 solutions from `140723`, bit-identical to its base, `pp512 +0.5 %` / `pp2048 -0.2 %`, decode
flat).  Recorded in `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/README.md` §2 arm G ("promotion decisions") and §4 P4; when this is cut
into a block it lands in `patches/README.md`, `ENVIRONMENT.md` and the release checklist.

## 261021.007 (r103) -- head-512 FA purity campaign closed (the point, not the rows) + three folded fixes

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r103`**, 12 blocks, fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `283b8b8ac`, tree
`7b45c00088a75d6f7331a63613a336c5537c3c7a`.  Two block amendments (05, 10), no new block:
`scripts/validate-set.sh` strict 12/12 from a fresh tarball (tree matches), `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh
--changed-from r102-tip` **3/3** (blocks 05, 10, 11).  *(Renumbered from the 261021.005 this session first
used: the gfx1201 box closed TODO #75 and seeded `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/` under 261021.005/.006 the same day,
and TODO #82 is theirs — the bf16 item below is #83.)*

### The campaign: `TODO` #81 closed, no FA row change (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §46 rewritten)

The r102 ledger's `0.0293 / 92.59 %` for the gfx1100 head-512 rows is the **marginal** pair (default vs the
delivery *without* the 512 rows).  Against **fully tile** the same build measures `0.046179 / 90.422 %`, and
the head-256 rows shipped since r5 already measure `0.044055 / 90.627 %` there.  More importantly the
*wikitext point itself* cannot decide a family switch: a pure same-kernel ubatch change (fully tile,
`-ub 512` vs `-ub 256`) measures **0.104989 / 85.000 %** — 21x the KLD limit — because gemma-4-26B-A4B is a
*reasoning* model and raw wikitext is 45x outside its confident range (base PPL 607).  At an in-domain point
(the model's own greedy continuations, now shipped as `prompts/fa-family-switch-gemma4-26B-A4B.txt`, base PPL
**2.65**) the same unmodified rows measure **0.001778 / 98.967 %** against the feature-off arm, with the
same-kernel control at `0.012049 / 97.333 %`.  Per switch, strictly (`--candidate-env`): head-512 **PASS**,
head-256 alone `0.005994 / 98.324 %` (top-p passes, KLD 20 % over), whole set `0.006150 / 98.227 %`.  PPL
parity 2.6515 vs 2.6530; throughput untouched (+34.3 % over the feature-off arm: pp2048 @ d32768 2570.07 vs
1913.30 t/s; tg128 127.37 vs 127.19); `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` 6389/6389.

Nothing in the kernel moves that number: fp32 PV accumulator (`T_C_VKQ`) 0.030489 marginal at **-32 %**
(below the tile arm); `nbatch_fa` 64 / 128 +-6 % at -19 / -14 %; `Q_in_reg=true` **bit-identical** at -29 %
(the win really is the VGPR spills); `nthreads=256` not instantiable; the two head-256 prefill levers
(`nbatch_fa`, `nbatch_K2/V2`) are bit-identical for a mechanical reason (a rescale by exactly 1.0 is exact,
and splitting the K loop does not reorder the fp32 mma accumulation).  The op-level oracle (CPU reference,
deterministic inputs, the model's own prefill shape kv=32768 nb=512 GQA 8 — the two cases are now in
`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`) puts the families within a factor 1.3 of each other, both ~10x under threshold.
Record: `archive/work/fa-rdna3-head512-purity/` (`RESOLUTION.md`, `MEASUREMENTS-2026-10-21.md`, every
experimental arm as a patch under `variants/`).

### The delivery changes (why r103 exists)

1. **gemma-4 bf16 K/V prefill no longer aborts (block 10, `rope.cu`).**  #83 (filed and closed in r103).  `rope.cu` instantiated
   float/f16 destinations for the NORMAL and NEOX modes but not **bf16**, and since r101 the iSWA `k_cur`/
   `v_cur` reorder lets the ROPE -> VIEW -> SET_ROWS fusion fire for Gemma's K, so `-ctk bf16 -ctv bf16`
   prefill died at `rope.cu:672` (`ggml_cuda_op_rope_impl<true>`).  Reproduced here on r102 first.  The four
   missing instantiations were added; the fused kernel stores with a single `ggml_cuda_cast<D>`, exactly like
   the `SET_ROWS` it replaces, so it must round identically — verified: **KLD -0.000000 / same-top-p
   100.000 %** against the `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_SET_ROWS=1` arm at bf16 K/V, and it is *faster* than the
   workaround (pp512 5136.70 vs 4973.06 t/s).
2. **FA test instrument (block 10, `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`).**  `LLAMA_TEST_OP_NMSE=1` prints the error
   magnitude every case already computes (not just pass/fail) and `LLAMA_TEST_SEED=<n>` pins the random
   input, so two kernel arms or two builds are comparable element by element — without the seed the data is
   redrawn per run and an NMSE moves by up to 13x, which is how the first "WMMA is more accurate" reading in
   this campaign was produced and then refuted.  Plus the two head-512 prefill-shape cases (kv 32768, nb 512,
   GQA 8, f16 and q8_0) the criterion reads.  Determinism verified (identical NMSE across runs).
3. **Latent `VKQ_C` sizing fix (block 05, `fattn-mma-f16.cuh`).**  The RDNA3 `VKQ_C` array was sized for the
   fp16 C tile's 32-column span, so an **fp32** C tile at `DV % 32 == 0` indexes out of bounds (the head-80/112
   fp32 rows escape it only because their DV is not a multiple of 32).  Unreachable in the delivery (every
   instantiated row is fp16 C, for which the expression is unchanged), found while trying the fp32
   accumulator; landed so the road to one is not a trap.

**Gates on the r103 tree** (gfx1100, `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`, one job at a time): `FLASH_ATTN_EXT`
6389/6389 · `ROPE`/`SET_ROWS` green · bf16 K/V prefill runs (5136.70 t/s pp512) and is bit-identical to the
unfused chain · prefill-logit **family-switch mode 0.001778 / 98.967 % (PASS)**, control 0.012049 / 97.333 % ·
default (wikitext) mode 0.046179 / 90.422 % (FAIL — the pre-existing head-256 calibration, unchanged) ·
pp2048 @ d32768 2570.07 t/s, tg128 @ d32768 127.37 t/s.  **Not re-validated on gfx1201/gfx1151 by this
session** (no such card on `fingon`): the rope change is dtype-only and inert unless a bf16 rope destination
is fused (which on those boxes is the same fusion, so it is a strict improvement), the test change is
test-only, and the VKQ_C expression is unchanged for every fp16 row.  The maintainer's other boxes should run
their usual gates.

**Docs:** `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §46 rewritten (calibrated point + same-kernel control; historical correction of

## 261021.006 (docs) -- `wip/hipblaslt-bypass`: P0 inventory + P1 VRAM answer; the driver is correctness; arm B refuted

**Docs only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change; `scripts/validate-set.sh` is unaffected.**
Same-day follow-on to 261021.005, which closed TODO #75 on the hipBLASLt per-start solution flip.  This entry
records the first campaign session, run on the maintainer's steer that **the concern is correctness, not
VRAM** (the slab-headroom attribution was theirs to test and it did not survive).

**P0 — the inventory is now measured, and it is the campaign's scope.**  One `llama-cli` run per model with
`HIPBLASLT_LOG_LEVEL=4` (5246-token prompt), hipBLASLt dispatches: **dense Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL = 0** (a
quantized dense model never touches it), **Gemma4-26B-A4B QAT = 29 for one F32 shape**, the router
`A[2816 x 128]` at N=375 (exactly §44), **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B = 159 for 3 F32 shapes** (`ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta`
`A[2048 x 32]` x2 + the router `A[2048 x 256]`), and **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ = 2790 for 27 BF16 shapes**
(attention/PLE projections, N in {42, 44, 512}).  So the correctness problem lives where F32 weights meet the
prefill band, and Flash-Next is the big consumer by count and is the one model where our own MMA path
(f16/bf16 WMMA) already exists.

**P1 — hipBLASLt's outside-slab footprint is a constant ~70 MiB, and it does not scale.**  Flash-Next GSQ,
2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48 -fa on`, `--load-mode mmap --lazy-mode off`, `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_STATS=1`, comparing
the slab's own `free_min` between the arms at identical config: **+70 MiB** at every point measured — 602 tok
`-c 16384` (wide-arm 735.0 -> 805.0, exit 351.5 -> 421.5), 5298 tok at `-ub 2048` *and* `-ub 8192` (exit
175.5 -> 245.5), **68 262 tok `-c 131072 -ub 8192`** (wide-arm +87, exit +70), and at `SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB` 512
and 256.  A per-call workspace would have to scale; the hipBLASLt log shows each call requesting 0 / 12 / 24 /
64 KiB, so the constant is **TensileLite code objects** plus a fixed small arena.  Therefore hipBLASLt is
~3.5 % of the slab's ~2 GiB headroom floor and **the campaign must not claim headroom as its motivation**;
the floor is the MTP draft buffer, the FA-QSA workspace, the pool high-water mark and the model's own
PLE/attention allocations.  (`ENVIRONMENT.md`'s "Why the cards sit near-full" lists hipBLASLt among those
consumers — this sizes it rather than removing the mention.)

**What a bypass must clear is not uniform.**  On 35B-A3B the F32 path is free (`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0`:
+1-3 % prefill, flat decode), but on Flash-Next it is worth **+51 % prefill** — 68 262 tokens, `-ub 8192`:
**2405.7 t/s with hipBLASLt vs 1595.1 without** (5298 tok `-ub 8192`: 966.8 vs 823.9; decode flat).  One
configuration (`5298 tok -ub 2048`: 630.9 on vs 823.1 off) does not fit that shape and is recorded as
unexplained, single-visit — do not quote it.  So the F32 job is a correctness win with no performance case
against it, and the BF16 job is a performance proposition first.

**P2 arm B ("raise `mmf`'s 16-column cap") is REFUTED as a cheap arm.**  Tried it behind `GGML_CUDA_MMF_MAX_COLS`
(patch kept at `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/tools/experiments/mmf-max-cols-ATTEMPT.patch`, applied to a working
`~/llama.cpp`, measured, **reverted**; never in `patches/`): on 35B-A3B the knob changes **nothing** (61
dispatches, same logits) because the F32 branch of `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmf` requires `amd_mfma_available`,
which is **CDNA-only** — `amd_wmma_available` covers RDNA3/4 but only f16/bf16, i.e. **RDNA has no native F32
MMA GEMM at all**.  On Flash-Next (BF16) raising the cap **aborts**:
`mmf.cuh:771 GGML_ASSERT(ids || ncols_dst <= 16)` — `cols_per_block` is a template argument and only the
`mul_mat_id` launch tiles columns (`block_nums_ids.y *= col_tiles`).  The 16-column cap is a **kernel** limit,
not a heuristic.  The tractable versions are a **column-tiled non-ids MMF launch** (bf16/f16 only) and a
**SIMT F32 skinny GEMM**, recorded as P3(i)/(ii) with the bars above.

**P2 arm A (pinning) is REFUTED as a shipping mechanism.**  Two attempts (`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/evidence/
p2-arm-a-pinning-attempts.txt`): `TENSILE_SOLUTION_INDEX=140215/140216` — the library's own "force a solution"
variable — has **no effect** on the rocBLAS→hipBLASLt dispatch (3 and 2 classes in 6 fresh starts each), and
`HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE`, written in the documented column layout for the shape hipBLASLt itself logs
(`A[R_32F 2048x32] x B[R_32F 2048x512]`, i.e. m=32, n=512, k=2048, `T,N`), is rejected outright:
*"The hipBLASLt git version and the override file git version are not the same"* — the file is locked to one
ROCm build, so it cannot live in `patches/`.  Determinism therefore has to come from **our code**: either an
explicit algo we select (arm G, `hipblasLtMatmul` with a deterministic `solution_id` — keeps the Flash-Next
+51 % prefill and is the recommended next step) or not calling hipBLASLt for the shapes that matter (P3).

**P2 arm G (deterministic algo in our code) is prototyped at the API level and is the session's main finding.**
A standalone probe (`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/tools/experiments/hipblaslt-algo-classes.cpp`,
`evidence/p2-arm-g-algo-classes.txt`) enumerates every hipBLASLt solution for the three shapes that matter, runs
it, hashes the output and times it.  The pool **splits into 3-4 bit-classes whose costs differ by up to 4x**,
and the class the heuristic lands in is the **slowest**: 35B-A3B alpha/beta `m=32 n=512 k=2048` f32 —
140215-140218 at 0.127-0.229 ms vs **140219-140222 at 0.045 ms** (3 classes, 12 runnable of 18); gemma4 router
`m=128 n=375 k=2816` f32 — 140215-140218 at 0.174-0.290 ms vs **140232 alone at 0.066 ms** (4 classes);
Flash-Next `m=320 n=512 k=10240` bf16 — 633 advertised, 3+ classes in the 78 that run, and the heuristic's
pick (110544) sits in a class none of them.  So a deterministic `getAllAlgos`-based pick is a determinism fix
**and potentially a prefill win**, and it keeps the Flash-Next advantage that makes arm E unacceptable.  A
necessary nuance, recorded so nobody over-claims: `hipblasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` was **stable** across 10+6
standalone fresh processes while the real run gives 3 classes in 8 starts, so the lottery lives in
**rocBLAS's** selection (`getAllSolutions()` heap order) — which is exactly the layer arm G bypasses.  What
remains for a future session is the end-to-end part only: call `hipblasLtMatmul` for the pinned shapes inside
`ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas`, add the `hipblaslt` link dependency, and prove one class across 12 fresh starts plus
a non-regressing interleaved prefill A/B.

**Docs.**  `wip/hipblaslt-bypass/README.md` gains §1.1 (per-model inventory), §1.3 (the VRAM answer), the arm-A
refutation, arm G with the class tables and its status in §4, plus `evidence/p0-inventory-all-models.txt`,
`p0-shapes-flash-next.txt`, `p1-hipblaslt-outside-slab.txt`, `p2-mmf-cap-attempt.txt`,
`p2-arm-a-pinning-attempts.txt`, `p2-arm-g-algo-classes.txt`, two experiment artifacts and a rewritten
`NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`; `TODO.md` #82 is retitled "correctness first" with the measured facts;
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44 gains the ~70 MiB constant and the model-dependent cost; `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` row refreshed.
The maintainer retracted the "hipBLASLt holds ~2 GiB" attribution in discussion #196 on the same day; the
measurement here agrees with the retraction.

## 261021.005 (docs) -- TODO #75 closed: the 35B-A3B per-start flip is the hipBLASLt solution lottery; `wip/hipblaslt-bypass` seeded

**Docs only: no patch, no `release.json` change, no tree change; `scripts/validate-set.sh` is unaffected.**
TODO #75 ("35B-A3B greedy text is not run-to-run deterministic with `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0`", filed
2026-10-19 at r90) is **CLOSED as external** — it is the same ROCm hipBLASLt per-process solution selection
that closed #67, on the GDN F32 `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` GEMM rather than on a router.  Record and reproducers:
`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/FINDINGS-2026-10-21-todo-75.md`.

**The witness, on the release runtime (gfx1201 `soar`, r102 build `7fa283979`, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 1 GPU, one
fresh process per sample).**  `llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 1 -fa on`, logits-dump hash: ROCm **10.1.0
default -> 3 classes in 8 starts** (`3629d90733a1` x5, `a855c2000912` x2, `6d32945460bd` x1);
**`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` -> 1 class in 8/8** (`2d9ed9ce03cb`); ROCm 10.0.0 libs -> 2 classes in 10 and 1 in
6/6 off.  `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` names the mechanism: the class *is* the TensileLite spine hipBLASLt
picked for that one F32 shape (`MT128x64x8` / `MT64x32x32` / `MT128x128x8` -> three different logit hashes,
61 dispatches each), and `HIPBLASLT_LOG_LEVEL=4` shows `getAllSolutions()` returning the same 18 candidates
(`140215`..`140232`) in **7 different orders in 8 fresh starts** — the heap-order defect
[rocm-libraries#11340](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries/pull/11340) fixes and no release we run contains.
Between two classes: **mean KLD 0.003479, same-top-p 98.431 %** — i.e. *just inside* the prefill-logit gate's
`0.005` / `98 %`, so the gate cannot see it by construction.

**Two method notes, both learned the hard way this session.**  (1) **A config that does not flip proves
nothing.**  `test-logits-width-probe` was single-valued on 10.1.0 (10/10 at 1 GPU, 8/8 at 2-GPU `-sm tensor`,
8/8 at P=1024) and still flips on the *perplexity* config — the instability is per-shape and per-run, so
validate on a config known to flip, with 8-12+ fresh starts.  (2) **A greedy-text hash is the wrong
instrument**: with the logits demonstrably class-varying, 200- and 500-token greedy text was identical 10/10
and 12/12.  Same lesson as #151; judge at the logits level.

**Why this is not the end of the story, and what replaced it.**  Chasing #75 exposed how little of our hot
path actually depends on hipBLASLt: `ggml-cuda` never calls it, rocBLAS dispatches to it only for a
**non-quantized `mul_mat` wider than `mmf`'s 16-column cap**, and on this set that is just the GDN F32
`ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` GEMM (`A[F32 2048x32]`) and the F32 MoE router (`A[F32 2048x256]`, 256 experts) —
the same pair structure on gemma4 — while a dense quantized 27B never reaches it at all (159 hipBLASLt
dispatches per 35B-A3B CLI prefill+32-token run).  On 35B-A3B/1 GPU `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` is
**free** (+1-3 % prefill, flat `tg128`, two interleaved visits) and saves **~70 MiB** of peak VRAM, not the
~2 GiB assumed in discussion #196 (that number, if it is real at all, is slab *headroom*, not hipBLASLt's
footprint — campaign step P1).  So the maintainer's follow-on is now a campaign rather than a TODO note:
**`wip/hipblaslt-bypass/`** (indexed in `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md`, tracked as **TODO #82**), with the design space
ranked cheap-to-structural (pin the solution via `HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE`; raise the `mmf` cap; a
native skinny-F32 GEMM; requantize the F32 weights), the gates for any candidate, and `tools/hbl-classes.sh`
/ `hbl-kernels.sh` / `hbl-shapes.sh` so the next session starts from an instrument rather than a hunch.

**Docs.**  `TODO.md` loses #75 (row + body) and gains #82 (row + scoping body); `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` gains the
campaign row; `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §44 gains the second call site and the Linux cost measurement; `README.md`'s
issue-#67 section notes that the GDN call site reproduces on 35B-A3B too.
## 261021.004 (r102) -- PR #199 (gfx1100 head-512 WMMA FA rows) and PR #200 (GDN / attention-gate decode fusions) promoted

Two contributor PRs folded as **two block amendments** (no new block): **v12-097cf33d9-r102**, 12 blocks,
fork point `097cf33d9`, tip `5e37fa61d`, tree `42679a04ff814600483326a05353d272227e186e`.  Every number below
was taken with `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` (issue #67) and one GPU job at a time, on the r101 tree plus the
patches; `scripts/check-gpu-faults.sh` clean on gfx1201, gfx1100.

**Block 05 gains the RDNA3_0 head-512 WMMA rows (PR #199, @briansp2020).**  The RDNA head-512 rows of
`ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_rdna` were tuned on gfx1201 with Q in registers, so on gfx1100 every
head-512 kernel sat at the 256-VGPR limit and spilled ~1.0-1.4k VGPRs per lane -- which is why head 512 was
capped back to the tile kernel on RDNA3_0 in r5 (issue #30).  RDNA3_0 now has its own rows (Q in shared
memory, 128 threads, 64-wide K/V/combine batches) and head 512 takes WMMA prefill again on top of the 256
cap; RDNA4/RDNA3_5 rows are untouched, other heads above 256 keep the tile kernel, and the decode/verify
band stays on tile.  Measured on **fingon** (gfx1100, RX 7900 XTX), gemma-4-26B-A4B QAT UD-Q4_K_XL, q8_0
K/V, pp2048: **d32768 1908.3/1909.2 -> 2549.1/2554.6 t/s (+34 %)**, **d65536 1209.3/1207.6 -> 1756.2/1757.5
(+45 %)**, tg128 at d32768 unchanged (127.74/127.74 -> 127.80/127.73).  `GGML_CUDA_FA_RDNA3_WMMA_512=0`
reproduces r101's text bit for bit (`cf175b78ecd1`); the default arm gives different text, as any prefill
kernel change does.  `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` 6391/6391 on gfx1100, and gfx1201 **and** gfx1151
output is byte-identical to r101 (gemma4 26B-A4B), so the claim "RDNA4/RDNA3_5 unchanged" holds.

**Prefill-logit: accepted deviation, documented rather than papered over (`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §46, TODO #81,
`wip/fa-rdna3-head512-purity/`).**  This is a tile->WMMA *family* switch and it does **not** meet the
absolute gate: mean KLD **0.0293**, same-top-p **92.59 %** on that model (the gate's point is out of its
calibrated domain -- base PPL 604 against 5.93 for the pinned 27B Q8_0).  Calibrated at the same point and
protocol: the **head-256 WMMA rows the set has shipped default-on for gfx1100 since r5 measure 0.0441 /
90.63 %**, a benign ubatch change on the same kernel ~0.12 per chunk, and issue #113's BF16 chunked GDN
0.62.  PPL is unchanged within its +/-5 % error bar (f16 K/V 604.06 vs 607.20, q8_0 617.85 vs 620.59).  So
the change is more faithful than the shipped equivalent switch, and the maintainer's decision was to ship
it default-on with the deviation recorded and a campaign to close it -- not to hand-wave the gate.
`GGML_CUDA_FA_RDNA3_WMMA_512=0` is the kill switch.

**Block 10 gains the four GDN / attention-gate decode fusions (PR #200, @briansp2020), plus a structural
guard.**  `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GATE_BETA_BF16` (qwen4exp alpha/beta BF16 projections + `softplus(alpha + dt) * a`
in one `mul_mat_vec_f` launch), `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_CONV_NORM` (the q/k l2 norm pair folded into the direct
conv kernel, only when both SCALE outputs are disjoint from the conv's `x`/state/weight/output -- the
allocator may place them over the state or `x`, which the direct kernel still reads, and without the check
35B-A3B varied run to run), `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_CONT_GATE_Q8_1` (the attention gate's row-strided view read in
place, so its `CONT` copies nothing) and `GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_NORM_GATE` (qwen4exp's GDN output `RMS_NORM * w`
computed inside the gate kernel).

The GDN-norm pair is the one fusion whose skip and emit are two decisions (the norm node precedes the gate
node that computes it), and the submitted form joined them with a context pointer guarded by two
`GGML_ABORT`s.  We instrumented the window instead of trusting it: on the only graph it fires on (qwen4exp)
it is always **span 4 with a fixed signature, `[RMS_NORM][MUL][MUL_MAT][RESHAPE][UNARY(sigmoid)]`**, and the
full chain including the gate matmul lookup is already validated at skip time -- so the only hazard is
another fusion *starting inside the window and spanning the gate*.  The guard makes that impossible: while a
norm is pending no other fusion may start before its gate node, and the pending norm's own `MUL` (dead: the
gate kernel reads `xn` and `w` directly) is skipped too.  The two abort tripwires therefore stay as
tripwires, unreachable rather than merely unlikely, and the window nodes run unfused at the cost of one
plain matmul per GDN layer (measured: no change to the 27B MTP gain).

Gates on the folded tree (r101 base, gfx1201): greedy text **identical in five arms** (27B plain and MTP n3,
35B-A3B 1 GPU and 2 GPU `-sm tensor`, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS 2 GPU `-sm tensor` + shared MTP head);
`test-logits-width-probe` per-W hashes identical to r101; the prefill-logit gate **0.000707 / 98.755 %** for
both builds (the r101 numbers exactly); `test-backend-ops` SSM_CONV 47, RMS_NORM 55, SCALE 9, MUL_MAT 2446,
0 failures; rule-5 batched decode within noise (B=1 1.008 vs 1.009 s, B=4 1.248 vs 1.247, B=8 1.743 vs
1.743).  Decode: **27B MTP +0.2-0.3 %** (48.6/48.6/48.5 -> 48.7/48.6/48.7), **Flash-Next 2 GPU tensor + MTP
+0.7 %** (83.4 -> 84.2 mean of 3), **35B-A3B 1 GPU tg128 -0.2 %** -- the submitter's +0.5 % there did not
reproduce, and 35B-A3B decode does not take the direct conv path anyway.  All four switches on vs all four
off on the patched build is 48.8/48.7 vs 48.5/48.4, so the mechanism is the delta.

**Fold rule.**  Block 05 owns `fattn.cu` / `fattn-mma-f16.cuh` and block 10 owns every file PR #200 touches

## 261021.001 (docs) -- MTP determinism closed: it is the per-start hipBLASLt solution pick (issue #67), not a code defect

**The 2026-10 MTP determinism item is closed as external.**  The residual run-to-run divergence of the
`gemma4 26B-A4B` + MTP + `-ncmoe 40 -sm layer` config on gfx1201 / Linux / **ROCm 10.1.0** is ROCm's
hipBLASLt solution selection being picked **per process start** for an untuned FP32 GEMM size --
issue #67 / ROCm/rocm-libraries#12126 -- not a defect in this patch set.

Instruments: the draft-candidate-logit fingerprint (a greedy text hash is *not* a determinism instrument on
this box; the rendered SSE stream varies per run regardless of the logits).  Numbers, one fresh process per
sample: default env **3 classes in 18 starts** (`6f6923ef36`x12, `51274cb0f2`x4, `10e1f21f4c`x2, call-0
top-1 0.458 / 0.352 / 0.439); **`ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` -> 10/10 at `-n 300` and 3/3 at `-n 3000`**
(904 draft calls).  `HIPBLASLT_LOG_MASK=160` shows the only BLASLt dispatch in the run -- gemma4's F32
**MoE router** (`m=128 n=375 k=2816 T,N f32_r`, 30 calls = one per layer) -- with `solution_index 140231`
vs `140232` per process, and on that shape the two are **not** bit-identical.

**Retracted: the graph/capture story.**  With the library path off, graphs on and graphs off give the *same*
single class, so capture/replay was never implicated.  Every arm of the hunt ("target graphs off is stable
at `8f795fbaf0`", draft-only off, decode-only off, verify-only off, force-recapture-every-replay) was this
lottery resolving to a class.  Also cleared directly: the draft's input embedding (`h_nextn` of the three
prompt ubatches agrees exactly across classes) and the async-input ring post-`0005` (`ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH=0`
is itself a stable class, `ASYNC_INPUT=0` is still a lottery).  `0005` stays a real fix (a genuine
cross-context ordering bug) -- it was not the last 20 %.

Docs: `AGENTS.md` "Critical facts" (pinned fresh-process comparisons, never a text hash) and
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` **§44** + invariant 9 (+ a correcting pointer in §41).  **hipBLASLt stays enabled in the
delivery** -- disabling it costs up to -15 % decode; `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0` is the tester's reproducibility
switch, and the upstream fix (`rocm-libraries` `c50ea60130f`, TheRock nightlies from 2026-10-06) removes the
cause.  Record: `wip/fix-gemma-4/evidence/MEASUREMENTS-2026-10-21d.md`.  No delivery artefact changed.

## 261020.014 (r100) -- issue #184 fix promoted (split-state walk scratch); PR #177 re-reviewed and still declined

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r100`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `db675e2db`, net tree
`4775fc92b9007b279062ad43a63150a8a2ebe7db`, **12 blocks**.  Block 09 amended, no new block.  One new
environment variable, a kill switch (`GGML_META_SS_SCRATCH`, default on).

### Issue #184 (`@briansp2020`) -- the split-state pre-warm walk allocates no heap nodes -- FIXED

The first phase (r86-candidate, `261018.010`) answered the reported r80 -> r82 3.5 % 4-stream regression:
not reproducible here (<= 0.4 %, sign unstable, 224 B of `.text`, no inlining change).  The reporter then
took the cold-helper direction himself and measured the remaining cost at the right place: **the walk's
containers**.  Per graph re-allocation his timers show ~2800 pre-warm walks, ~150k visited tensors, ~4.7k
split states and **94 % of the `malloc` calls under `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph` in `wseen`'s inserts** (one
heap node per visited tensor plus the rehash and the frees); a `std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource` over a
reused 1 MiB per-thread buffer took his re-allocation from 21.1 to 16.0 ms, four concurrent streams +5.0 %,
TTFT -26 ms, output identical.

**Landed (block 09, 22 lines):** `wstack`/`wseen` are `std::pmr::vector` / `std::pmr::unordered_set` over a
reused `thread_local` 1 MiB `monotonic_buffer_resource`, released at the top of each walk;
`GGML_META_SS_SCRATCH=0` selects the default (heap) resource, so the A/B is one binary and one env.  Only
the outermost call walks, so the resource is never re-entered; the walk visits the same tensors in the same
order; an exhausted arena falls back to the upstream allocator, so nothing is capped.

**Gates** (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0, release tree `4775fc92`, A/B by swapping only
`libggml-base.so.0.26.0`): 4B Q8_0 3 GPU coherence `1c5d32ac537d` == r99; 27B UD-Q4_K_XL 2 GPU tensor q8_0
KV 200-token greedy `5067a0089fc1` (plain == `draft-mtp` n3 == r99) **with and without
`GGML_META_SS_VERIFY=1`** (which recomputes every outermost cache hit and aborts on a stale entry, so the
states are proven identical); prefill-logit KLD **0.000707 / 98.755 %** (== r99, PASS);
`test-backend-ops -o RMS_NORM,ADD,MUL_MAT,CPY,CONCAT,SSM_CONV` on ROCm0+ROCm1 **6262 OK / 0 FAIL**, 3/3
backends; per-block build 3/3 (blocks 09-11); `validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 from a fresh
tarball, tree `4775fc92`); every r100 log clean under `check-gpu-faults.sh` (the kernel journal has one
fault cluster at 13:49 from an earlier session, nothing during any r100 run).

**Perf.**  `llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8` (27B UD-IQ3_S, 3 GPU tensor, q8_0 KV, total
t/s, 3 interleaved rounds): **B=1 61.3 -> 62.4 (+1.6 %)**, **B=4 201.5 -> 202.7 (+0.6 %)**, **B=8 317.9 ->
319.5 (+0.5 %)**.  The reporter's 4-stream server shape (Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2 GPU tensor `-ncmoe 47`, MTP
n3): pre-warmed pure decode **+0.29 %** (3 pairs), 4 concurrent chats with the prefills in the window
**+0.36 %** mean over 7 pairs (paired -3.5 .. +4.9 %).  Smaller than his +5 % for a measurable reason: his
workload re-allocates ~230 times per run, this box's config reports 1-5 `graph reallocs` per request, so
the walk is a proportionally smaller share of wall time.  Shipped because it is neutral-to-positive on
every gate here and removes ~4.7k heap nodes per re-allocation on the shape that has the churn.

Record: `archive/work/issue-184-meta-r80r82/RESOLUTION.md` (+ `ab.py`, `ab_mixed.py`); `ENVIRONMENT.md` §2;
`patches/README.md` block 09.

### PR #177 (`gdn-conv-snapshot-fold`, `@briansp2020`) -- re-reviewed, still DECLINED (determinism)

Re-cut onto r99 (one conflict: the RDNA3_0 verify-batch comment) and gated on the same probe.  **The dense
claim now holds**: 27B UD-Q4_K_M 1 GPU is bit-identical to stock and stable at P=256
(`0e33b420b37beba4`) and P=3584 (`9c12636638742221`), 2/2 each.  **35B-A3B is the blocker**, and the bisect
narrowed it: stock r99 is stable (`97ad459c74d8a694` / `d24b26226690e95b`, 3/3 each) while r99 + #177 is
stably *different* at P=256 (`29cb3722a842846a`, 8/8) and **nondeterministic at P=3584**
(`2b1caf3bd5cfe4e3` x3 / `c2336484ebf6dab2` x2); the kill switch reproduces stock exactly.  Not the expert
cache, staging, dev gather, gather index or the gather fusion; `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0` moves it to a
third value.  Keeping the snapshot CPY reproduces stock even with the conv kernel writing the same
destination (the destination hash is identical after both writes), so **the fold's write is byte-exact**;
and a node-by-node F32 hash of the prefill puts the first difference at the `ssm_alpha` LoRA `MUL_MAT`,
upstream of every write the patch moves.  Adding `gdn_concat_tail` alone moves the result to a third
value, so this model's prefill is sensitive to the launch sequence itself (the open `TODO.md` #75 class).
Re-entry is unchanged: identical probe hashes to stock across 5 runs at P=256 and P=3584 on both models,
with graphs on.  Record: `archive/work/gdn-conv-snapshot-fold/RESOLUTION.md` (second-review section);
comment on the PR.

**A note on instruments:** a *terminal* `llama-cli` text hash is not valid for a determinism claim -- the
stream carries `\b` corrections, so raw output differs by streaming chunking even when the text is
identical.  Use `scripts/extract-generated.py`.  (An intermediate conclusion in this session, that stock
r99 gives three different 35B-A3B texts at `-sm tensor`, was such an artifact and is retracted: with
`extract-generated.py` the release build is stable 4/4 at `0c2291183d46`.)

(`722063f3e28d` / `e3b891655a80` / `27d50a6d97f5`) on the plain default path.  r97 (`WORKLOG.md` 261020.008)
made `ggml_cuda_async_input_flush_done` unconditional on the `=0` arm, so the question was whether that
fixed it.

**Result: not reproducible here, on either side of the fix.**  30 fresh-process runs, r99 (`6adf0b802`),
1 device, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, `-ngl 99`, seed 42, temp 0:

| arm | runs | distinct results |
|---|---|---|
| `ASYNC_INPUT=0`, `-n 400` | 6 | **1** text |
| `ASYNC_INPUT=0 -ub 8` / `-ub 1` | 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| `ASYNC_INPUT=0 --ignore-eos -n 400` | 3 | 1 text |
| default (async **on**), `--ignore-eos -n 400` | 4 | 1 (same text as the `=0` arm) |
| `test-logits-width-probe`, W=1..8, `=0` | 5 | W=1 hash `5e73d60b4c4df784` every run, `width_purity=PASS` every run |
| **r95** (`fe1befcf7`, **pre**-r97), `=0 --ignore-eos` | 3 | 1 text |
| r94-era (`eb81ac725`), same | 3 | 1 text |

The pre-r97 builds are equally deterministic, so gfx1151 cannot distinguish "r97 cured it" from "this box
never showed it": it is not a valid witness either way.  (The text hash is stable at the *logits* level too,
so this is not a text-vs-ULP masking artifact.)

**Two findings worth carrying forward.**

1. **`-n 400` is not 400 tokens on this model/prompt.**  It EOS-terminates at 1505 chars (~150 t), so a
   naive 400-token comparison silently measures a shorter generation than the original finding.  The runs
   above use `--ignore-eos` (1895 chars, the full 400) — the next attempt must do the same, or use a long
   prompt.
2. **Which builds a bisect must cover.**  Since #75 was filed at r90 the only async-ring change is r97's
   unconditional flush.  But the original observation is stock **r88**, i.e. *before* r89's batched uploads
   (PR #182) and r90's split-input snapshot fix, so the A/B is r88 -> r89/r90 -> r97 -> r99, not just
   r95 vs r99.

**Next step (gfx1201 box).**  Re-establish the witness on the r88 binary if it is still available (6+ runs,
`ASYNC_INPUT=0 --ignore-eos -n 400`, both the 1-GPU and the 2-GPU `-sm tensor` arm), then the same on r95 and
r99, reusing the original harness/prompt (`archive/work/kv-quant-purity-followups/tools/textgen.py`, 12-hex
text hashes) for a like-for-like comparison.  r88/r95 mixed + r99 single => r97 is the cure and #75 closes on
it; r88 single too => the witness is gone on the current stack and #75 needs re-scoping.

## 261020.011 (r99) -- TODO #56 fixed (upstream MoE cache callback) and PR #198 (RDNA2 FA follow-ups) promoted

### TODO #56 -- the scheduler never invoked the copy callback (block 09) -- FIXED

The delivery's rewritten `ggml_backend_sched_copy_input` kept no `sched->callback_copy` call, and that call
is the only thing in the tree that drives `llama_moe_cache::copy()`.  With `--moe-cache-mib` set the slot map
therefore stayed `0xff` (-1) while the graph had already swapped the routed op's `src0` for the cache bank and
its ids for `GET_ROWS(slot_map, ids)`, so `MUL_MAT_ID` indexed the bank with `-1`: a silent wrong value where
the page below the bank is mapped (gfx1201, NMSE 4.02e-03) and an HSA page fault where it is not (gfx1151;
gfx1201 with `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0`).

Base's call is restored at base's position (after the wait-before-overwrite) and in the branch with no
`MUL_MAT_ID` consumer, which is where the slot map lands (its consumer is a `GET_ROWS`); the delivery's own
expert branch (device gather, cache take-over, pruning) is byte-for-byte unchanged, so no host expert table
can reach the callback.  `llama_context::sched_copy_experts` now answers only for the upstream cache: its
per-op staging/pruning body and `copy_experts_info` state are deleted (dead since block 09's scheduler took
that over, and they would double-stage every host expert table now that the callback is wired).

Gates (gfx1201, canonical r99 build): `test-llama-archs -s 42` **375/375** (r98 373/375), also 375/375 with
`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0`; the `deepseek2` `MoE cache` row reads **2.10e-10** (the upstream base's own value)
where r98 read 4.02e-03; host-expert greedy text identical to r98 (35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`, `4ae79b6e45fc`);
prefill-logit KLD 0.000000 / 100.000 %.  Inert unless `--moe-cache-mib` is set.

Accepted, recorded in the archive record: the upstream cache's large-batch `copy_experts()` arm stays
unreached (values identical either way, so a missing upstream optimisation rather than a correctness gap),
and `--moe-cache-mib` is now correct but slower than `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` on this box (decode 50.1 -> 37.8
t/s on 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`), so it is documented as "works, not recommended".  **TODO #56 is closed.**
Record: `archive/work/todo-56-moe-cache-callback/` (with a `RESOLUTION.md`; the `wip/` entry is deleted, no
stub left behind).

## 261020.010 (r98) -- PR #195 (q8_0 FA fetch-ahead) promoted into block 05; PR #194 declined

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r98`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `aafd389b0`, net tree
`7b6b428011320af45168dee6278716c55e3eb6c1`, **12 blocks**.  Block 05 amended, no new block.

### PR #195 `rdna4-band-fetch-ahead` (`@overdoingism`) -- PROMOTED, block 05, default on

With `q8_0` K and V read in place (decode/verify, `n_q <= 8`, head 256) the RDNA4 band launches a second
kernel variant, `flash_attn_ext_f16<..., band_fetch_ahead = true>`, that fetches the raw q8_0 bytes of the
next K/V batches into registers ahead of use and converts a batch into shared memory only when it is due.
Its barriers order shared memory only (release / `s_barrier` / acquire on `"local"`): `__syncthreads()`
also waits for every outstanding global load, which would drain the fetches.  The quants stay packed in
32-bit words and an empty `asm volatile` pins the conversion at the stage point.  64-column block (widths
5..8): two batches in flight, Q in registers.  32-column block (widths 1..4): one batch in flight and the
stream continues across the iteration boundary into the next unmasked KV block, Q read from shared memory.
The variant is compiled in two generated translation units of its own, so every other launch keeps its
compiled code.  `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_FETCH_AHEAD=0` runs the kernel without it.

**The claim that mattered, and it holds.**  Device objects were extracted from both builds and the gfx1201
ISA diffed with mangled names normalised: **0 differing instructions** in both `dkq256` band instances, a
`dkq128` instance, `fattn-tile`, `fattn-vec` and `fattn.cu`.  The variant kernel is `W` in its own
generated TU and `U` in the two `-case-` TUs that select it (the FA instantiation rule).

Gates (gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, 27B UD-Q4_K_XL with `q8_0` K/V unless noted), all on the **canonical** r98
build after a fresh `validate-set.sh` apply:

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` | 6391 OK / 0 FAIL on both builds, identical per-case |
| prefill-logit KLD (27B Q8_0; and `-ub 8` / `-ub 1` on 27B UD-Q4_K_M) | 0.000000 / 100.000 % in all three |
| greedy text vs r97, 8K and 110K context | identical (`a9296d829c35`, `1580326fb41e`) |
| greedy text vs r97, 2 GPU tensor 8K / gemma4 12B (head-256 SWA) | identical (`63b6b7cf6fdf`, `dbe017af390a`) |
| 4-axis MTP `-n 3000` (P/C/K/R) | text and acceptance identical; P 71.7 C 80.8 K 86.4 R 59.8 t/s |
| `n7` vs plain (64-column, depth 2) | identical text |
| `llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8` | B=1 29.47 -> 30.12, B=4 95.73 -> 97.70, B=8 flat |
| kill switch (`GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_FETCH_AHEAD=0`) | identical text and throughput |
| `check-gpu-faults.sh` | clean |

The 4-axis gate was run on dense 27B (1 GPU, `q8_0` K/V) rather than the qwen4exp cell, because the tree
gated here is byte-identical to the tree PR #195 was verified on and the only delta is the q8_0 band
variant; the dense cell exercises both band blocks (widths 1..4 at `n3`, 5..8 at `n7`).

Speed, 3 interleaved pairs each: **8K 29.3 -> 29.5 t/s** (+0.7 %, r98 canonical build 29.7), **110K
24.5 -> 25.1 t/s** (+2.4 %, canonical 25.1), 2 GPU tensor 8K 45.2 -> 45.6; prefill unchanged (840.0 ->
839.2 t/s at 110K).  The submitter's end-to-end note (measured on an earlier single-kernel form) is
therefore conservative for the shipped form.

Record (with the submitted patch and README): `archive/work/rdna4-band-fetch-ahead/`, `RESOLUTION.md`.

### PR #194 `set-tensor-async-ring` (`@briansp2020`) -- DECLINED, no delivery change

It keeps r90's `set_tensor_async` snapshot guarantee (self-KLD control 100.000 % at `-ub 8` and `-ub 1`),
but it **drains the graph-input upload queue** before every direct copy, which turns the batched upload
kernel (`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH`, PR #182) back into per-copy uploads.  Measured on r97, 3 interleaved
pairs: Flash-Next 2 GPU tensor `-ncmoe 10` MTP n3 **131.4 -> 129.8 t/s (-1.2 %)**, 35B-A3B 2 GPU tensor
`-ncmoe 10` MTP n3 **184.6 -> 180.3 (-2.3 %)**, dense 27B neutral (1 GPU plain and 2 GPU tensor MTP).  With
`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH=0` both builds read exactly 129.1 t/s, which isolates the mechanism.

The PR reply asks for the drain to be scoped to the destination-overlap case (`ggml_cuda_async_input_set`
already does that), and notes the two smaller points: the per-context ring takes no lock where the
per-device ring takes `d.mtx`, and `cudaEventSynchronize` on a half switch is a host-blocking wait in the
upload path.  Record: `archive/work/set-tensor-async-ring/` (no `wip/` stub; the PR arrived as a branch).

## 261020.008 (r97) -- halo arch-independent fixes (CPU-only MoE, QSA CPU form, reserve sequence count) + two defects they exposed

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r97`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `b37a3b5ad`, net tree
`f81213c4dcb057636ef6afdfef7e4c4907a4d83f`, **12 blocks**.  Blocks 09 and 10 amended, no new block.

**What landed (gfx1151 handover, rebased onto r96 and folded per block).**

* **Block 09 — the host-expert account keys a real device only.**  `moe_host_expert_account` inserted
  `acc[buft_dev]` unconditionally, and `ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type()` has `.device = NULL` upstream, so a
  CPU-only model (or `--override-tensor exps=CPU`) keyed a null device and `llama_context` aborted in
  `ggml_backend_dev_memory()` while auto-sizing the staging ring.  The fix **skips a host buft that carries
  no device** rather than keying the layer's device: a pageable master is not served by this block (the
  arena, ring and cache read the master in place from a device kernel, which needs pinned memory) — it is
  copied by the upstream `llama_moe_cache` engine, so it must stay unaccounted.  A pinned host buft always
  carries its device, so every `-ncmoe`/`-cmoe` path is unchanged.  (The handover patch keyed the *layer's*
  device instead; that also fixes the abort but reserves a ring/arena for a master this block then cannot
  use, and it measured identical on every arch-test row — the skip is the tighter rule.)
* **Block 10 — the QSA derived-visibility form is gated on the acting backend.**  The CPU reference
  implements the mask form of `FLASH_ATTN_QSA` only, but the sparse path allocated `cell_vis`/`q_vis`
  (`src[5]`/`src[6]`) even on a CPU layer and aborted.  CPU `supports_op` now refuses the derived form
  (there is no CPU kernel for it), and `qwen4exp` probes the form the graph will actually build
  (`qsa_derived_vis_supported`), falling back to the dense masked path when the device cannot run it.
  This is also what closes **#57**: the `qwen4exp` CPU row's `Mixed batch` reads **3.32e-14**, the same as
  the upstream base (`deepseek2`'s CPU `Mixed batch` is 1.11e-09, also the base's value).
* **Block 10 — the rollback/narrow reserve uses the real sequence count.**  The synthetic reserve used
  `ubatch.n_seqs` (a *shape* value: 64 for a 64-token single-sequence ubatch) as the sequence count, so it
  built a 64-stream 4-D kq mask against a single-stream query and `deepseek2` aborted in
  `ggml_flash_attn_ext` (`q->ne[3] % mask->ne[3]`).  It now uses `ubatch.n_seqs_unq`, except for the dsv4
  compressed cache (`LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4`, and DFLASH with `dsv4_hc_mult > 0`), whose raw attention needs
  the per-stream index fanout shape and which therefore keeps `ubatch.n_seqs` — exactly its previous
  behaviour.  A side-effect-free reserve for that cache remains a follow-up.  The one line that lived in
  **block 11** code (the r96 early narrow floor probe) was folded there, not into block 10.

**Two defects the fixes above exposed, and what was done about them.**

* **`test-llama-archs -a deepseek4` was wrong under `-sm tensor` (found on gfx1201, FIXED here).**  Block 10
  flipped `cparams.fused_dsv4_hc_post` from on to off (the `hc_combine_norm` chain measured +0.9..+1.8 %
  prefill on one gfx1151 device).  That chain is **not correct across a tensor split**: its broadcasts are
  split-state sensitive, and `deepseek4`'s `Meta` row read NMSE **1.74e-01** (2 GPUs 1.25e-01; 1 GPU and
  `-sm layer` bit-identical to the CPU reference).  Bisected to that single line (reverting
  `src/llama-context.cpp` alone fixed it; the fused op gives 6.5e-06, and the whole delivery's
  `ggml-cuda`, `llama-kv-cache`, `llama-model`, split-state and kernel changes were all excluded by
  file-level reverts + a per-node dump).  The default is now split-mode aware: the **op** whenever a Meta
  device is in play, the faster chain on one device; `LLAMA_FUSED_DSV4_HC_POST` still forces either arm.
  `deepseek4` is 5/5 (Meta 6.53e-06), `qwen4exp` 5/5, `deepseek2` unchanged.
* **`deepseek2`'s `MoE cache` rows are now reachable on gfx1201 and fail numerically (TODO #56).**  Before
  this release the arch test aborted before those rows (context creation, then graph build), which is why
  the memory fault was only ever seen on gfx1151.  Here they read NMSE **4.02e-03** and the run completes;
  the base `097cf33d9` passes them (2.10e-10).  Everything the delivery owns is inert for these rows
  (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0`, `GGML_CUDA_SLAB=0`, `GGML_SCHED_STAGE=0`, `GGML_SCHED_MOE_DUP_SPLIT=0`,
  `GGML_MOE_CACHE_STAGE=0`, `GGML_MOE_CACHE_MAX_TOK=1`), `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID` is 947/947, and
  the upstream cache implementation, `build_moe_cache_slots` and `sched_copy_experts` are byte-identical to
  upstream — so this is still the block-09 plumbing around the upstream `llama_moe_cache` engine, i.e. #56
  itself, recorded there with these numbers.  It is **not** caused by this set: it reproduces with the
  accounting disabled and with only the block-09 fix applied.

**A third defect, also fixed here: `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0` was broken.**  The kill-switch arm died in
`ggml_cuda_async_input_copy_locked` with `ROCm error: invalid resource handle` the first time a device was
reused by a second context (`test-llama-archs -a deepseek4`'s `Meta` row, i.e. the first context on device 0
after the per-device row's context was destroyed).  `ggml_cuda_async_input_flush_done` still early-returned
on `!g_async_input_on`, but since r90 the pinned ring also carries the `set_tensor_async` /
`set_tensor_2d_async` snapshots **unconditionally**, so context teardown left a *pending* done-event naming a
stream that the destructor then destroyed and the next context recorded on the dead handle.  The flush is now
unconditional (a no-op when nothing is pending), matching the done guard and `ggml_cuda_async_input_wait`.
`deepseek4` with `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0` is 5/5, Meta 6.53e-06 — identical to the default arm.
**Side finding for #56:** with the kill-switch arm now working, `deepseek2`'s `MoE cache` row on gfx1201
reproduces the **recorded HSA memory fault** (`mul_mat_vec_f<float, float, 1, 64, false, true>`, faulting
address in a host/pinned range) instead of the 4.02e-03 numeric mismatch the default arm shows — so the
upstream cache engine's over-read is real on this box too, and the async-input path is what changes its
manifestation.  Both arms are recorded in `TODO.md` #56.

**Tooling.**  `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh` now defaults to `/opt/rocm-10.1.0-gfx120X` (env `ROCM_DIR`;
the old `ROCM_714` is still honoured) and passes the joined `-isystem<rocm>/include` in `CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS`
with the `flags.make` include-order guard — the same rule as `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`.  Without it the gate
resolved HIP headers from Fedora's ROCm 7.1 `/usr/include`: on 10.1 every TU fails
(`__ocml_exp10_f32` undeclared), on 7.14 it silently compiled the distro headers.  `ENVIRONMENT.md`'s
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` example now names the 10.1 tree; dated records were left alone.

**Validation (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0).**  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (12 blocks, strict
apply on a fresh tarball, tree `c2f1bc29…`); `scripts/gate-per-block-build.sh --changed-from 59d069467`
3/3 (blocks 09/10/11 build `all`); `test-llama-archs -s 42` -> `qwen4exp` 5/5, `deepseek4` 5/5,
`deepseek2` 5/7 (only TODO #56's two `MoE cache` rows); CPU-only `gpt-oss-20b -ngl 0 -n 4` generates (the
pre-patch build still aborts at `ggml-backend.cpp:921`); `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_QSA` 26/26 per
ROCm backend + a direct `supports_op` probe showing the CPU still accepts the mask form and refuses the
derived one while ROCm accepts both (so the GPU rows keep the sparse derived path); `gate-prefill-logits.sh`
PASS (mean KLD 0.000707, same-top-p 98.755 %); dense 4B Q8_0 3-GPU tensor greedy text identical to the
r96 build; 35B-A3B Q4_K_M `-sm layer -ncmoe 40` runs on the pinned accounting path (84.7 t/s tg).

**Note for gate writers.**  `test-backend-ops` skips the CPU backend unconditionally (it only runs CPU in
`MODE_GRAD`), so `-o FLASH_ATTN_QSA` does **not** exercise the CPU mask-form oracle; and
`test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` never reaches `qsa_derived_vis_supported` (the synthetic model builds no QSA
derived path), so that test cannot confirm which QSA form the GPU takes — the `supports_op` probe does.

## 261020.007 (r96) -- sched-moe-dup-consumer + state-read-batch promoted (PR #186 + PR #189), and the `-sm layer` MTP corruption they fix

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r96`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `2fc3b2f53`, net tree
`cad83cc3af1b1a678d743926470764ab4fd198b3`, **12 blocks**.  Blocks 09 and 11 amended, no new block.
Both PRs are from `@briansp2020` and were cut against r89/r91; both are commented with the release and the
verification below, then closed.

**What landed.**

* **Block 09, PR #186 (`wip/sched-moe-dup-consumer`).**  In `ggml_backend_sched_split_graph`, a
  cache-managed routed op whose expert weights are already an input of the current split now starts a split
  of its own, so the existing re-registration path stages them again for that consumer's own routing.
  qwen4exp's last layer has two `MUL_MAT_ID` consumers of one table (the gathered logits tail and the
  full-row MTP export tail), and with both in one split neither can be served by the expert cache, so the
  scheduler's guarded fast paths decline.  `GGML_SCHED_MOE_DUP_SPLIT=0` restores the merged split (new,
  default-on; A/B and bisection only).  `Fold (r96, PR #186)` note at the site.
* **Block 09, PR #189 (meta half).**  `ggml_backend_meta_get_tensor_async` now shares the synchronous read's
  split arithmetic (it no longer asserts `offset == 0` and one segment), so a caller can queue an arbitrary
  row range across the simple backends and synchronize once.  Calls that worked before issue the same copies.
* **Block 11, PR #189 (context half).**  `llama_io_write_host` queues its deferred state-save reads as
  `ggml_backend_tensor_get_async` into one pinned staging buffer kept by the context (`state_stage`), then
  synchronizes each backend once and copies to the caller's buffer.  `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0` restores the
  synchronous path; `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB` (default **256**) bounds the state that takes it, so a
  whole-slot save never pins gigabytes.  Restores are unchanged.  The staging buffer is retained per
  context (16 MiB granular, bounded by the cap) and is one buffer per context, so state saves on one
  context must not run concurrently; both are recorded in `ENVIRONMENT.md` and in the code.
* **The patch as submitted does not compile on this tree**: `llama_state_sync_all` uses `std::find` and
  `src/llama-context.cpp` has no `#include <algorithm>` (`no member named 'find' in namespace 'std'`).
  The include is added in the fold (block 11) and was reported back on the PR.

**Fold.**  `git blame` on the pre-fold 12-block tip confirmed ownership: `ggml-backend.cpp` (split) and
`ggml-backend-meta.cpp` (async read) -> block 09, `src/llama-context.cpp/.h` -> block 11.  Blocks 00-08 came
out as **identical commit objects** (their patch bodies are byte-identical; only the `From <sha>` line
changes because the chain is re-cut), and the pre-fold tree (`r95 + both PRs + the include`) and the folded
tree are both `cad83cc3af1b1a678d743926470764ab4fd198b3`.  Regenerated with `make-patches.sh` +
`make-release.sh`; `validate-set.sh` green (checksums, strict 12/12 `git am` on a fresh tarball, applied tree
`cad83cc3`); `gate-per-block-build.sh` **12/12, 0 failed**.

**The finding: #186 also fixes a pre-existing r95 correctness bug.**  On r95, `-sm layer` + `--ncmoe` +
`draft-mtp` on a qwen4exp model intermittently emits text that is not greedy pure, with 0.00000 draft
acceptance: the merged split's second consumer reads the expert-cache arena slots staged for the *first*
consumer's routing.  Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS + the shared Q8_0 MTP head, 2 GPU, `-sm layer -ncmoe 10`,
`-n 48`, seed 42, temp 0:

| arm | text | acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| plain decode (`--spec-type none`) | 172 chars `de61b9b1bed7` (the truth) | n/a |
| r95 + `draft-mtp`, 6 natural runs | 5x `de61b9b1bed7`, 1x `a2b6c01a0a19` (223 chars) | `0.00000` on the bad run |
| r95 + #186, 6 runs | 6x `de61b9b1bed7` | healthy |
| r96, 6 runs | 6x `de61b9b1bed7` | healthy |

Pinning one captured **heat-map** state reproduces the bad output 2/2 (so the flip is persisted state, not
run-to-run noise); `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0` restores purity, while `GGML_SCHED_DEVGATHER=0`,
`GGML_SCHED_STAGE=0` and `GGML_SCHED_STAGE_MIN_TOKENS=999999` do not.  On r96 the same pinned state gives
`de61b9b1bed7`, and `GGML_SCHED_MOE_DUP_SPLIT=0` reproduces `a2b6c01a0a19` exactly, which confirms both the
cause and the switch.  `-sm tensor` is immune (no cache gather on the meta backend) and 35B-A3B is immune
(one consumer).  No TODO item: the bug is fixed by this release.  Invariant, numbers and why the existing
gates could not see it: `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §43.

**Claim verification (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1.0, 2 GPU `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10`, prompt cache on).**
Client TTFT, 4-turn chat, 10 rounds per arm, median (spread ~5 ms):

| turn | r95 | r96 | r96 `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0` (= #186 only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (cache warm) | 238 ms | **119 ms (-50 %)** | 155 ms |
| 1 (~34 new tokens) | 656 ms | **393 ms (-40 %)** | 458 ms |
| 2 (~28 new tokens) | 644 ms | **283 ms (-56 %)** | 350 ms |
| 3 (~3.2k new tokens) | 2200 ms | **1938 ms (-12 %)** | 2018 ms |

So #186 is 65-67 ms of turns 1-2 and #189 is another 65-67 ms, isolated by the same-binary kill switch
(a separate #186-only build agrees with the `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0` arm to 0.4 ms).  Both PRs understate their
win on this host, which is consistent with a PCIe 5.0 x4 uplink: #186 avoids a 1062 MiB table copy per
affected prompt chunk.  The controls close the loop: r96 with **both** switches off
(`LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC=0 GGML_SCHED_MOE_DUP_SPLIT=0`) is 243/657/652/2206 ms, i.e. r95 (238/656/644/2200) within
noise, so both features are genuinely default-on and the two kill switches restore r95 exactly.  No
regression: a 4200-token prefill 3211.6 -> 3012.5 ms, Flash-Next decode
101.7 -> 102.1 t/s, 35B-A3B `-sm layer` 30.0 -> 77.6 t/s on the fixed path (the r95 number was the 0 %
acceptance run).

**Release gates.**  Coherence 4B Q8_0 3 GPU `1c5d32ac537d` (r95 == r96).  Flash-Next + MTP, `-sm tensor
-ncmoe 10`: prose400 `ee262db5a7e6`, code400 `1f661d931013` (both == r95).  35B-A3B Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40`
`-sm tensor` and `-sm layer` `4ac3a523160f` (== r95).  Four-axis adaptive-MTP gate, `-n 3000`, reasoning
pinned, r95 vs r96: **R 56.0/56.0, P 74.5/74.6, C 78.9/78.8, K 86.5/86.6 t/s**, acceptance identical to five
decimals (0.51169 / 0.81835 / 0.87068 / 0.99200), and `draft-mtp-adaptive` beats plain decode on every axis
(plain 30.5-31.3 t/s).  `llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8` on 27B UD-IQ3_S, 3 interleaved
rounds: **B=1 37.04/37.03, B=4 118.7/118.7, B=8 164.9/165.1 t/s** (r95/r96; round 1 is a cold first run in
both arms and is excluded).  `gate-prefill-logits.sh`: mean KLD **0.000707**, same-top-p **98.755 %**
(identical to r94/r95).  `test-backend-ops -b ROCm0 -o RMS_NORM,ADD,MUL_MAT,CPY,CONCAT,SSM_CONV`
**3130/3130**.  `check-gpu-faults.sh` over every r96 log plus the kernel journal: clean.  `.github`
workflows unchanged.

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `GGML_SCHED_MOE_DUP_SPLIT`, `LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC` and
`LLAMA_STATE_ASYNC_MAX_MIB`; `patches/README.md` blocks 09 and 11 carry the two changes and the new
invariant; `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §43 is the rulebook entry.

## 261020.004 (r94) -- issue #187 (captured graph replayed over a released slab work region) + the per-block boundary repair

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r94`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `c6b8107a3`, net tree
`40d43e3044051ea8168c02cd1a899877b5d8574d`, **12 blocks**.  Blocks 02/06/09/10/11 amended, no new block,
no new environment variable.  Campaign record: `archive/work/issue-187-drop-transition/` (moved out of
`wip/` with this release).

**Issue #187 (`@briansp2020`) -- the fault.**  `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-IQ3_XXS` + the shared Q8_0 MTP head,
2x R9700, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 10`, MTP n-max 3, 4 concurrent streams: after the first slot of the second
round is released the server aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` in
`k_set_rows_q8_0_group`.  Reproduced **2/2** on r93.  The reporter's r87-hunk revert does hide it, but it
restores the r85 regression (the second request keeps the wide compute layout and a small arena).

**Root cause.**  Not the r87 drop condition: the r87 forced drop only un-suppresses a **legitimate**
prefill -> decode drop (`cur = 5568 MiB` vs the recorded narrow `was = 1792 MiB`).  The drop frees the wide
compute view and the narrow re-reserve **shrinks the slab work boundary**, handing the bytes above it back
to the MoE arena.  `ggml_cuda_slab_work_alloc`'s shrink path never bumped `ggml_cuda_graph_mem_gen`, so a
captured HIP graph was replayed with addresses in the released region (here the KV `set_rows` source
indices) and faulted.  Evidence: `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` on the unfixed tree is clean 3/3 with the same
drops/re-arms; the instrumented decision log shows the drop -> `re-armed 54` -> two decode steps -> fault.

**Fix (block 10, `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda-slab.cu`).**  The work-boundary shrink now calls
`ggml_cuda_graph_mem_freed(device)` (the existing "recapture a graph whose captured memory was freed"
mechanism) before returning the bytes to the arena; a `GGML_CUDA_WORK_ALLOC_DEBUG` line reports it.  The
drop condition and `slab_narrow_boundary` bookkeeping are untouched, so r87's second-prefill repair stands.
The invalidation fires only on real shrinks (6 events / 5 drops over a 3-round run), never per token.

**Per-block build gate -- a pre-existing failure, repaired.**  Running the gate for this release exposed
that the 12-block set had not satisfied its own "every block builds the `all` target" contract since
r58/r86.  Each defect was a block split that the *tip* hides (the tree is unchanged by the repair):

1. **block 02** calls `llama_model_set_embeddings_layer_inp_preset`, whose declaration/definition/field
   lived in block 11 (r58 split) -> the API moved to block 02.
2. **block 06**'s `mmb.cu` carried a stray `}` and a duplicated `c.f32split_mode = 0;` (a re-cut artifact)
   that block 10 removed -> the removal moved to block 06, where the defect was introduced.
3. **block 09** declared the whole appended device-iface surface but its positional initializers were only
   filled in block 11 -> the fills moved to block 09 (the CUDA/Meta callbacks whose definitions are block
   10 stay `nullptr` at block 09 and are wired by block 10).
4. **block 09** used `ggml_cuda_pool_wide_pin` and `ggml_cuda_slab_seed_floor`, both defined in block 10
   (r86 split) -> those uses moved to block 10, where the definitions and the pool-wide routing live.
5. **block 09** used the 4-argument `common_speculative_init_result` / `init_from_params` and
   `common_speculative_load_model`, but the definitions were in block 11 (r86 loaded-draft handoff split)
   -> the whole handoff moved into block 09, together with `common_init_result::take_draft_model`.

The repair is **tree-identical** (`git diff` between the pre- and post-repair tips is empty; the net tree
is still `40d43e30`).  Per-block evidence (each block's tree is unchanged since the run that passed it):
blocks 00-05 pass; 06-08 pass after the block-06 repair; 09-11 pass after the block-09 repairs.  The
`--changed-from` shortcut is **not** valid for a boundary repair (it compares each commit's own delta, so
it skips blocks whose tree changed but whose delta did not).

**Release gates.**  `validate-set.sh` green (checksums + a strict 12/12 apply on a fresh tarball, applied
tree `40d43e30`).  Coherence (4B Q8_0, 3 GPU, seed 42) `sha=1c5d32ac537d`, identical to r93.  Prefill-logit
mean KLD **0.000707** / same-top-p **98.755 %** against the recorded base (measured on the identical tree,
PASS).  Issue #187 reproduction on the release binary: **3/3 rounds clean**, `check-gpu-faults.sh` and the
kernel journal clean.  `-sm layer`, one stream, 6-turn x 2-cycle multi-turn with `cache_prompt`: clean on
both stock and fixed r93 (the report's `-sm layer` arm did not reproduce here; r90's `set_tensor_async` UAF
fix landed after r89, so the reporter should retest that arm on r94).  `.github` workflows unchanged.
