## 261019.014 (no release) -- `wip/nwarps` RESOLVED: the RDNA3_0 per-shape `nwarps` impurity was the *fusion exclusion*, not a missing reduction-mapping derivation

**Campaign resolved (promotion pending the maintainer; record stays in `wip/nwarps/` until it is promoted or
dropped).**  Patch `wip/nwarps/patches/per-shape-nwarps-rdna3-0.patch` (sha256 `eb32d36c…`, applies clean to
the r91 tree `90507dfb5`, `git apply --check` + full apply verified on a fresh worktree), default **OFF** =
byte-identical to the delivery (width-probe hashes unchanged at threshold 0).  gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX), ROCm
10.1.0, single GPU, built with `~/bin/build-llama-rocm`.

**Root cause found.**  The candidate excluded the *fused* single-token launches
(`small_m = … && !has_fusion && M <= threshold`), so for a scoped tensor the rms_norm→Q8_1 fold / SSM
gate-beta / shared-expert-down fusion ran at the table's **8** warps at `W = 1` while the plain ksplit launch
ran at **1** warp at `W = 2..8` — a decode-vs-verify K-split-order split, i.e. the impurity itself.  **No
reduction-mapping re-derivation was needed**: the ksplit K loop is `kbx = tid/(qi/vdr) + m*blocks_per_iter`
(a fixed per-thread residue class, independent of `ncols_dst` / `rows_per_block` / token index) and the
warp + serial cross-warp trees are fixed for a given `nwarps`, so one value per shape *is* the width
invariance requirement.  Fix: forward the row-scoped value to every launch of the tensor, including the
three fusion kernels that reproduce a dense weight launch (`ssm_gate_beta`, `ssm_conv_l2_gatebeta`,
`shexp_down_gate`) — the contract those kernels already document for `long_k`.

**Purity (the blocker) — PASS everywhere** (`test-logits-width-probe` P=1024 ub=512 KV=f16).  All four
models (35B-A3B Q4_K_M, gemma-26B Q4_K_XL, gemma-12B Q8_0, 27B Q4_K_M) PASS at the recommended `=8192`,
and every *previously failing* cell is now `PASS maxdiff 0`: 35B 2048 (was 0.150), gemma-26B 4096 (was
**3.35**), 27B 6144 (was 0.165), and 35B / gemma-26B / gemma-12B / 27B blanket 1e9 (27B was 0.166).
27B × the eight native KV types at 8192: all PASS.  35B-A3B PPL 5.7861 both thresholds (per-chunk
losses identical); greedy text coherent.

**Retuned from measurement** (`tg128 -d 16384`, `r=3`): the 35B's win is its **M = 8192** Q8_0 shapes only
(nothing below 8192: 2048/4096 are flat-to-negative), gemma-26B gains from Q4_0 at *every* row count
(lm_head worth ~1.8 %), gemma-12B loses 2 % when **M = 15360** flips, 27B loses 0.6 % when its `M = 48 /
1024` Q8_0 or its Q6_K/IQ4_NL shapes flip.  Shipped rule: `Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1` narrow always, `Q8_0`
narrow for `2048 <= M <= GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_RDNA3_SMALL_M`, `Q6_K/IQ4_NL` unchanged.

**Numbers at the recommended `=8192`:** 35B-A3B tg128 d16384 125.09/125.59 → 127.23/127.38 (**+1.7-2.0 %**);
gemma-26B 125.14 → **131.45** (**+5.0 %**); gemma-12B d0 54.05 → 54.28 (+0.4 %); 27B d16384 40.14 → 40.16
(neutral).  35B-A3B MTP n3 (`-n 400 --temp 0`, repeatable): prose 200.6 → **222.0 t/s (+10.7 %)**, code
235.5 → **250.2 (+6.3 %)**; acceptance 0.653→0.750 / 0.801→0.851, so part of the MTP gain is an
acceptance shift (a changed reduction order moves near-ties), while the plain-decode gains are kernel time
only.  **The old record's `+2.1 % MTP / +9 % blanket` figures are superseded** — they were measured with the
impure patch.

**Cost.**  The template axis is `if constexpr`-gated to the 7 RDNA3_0 wide types and `ncols_dst <= 8`:
`mmvq.cu.o` 13.64 → 15.36 MiB (+12.6 %), `mul_mat_vec_q_ksplit` symbols 2188 → 2640 (+20.7 %) vs
+41 %/+100 % for the ungated original.  **Promotion recipe** (knob default-on + `GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_RDNA3_SMALL_M=0`
kill-switch, then the W-probe / four-axis MTP / PPL / batched-bench / prefill-logit gates) is §6 of
`wip/nwarps/README.md`.

## 261019.012 (no release) -- the unified-KV cell-offset campaign closes: the quantum is the FA KV-split period, and the shared decode head is the variable

**Campaign closed (no delivery change).**  `wip/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/` ->
`archive/work/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`; **TODO #52 part C is CLOSED**, the
consumer/rulebook gotcha is sharpened (`README.md`, `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §38), and nothing in `patches/` or
`release.json` moves.  Issue #134 stays upstream-inherent; the workaround is unchanged
(`--no-kv-unified` when strict reproducibility is required).

**The campaign's parked model was directionally right but named the wrong quantum.**  The 2026-10-11
finding said "a sequence's attention result depends on its whole physical cell set, modulo the FA
reduction tile, so a fixed alignment is not enough".  Re-derived from the launcher and measured on r91
(gfx1151 / ROCm 10.1, 1 GPU), the rule is: the result is a function of the sequence's KV cells' tile
indices **modulo the per-launch KV-split period** `pb x nbatch_fa` -- `pb` = `parallel_blocks` for the
decode/verify tile kernel (from an efficiency search over `ntiles_KV = ceil(n_kv/nbatch_fa)`, i.e. the
**shared** view length) or the fixed band `P` (`nsm`, `(3*nsm)/4` for 2-byte K/V).  The kernel takes KV
iterations round-robin by `pb` and `flash_attn_combine_results` sums the partials linearly in block
order, so a shift by **one period is bit-identical** and any smaller shift can change the rounding.

**Measured (new probe `test-multiseq-runs.cpp`: the report sequence's token stream and positions are
held fixed, only its physical cell placement changes; `fa-config-diag.patch` prints `pb`):**

| arm (4B Q8_0 f16 KV, `nbatch_fa` 32, decode `pb` 30) | logits hash |
|---|---|
| offset 32 / 64 / 96 / 128 (all **tile-aligned**) | `b8bc508b86b0614e` / `5ab10c344414cf93` / `41b96d97e4bac7f2` / `9ba3b5ea1888eb3b` -- 4 distinct |
| offset X vs **X + 960** (= `pb x nbatch_fa`), X = 32/64/128/256/288 | **bit-identical** every pair |
| prompt cells fixed at 288; only the **final decode cell** moves into a block the prompt already uses (T=1344) | `ba09fe281f969372` vs `fbc7a801f51babc0` (T=1120/1600/2560/3520, no collision) |
| `--no-kv-unified`, offsets 32/288/544/1024 | one hash (`fbc7a801f51babc0`) -- green |
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (`ncols2` 8 -> `pb` 60, period 1920): offset 32 vs 1952, 512 vs 992 | bit-identical; 32 vs 272 differs |

So the quantum is `pb x nbatch_fa`, not the tile, and the decisive variable is the **decode head**: under
`--kv-unified` every new token takes the shared head, so its residue class follows the co-resident
session's allocation history.  (The campaign's observed "quantum 64" is the regime where
`pb == ntiles_KV`, so every tile owns its own accumulator and any tile-aligned placement is invariant.)
The **prefill** path is not exposed: prefill logits are invariant both to tile-aligned offsets and to the
padded view length with the cells held fixed (`LLAMA_KV_N_PAD_MIN` 256->4096).

**The proposed cheap fix is refuted.**  "Chunk all unified sessions by the decode band width and start
every prompt at a band boundary" fails on two measured grounds: (a) a tile-aligned start is not invariant
(only a **period**-aligned one is); (b) even period-aligned prompt starts leave each decode token at the
shared head, and moving only that one cell is enough to change the result.  **A sufficient fix exists but
is deliberately not implemented:** period-granular per-sequence cell *ownership* (each session's cells are
whole period-aligned `pb x nbatch_fa` blocks that no other session writes into; its head lives inside its
own block).  Cost is at most one period of reserved-unwritten cells per live session -- measured 960
cells = **30 MiB** (4B) and 1920 cells = **37.5 MiB** (35B-A3B) -- but it is an upstream allocator redesign
(`find_slot`/`apply_ubatch`/`seq_rm`/`seq_cp`/shift/SWA reuse/head-reset/mask-skip assumptions) with no
throughput win.  Re-entry conditions and the validation plan are in the `RESOLUTION.md`.

**Records.** `archive/work/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/` (`RESOLUTION.md` = the definitive record;
`README.md`, the 2026-10-11 `FINDINGS-offset-mechanism.md` and the 2026-10-16 revalidation kept as
dated history; `tools/` gained `test-multiseq-runs.cpp` and `fa-config-diag.patch`).  `TODO.md` #52,
`GREEDY-PURITY.md` §38, `README.md`.  No release, no fork-branch refresh, no container build.
## 261019.013 (r92) -- 2-byte band arm joins the 32-column block (TODO #27); the head-512 prefill row is fixed (issue #188)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r92`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `47c5b2dd6`, net tree
`da55e8282512084eae8f414c911cb4515be8e5cc`, **12 blocks** (block 05 amended, no new block).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, tree matches).  Two flash-attention changes,
both in block 05, from one campaign (`wip/fa-band-2byte-row/` -> `archive/work/fa-band-2byte-row/`, TODO
#27 closed) and one filed issue (#188).

### 1. The 2-byte band arm gets the 32-column block, not a `ncols == 16` row

The campaign's proposal (add a band row for `ncols == 16`, keeping `ncols1 = 2` for f16/bf16) was built
and measured: it wins 14 % at `n_q = 1` and **loses 15 % at `n_q = 3..4`**, because a 2-column arm needs
`ceil(n_q/2)` output tiles and every tile streams the whole KV cache.  The delivered fix is
`ggml_cuda_fattn_band_wmma_ncols1() -> 4` for **every** K/V type plus the 2-byte band split
`3*nsm/4 -> nsm/2`:

| head 256 GQA 6, us/call | n_q 1 | n_q 4 | n_q 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| f16 kv 16384 (r91 -> r92) | 106.5 -> 102.2 | 133.9 -> 105.9 | 221.1 -> 175.9 |
| f16 kv 98304 | 760 -> 684 | 763 -> 695 | 1142 -> 823 |
| bf16 kv 98304 | 813 -> 685 | 869 -> 696 | 1451 -> 832 |

Model (27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1 GPU): `tg128 @ d98304` f16 22.63 -> **23.28 (+2.9 %)**, bf16 21.88 ->
**23.25 (+6.3 %)**; `tg128` at d0/d1024/d4096 flat; deep MTP (53k prompt, `draft-mtp n3`) bf16
63.8 -> **68.3 (+7.0 %)** / f16 64.3 -> **68.4 (+6.4 %)**.  Four-axis gate (bf16, `-n 3000`, Protocol A):
R 58.9 -> 60.7, P 72.1 -> 75.3, C 80.1 -> 80.2, K 86.2 -> 86.5, plain flat, acceptance
0.576 / 0.799 / 0.904 / 0.992 -> 0.601 / 0.844 / 0.902 / 0.992.

### 2. Issue #188: head-512 prefill was a config-row regression, not a tile-vs-MMA verdict

The RDNA `(512, 512, 32)` MMA row is the **only** head-512 row the AMD dispatcher can reach
(`switch_ncols1` forces `ncols = 32/ncols2` for `DKQ > 256`).  The 2026-09-14 RDNA prefill sweep
replaced upstream's `128, 2, 32, 128, 128, 128, 1, true` with `256, 2, 128, 96, 16, 16, 1, true`
(8 warps, 128 KV rows, `nbatch_V2 = 16`), which is ~1.35x **slower than the tile kernel**, so RDNA4's
WMMA cap of 576 made every Gemma 4 global layer pay.  Retuned to 4 warps / 32 KV rows / one 128-half2
K/V batch / combine 64 / Q in registers:

| gemma-4 31B global-attn (D=512, 4 KV, 32 Q, ub 512), ms/call | r91 | tile | r92 |
|---|---|---|---|
| q8_0 kv 32768 | 126.1 | 92.4 | **42.3** |
| q8_0 kv 98304 | 377.0 | 283.6 | **128.1** |
| f16 kv 98304 | 374.2 | 250.9 | **127.9** |

End to end `llama-bench pp512 -ub 512 -ctk/-ctv q8_0`: **Gemma-4-31B** d0 1133 -> 1182 (+4 %), d32768
299 -> **583 (+95 %)**, d98304 122 -> **299 (+144 %)**; **Gemma-4-26B-A4B** +3.8 % / +96 % / +141 %;
`tg` unchanged on both (decode for head 512 stays on the tile kernel).  The row is unreachable on
RDNA3_0/3_5 (their WMMA caps are 256/320), so this is RDNA4-only in practice.  An upstream candidate
(raise the RDNA4 WMMA cap; upstream's 512 row is already the fast shape) is in
`upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-fa-512-rdna-head-cap.md`, and issue #188 is closed pointing at it.

### Gates (both changes together)

`FLASH_ATTN_EXT` **6391/6391 OK, 0 FAIL**; `test-logits-width-probe` W = 1..8 PASS (`maxdiff 0`) on 27B
f16/bf16, 35B-A3B f16/bf16 and Flash-Next 2 GPU f16/bf16; greedy `plain == draft-mtp n3 == n7` on the
27B (f16/bf16) and the 4B P=192..256 grid, and byte-identical to r91 at 200 tokens; prefill-logit 27B
Q8_0 **0.000707 / 98.755 %** (identical to r91).  Full tables:
`benchmarks/2026-10-19-fa-band-2byte-and-head512.md`.

### Finding: the gemma4-12b prefill-logit instrument cannot gate a head-512 kernel change

Against the r91 base, gemma4-12b measures **0.0957 / 90.1 %** for the new 512 row, **0.1180 / 89.1 %**
for the pre-existing tile kernel and 0.1286 between the two, i.e. every legal head-512 implementation
lands at 0.10-0.13 on this model while PPL is unchanged (no-FA reference 220.30, tile 223.92, r92
224.55, r91 225.16; all inside the +/-12.0 s.e.) and 120-token greedy text is closest to the `-fa off`
reference for r92.  The canonical instruments (27B Q8_0, Flash-Next) contain no head-512 layers, so the
gate structurally cannot see this change.  Recorded as a measurement property of that model, not a
threshold change; the maintainer approved the change on the PPL + reference evidence.

## 261019.011 (no release) -- rdna35 mmvq fusion: the impurity is the preempted `GLU -> MMQ down` fusion, not the fused gate/up

**Campaign closed (ending B).**  `wip/rdna35-mmvq-fusion-perf/` -> `archive/work/rdna35-mmvq-fusion-perf/`
with a `RESOLUTION.md`; TODO item 16 closed; the skip stays.  Tree r91 (`45f817cc3`), gfx1151, qwen4exp
UD-Q4_K_XL, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt` P=256.

**The old premise is refuted.**  Temporary ksplit dumps (reverted) of the `blk.47` dense shexp
(Q8_0 2560x640, `nwarps=2`, rpb=1) compared the fused GLU launch with the default path's **dual-output**
gate+up fusion: all **640 rows x 3 passes** had bit-identical `up` and `gate`.  Codegen/FMA contraction and
the Q8_1 cache are exonerated; the fused kernel does reproduce the standalone `mul_mat_vec_q` arithmetic.

**Mechanism.**  The default path fuses `GLU + down` into an **MMQ** down matmul
(`ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q_swiglu_try_fuse`, `target_qwen4exp`; trace: `ffn_swiglu-47 -> ffn_shexp-47`).  Enabling
the dense gate+up+GLU fusion consumes the GLU node, so that fusion cannot fire; W=1 then takes the normal
down path while W>=2 still takes the GLU+MMQ fusion.  The down-kernel-family change is the whole W=1/W=8
difference.

**Hashes (row 0):** default W=1 = W=8 = `578528d234936576` (PASS); env ON W=1 `173282800f97009f` vs W=8
`578528...` (FAIL, maxdiff 0.323269); env ON + GLU->MMQ off W=1..8 = `1732828...` (PASS); default +
GLU->MMQ off W=1..8 = `1732828...` (PASS).  The sibling weighted-down tail is pure once the down path is
uniform (env ON + GLU->MMQ off, weighted-down on: PASS).

**Candidate A (validated, not promoted).**  Default-on dense gate+up fusion on RDNA3_5 + suppress the
GLU->MMQ down fusion for dense GLUs on RDNA3_5.  tg128 26.39 ± 0.05 -> 26.55 ± 0.06 (+0.6 %); pp512/2048
953.87/964.89 -> 954.97/961.04 (flat); batched-bench npl 1/4/8 TG 25.92/64.45/85.76 -> 26.05/64.55/85.59;
qwen4exp plain == draft-mtp n3 text 35 chars `sha=359ff4337837`; 4B f16/bf16/q8_0 same-seed text identical
(280 chars `sha=7386359e5dac`).  Not promoted because it changes the band hash `578528...` -> `1732828...`
(text unchanged on the tested prompts) and disables a prefill fusion globally on RDNA3_5; preserving the
current hash needs a three-way gate+up+GLU+MMQ-down fusion, which the ~0.6-0.9 % win does not justify.
Record: `archive/work/rdna35-mmvq-fusion-perf/RESOLUTION.md`.

## 261019.010 (r91) -- the rollback-boundary and umem-arena campaigns close; the bound is enforced by `n_rs_batch`

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r91`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `45f817cc3`, net tree
`90507dfb528cbfe0c688261226d18934653b1b61`, **12 blocks** (blocks 03, 09 and 10 amended, no new block).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, trees match).  Both WIP campaigns are closed:
`wip/rs-rollback-boundary/` and `wip/umem-arena-guard/` move to `archive/work/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`
each.  Work done on the primary box (gfx1201, 3x R9700); the gfx1151 box wrote the patches.

### The code question: is the rollback bound enforced, or only observed?

**Enforced, by construction** -- the campaign's "an ngram-mod draft (n_max up to 64) is a future exposure"
claim is **wrong**.  The chain is:

    common: cparams.n_rs_batch = max(1, common_speculative_n_max(&params.speculative) + 1)
      -> llama_context: n_rs_batch = max(n_rs_seq + 1, params.n_rs_batch)
      -> delta-net-base: ggml_gated_delta_net(..., K, cparams.n_rs_batch)   (op param 1)
      -> gated_delta_net.cu: GDN_CHUNKED_MIN_TOKENS = max(K > 16 ? K : 16, n_rs_batch)

`common_speculative_n_max()` ranges over **every** enabled speculator type -- draft simple/mtp/adaptive/
eagle3/dflash/dspark and ngram simple/map-k/map-k4v/mod/cache -- so the bound always tracks the widest
enabled drafter.  Measured from the `llama_context` log (4B Q8_0, `-v`):

| config | `n_rs_seq` | `n_rs_batch` | threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3` | 3 | **4** | 16 |
| `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 20` (clamped to 15) | 15 | **16** | 16 |
| `--spec-type ngram-mod --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64` | 0 | **65** | 65 |
| ngram-mod 64 + draft-mtp 3 | 3 | **65** | 65 |

So a verify batch is `1 + n_draft <= n_rs_batch <= threshold` and can never take the chunked path; it
always falls through to the sequential kernel and restores snapshots it wrote.  With ngram-mod alone
`n_rs_seq == 0`, i.e. there is no recurrent snapshot path at all (`need_n_rs_seq()` only counts
mtp/adaptive/eagle3/dflash/dspark).  The clamp comment in `common/common.cpp` already said this; the
kernel comment said it was "Verified" (an observation) and the campaign treated it as an assumption.
**Fixed by stating the invariant** in `gated_delta_net.cu` (r91).

What remains is the **non-speculator** partial rollback -- a server cancel / `--cache-reuse` rewind that
lands inside a prefill batch.  That path has never been observed (and with the tracker fixed it no longer
fires spuriously), but it is not structurally excluded, so the sequential tail is kept as the closure.

### Promoted

* **block 03** -- `src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp`: `prepare()` folds **every** ubatch of the list into
  the per-sequence rollback tracker, oldest first (the issue-#131 **false positive**), plus
  `LLAMA_RS_ROLLBACK_DEBUG` (`RSPREP`/`RSROLL`).  `TESTING.md` said this belonged to block 02; the code
  (`warned_rollback_boundary`, `last_ubatch_nseq_tokens_by_seq`) is **block 03's**, so it lands there.
* **block 10** -- `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/gated_delta_net.cu`: the chunked prefill runs the chunked kernel on
  `n_tokens - D` and the **sequential** kernel on the last `D = max(K>16?K:16, n_rs_batch)` tokens in the
  same launch, so snapshot slots `0..D-1` exist for every single-sequence batch.  `GGML_CUDA_GDN_TAIL=0`
  restores whole-batch chunking.  Folded into block 10, not block 03, because block 10 owns the current
  dispatch region (`launch_chunked`, the bf16/arch selection, the env-hygiene rewrite) and the patch's base
  blob *is* the post-block-10 file; folding it into 03 would have been overwritten by 10's replay.
* **block 09** -- `moe-expert-cache.cu` + `common/fit.cpp`: refuse the MoE expert arena on a shared
  host/device memory pool (`prop.integrated`), opt back in with `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_UNIFIED=1` + explicit
  `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` **and** `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RESERVE_MIB`.

Not shipped: the trailing-ubatch splitter (`LLAMA_RS_TAIL_TOKENS`, -13.7 % pp512) and the fixed-window /
checkpoint+replay designs.  The campaign's patch set and probe are archived.

### Gates (gfx1201 unless stated)

| gate | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|

## 261019.007 (r90) -- the async graph-input nondeterminism is FIXED (split-input uploads snapshotted); `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT` default-on

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r90`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `529135aed`, net tree
`111559e57e820ce5d7fcac511a84ba70604604a0`, **12 blocks** (**block 10** amended, no new block).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, tree matches).  Closes **TODO #73** and the
follow-up to **PR #182** (`@briansp2020`), whose batched uploads (r89) are what made this defect cheap to
find.

**Root cause (not the ring).**  `ggml_backend_cuda_set_tensor_async()` issued a pinned-source
`cudaMemcpyAsync` **straight from the caller's live host pointer**.  A pinned-source async copy is read by
the copy engine when the stream reaches it, not when it is issued, so the caller must not modify the source
until it completes.  The scheduler uses that path for a host-resident *split* input, and the one that bites
is a **CPU split's** output (`node_1` / `model.input_embed` in a `ROCm_Host` buffer), which the next
ubatch's CPU split rewrites in place.  With `ASYNC_INPUT=1` the host runs ahead, so the copy could read the
next ubatch's bytes (or a torn mix): a rare single-graph corruption in **layer 0** that propagates to the
end of the chunk.  That is why it needed a captured graph (without capture the host is the bottleneck and
never gets ahead), why any host delay fixed it, and why the per-chunk cache reset made it look "bounded and
re-converging".  `ggml_backend_cuda_set_tensor_2d_async()` had the same shape on the meta/tensor-split
splice path.  The uploads themselves were innocent: 769 graphs x 9-10 uploads verified byte-correct at the
graph's first read, and forcing every upload onto the compute stream (stream order alone) still diverged.
Record: `archive/work/async-input-graph-ordering/` (`FINDINGS-2026-10-19b.md`).

**The change (block 10 only, `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`).**  Both async set paths now **snapshot
the source through the pinned upload ring** (a slot is not reused until the ring wraps, and the wrap is
guarded by a device sync), unconditionally -- it is a correctness fix, not an async-path optimisation --
with a fallback to the old copy when the ring cannot take it.  The ring's completion wait and its
"previous graph done" guard become unconditional so the snapshots are ordered with `ASYNC_INPUT=0` too.
`GGML_CUDA_SPLICE_GATHER` now only chooses the *shape* of the queued copy (compacted 1-D vs strided 2-D);
every arm is snapshotted.  **Default flip:** `g_async_input_on` is now on unless
`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=0` (env only disables, per the default-on policy), and the stale block-10 comment
that blamed the `done_ev` wait / HIP graph replay is replaced with the corrected rationale.

**Correctness (self-KLD, `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base`, same binary; noise floor 99.967+)**
4B Q8_0 12 chunks `-ub 8`: **91.0 / 90.8** before -> **99.967** after (x5); 24 chunks 92.5 -> **99.984**;
`-ub 1` 95.1 -> **99.967**; `BATCH=1` 91.3 -> **99.967**; 27B `UD-Q4_K_M` 91.6 -> **100.000**; 35B-A3B
2 GPU tensor and `-ncmoe 40` **100.000**; `-ub 512` 100.000 both arms.  Deterministic with every diagnostic
switch off and with a 300 us post-launch host delay.

**Gates (r90 build, async default-on).**  4B `-n 64` seed 42 `7386359e5dac` (default / `ASYNC_INPUT=0` /
`-ub 8`); 27B 48-token `ad1333a99867` (default / off); `test-logits-width-probe` W=1..8 identical hashes,
`width_purity=PASS`; **prefill-logit 0.000707 / 98.755 %** against the recorded r89 base (identical to

## 261019.006 (no release) -- correction: the async-input nondeterminism is not the ring; first campaign session

**No delivery change.**  `release.json` stays `v12-097cf33d9-r89`; no patch, block or `release.json` byte
changes.  This entry corrects the *cause* recorded in 261019.004 (the fold) and in the block-10 code
comment, and records the first debugging session of `wip/async-input-graph-ordering/`.

**Correction.**  261019.004 said the missing piece was "the transfer -> graph-replay completion
dependency" (i.e. the ring's uploads landing after the replay read them).  That is **withdrawn**.  With
the scratch instrumentation preserved as `wip/async-input-graph-ordering/tools/DEBUGBUILD.patch`:

- a D2H snapshot of each upload destination, taken on the compute stream **immediately after
  `ggml_cuda_async_input_wait()`** (exactly where the graph's first read happens), matched the uploaded
  bytes in **1024 / 1024** cases with no intervening device sync;
- the ring bookkeeping is consistent (`wait` sees `pending` every time, one thread, one stream pair) and
  `hipEventQuery(done_ev)` reports the previous graph **complete** at all 14227 uploads, i.e. consecutive
  graphs do not overlap in this workload at all;
- the per-graph host writes are only the async ring (verified) and the main-stream
  `set_tensor_2d_async` splice-gather; the sync-path `set_tensor` calls are model-weight loads at startup;
- HIP's primitives are correct in two standalone reproducers (`tools/ain_hip_test{,2}.cpp`): a
  `hipStreamWaitEvent` before `hipGraphLaunch` orders the replay, and an event recorded after the launch
  covers the replay's execution, including a slow graph with the host running several graphs ahead;
- **every** switch that made the run deterministic only slows the host -- a host delay *before* **or
  *after* the launch**, `AIN_SYNC_SET/COPY/COMPUTE/DEVICE`, and the scheduler synchronize before
  `set_inputs`.  So none of them is a diagnosis, and the effect is global host speed, not a copy->launch
  window;
- not GDN (dense 27B diverges identically), not the fusions (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1` still diverges),
  not the per-thread default stream (`AIN_EXPL_STREAM` still diverges), not the r25 graph-lifetime
  machinery (`GRAPH_MEM_GEN=0`, `HIP_GRAPH_FORCE_UPDATE=1` still diverge).

Per-graph output checksums differ in a *bounded* region (graphs 97-128 and 289-298 of 299) and
re-converge, which a diverged KV write could not do.  Combined with the absence of inter-graph overlap,
the remaining difference is produced **inside a single graph's execution**; the top suspect is the
scheduler's cross-backend split hand-off (`graph: nodes = 2025, splits = 2` on one GPU), i.e. the host
not waiting for a device signal at a split boundary.  Next steps are in
`wip/async-input-graph-ordering/FINDINGS-2026-10-19.md`.

**Consequences recorded.**  `AGENTS.md` and `ENVIRONMENT.md` now say the async path is the trigger, not
the defect.  The one-line block-10 code comment in the r89 tree still carries the withdrawn wording and
should be fixed in the next block-10 amendment (it is a comment only, so it does not affect behaviour).
PR #182's batching remains an amplifier of the exposure (85-90 % vs 96 % same-top-p), which is why it is
documented as such rather than reverted.  Campaign record: `wip/async-input-graph-ordering/`
(FINDINGS-2026-10-19.md, tools/, TODO #73).

## 261019.004 (r89) -- PR #182 (batched async graph-input uploads + lazy done event) folded into block 10

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r89`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `399610a83`, net tree
`ca9598a22946e52b74a8d6869a1ff917b181455b`, **12 blocks** (no new block; **block 10** amended).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, tree matches).  **Two new environment
variables** (`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH`, `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT_LAZY_DONE`), both default-on inside
the opt-in async path.

**Provenance.**  Folds `@briansp2020`'s PR #182 (`wip-async-input-batch`), two format-patches on the r82
tree (sha256 `c0eba29b…` / `06b201c8…`, identical to the PR).  Block 10 owns the async graph-input ring in
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu` (r46/PR #125, default-off since r69), so both parts fold there.  The
PR's `wip/async-input-batch/` packaging is **not** taken (same rule as #167/#172/#181); the record is
`archive/work/async-input-batch/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`, and no `wip/` stub was created or removed.

**The change.**  `0001`: with `GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=1` every small graph input was its own
`cudaMemcpyAsync` from the pinned ring plus an event record.  The uploads are now queued per device and
copied by one `ggml_cuda_ain_batch_kernel` on the compute stream when the next graph starts; every other
buffer/backend access drains the queue through the old per-copy path and orders `cudaStreamPerThread`
after the last batch kernel (`flush_ev`), an overlapping upload / full queue / ring wrap drains too, and a
`cudaHostGetDevicePointer` failure falls back to per-copy.  Byte-exact.  `0002`: `done_ev` is recorded by
the next upload instead of after every `graph_compute` (a decode step runs hundreds of graphs per device);
a context destructor flushes a still-pending event before its streams die.  **Default flip:**
`ASYNC_INPUT_BATCH` is now on wherever the async path is on (`=0` restores per-copy) and `LAZY_DONE`
defaults to it (`=0`/`=1` override).  **`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT` itself stays opt-in** -- see below.

**Measured (gfx1201, 3x R9700, ROCm 10.1).**  One binary, env-selected arms, interleaved rounds,
400-token greedy, `-fa on`, q8_0 KV, `-ub/-b 2048`; per-arm spread <= 0.4 % over 5 rounds (3 for MTP/1-GPU):

| config | async off (delivery) | `ASYNC_INPUT=1` before | `ASYNC_INPUT=1` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 2 GPU tensor | 109.5 t/s | 110.7 (+1.1 %) | **115.8 (+5.8 %)** |
| 27B Q4_K_M MTP n3, 2 GPU tensor | 83.2 t/s | 85.0 (+2.2 %) | **86.2 (+3.6 %)** |
| 35B-A3B, 1 GPU | 100.0 t/s | 97.8 (-2.2 %) | 99.6 (-0.4 %) |
| 27B, 1 GPU | 31.7 t/s | 31.8 | 31.8 |

The contributor's split reproduces: at 35B-A3B 2 GPU tensor, `0001` alone +1.4 %, `0002` alone +3.4 %,
both +4.6 % over `ASYNC_INPUT=1` (they measured +0.23 / +3.87 / +4.26 %; their MTP and 1-GPU rows match
too).  Prefill `pp4096` (35B, 2 GPU tensor) 5449 -> 5437 -> **5486** t/s: flat.  The delivery default
(`ASYNC_INPUT` unset) is untouched: 109.6/109.7 t/s against the stock r88 binary's 109.3/109.8, and 27B
greedy text identical (`e4b7ece03d7e`).

**Gates (r89 build).**  4B Q8_0 `-n 64` seed 42 `7386359e5dac` with async off / on / `BATCH=0`
(== the r68 known-good); `test-logits-width-probe` W=1..8 identical hashes + `width_purity=PASS` (2
starts per arm); 27B 1-GPU (`e4b7ece03d7e`) and 27B MTP 2-GPU (`2d0766a77581`) greedy byte-identical
across every arm; prefill-logit **0.000707 / 98.755 %** PASS (identical to the recorded base);
`test-backend-ops` `ADD`/`GET_ROWS`/`CPY` and `MUL_MAT` (2864 cases) pass with the batch path on;
`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean (kernel journal + logs).  `validate-set.sh` green.

**Why `ASYNC_INPUT` is still opt-in -- and a new lead.**  The r69 run-to-run nondeterminism is **not**
fixed by this PR and is not caused by it: on the r88 tree the r69 instrument diverges (95.8-96.5 %
same-top-p) with or without the patches.  But it is now characterised.  It needs a **captured graph**:
`-ub 512` is `100.000 %` while `-ub 8` and `-ub 1` diverge, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` and
`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_VERIFY_GRAPHS=1` (the `-ub 8` case) are `99.984 %`, and all of it happens with
`n_seq = 1` (so r69's "multi-sequence" reading was incidental).  A scratch build with
`cudaStreamSynchronize` inserted between `ggml_cuda_async_input_wait()` and the graph launch is
`99.984 %` for both the per-copy and the batched arm, so the copies are byte-correct and the missing
piece is the transfer -> graph-replay completion dependency.  The batched/lazy patch makes the race
**wider** (85-90 % vs 96 %) because it defers the copy later -- kept deliberately: it is the better
amplifier for bisecting.  Reproducer, full arm matrix, controls and hypotheses (including the dual
scheduler / shared-state hole class of r84 and a per-thread-`cudaStreamPerThread` ring-wrap hazard found
in review): `wip/async-input-graph-ordering/`; tracker item **#73**.  Fixing it makes async default-on
worth the +5.8 % / +3.6 % above.

**Also observed (not this change).**  On 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (1 GPU and 2 GPU tensor) the **stock r88 binary**
already produces 2-3 different 400-token greedy texts across runs with `ASYNC_INPUT=0`
(`722063f3e28d` / `e3b891655a80` / `27d50a6d97f5`), so a text hash is not a usable coherence gate on that
model; the 4B and 27B are deterministic and were used instead.  That default-path nondeterminism is
unrelated to the async ring and is not tracked yet.

**Review nits (not changed).**  `ggml_cuda_async_input_drain()` calls `ggml_cuda_set_device()` only when
there is work, so the current device after the call depends on the queue state; every caller that needs
a device sets it explicitly (and the `buffer_cpy_tensor` D2D/peer paths are device-explicit), so this is a
latent inconsistency rather than a bug.  The per-device `done_ev`/`flush_ev` events are never destroyed
(unchanged from r46).

## 261019.003 (r88) -- RDNA2 (gfx1030) FA gate fixes folded into block 05 (PR #181)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r88`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `f2e884648`, net tree
`04d37db108a01e04efa94bbdc77a2eb37eb1713d`, **12 blocks** (no new block; **block 05** amended).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, tree matches).  **No new environment
variable.**

**Published.**  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r88` pushed (annotated, on the release commit); CI **Validate
delivery set** green on `main` and on the tag, **Release patch set** green (assets
`rdna-boosts-all.patch`, `patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`).  Fork branch refreshed:
`stew675/llama.cpp@rdna-boosts` rebuilt at the same base and force-pushed with
`--force-with-lease` from `441b38fbc` to `f2e884648` (verified tip and tree `04d37db1`).  Container
images are the off-host worker's job (`scripts/container-watch.sh` on `radiance`); the watcher polls
for the new `v12-*` tag, and `radiance` was unreachable from the primary box at publication time
(no route to host), so the image build is queued rather than confirmed.  PR #181 was closed as folded,
with the two follow-ups (TODO #71/#72) and the guard-tail gating reported to `@slavap`.

**Provenance.**  Folds `@slavap`'s PR #181 (`rdna2-fa-r81`), a three-bug fix for the
`test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` abort on gfx1030 (Radeon Pro V620: "ROCm error: an illegal memory
access", RC=134, with `MUL_MAT` blocked behind it).  The PR's own packaging (`patches-rdma2/`,
`release-rdma2.json`, `scripts/apply-rdma2.sh`) is **not** taken: it is a third kind of source outside
`patches/`, and its manifest pinned the `r82` base within a day of being written.  Folding into the
block that owns the code is the r76 precedent (PR #165 -> blocks 05/07).

**The three defects** (all in block 05's files, all verified against the r87 source before folding):

1. `ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_alloc_size` (TILE branch) mapped `FATTN_KV_NATIVE_BF16` to
   `GGML_TYPE_BF16`, so `need_f16` stayed false.  On hardware without native BF16 tensor cores the tile
   case chooser instantiates **F16** (the BF16 instantiation is selected only under
   `bf16_mma_hardware_available`, and gfx1030 has no `V_DOT2_F32_BF16`), so the whole-cache converter
   wrote past the node's allocation: sentinel clobber, then an illegal access.  The allocator now maps
   `FATTN_KV_NATIVE_BF16` to F16, matching the chooser.  The same latent mismatch existed on RDNA1 and on
   pre-Ampere NVIDIA / older MUSA (`bf16_mma_hardware_available` false there too), so those get the fix
   as a side effect; their behaviour with a bf16 KV cache was equally wrong before.
2. `launch_fattn_tile_switch_ncols1`: the decode/verify band (`Q->ne[1] <= 8`) was the only one of the
   seven `launch_fattn` sites in the tile file that stopped at the `warp_size` argument, leaving `q_h2`
   at its default `false` while a wide RDNA2 kernel (`q_global`: `GGML_CUDA_FATTN_TILE_Q_GLOBAL`,
   `DKQ <= 256`, `ncols >= 16`) read Q from the `Q_h2` half2 buffer that was never allocated -- a null
   pointer and a fault near 0x1000.  Only GQA-16 decode shapes trip it (`ncols >= 16`); in the FA matrix
   that is `hsk=192` with `nr23=[16,1]` and `n_q <= 8`.  It now passes the same condition as the other
   six sites.
3. `ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_f16_extra_data`: the `ncols2 > 1` tile branch runs with
   `oob_check = false` for every tile including the last, so the last tile reads up to
   `nbatch_fa - 1` rows past the operand.  The KV cache allocation has always had that slack, but the
   converted F16 scratch is exact size and sits at the end of the node's allocation, so the read landed
   in the next allocation.  A 511-row guard tail is reserved after each converted operand.

**Deviation from the PR (maintainer decision).**  The PR applied the guard tail (fix 3) on every backend.
We gate it on `GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA2` (new `guard_tail` argument, passed by both callers), so
gfx1100/gfx1151/gfx1201 and every non-AMD backend keep their previous allocation sizes exactly.  The
bound was also re-derived for the comment: the `nbatch_fa` config field is 9 bits wide but the config
table `static_assert`s `<= 256`, and both the K tile (`I = nbatch_fa`) and the V chunk (`nbatch_V`, with
`static_assert(nbatch_fa % nbatch_V == 0)`) are bounded by it, so 511 rows is a safe bound with 2x margin.

**Validation (ours).**  Nothing in the change is device code: all three hunks are host functions, compiled
in all three builds below.  A/B is the same delivery tree (`76a17b4b` = r87) with and without the fold.

| box | arch | same-seed greedy text | prefill-logit KLD | `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` |
|-----|------|-----------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| local | gfx1201 | identical (also `-ctk/-ctv` f32, bf16, q8_0, ~600-token prefill) | 0.000000 / 100.000 % | OK (both arms) |
| fingon | gfx1100 | identical | -0.000000 / 100.000 % | OK (both arms) |
| halo | gfx1151 | identical | -0.000000 / 100.000 % | OK (both arms) |

The f32-KV arm is the one configuration where the guard tail is active off RDNA2 (it is the only
steady-state `need_f16 == true` path on gfx11xx/12xx now that quantized and bf16 KV are read natively):
text is unchanged there too, so even the gated reservation is numerically inert.

**RDNA2 evidence is the reporter's.**  We cannot build gfx1030 here at all -- *with or without* this
change: both local ROCm trees (7.14.1 and 10.1.0) fail gfx1030 codegen in `amd_hip_fp16.h` with
`use of undeclared identifier '__builtin_elementwise_exp10'` (verified identical on the pristine r87
tree, so it is a toolchain limitation, not a regression).  @slavap's numbers stand as the RDNA2 gate:
ROCm 7.2.4, one `gfx1030;gfx1100` build, V620 (gfx1030) `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` 6389/6389 and `MUL_MAT`
2444/2444, RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) the same, with the `hsk=192,hsv=128,nr23=[16,1],kv=512,bf16` repro
aborting before the fix and passing after.

**Follow-ups (reported to the reporter, PR closed as folded).**  (1) The guard tail protects the
*converted* scratch only; a natively-read operand (f16 KV) in the same unchecked `ncols2 > 1` branch can
still read up to `nbatch_fa - 1` rows past the KV **view**.  That stays inside the KV cache allocation for
real models (the cache is one tensor) but not for an exact-size tensor as in `test-backend-ops`; asked
@slavap whether to extend the guard to the native path (TODO #72).  (2) The tile K/V type is now chosen in two
hand-kept places (`fattn-tile.cu`'s case chooser and `fattn.cu`'s alloc size); this is the third time
they drifted (the q4_0 arm, the mixed-K/V NaNs, and now RDNA2 bf16), so a shared
`ggml_cuda_fattn_tile_type(K, V, cc)` helper is TODO #71.

## 261019.002 (r87) -- the post-prefill drop is forced on a wide -> narrow transition (r85 regression: second request at half speed, GPU fault on the fifth)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r87`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `441b38fbc`, net tree
`76a17b4b059d808fa24631ea249fc1308238cad2`, **12 blocks** (no new block; **block 09** amended).
`validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12 on a fresh tarball, tree matches).

**Published.**  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r87` pushed (annotated, on the release commit); CI **Validate delivery
set** green on `main` and on the tag, **Release patch set** green (assets `rdna-boosts-all.patch`,
`patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`).  The personal fork's `rdna-boosts` branch was force-pushed
(`--force-with-lease`, personal fork only) to `441b38fbc` / tree `76a17b4b`, matching `release.json`
(verified by `git ls-remote`); the local canonical `~/llama.cpp` was refreshed to it and rebuilt (dense
text unchanged).  The ROCm container images are built and pushed off-host by the worker watcher
(`scripts/container-watch.sh` on `radiance`): it was still finishing the r86 build when r87 was tagged and
picks r87 up on its next poll after that.

**The regression (r85, field r86).**  On the Flash-Next IQ4_NL field config (2x R9700,
`-sm tensor -ncmoe 46 -b/-ub 6144`, MTP adaptive n6, `--cache-idle-slots`, `--no-kv-unified`) the second
and later chat requests decoded at **~half speed**: a 10-prompt series measured **63.3 -> 31.8 -> 36.8 ->
38.0 t/s** and then **crashed at request 5** (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` in
`k_get_rows_float<float,float>`, the same faulting address on both GPUs, immediately after a re-arm).  It
reproduced on every run.  `MoE arena` decayed **33 560 -> 33 137 -> 32 835 MiB**; only one or two re-arms
ran.

**Root cause.**  r85 records `slab_narrow_boundary = max(re-reserved narrow, drop_observed)`, but at a
prefill -> decode transition `drop_observed` is the **wide prefill** work region (6 976 MiB).  The next
equally-wide prefill therefore compared equal (`cur >= was + 512` false), so `drop_now` stayed false: the
wide compute layout was never released and `moe_cache_rearm` never ran.  The arena kept shrinking; by
request 5 the re-arm hit a partial-slot table (`layer=47 ... 344 requested, only 202 fit`) with the
wide-aux region starved, and the next graph faulted.  The classic `n_tokens_prev > 8` condition was
dropped when the slab branch replaced it with the self-calibrating width compare.

**Fix (block 09, `src/llama-context.cpp`).**  A wide -> narrow transition always drops:
`if (n_tokens_prev > 8 || cur >= was + GGML_DROP_RESERVE_SLACK_BYTES)`.  r85's narrow -> narrow slack
compare is kept (the MTP verify-width loop stays fixed), and the forced drop restores the arena every
request.

**Measured (tree `76a17b4b`, exact field env, 10 sequential chat prompts).**  **63.5 / 65.7 / 83.0 /
82.1 / 80.9 / 83.6 / 87.2 / 84.2 / 63.5 / 82.5 t/s, no fault**, `MoE arena` 41 349 MiB on every request.
The r86 build on the same series: 63.3 / 31.8 / 36.8 / 38.0, **GPU fault at request 5** (reproduced twice).
A 20-prompt fixed run was also clean (62.7-87.0 t/s).

**Release gates (tree `76a17b4b`).**  Dense `Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0` and host-expert `35B-A3B -ncmoe 40` greedy
text byte-identical to r86; prefill-logit mean KLD **0.000707 / 98.755 %** PASS; adaptive-MTP 5 axes exactly

`5ebd156073f6`); `llama-batched-bench -npl 1,4,8` TG 100.4 / 328.1 / 478.3 (r86: 99.8 / 328.8 / 481.7);
`check-gpu-faults.sh` clean on the r87 run.

## 261018.010 (no release) -- issue #184: the r80 -> r82 Meta change is not a 4-stream regression here

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json` and the r86-candidate chain are untouched).  Issue
[#184](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/issues/184) (`@briansp2020`, 2x R9700, r80 vs
r82, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 47`, shared-MTP n-max 3, 4 concurrent chats) reports **-3.48 % [-5.60, -1.37]**
from the r82 `ggml-backend-meta.cpp` hunks alone (the #170 `[TAG_META_UNALLOC_ALIAS]` /
`[TAG_META_ALLOC_FAIL]` pair) with the host profile on `ggml_backend_meta_get_split_state`.  Investigated,
reproduced as a paired A/B, and **refuted as a 3.5 % effect**: on this box the two builds are equal within
+/-0.4 % with no stable sign.

**The two arms are the same program for his config.**  The alias path only runs for a tensor in the
split-state walk with no buffer of its own; on r80 that tensor asserted in
`ggml_backend_meta_buffer_n_bufs`, so every graph that ran on r80 never reached it.  All that remains is
codegen, measured with the exact `ggml-base` flags on **both** the reporter's clang (ROCm 10.0.0) and
10.1.0: `.text` of the object **82 633 -> 82 857 B** (10.0) / **82 681 -> 82 905 B** (10.1), i.e. **+224 B
(+0.27 %)**; the dispatcher is **out of line in both arms** (454 B vs 385 B) so the call structure is
identical, and the only hot-path change is one `buffer == nullptr` test plus the classification reading a
hoisted local.  The reporter's `+26/+28/+31 %` profile triple is most likely the same recursion
re-attributed by `perf` when the prologue/branch layout shifts (all three frames are the same walk); on
this box it does not become wall time.

**Measured** (2x R9700, ROCm 10.1, r86-candidate tree, only `libggml-base.so.0.26.0` swapped between
arms -- the reporter's own setup; GSQ-IQ3_XXS + shared Q8_0 MTP, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 47 -fa auto -ctk/-ctv
q8_0 -c 131072 -b/-ub 2048 -t 8 -np 4 --fit off --load-mode none --lazy-mode off
--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 3`, four concurrent greedy 192-token completions):

| session | pairs | r82 meta | alias reverted | paired |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 99.87 t/s | 99.63 t/s | +0.24 % |
| 2 | 4 | 99.39 t/s | 99.77 t/s | **-0.39 %** |
| 3 | 4 | 100.22 t/s | 100.24 t/s | -0.02 % |

Greedy text identical in every run.  Control arms: the pre-#170 hot dispatcher restored (cold-path
`noinline` helper for the #170 resolution) **-0.06 %**; the r84 graph-layout fingerprint disabled
**-0.07 %**; the pristine delivery build **-0.05 %** (validates the swapped `.so`).  Same-`.so` drift
across sessions is 0.8 %, so only same-session pairs are used.

**Sensitivity calibration (a null is only worth something if the instrument could see the effect).**  The
hot dispatcher was pessimised deliberately (a `volatile` add-loop at the top of every call): +100
iterations measured **+0.23 %**, +1000 iterations measured **+1.17 %** -- so the harness resolves host-path
cost to ~0.2 %, 3.5 % is ~3x the 1000-increment arm, and the whole r82 delta is **one branch per call**
(~1 % of what the 100-increment arm adds per call, two orders of magnitude under the floor).  Our
per-token decode is also 1.4x the reporter's (36.9 ms/token/stream vs ~25.8 from his 4 x 155 t/s), so host
cost weighs more here, not less.  The r82 hunks cannot produce the reported figure by instruction count --
if it is real on his box it is layout or inlining, which the `nm` ask settles.

**Measurement pitfall (recorded because it produced a 2.2x false bimodality).**  With the four prefills
left in the window the decode streams do not overlap for the whole window (a slot starts decoding as
soon as its prefill ends), and the same build then measured 63.8 / 63.8 / 63.8 / **139.2** t/s.  The
harness here caches every slot's prompt first (`cache_prompt`, one `n_predict: 1` request per slot), which
reproduces to 0.1-0.3 % within an arm.  Also checked: a pre-warmed 4-stream 192-token request reports `graph
reallocs = 2 / 2 (same size) / (changed size)` against `graphs reused = 72` -- the verify graphs are
**not** re-allocated each step,
and the r84 fingerprint is not adding re-reserves, so "graph identity for parallel sessions" is not
paying on this workload either.

**Issue reply**: posted 2026-10-18 ([#issuecomment-6259247216](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/issues/184#issuecomment-6259247216)),
label `needs more info` added; draft kept in `archive/work/issue-184-meta-r80r82/COMMENT-2026-10-18.md`.

**Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-18): bank it, no standalone release.**  The cold-path restructure is
staged as `beta/0013-meta-hot-dispatcher` (patch sha256 `d4303170...`, cut against the r86-candidate tree,
verified with strict `git am` on a fresh `apply-all.sh --include-beta` checkout: 12/12 blocks + beta 12 +
beta 13, tree `bb825861` for the pair, `82360b48` for this one alone) and folds into **block 00 at the next
revision**, where its gates run (the #170 24 GiB-parity reproduction first among them).  Measured: the
dispatcher drops **454 -> 287 B** (below the 385 B of the pre-#170 build) with the cold helper out of line
at 164 B, throughput -0.06 % (nothing), greedy text identical.  The upstream staging patch
(`upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-meta-split-unalloc-alias-and-alloc-fail.patch`) must be re-cut at the same time.

**The candidate shape (hot dispatcher exactly as pre-#170, all alias/host resolution in
a `noinline, cold` helper) is semantically identical, measured at zero, and would force a re-cut of
`upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-meta-split-unalloc-alias-and-alloc-fail.patch`; the maintainer decides whether to
take a measured-zero code motion.  Reply draft with the three diagnostics that would settle it on the
reporter's box (dispatcher `nm -S` sizes, the per-request `graph reallocs` counters, and a
layout-control arm built from two harmless perturbations of the same source):
`archive/work/issue-184-meta-r80r82/COMMENT-2026-10-18.md`; record + harnesses in the same directory.

**Separate finding (new, TODO #68).**  `gemma4` **dense** 12B Q8_0 + `-sm tensor` on 2 devices with
`-ctk q8_0` aborts at the warmup decode: `ggml-backend-meta.cpp:900 unsupported mul_mat split states:
node=... src0=#attn_inp_k_rot#0 axis=10 src1=Kcur_pos-5 (reshaped) axis=0`.  `attn_inp_k_rot` is the
K-rotation matrix (`n_rot_k > 0` only for a rotated cache type), so the rotation `ggml_mul_mat(rot, Kcur)`
reaches an unsupported split state; `-ctk f16`/`bf16` are fine, and it is independent of `-np`,
`--kv-unified`, `-fa` and the rope/fusion kill switches.  (`gemma4-assistant` + `-sm tensor` is rejected
cleanly by `llm_arch_supports_sm_tensor`, which is intended.)

## 261018.009 (r86 candidate) -- the band test is `ring_armed`, not "boundary above the floor" (block 10; NOT tagged)

**Not a release: `patches/`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` and `release.json` are regenerated for the r86
candidate (`tip 0190f6d96`, tree `f6f55ffc…`) but no tag is cut** -- the tag is cut with the maintainer's
incoming PR merge, which picks this up.  One-hunk refinement of r85's fix, in **block 10**.

**Why.**  r85 gated the band learning on `boundary > narrow_floor || ring_armed`.  The gfx1100 `-ncmoe 40`
trace (`fingon`, RX 7900 XTX, ROCm 10.1.0) shows why that is too strict: the boundary sits one chunk above
the floor for an unrelated narrow view (floor 1280 MiB, boundary 1536 MiB), so a **1536 MiB decode view**
was still classified wide and placed above the ring (`ret_off` = 1280 + 4160 = 5440 MiB), costing one arena
eviction per prefill -> decode transition (milder than the gfx1201 loop, same class).  The correct test is
**`ring_armed` alone**: it is set exactly when the boundary covers the carved ring, i.e. when a live wide
(prefill) view actually owns the ring region.  `ring_used` is not usable either -- it is a bump cursor that
stays at the end after a prefill.

**Measured.**  gfx1100 (`-ncmoe 40`, Q5_K_M, 15.8k prompt, MTP n4): before the refinement, floor 1280 /
view 1536 -> above the ring, 1 eviction at the transition; after, **floor 1280 -> 1536 (learned), view at
base 0**, one eviction during the prefill (the wide view taking chunks) and **one re-arm at the normal drop,
nothing after it**; decode 89.3 t/s, prefill 3146 t/s; the two greedy references are **unchanged**
(`Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M` 1034 chars `5380385a9fc4`, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M` 1020 chars
`b4f211677394`).  gfx1201 (the reported loop config): still **1** re-arm, decode **43.8 t/s**, prefill
1494 t/s; 16k prefill 1079.9 -> 1406.1 t/s with hash `a60a39e11133`; dense coherence `1c5d32ac537d`;
prefill-logit **KLD 0 / 100 %**.

**State.**  `release.json` names `v12-097cf33d9-r86` with tip `0190f6d96` / tree `f6f55ffc…` and
`validate-set.sh` is green on it (strict 12/12, tree matches); no tag, no GitHub release, and the personal
fork's `rdna-boosts` branch still points at the released r85 chain (`a3e721ac3`) until r86 is cut.

## 261018.008 (r85) -- gfx1100 cross-check: r85 is text-identical to r84 and the narrow-band loop does not occur on RDNA3

**No delivery change** (`release.json`, `patches/` and the tag are unchanged).  Independent validation of
`v12-097cf33d9-r85` on a second RDNA family, on a contributor-class box: `fingon`, single RX 7900 XTX
(gfx1100), ROCm 10.1.0-gfx1100, `~/bin/build-llama-rocm-101`, in-tree build of the r85 set (tree
`a121eb0f`, verified) and an r84 control built the same way (tree `c381b745`, `~/llama-r84ctl`, since the
r82-era gfx1100 figures were produced with ROCm **7.14** and are not comparable).

**Greedy text (fully resident, q8_0 K/V, `-n 128 --seed 42 --temp 0`, `prompts/reasoning.txt`).**

| model | r84 (ROCm 10.1.0) | r85 (ROCm 10.1.0) | r82 record (ROCm 7.14) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M` | 1034 chars `5380385a9fc4` | 1034 chars `5380385a9fc4` | 1064 chars `c606b3d55f24` |
| `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M` | 1020 chars `b4f211677394` | 1020 chars `b4f211677394` | 1046 chars `2c04f104b88e` |

r84 == r85 exactly on both, so the slab change is bit-identical on gfx1100; the difference against the r82
figures is the toolchain (7.14 -> 10.1.0 on this box), which is the known layout-sensitive
hipBLASLt/rocBLAS class and not attributable to this release.

**Host-expert MoE + embedded MTP** (`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M`, `-ngl 99 -ncmoe 24 -fa auto -ctk/-ctv
q8_0 -c 32768 -b/-ub 4096 --load-mode none --lazy-mode off --spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive
--spec-draft-n-max 4`, 15.8k-token prompt, 128 tokens): the slab arms (arena 10.81 GiB, **96.9 %
residency**), and **0 `moe_cache_rearm` / 0 `moe_cache_evict_slab_range` events on both r84 and r85** --
the narrow-band loop does not occur on this configuration; decode **135.6 t/s** (r84) / **152.9** (r85),
prefill **3413** / **4049 t/s**.  The fix is inert there (its condition - a decode view wider than the
band - is not reached), which is the expected outcome for a single-device 24 GB card.

**Finding (pre-existing, r84 and r85 alike).**  On a 24 GB card the **stock reserve** (headroom 4096 + aux
4096 = 8 GiB) leaves no room for the slab on a 20-25 GiB host-expert model: the slab is refused and the
cache is disabled with an explicit message ("the movable-boundary slab does NOT fit ... only 5632 MiB is
available after the 8192 MiB reserve ... the experts will STREAM"), i.e. a gfx1100 user with `-ncmoe` on
one 24 GB card gets the streaming path unless they lower `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB` /
`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_AUX_RESERVE_MIB` (1024/1024 was used on both arms here).  Worth a note in the
`-ncmoe` guidance for 24 GB cards; not caused by r85 and not changed by it.

**Correction (same day, after a bench on the same box).**  The paragraph above overstates the reserve
finding: `llama-bench -fa 1 -m <Q5_K_M> -ctv q8_0 -ctk q8_0 -ncmoe 40` runs fine on fingon at the **stock**
8 GiB reserve.  What does not fit is a *partially* offloaded config (`-ncmoe 24` on the Q4_K_M, or the
25 GiB Q5_K_M at `-ncmoe 16`), where the GPU still holds enough expert bytes that the free VRAM after
weights/KV cannot cover `reserve + work + ring + arena floor`.  With `-ncmoe 40` the slab arms normally
(free 20.58 GiB, arena 11 067 MiB, 48.8 % residency) and the expert cache is active, so "24 GB cards
cannot use the cache" is wrong -- the correct statement is "lower the reserve (or offload more layers)
when the slab does not fit", which the existing error message already says.

**Not validated:** gfx1151 (unified memory - host-expert offload is not meaningful there, so the slab path
is not exercised), ROCm 7.14 for this release (the box's 7.14 tree was superseded by 10.1.0), and 3-GPU.

## 261018.007 (r85) -- the slab narrow band is learned from the real decode graph (blocks 09, 10)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r85`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `a3e721ac3`, net tree
`a121eb0fb443a928d42773b2035fda89ccbdcf36`, **12 blocks** (block 00 + 01-11).  **Block 09 amended** (the
prefill -> decode drop reference) and **block 10 amended** (the slab's narrow band); no new block, no new
environment variable.  `release.json` regenerated; `validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 12/12,
tree matches).  Folded from `beta/0013-slab-narrow-floor/` (record moved to
`archive/work/slab-narrow-floor/`), which was staged against r83 while the r84 block-00 fix landed and then
re-cut onto the r84 base.

**Published.**  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r85` pushed (annotated, on the release commit); CI **Validate delivery
set** green on `main` and on the tag, **Release patch set** green (assets `rdna-boosts-all.patch`,
`patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`).  The personal fork's `rdna-boosts` branch was force-pushed
(`--force-with-lease`, personal fork only) to `a3e721ac3` / tree `a121eb0f`, matching `release.json`; the
local canonical `~/llama.cpp` was refreshed to it and re-gated (dense coherence `1c5d32ac537d`, 16k prefill
1405.9 t/s, hash `a60a39e11133`).  The ROCm container images are built and pushed off-host by the worker
watcher (`scripts/container-watch.sh` on `radiance`), which polls for the new tag.

**The report.**  Field config (2x R9700, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_NL`, 131k ctx, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 46`,
`-b/-ub 6144`, q8_0 K/V, MTP `draft-mtp-adaptive` n6, `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=ce`, stock slab defaults):
after a ~70k-token prefill the first decode produced a degenerate eviction sequence for seconds --
`moe_cache_rearm: re-armed 66 stood-down expert-cache tables` followed ~3 ms later by
`moe_cache_evict_slab_range: evicted 3654 / 3664 MiB`, every ~165 ms -- with decode 17-25 t/s instead of
~45, until it self-terminated.

**Root cause (a mis-measured band, not an overwrite).**  The always-resident narrow band
(`narrow_floor`) is estimated before the first ring carve from a `split_only` reserve of the
`n_rs_batch` shape = **1792 MiB**, and `ggml_cuda_slab_set_narrow_floor()` is raise-only *and returns
silently while `ring_used > 0`* (the ring's VA is frozen once it holds blocks).  The real MTP
decode/verify graph needs **2304 MiB**, so `work_alloc` classified a *decode* view as wide, placed it above
the H2D staging ring (`narrow_floor + ring_region` = 3968) and grew the boundary into the arena.  The
prefill -> decode drop then re-reserved the 1792 MiB shape and recorded *that* as its reference, so the
next step was "materially wider" again (512 MiB slack) -- one drop per decode step, 66 tables re-armed and
~3.65 GiB/device evicted each time.  Scaling confirms the MTP attribution: n-max 6 -> 18 cycles, n-max 2 ->
2, `--spec-type none` -> 0.

**Not new in r83, and r84 does not fix it.**  The r82 build reproduces the identical 18 cycles / 36
evictions, and so does the r84 tree (block 00's allocator fingerprint does not change the band estimate).
r83 is only a catalyst: its prefill is faster (1305 -> 1506 t/s in the same run), so the same churn costs
relatively more.

**The fix.**  *Block 10 (slab)*: `work_alloc` learns the band from the real graph -- a view that is not a
requested wide (prefill) pass is narrow even when it exceeds the floor, provided no wide view is live (the
ring region is only carved while one is); the floor and ring are then re-carved from it (the ring is idle
there, so its VA may move).  With a wide view live the above-the-ring placement is kept, and a refused
raise is now reported instead of dropped silently.  *Block 09*: the drop reference becomes
`max(work region observed before the drop, shape the drop re-reserved)`.

**Measured** (2x R9700, 73.5k-token prompt, 90 generated tokens, same config):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode `re-armed` cycles | 18 | **1** (the normal prefill -> decode drop) |
| decode t/s | 23.6 (r82) / 23.4 (r84) / 34.2 (r83) | **45.6** (`-sm tensor`), **35.5** (`-sm layer`) |
| prefill t/s, 74k tokens | 1506-1510 | 1511 |
| 16k prefill `-ub 4096` | 1443 | **1406 (-2.6 %)** |

**Cost, recorded deliberately:** a correctly sized band moves the ring up 512 MiB, so the wide (prefill)
layout starts 512 MiB higher and the arena is 512 MiB smaller during a prefill -- that is the 16k
`-ub 4096` delta above (staging off is unchanged at 1080.7).  Overlapping the band into the ring VA was
rejected: it is the same hazard class as the MTP-drafter/ring-sizing incident.

**Gates (r84 base, delivered tree `a3e721ac3`).**  Dense `Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0` coherence `1c5d32ac537d`;
Flash-Next 16k staging off/on 1080.7 -> 1406.3 t/s with hash `a60a39e11133`; prefill-logit **mean KLD

## 261018.006 (r84) -- issue #183: the graph allocator only reuses its layout for the graph it was computed for (block 00)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r84`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `adf90e2de`, net tree
`c381b74523086cc5db90632f54e7abd2c5f2e392`, **12 blocks** (block 00 + 01-11).  **Block 00 amended, no
new block, no new environment variable** (`release.json` regenerated; `validate-set.sh` green -- checksums
OK, strict 12/12 `git am` on a fresh tarball, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  Fixes
[issue #183](https://github.com/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts/issues/183) (`@overdoingism`, r82, gfx1201):
DFlash drafting on a `--parallel 4` server worked on the first slot that served a request and collapsed
to ~1 % acceptance on every other slot, 2.5x slower per token; `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` hid it.

**Root cause (allocator, not DFlash).**  `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph()` reapplies the recorded
`node_allocs`/`leaf_allocs` **positionally** and only recomputes them when `ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()`
says so; that check compared the node/leaf *count* and, per node, `size_max >= size` -- nothing about node
order, ops, shapes or which tensors carry `GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_OUTPUT`.  The in-graph sampling graph
(`build_sampling`: one chain per sequence x output row, selected with `ggml_build_forward_select`) keeps
its node count but changes **both** its node order and its output set when a different chain is selected --
which is exactly what happens when another slot starts drafting.  In the reused layout the previously
inactive chains' `top_k` outputs were dead (not outputs, so their block is recycled and shared), so the
newly active -- now `OUTPUT` -- `top_k` tensors all inherited that one address: every output row then read
the last computed candidate ids.  The sampled top-k *logits* stayed correct, which is why only the
drafted token ids (and therefore acceptance) were wrong.  r65's second scheduler (block 09) is what puts
two consecutive same-node-count step graphs on one scheduler; with `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` the 84-node
injection graph alternates with the 335-node step graph, so a re-layout happens on every call anyway --
the 0.5 ms/cycle the second scheduler exists to remove, and the reason the single-scheduler path never
saw it.

**Fix (block 00, `ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c`, +53 lines).**  `ggml_gallocr` records an FNV-1a fingerprint of
the graph its layout was computed for -- node/leaf order, op (in-place eligibility), element type and
`ne[]` (sizes), `view_src`, and the INPUT/OUTPUT/COMPUTE flags, plus the node/leaf split -- and
`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` requires a match.  A topology change now re-reserves instead of applying a
foreign layout.  This is the generic invariant block 00 was already about (it holds the allocator fix for
unused-view `n_views` and the "outputs are never freed" rule), so every block -- and any future
speculative mechanism -- can rely on it rather than handling it case by case.  It only ever *adds* a
re-reserve (one per topology change, ~once per slot switch here); it never skips one.  There is no kill
switch because there is nothing to disable: the old behaviour was simply wrong.

**Evidence (gfx1151, r83 tree, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M + dflash-Q8_0 draft, prose prompt, 256 greedy tokens, one
request per slot in one process).**  r83: slot 0 `193/303 = 0.637` / 18.3 ms per token, slots 1-3
`6/1230 = 0.005` / 46 ms.  With the fix (and identically with `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0`): **every slot
`193/303 = 0.637`, 18.0-18.3 ms, text `b1e6c82b5688`** in all cells, including the case where the request
order starts at slot 3 and a different-prompt pair.  Instrumentation showed: the denoise graph receives
identical k_idxs / mask / K-cache hashes in both arms and the selected top-k logits are identical, while
the candidate ids differ; on the second sequence all six `res->t_candidates[i]->data` are the *same*
address (six distinct addresses on the first sequence, and the gathered `top_k_rows` stay distinct);
`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` returned 0 for a graph whose node-count-unchanged fingerprint differed;
`--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling`, a second scheduler on the injection graph only, or on both graphs,
all fix it (only "step graph on the second scheduler, injection on the main one" breaks).

**Gates (delivered tree `c381b7452`, gfx1151).**  Same-seed greedy text **byte-identical to r83**: dense
`Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0` `-sm tensor` `7e6229b260f6` (111 chars), MoE `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M -ncmoe 40` (host
master / slab path) `8d733a56c740` (271 chars).  `llama-bench -p 512 -n 64 -r 3` (MoE, `-ncmoe 40`):
pp512 2127.2 +/- 6.2, tg64 61.05 +/- 0.25 against r83's 1991.3 +/- 220.4 / 60.93 +/- 0.40 (the pp
spread is the unchanged-build noise; no regression).  Four concurrent requests (`-np 4`): fixed arm ==
`SCHED2=0` arm == r83 arm, same acceptance and text per slot (that shape never triggered it).  No new
`ENVIRONMENT.md` row (no knob); `check-gpu-faults.sh` not run (no kernel changed and no fault was seen in
any arm).  **Not run: the gfx1201 3-GPU box, the adaptive-MTP gate (the local 35B-A3B GGUF carries no MTP
head) and `gate-prefill-logits.sh`** -- this is an allocator-invariant change with byte-identical generated
text on both a dense and a host-expert MoE model, so the prefill-logit instrument (which compares prefill
logits, issue #113) has nothing to see; re-run it on the primary box if the maintainer wants a gfx1201
record before publishing.

**Upstream status.**  The insufficient assumption ("same node count and sizes => same layout") is upstream
`ggml-alloc` code, but **no vanilla llama.cpp configuration was found that triggers it** (tested: no
speculative decoding at all, backend sampling on, `--parallel 4`, 4 slots -- pre-fix and fixed builds
produce the same text on every slot `a063a316d1df`), and r83 with `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` is byte-identical
to the fixed build.  So it is not staged under `upstream/` for now; the delivery's own feature exposed it.
The MTP draft context has the same shape (step graph only on the second scheduler) and is expected to be
protected by the same fix, but that is unverified here (no MTP head locally).  Revisit the upstream
candidate if a vanilla reproduction ever appears.

**Records.**  Candidate patch and reproduction harness (issue-183 repro, concurrency harness, before/after
binaries) were session-local; the fix itself is the block-00 delta above.  The related campaign record is
`archive/work/draft-sched2/` (the r65 second scheduler this exposed).

**Published.**  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r84` pushed (annotated, on the release commit `3cbfeeb9`); CI
**Validate delivery set** green on `main` and on the tag and **Release patch set** green (assets
`patches.tar.gz`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` sha256 `8194355321173e58...` = `release.json.all_patch`,
`release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`).  Fork `rdna-boosts` re-cut to `adf90e2de` (tree `c381b7452` =
`release.json.tree`, only the block-00 commit message differs from the gated build) and force-pushed with
lease to the personal fork only.  The worker watcher on `radiance` builds and pushes the ROCm 7.14.1 / 10.1
container images off the tag (not yet confirmed at the time of writing).  The block-00 commit body and

## 261018.005 (r83) -- the slab narrow-band eviction loop: found, root-caused and staged as `beta/0013` (no delivery change)

**Not a release; no `patches/`, `release.json` or tag change.**  A report from the field (2x R9700,
`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_NL`, 131k ctx, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 46 -b/-ub 6144`, q8_0 K/V, MTP adaptive n6,
`GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=ce`, stock slab defaults) showed a long degenerate eviction sequence during the
first decode after a ~70k-token prefill: every ~165 ms `moe_cache_rearm: re-armed 66 stood-down
expert-cache tables` then `moe_cache_evict_slab_range: evicted 3654/3664 MiB`, decode 17-25 t/s instead
of ~45.

**Reproduced and attributed.**  Same 73.5k-token prompt + MTP decode: **r82** does the identical 18
cycles / 36 evictions, so it is **not new in r83** (r83 is only a catalyst: prefill 1305 -> 1506 t/s in
the same run, and decode 23.6 -> 34.2 t/s inside the churn).  It scales with the draft depth (n-max 6 ->
18 cycles, n-max 2 -> 2, `--spec-type none` -> 0), i.e. it is the MTP decode/verify layout.

**Root cause (measurement, not an overwrite).**  `ggml_cuda_slab_set_narrow_floor()` is raise-only and
returns silently while `ring_used > 0` (the ring's VA is frozen after the first prefill), so the
always-resident narrow band stays at the pre-carve `split_only` estimate of the `n_rs_batch` shape --
**1792 MiB** -- while the real MTP decode graph needs **2304 MiB**.  `work_alloc` therefore classified a
*decode* view as wide, placed it above the H2D staging ring (`narrow_floor + ring_region` = 3968 MiB)
and grew the boundary into the arena (3.65 GiB/device evicted).  The prefill -> decode drop then
re-reserved the 1792 MiB shape and recorded *that* as its reference (`slab_narrow_boundary`), so the next
step was "materially wider" again (512 MiB slack) -- one drop per decode step.

**Staged fix (`beta/0013-slab-narrow-floor`, `0013-slab-narrow-floor.patch`, sha256 `16cee76f…`, cut
against the r83 tree).**  `work_alloc` learns the band from the real graph (a non-wide view is narrow
even above the floor while no wide view is live; the ring is idle there, so it is re-carved);
`set_narrow_floor` reports a refused raise instead of dropping it; the drop reference becomes
`max(observed-before-drop, re-reserved)`.  Measured on the fix: **1** re-arm (the normal drop),
decode **45.4 t/s** (`-sm tensor`) / **35.8** (`-sm layer`), prefill unchanged at 74k tokens; 18 -> 1
cycles on the `-ub 4096` variant; gates green (dense coherence `1c5d32ac537d`, Flash-Next 16k hash
`a60a39e11133`, prefill-logit KLD 0 / 100 %, adaptive-MTP 4 axes + phase probe exactly equal to r83).
Cost recorded: 16k prefill **1443 -> 1411 t/s (-2.2 %)** because the correctly sized band moves the ring
up 512 MiB (disjoint regions kept deliberately -- overlapping the band into the ring VA is the
MTP-drafter/ring-sizing hazard class).

**Folds into block 10 (creates `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`) + block 09 (owns `slab_narrow_boundary` in
`src/llama-context.cpp`).**  Held as a candidate because an r84 block-00 fix is landing; re-cut onto that
base before promotion.  Record: `beta/0013-slab-narrow-floor/{README,BETA-TESTING}.md`.

## 261018.004 (r83) -- the ring and the copy: why R1 is parked, and the pin-scope argument (docs only)

**No code, `patches/`, `release.json` or tag change.**  Records the design decision that closed the
R1 (in-place MMQ read) question after r83, and fixes a documentation error in the campaign record.

**The decision.**  The ring and its arena -> ring copy stay; **R1 is parked, not pending**.  The copy is
not free (~24 GiB read + ~24 GiB written per ubatch/device, ~74 ms at HBM speed = ~2-3 % of prefill
wall, plus ~2.1 GiB/device of ring), but it keeps a **short pin on the uncontended resource**, and three
properties depend on it:
1. **Masking** - the ring is the prefetch mechanism: each table's bulk fill is issued on the copy stream
   per split and consumed after its event, so the next table streams while the current split computes
   (~144 fills/ubatch/device).  Redirect mode (`GGML_SCHED_STAGE_MODE=1`, which drops the
   `ring -> input_cpy` hop) measured neutral (1547.0 vs 1549-1559 t/s, same hash), as block 09's own
   2026-10-06 note already recorded.
2. **Liveness decoupling** - once copied, the arena is free to evict, refill or be stood down (the
   movable-boundary slab does all three): the staged bytes are private to the ring slot, a mid-prefill
   stand-down degrades to the plain upload (`unusable=287-315`/run, `geom_decline=0`), and the map is
   only consulted at fill time.  An in-place resident read would need the arena's hot slots - the ones
   decode re-admits - to stay valid for the whole graph.
3. **Pin scope** - the copy is "pin -> copy -> release" over one table (~4 ms H2D part, sub-ms D2D),
   with the pinned bytes being private staging scratch rather than part of the eviction policy.  The
   75/25 freeze and the per-layer/per-ring-slot pin attach the pin to the **arena** for a **phase**, and
   that scope is what measured as a loss (A long prefill 889.4 -> 830.4 t/s, B short prefill 1479.1 ->
   1150.1, staged H2D 33 -> 36.5-49.1 %, decode hit rate flat).  Under a truly concurrent scheduler the
   gap widens: a graph-lifetime pin would stall decode's eviction policy for a multi-second prefill.

**Why R1 loses either way.**  Its cold-half in-place read removes the last H2D but replaces a prefetched
bulk copy with demand PCIe reads inside each MMQ launch (loses masking); its resident-half read saves the
D2D but re-introduces the contended pin for the bytes that churn most (loses the liveness decoupling).  The
"proven ~2x" the campaign record attributed to R1 was the *combination* (staging + in-place) on an r33
baseline whose upload was largely unmasked (2.9k 794 t/s, 61k 1384 t/s on IQ3_XXS/256k); R2 already took
the masking half of that win.

**Documentation error fixed.**  The record claimed the remaining serial cost was the `ring -> input_cpy`
D2D and that R1 "removes the ring copy and gets closer to the compute floor".  The redirect A/B prices
that hop only; the **arena -> ring fill** of the resident 73 % is a different copy, sits inside R2's
measurements, and has never been priced in isolation.  If it ever needs pricing, sweep residency at a
fixed prompt (`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB` 72 -> 85 -> 95 %): it swaps D2D bytes for saved H2D bytes one-for-one,
so prefill t/s versus residency *is* the net marginal cost - an arena-sizing probe for
`archive/work/moe-cache-coverage/`, not an R1 prerequisite.

**Forward note for `archive/work/moe-cpu-overlap/`.**  R2's copy-time pin is implicit today (the scheduler
serialises; the order event covers writes-before-fill).  Under real prefill/decode overlap it must be
named: a per-slot in-flight event so an admission waits for an outstanding fill or takes another slot,
plus map-vs-write atomicity (`g_write_seq` check -> map build -> fill) - the pattern already used by the
bounded host pool's per-`(slot, device)` events and the Q8_1 arena's outlive rule.

**Record:** `archive/work/prefill-arena-residency/README.md` §9 (new design note) plus corrected R1
framing in its §3/§4/§7 and the freeze notes, and a superseded-by pointer in
`CONCURRENCY-2026-10-18.md`.

## 261018.003 (r83) -- prefill cache staging: upload only the experts the cache arena does not already hold (blocks 09, 10)

**Release `v12-097cf33d9-r83`**: base `097cf33d9`, canonical tip `ca236e6b5`, net tree
`a130971754b5abfb4a153e6fd1144fd578f1154a`, **12 blocks** (block 00 + 01-11).  **Block 09 amended** (the
cache engine) and **block 10 amended** (the staging hook; block 10 is what creates
`ggml-cuda-moe-cache-hooks.cu`, so the change cannot all live in block 09).  No new block.
`release.json` regenerated; `validate-set.sh` green (fresh tarball, strict 12/12, tree matches).
Promoted from `archive/work/prefill-arena-residency/` (the R2 prototype, `r2-prototype.patch`): the revival of
PR #121's cache-aware staging **without** the device-remap policy removed at r40, plus the smaller
inspection surface.

**What landed.**  Every prefill ubatch used to push the whole host-resident expert set over PCIe
(`-ncmoe 48` on a 176B-A3B: 48 layers x 3 tables x ~225 MiB/device ~= **32 GiB/device/ubatch**).  The
scheduler's whole-table staging copy is now filled by one kernel per table: an expert already resident
in the cache arena is copied from its slot (D2D, the device's compact `expert_bytes` slice), the rest
from the pinned host master (H2D), into the ordinary staged table **in expert order**, so every
consumer is unchanged and the bytes are identical.  Both staging call sites are covered
(`stage_upload` under `-sm layer`, `stage_gather` under the `-sm tensor` meta split).  The source map
is a per-table **prefill residency snapshot**: a small device copy of the authoritative host
`expert_slot`, rebuilt when the cache writes (`g_write_seq`), the arena moves or the slot count
changes, uploaded on the copy stream (the copy stream is ordered after compute only when the arena
may have been written, so a pure prefill keeps overlapping), never mutated by decode.  It declines to
the plain upload for a table the movable-boundary slab stood down mid-prefill, an unpinned host master
(issue #116) or a geometry mismatch.  **DEFAULT ON**; kill switch `GGML_MOE_CACHE_STAGE=0` restores the
full whole-table upload.  `moe_cache_report` now prints the staged arena/host split and the H2D
percentage.  `ENVIRONMENT.md` corrected: the r36 `GGML_MOE_CACHE_INPLACE` row is gone (that path was
removed at r40) and `GGML_MOE_CACHE_STAGE` is documented as it now behaves.

**Measured** (2x R9700 gfx1201, ROCm 10.1.0, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_NL` 176.9B-A3B, `-sm tensor
-ncmoe 48 -fa 1 -ctk/-ctv f16 -t 8`, field loader `--load-mode none --lazy-mode off`, greedy `-n 64`
seed 42, stage 0 = the kill switch):

| prompt / `-ub` | off | **on** | gain | greedy sha |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 15 800 tok / 2048 | 582.1 | **836.4** | +43.7 % | `7171139467ce` |
| 15 800 tok / 4096 | 1091.6 | **1442.8** | +32.2 % | `a60a39e11133` |
| 31 555 tok / 4096 | 1182.4 | **1585.0** | +34.1 % | `98800fdba634` |
| 15 800 tok / 4096, `-sm layer` | 755.0 | **1160.2** | +53.7 % | `37ea05798d5d` |
| 15 800 tok / 2048, `--host-experts pool` | 472.7 | **662.9** | +40.2 % | `7171139467ce` |

Staged H2D falls to **27.1 %** of the table bytes (arena 46 604 MiB = 71.9 % residency, 368/512
slots/table), `geom_decline=0`, `nomatch=0`; `unusable` (287-315 tables per run) is the slab standing
tables down mid-prefill, and those correctly fall back.  PRS rebuilds = one per table per ubatch
(the map is 2 KiB; the cost is the copy-stream ordering, not the map).  Two-slot concurrency
(`-np 2`, 64k/slot, `-b/-ub 4096`, harness in `archive/work/prefill-arena-residency/tools/`): long prefill
**750.8 -> 877.4 t/s**, short prefill **1091.4 -> 1285.2**, and the long decode still collapses to
~4 t/s under a prefill stream **with the staging off and on** -- that is the serialized two-slot
scheduler, not this cache.  **Redirect mode** (`GGML_SCHED_STAGE_MODE=1`) is neutral (1437 vs 1443
t/s, same hash).

**Beta 12 interaction, measured but not delivered** (`beta/0012-slab-transient-absorption`, still a
beta): on top of this r83 code beta 12 adds **+8.6 … +9.6 %** more prefill (arena 46.6 -> 52.3 GiB,
residency 71.9 -> 80.7 %, staged H2D 27.1 -> 17.6 %) and costs ~1 % with the staging disabled; both
apply orders give byte-identical content, and the two-slot stress is unchanged.  So when beta 12
promotes onto an R2-carrying tree it should be a win on both prefill and decode.  Record:
`archive/work/prefill-arena-residency/BETA12-INTEGRATION-2026-10-18.md`.
