## 261015.005 (r67) -- block-09 host-expert ring arming + the r66 MUL_MAT_ID prefill regression

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r67` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`c536e9703`, net tree `3ccabe1522d480cef2001ee87712d56acef0d1eb`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball -- strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  **No new block:**
blocks 09/10/11 are amended.  Because block 10's refactor owns `ggml-cuda.cu`, `ggml-cuda-slab.cu` and
`mmid.cu`, and block 11 last touches `llama-context.*`, each fix is folded into the last block that owns
the file -- **09** `moe-expert-cache.cu`; **10** `mmid.cu`, `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`, `ggml-cuda.cu`; **11**
`llama-context.{h,cpp}`.  No block bodies outside those three change.

**r66 prefill regression -- root cause and fix (block 10, `mmid.cu`).**  The r66 block-00 MUL_MAT_ID
duplicate-ids fix replaced `mm_ids_helper`'s specialized templates with a generic kernel that processes
**one token per warp iteration with two warp reductions per token** (`warp_reduce_sum` +
`warp_prefix_inclusive_sum`) and reads `ids` twice; that is ~8x the r65 helper cost, and it runs once per
MoE MUL_MAT_ID.  Bisection (35B-A3B Q8_0, `-t 8 -fa on -ub 4096 -p 4096`, fully resident): r65
**8357** -> r66 **6430** t/s; dense 27B unaffected (1971 -> 1974, so MUL_MAT_ID-only); reverting the 5
MUL_MAT_ID files recovered it (8386); `mmid.cu` alone reproduced it (6473); `mmq`/`mmf` alone did not
(8337).  Fix: restore the `n_expert_used` {2,4,6,8,10,16,32} template fast path, **duplicate-correct**
-- `warp_size/neu_padded` tokens per iteration and the per-token count/rank from
`warp_reduce_sum<neu_padded>` / `warp_prefix_inclusive_sum<neu_padded>` inside the token's padded lane
group, so every repeated `(token, iex)` occurrence is its own compact row in `(token, iex)` order; the
generic kernel stays as the `n_expert_used == 0` fallback.  Recovered: fully-resident **8243** t/s (r65
8357), `-ncmoe 4` **6859** (r65 6522 -- the kept r66 `mmq`/`mmf` changes beat r65).  Correctness:
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID -p dup=1` **16/16**, full `-o MUL_MAT_ID` **947/947**.

**Block-09 host-expert fixes (from the `archive/work/block09-cache-ring-arming/` handover).**

1. **Cache completeness (block 09, `moe-expert-cache.cu`).**  The deferred arena sizing compares the
   **total** registered host-expert bytes against the preflight total instead of each device's even
   `bytes/n_dev` guess.  On the GSQ 40/60 split the per-device gate never latched, so the arena was
   never sized and every step streamed (GSQ `-ncmoe 48`: 14.8 -> 62 t/s).
2. **Pageable weight source (block 10, `ggml-cuda.cu`).**  `ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor`
   bounces **any** pageable source, dropping the `usage != WEIGHTS` exemption, so the `-lm none` +
   `-sm tensor` Meta whole-tensor upload no longer issues a bare `cudaMemcpyAsync` from anonymous
   memory (the SDMA0 fault, issue #137 class; IQ4_NL 5/5 clean loads).  A pinned source still copies
   directly.
3. **Early narrow floor + ring arming (block 10 `ggml-cuda-slab.cu`, block 11 `llama-context.*`).**
   The narrow (verify) floor is pinned before the first prefill (not only at the prefill->decode drop),
   and a prefill ubatch (`n_tokens >= 64`) is placed **above** the ring even when its compute buffer is
   no larger than the narrow floor -- the 35B-A3B / GSQ layouts are size-independent, so a size-only
   test left the carved ring unarmed and the H2D staging fell back to a capped `cudaMalloc`.  A
   narrow->wide transition drops the reused narrow buffer so the prefill actually re-reserves; the width
   threshold is `< 64` to match the ring gate (GSQ's first prefill ubatch is 42 tokens).  Proof:
   `WORK_ALLOC ... narrow=0 ret_off=narrow_floor+ring_region` on all three models and
   `ring_slot_capacity > 0`.  GSQ `-ncmoe 48` prefill **645 -> 687** t/s (r65 651).

**DoD matrix (gfx1201, 2x R9700, `tools/dod.sh`, `-b/-ub 2048`, 31.5K prompt; 0 faults; ring armed on
all three; "field 70K" = the IQ4_NL 70K MTP n7 config).**

## 261015.004 (docs, campaign closure) -- archive `moe-layer-stagger` as refuted/superseded (tail-set host residency covers the win)

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` untouched; no release).
TODO item **63** is **closed as refuted**, and `wip/moe-layer-stagger/` moves to
`archive/work/moe-layer-stagger/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

The campaign proposed **striding** the host/device expert-layer split (even layers device, odd host at
a 50:50 split) so the H2D expert upload would be spread across the prefill instead of exposed as one
contiguous host-only stretch.  Two things settle it:

1. **Placement is a no-op.**  With the page-cache confound removed (run from a tmpfs model copy; the
   disk-backed first pass drifted 1168 -> 1500 t/s, +28 %, purely from warm-up), four **disjoint** host
   sets (`0..23`, even, odd, `24..47`) are identical to **0.1 %** at `-ncmoe 24` (`-ub 2048`:
   pp4096 1578.8 / 1576.8 / 1578.8 / 1578.6).  Partial-offload prefill is bound by the H2D of the whole
   host table per ubatch (~52-67 ms per host layer, 21.4 GiB per ubatch at ~15-18 GB/s against a PCIe
   **x4** upstream link), so the *schedule* cannot matter -- only fewer bytes (`-ub`: **+37 %** from
   `2048 -> 4096`), a correct gather, or residency.  The ring does not lead the upload (split N's upload
   overlaps split N-1's compute, one deep), and a deeper pipeline cannot beat the link.
2. **The wished-for speedup is already the delivery's.**  **r63** makes `-ncmoe N` host the **last N**
   trunk layers (rear-fill) instead of the first N -- the tail layers carry the colder routing and have
   preceding resident compute to overlap the upload with.  Measured 35B-A3B Q8_0, 2x R9700, `-ncmoe 20`:
   `pp4096` **4264 vs 4120**, `tg500` **87.5 vs 82.6**, `pp512` **871 vs 635** (`WORKLOG.md` 261014.008).
   A per-layer stride generalises nothing on top of that.

The `-sm tensor` + `-ncmoe` corruption found while running the campaign (garbage/NaN on 35B-A3B, gemma4
26B-A4B, Flash-Next GSQ unless `GGML_META_SPLIT_COPY=0` or `-sm layer`) was fixed in **r62** and folded
into block 10; it is unrelated to the stagger question and is not a residual of this closure.

**Artefacts.**  `archive/work/moe-layer-stagger/{README.md,RESOLUTION.md,FINDINGS-2026-10-14.md}` plus
`logs/` and the env-gated scratch knob `tools/ncmoe-layer-select.patch` (inert unless set).  Nothing was
promoted; `TODO.md` #63 and `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` are updated, and the `wip/` entry is deleted with no stub.

## 261015.003 (r66) -- upstream MUL_MAT_ID duplicate-ids fix (block 00), env-read caching, -Wshadow sweep

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r66` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`6b54e57be`, net tree `4397ae5570b724d0896d1ad3a48298aaccbab47a`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green
on a fresh tarball -- strict 12/12 `git am`, applied tree equals the recorded tree).  **No new block:**
each change is folded into the block that owns its concern.

**MUL_MAT_ID duplicate expert ids -- block 00 (foundation).**  The delivery carried the upstream CUDA/HIP
duplicate-ids bug until now (recorded as the unfiled `upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-mul-mat-id-dup.{md,patch}`):
`mm_ids_helper` kept one compact column per `(token, expert)` pair, so a token whose id row repeated an
expert left the compact `ids_src1` tail uninitialised -- the MMQ path then read it in
`quantize_mmq_q8_1_cuda` (wrong results for f16/q8_0/q4_0, then a GPU page fault), and the MMQ/MMF
column-tile grids were sized from the token count.  The fix (every occurrence is its own compact row;
the routed MMQ tile loop iterates the expanded per-expert column list; the non-compact MMF path is
gone; the host sorted fallback emits every match) is applied to **block 00** as a generic upstream
foundation fix, since block 00 touches none of its files and every later MUL_MAT_ID block (06-10)
then builds on correct duplicate handling.  The qwen4exp 512x10 fast path (block 10) keeps its own
per-occurrence atomics and is merged onto the new generic helper.

**Environment reads cached to internal state -- blocks 00/05/08/09/10.**  getenv() takes a lock and
rescans the environment block on Windows, so every behaviour-affecting read that sat on a hot path is
now resolved once into a function-local static (or value) instead of per call:

| owner block | reads |
|---|---|
| 00 (generic upstream hygiene) | `GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_COMPUTE_TYPE` (per cuBLAS matmul; cached as the parsed enum), `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY` (per device alloc), `GGML_CUDA_REGISTER_HOST`, `GGML_CUDA_NO_PINNED`, `LLAMA_GRAPH_INPUT_DEBUG` (per graph input object), `LLAMA_BATCH_DEBUG` (per batch) |
| 05 | `GGML_CUDA_FA_WMMA_256`, `GGML_CUDA_FA_WMMA_MAX_HEAD` |
| 08 | `GGML_CUDA_MMQ_J_MAX`, `GGML_Q6_COMPACT_J` (in the shared `ggml_cuda_mmq_select_J`, per MUL_MAT(_ID)) |
| 09 | `GGML_SCHED_STAGE`, `LLAMA_DROP_COMPUTE_BUFFERS`, `GGML_CUDA_WORK_ALLOC_DEBUG` + `GGML_CUDA_CACHE_GEOM_DEBUG` (new `common.cuh` helpers), `GGML_CUDA_POOL_MIN_FREE_MIB`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_VALIDATE_LAYER` |
| 10 | `LLAMA_QSA_PLE_HOSTGATHER`, `GGML_CUDA_GDN_CHUNKED`, `GGML_CUDA_GDN_CHUNKED_BF16`, `GGML_CUDA_QSA_SLICES`, `GGML_CUDA_SPLICE_GATHER`, the `GDN_DBG_SKIP_*` diagnostics, and the slab `GGML_CUDA_WORK_ALLOC_DEBUG` sites |

`GGML_ENV_STR` (blocks 09) now caches the **value** in a `std::string` rather than the `getenv()`
pointer: the MSVC CRT returns a buffer that the next getenv() call overwrites, so a cached `const char *`
is not safe on Windows (this affects `GGML_SCHED_STAGE`, `GGML_SCHED_EVENTS`, `GGML_SCHED_MODE`, ...).
The same pointer-cache class in `gated_delta_net.cu`, `fattn.cu`, `fattn-qsa.cu`, `ggml-cuda.cu` and
`moe-expert-cache.cu` is converted to a value.  No environment variable changes its name, default or
two-idiom semantics.

**-Wshadow sweep -- block 00.**  The block-00 `-Wshadow` enablement missed nine upstream shadowing
declarations the clang/GCC host build reports; all are renamed in **block 00** (they are present at the
fork point): `step35.cpp` (per-layer `n_embd_k_gqa`/`n_embd_v_gqa`), `llama-moe-cache.cpp` (`init_ctx`),
`llama-vocab.cpp` (`_try_copy`), `llama-quant.cpp` (`layer_info`), `llama-model.cpp`
(`make_gpu_buft_list`, `get_tensor`).  **Block 11** also fills the newly appended `slab_compute_plain`
device-iface entry (NULL) in the CPU and RPC device interfaces -- the field was appended by block 09 after
those iface fills were written -- clearing the last two `-Wmissing-field-initializers` warnings.

**Gates.**  `validate-set.sh` green (strict 12/12, tree `4397ae55`); build clean with
`LLAMA_ALL_WARNINGS=ON` (`-Wshadow`) and no shadow warnings; `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID -p 'dup=1'`
**16/16** (was failing + page-faulting), `-o MUL_MAT_ID` full **ROCm0 OK**, `MUL_MAT`/`MUL_MAT_ID`
`type_a=q4_K`/`q6_K` all OK; `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (mean KLD **0.000707** / same-top-p
**98.755 %**, identical to the recorded gfx1201 base); `llama-cli` 4B Q8_0 `-sm tensor` same-seed
greedy identical to r65 (the only diff is the build-id and timing lines).

buffer type when the output device is a meta (tensor-split) device with no host buffer type of its own
(`LLAMA_OUTPUT_PINNED=0` kill-switch; the meta device's own `get_host_buffer_type` is unchanged).  Under
`-sm tensor` the output buffer was pageable, so every per-step D2H read of the logits/embeddings/MTP
hidden state blocked the host until the GPU finished.  Record: `archive/work/output-pinned/`.

**PR #154 `draft-sched2` (blocks 09 + 10).**  The MTP draft context's graphs with outputs run on a second
scheduler (`llama_context::sched_alt`), swapped into `sched` only for the duration of a `decode`/`encode`
and swapped back by a scope guard, so the no-output ingest graph and the 1-token draft-step graph both
stay allocated and reused instead of being re-split/re-allocated every cycle.  Supporting: a per-scheduler
meta view slot (`ggml_backend_meta_set_view_slot`, so two live graphs do not clear each other's external
views) and a new optional device-iface entry `slab_compute_plain` (the second scheduler's small COMPUTE
buffer bypasses the slab and the chunk quantization).  `LLAMA_DRAFT_SCHED2=0` kill-switch.  Record:
`archive/work/draft-sched2/`.

**PR #159 `rdna3-mmvq-vecdot-alu` (block 07).**  Two output-preserving instruction reductions in the
mmvq dot products: the Q4_K VDR-2 mins term becomes `(d8 * float(dot2)) * float(m)` (both forms are a
single rounding of the same exact value, and the two factors are separately column- and row-dependent so
a multi-row/multi-column block computes each once), with the 6-bit scales/mins packed into one word; and
the HIP-only Q6_K VDR-2 unpack replaces `(vil | 16*h) - 32` with one `v_perm_b32` lookup plus an OR.
Record: `archive/work/rdna3-mmvq-vecdot-alu/`.

**PR #155 `rdna3-mmb-tile-spill` (block 06) and PR #156 `rdna3-mmvq-q4k-rpb` (block 08, gfx1100).**  A per-arch
`mmb_arch_cfg.big_q4k_only` (set for RDNA3_0) keeps the 128x256 MMB dense tile only for Q4_K, so the
other weight types take the non-spilling 128x128 tile and a spilling MMB kernel can no longer coexist
with the spilling head-256 WMMA FA kernel under WSL2 (the
`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` fault); and `calc_rows_per_block_weight` returns 4 rows per
block for a Q4_K verify batch on the RDNA3_0 table (bit-identical, the q8_1 columns load once per
block).  Both are runtime no-ops on gfx1201.  Records: `archive/work/rdna3-mmb-tile-spill/`,
`archive/work/rdna3-mmvq-q4k-rpb/`.

**Gates (integration build, gfx1201).**  Coherence 4B `-sm tensor` identical to the r64 binary
(`f051d98e4e30`, 64-token arm); prefill-logit **PASS** (mean KLD 0.000707, same-top-p 98.755 %,

## 261015.001 (r64) -- segmented Meta writes, splice-gather ring ownership, qwen4exp image+MTP

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r64` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`5eeff4da5`, net tree `ca68f3ed0557d9cb2168f8b4773ab32476f84feb`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball).  **Blocks 09 and 10** are amended; no new block.

**Block 09 -- the segmented `set_tensor_async` classifier (r63 residual, `archive/work/gemma4-drift-and-meta-async/`).**
`ggml_backend_meta_set_tensor_async` classified a segmented write by `offset % row_stride == 0` alone,
so an aligned-offset mid-row range was misrouted to the old sync splitter (axis-0 assert / axis-1 bogus
tail); a reverted attempt to tighten the predicate stranded per-op ranges in a whole-tensor accumulator
and hung the rear placement.  Fix: the segmented sync splitter now splices an arbitrary
`[offset, offset+size)` write (head partial row + full rows + tail partial row), and `set_tensor_async`
forwards every segmented range to it; the accumulator and the classifier are gone.  Instrumentation
showed the 35B rear `-ncmoe 20` run never enters the segmented branch (6548 single-segment calls), while
Gemma4 `-ncmoe 8` does (`blk.22..29.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight`, `axis=1, nr0=2`); with the r63 loader guard
removed the pre-fix tree aborted 15/15 on the axis-0 assert and the fix makes it 24/24 clean.

**Block 10 -- CUDA splice-gather ring ownership.**  The pinned ring in
`ggml_backend_cuda_set_tensor_2d_async` was a function-local `static thread_local`; the loader's
non-mmap async uploader builds a temporary Meta backend (and CUDA contexts) and frees them, leaving ring
events recorded on destroyed streams, so a later decode reuse failed `hipEventSynchronize` with
`hipErrorUnknown`.  The ring is now owned by `ggml_backend_cuda_context` and freed with its streams.
Latent for the delivery (the r63 loader guard keeps the Meta device off the loader async path); fixed
so the sibling async-upload re-enable can land on top.

**Block 10 -- qwen4exp image+MTP (PR #160, martino2k6; PR merged to `main` for authorship).**  Dropped
`GGML_ASSERT(ubatch.token && "QWEN4EXP MTP requires token input")` in the `graph_mtp` constructor: mtmd
feeds the projector output as an embedding-only ubatch, and the graph's `inp->embd` else-branch already
handles it, so the assert made every image request SIGABRT with `--spec-type draft-mtp`.  Token-capable
ubatches are unchanged.

**(A) Gemma4 26B-A4B front-vs-tail residual -- proven a near-tie, accepted.**  At the first divergent
token (step 4) the candidates are ` README` and ` long`, and the top-2 margin is 0.051 / 0.020 / 0.023 /
0.261 across the four `(placement, cache)` arms, inside the ~0.1-0.2 arm-to-arm logit perturbation.
Both outputs are coherent, `-ncmoe 0` reproduces one arm, and `-sm layer` is self-consistent; this is
MoE fusion-order drift of the class the MTP methodology already accepts.  No code change.

**Gates (fresh build of the r64 tree).**  Coherence: 4B `1c5d32ac537d`, 35B `627b2ebd7792`, Gemma4
bit-identical to r63 (`0d2717074ba2` / `468a953af132`); `gate-prefill-logits.sh` PASS (0.000707 /
98.755 %); `gate-qwen4exp-quant-coherence.sh` PASS (IQ3_XXS/IQ4_NL/Q4_K_M, 0 `////`, gather ON == OFF);
adaptive-MTP `none == draft-mtp n3` bit-identical on the 35B (`-sm tensor -ncmoe 99`, `-n 3000`,
prose `9840cd63290c`, mixed `5571e0424738`); 35B `-ncmoe 20` hang loop 10/10 (`-lm auto` and `-lm none`).
See `archive/work/gemma4-drift-and-meta-async/FINDINGS-2026-10-15.md`.

## 261014.007 (r62) -- fix the `-sm tensor` + `-ncmoe` below-gate upload race (block 10)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r62` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`e909c529a`, net tree `386a6a3d4e202d46fad21f9b63ee9a4aba3fb80e`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on
a fresh tarball).  **Block 10** is amended, no new block; block 11 re-cut unchanged on top.

**Bug (correctness).**  `ggml_backend_cuda_set_tensor_2d_async`'s compact splice-gather issued its 1-D
H2D on `cuda_ctx->copy_stream()`, but the scheduler's `wait_before_overwrite()` -- a wait on the split
backend's previous-split event, needed because the graph allocator **reuses the split-input buffer
across splits** -- is enqueued on the **main** stream.  The gather only ordered the *consumer*
(`cudaStreamWaitEvent(main, s.ev)`), so the H2D could overwrite the split-input buffer while the
previous split still read it.  It corrupted the `-sm tensor` + `-ncmoe` **below-gate** path (ubatch <
`sched_stage_min_tokens`, i.e. the default `llama-cli` `-ub 512` and any `GGML_SCHED_STAGE=0`): 35B-A3B
`3333…`, gemma4 26B-A4B `<unused32>…`, Flash-Next GSQ `3333…`; `llama-perplexity` `[1]nan … [8]nan`
(`Unexpected negative standard deviation of log(prob)`).  Clean on `-sm layer`, `-ncmoe 0`,
`GGML_META_SPLIT_COPY=0` (mirrored) and `GGML_CUDA_SPLICE_GATHER=0` (plain 2-D, main stream).  The plain
2-D arm was always on the main stream, which is why only the gather was wrong.  Independent of the heat
map (`MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` and default both fail, no sidecar), the expert cache
(`MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=0` and auto both fail), `--lazy-mode` and the load mode; present in the
`build-r55-ref` tree, so it is not an r60/r61 regression.

**Fix (block 10, +12/-1).**  Use `cuda_ctx->stream()` for the gather's 1-D H2D (the pinned gather ring
and the single H2D are unchanged; only the stream moves).  The copy stream bought nothing here -- the
transfer must wait for the reused-buffer read regardless -- and the measurement agrees.

**Validation (gfx1201, 2x R9700, ROCm 7.14.1).**  35B-A3B `-sm tensor -ncmoe 20` PPL = **6.1802**,
exactly equal to `-ncmoe 0`; gemma4 `-ncmoe 20` finite (1140.85; `-sm layer` 1261.86).  Coherence
(product env, 32- and 250-token greedy) clean on 35B-A3B, gemma4 26B-A4B and Flash-Next GSQ.  Dense 4B
`Qwen3.5-Q8_0 -sm tensor` same-seed `1c5d32ac537d` (golden); `gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS**
(0.000707 / 98.755 %, identical to base); adaptive-MTP `none == n3` (`89951c23872e`) on 35B-A3B
`-sm tensor -ncmoe 99` + auto cache.  Perf-neutral (35B-A3B `-ncmoe 20 -ub 2048`: **2487.9 pp / 73.35
tg** vs plain 2-D 2495.3 / 73.36 vs mirrored 1501.5 / 21.33 -- the split still beats mirrored by +66 %
prefill / +244 % decode).  `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID`: the same 4 pre-existing upstream `f16
dup=1` fails as r53 (reproduced identically on `build-r55-ref`) and the accompanying test spin; no
regression.

**Campaign.**  Found while parking `wip/moe-layer-stagger/` (that hypothesis is refuted: with the
page-cache confound removed, four disjoint host-layer sets are identical to 0.1 % at `-ncmoe 24`;
partial-offload prefill is H2D-bound, so the upload schedule cannot matter).  The fix's record moved to
`archive/work/meta-split-copy-splice-race/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`; the stagger record stays parked
under `wip/moe-layer-stagger/`.

**Published (2026-10-14).**  The delivery repo `main` was pushed (`5ba3cc8..dc81bb8`) and the release
tagged `v12-097cf33d9-r62` (annotated, on the release commit `dc81bb8`); `release.yml` published the
GitHub Release assets (`rdna-boosts-all.patch`, `patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`), and

## 261014.006 (r61) -- the heat map can be frozen (read-only file / `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=load`) (block 09)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r61` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`7f15fb91d7eceb475045a317c45dd989ce17d928`, net tree
`047807d7b2a7aa611c0fd76c3efcaedb23a8ac78`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green).  **Block 09** is
amended, no new block; blocks 10/11 re-cut unchanged on top.

**Bug (measured).**  The r60 save path never checked the heat-map file's mode: `g_heat_write_ok` was set
but never read, and the staged write is a `tmp` + `rename`, which replaces a read-only target whenever
the *directory* is writable.  So `chmod 400 <gguf>.moe-heatmap` did **not** freeze the map: a run
overwrote it (measured sha `db3116f3...` -> `75029f30...`).  A read-only model *directory* also did not
freeze it: with a sidecar present the code relocated to a cache directory and kept learning there,
silently ignoring the curated map.

**Fix.**  The heat-map **file's** mode is now the freeze signal, with no directory-based override:

- A readable-but-not-writable sidecar is loaded and used to seed, is never overwritten, and is **not**
  relocated (no fallback).  `chmod 400 <gguf>.moe-heatmap` is therefore sufficient, and making it
  read-only while a server is running freezes it at the next flush boundary (the save re-checks
  `W_OK`).
- `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=load` (aliases `ro`, `read-only`) is the explicit in-band equivalent: load and
  seed, never write.  `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` still disables the feature entirely (no load, no write).
- The container path is unchanged: with **no** sidecar next to the model and a read-only model
  directory, the map is learned in `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DIR` / the XDG cache as before.

**Gates.**  `validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball.  Functional: read-only file (400) -> 120 tables
seeded, file sha unchanged, log *"heat map ... is read-only; loading and seeding from it, not updating
it"*; `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=load` -> 120 seeded, sha unchanged; `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP=0` -> 0 seeded, 0
loads, 0 saves.  The change is on the persistence path only (open/save); it does not touch the tally,
the seed math or any kernel, so same-seed coherence, the prefill-logit gate and the MTP field gate are
unaffected (r60 results carry).

**Published (2026-10-14).**  The delivery repo `main` was pushed (`c3b6857..92b05b0`) and the release
tagged `v12-097cf33d9-r61` (annotated, on the release commit `92b05b0`); `release.yml` published the
GitHub Release assets (`rdna-boosts-all.patch`, `patches.tar.gz`, `release.json`, `SHA256SUMS`), and
`validate.yml` is green on both the tag and `main`.  The fork's `rdna-boosts` branch was force-pushed to
the personal fork (`a3459aad -> 7f15fb91d`, `--force-with-lease`).  The ROCm container images were
rebuilt and pushed locally (`scripts/build-containers.sh --force --rocm "7.14.1 10.1" --push --prune`):
15 tags, confirmed present in the GHCR package (`latest`/`rocm-10.1` updated 15:36Z); the registry
retention prune deleted 0 versions (the previous base survives).

## 261014.005 (r60) -- the persistent cross-run MoE expert heat map (block 09)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r60` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`a3459aada97288b520504f5716c37d628f41a58d`, net tree `ec37675ec797392508e560616d320d8cc09efd86`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green on a fresh tarball, checksums + strict `git am` + tree match).  **Block 09**
is amended (no new block); blocks 10/11 are re-cut unchanged on top (their patch SHAs change with the
rebase).

The host-resident MoE expert cache now learns **which experts are hot across runs** and starts warm:

- **A device-side prefill routing tally (R2).**  `moe_cache_heat_observe` is launched from the **outer**
  `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_id` entry (the cache's slot-remap redirect re-enters that function with a stack
  `src0` whose `buffer` is null, so the outer entry is the one that still carries the graph's true raw
  ids).  This is what makes the tally cover **every** path: the identity take-over, the eager host-routing
  path, and the staged prefill that never reaches the host hook.  The decode band is tallied on the host
  instead (`moe_cache_update_host`, which already iterates the true routing), so the two feeds are
  band-disjoint, nothing is double-counted, and the decode latency path gains no launch.  Before this a
  **fully-resident** run recorded no per-expert heat at all (`takeover=1`, `hits=16`); now it produces a
  full map from the prefill tally (measured: heat total 4.9M, 27873/29952 experts nonzero, top L38
  e209 = 4554) -- and the prefill routing turned out to be an excellent proxy for the decode hot set
  (L38 e209: 4571 on a partial run vs 4554 prefill-only).
- **An on-disk sidecar** `<gguf>.moe-heatmap`, derived from the GGUF path the loader already hands the
  host pool (`moe_cache_set_host_source`), so no new loader/iface plumbing.  `MHT1` fixed-size records
  keyed by `(layer, sem_role, n_experts, host_bytes)`; a mismatch (a re-quantised model) is a cold table,
  never fatal.  Atomic staged write (`<path>.tmp.<pid>` -> `fsync` -> `rename`), debounced
  (`MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DEBOUNCE_S`, default 60 s) at the server's per-turn `moe_cache_get_stats` seam with
  a mandatory process-exit flush, and merge-on-save (a long EWMA across runs).  A non-writable model
  directory (the container case) falls back to `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DIR`, else the XDG cache.  Persistence
  failures are non-fatal and disable it for the session after `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_MAX_FAILS` (default 3).
- **A seed at sizing.**  `apply_heat_seed_locked` bulk-admits the top-`slots` experts as **provisional**
  slots (they yield to a real hot expert immediately), applied before the in-run prefill seed.
- **Heat-ordered layer placement** (the `moe-arena-defrag` campaign's phase 1): `alloc_all_locked`
  allocates layers in **descending heat**, so the hottest sit highest in VA and are the last the
  work-pool boundary reaches; the order is frozen at sizing and falls back to ascending layer when no
  heat is present.

Env (all documented in `ENVIRONMENT.md` §1.2): `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP` (**default 1**, kill switch),
`MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DIR`, `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_DEBOUNCE_S`, `MOE_EXPERT_HEATMAP_MAX_FAILS`.

**Measured (35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M, `-sm layer -ncmoe 40`, `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_MIB=4096`, 5256-token prompt,
same seed).**  The arena no longer starts cold:

| turn | run | hit rate | fills | decode t/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 48 tok | cold (no map) | 0.7674 | 11748 | 38.15 |
| 48 tok | warm (seeded) | **0.9402** | **2976** | **51.30 (+34 %)** |
| 256 tok | cold (no map) | 0.9060 | 19452 | 48.53 |
| 256 tok | warm (seeded) | **0.9561** | **6912** | **53.55 (+10.3 %)** |

Prefill is unchanged (1050 vs 1059 t/s) and the seed cost lands in the warmup/sizing phase, not the
measured turn.

**Gates.**  Same-seed coherence heat-on vs heat-off **byte-identical**; `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh`
**PASS** (mean KLD **0.000707**, same-top-p **98.755 %**, exactly the recorded base); adaptive-MTP purity
on the field config (`-sm tensor -ncmoe 99`, auto cache) `none == n3` **identical**;
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID` the same **4 pre-existing** upstream `f16 dup=1` fails as the r53
baseline (documented), no regression; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green.

**Residuals** (deliberately not promoted) are `TODO.md` #64: the `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_PREFILL_SEED`
repair / host-pool warm order, the decode-identity tally gap, and the now-dead `moe_cache_observe`.
The campaign record (decisions, the phase map, the design Q&A) moved to
`archive/work/moe-heatmap-persistence/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

**Published (2026-10-14).**  The **delivery repo** itself was pushed to `main`
(`3075e11..1091fd2`) and the release tagged `v12-097cf33d9-r60` (annotated, on the release commit
`6796a51`), which triggered `release.yml`: the GitHub Release carries `rdna-boosts-all.patch`,

## 261014.004 (r59) -- issue #139: the AR spin budget uses the wall clock, and a soft timeout keeps waiting (block 01)

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r59` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`e1b2a41ed656b6bc6b690501f0df42bd1a699269`, net tree `59b9a7faeb2c975994fabdb2cfb6761a6beda560`; 12
blocks; `validate-set.sh` green; whitespace-clean under `git am --whitespace=error-all`).  **Block 01**
(`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/allreduce-hip.cu`) is amended, **no new block**:

- **The spin budget is now wall-clock time.**  `wait_t0` and the budget check use `wall_clock64()` (a
  constant-rate realtime counter, 100 MHz on gfx12) instead of `clock64()`, and the budget is
  `GGML_CUDA_AR_SPIN_TIMEOUT_MS * hipDeviceAttributeWallClockRate` (kHz, fallback 100000) instead of
  `ms * 2e6` shader cycles.  On gfx1201 `clock64()` reads `HW_REG_SHADER_CYCLES` and steps **backwards**
  while a queue is stopped (reported: 1089107279 -> 1075226717 over 1.6 ms of wall time), so
  `(clock64() - wait_t0)` wrapped to ~2^64 and passed any budget: a slightly-late peer was treated as
  lost.  The `GGML_CUDA_AR_PROFILE` `prof_start` / `prof_spin` fields and their tick->us conversion use
  `wall_clock64()` + `hipDeviceAttributeWallClockRate` too, so the profile no longer reports bogus spin
  values.
- **A soft timeout now keeps waiting (B2).**  `GGML_CUDA_AR_SPIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (default raised 20 ms ->
  **2000 ms**) is a **soft** deadline: a peer wait that exceeds it is a late peer from a driver queue
  stop, not a lost one.  The kernel reports it once (a host-mapped `slow` flag, logged at the next
  call) and **keeps waiting**, then completes the normal phase-3 reduction, so no consumer ever sees a
  local shard.  A new **hard** cap, `GGML_CUDA_AR_SPIN_HARD_MS` (default **20000 ms**), finally sets the
  poison and falls back to the meta butterfly, preserving the last-resort bound that keeps an unbounded
  spin from making the compute queue non-removable (the MES `REMOVE_QUEUE` hazard).  `soft` 0 = no soft
  check, `hard` 0 = never poison; a hard value below the soft one is clamped up.

**Finding: the same-call butterfly re-run (B1) was implemented, measured and rejected.**  The
"preferred" fix (observe the poison in the same call and re-run that tensor through the butterfly) was
built exactly as specified: after the chunked kernels launch, wait for them, read the poison and return
`false` so the meta backend butterflies the same subgraph.  It is correct, but `AR_PROFILE` shows
**4096+ internal AR calls** (the profiler caps at 4096) over a ~69-step run on 4B, roughly **59 small
ARs per token**, so a host event sync per call destroys the host's run-ahead pipelining:

| model | B1 on | B1 off | B2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4B Q8_0 `tg128` | 89-90 t/s | 118 t/s | **117.6 t/s** |
| 27B Q4_K_XL `tg64` | 31-34 t/s | 42-43 t/s | **43.0 t/s** |

B2 has no host participation on the hot path (the poll loop is unchanged; only the timeout branch
differs), so it matches B1-off exactly.

**Gates (gfx1201, 2-3x R9700, ROCm 7.14.1, `~/llama.cpp/build-rocm-hybrid`).**  Build `all` green.
`AR_PROFILE` with the real config shows the wall clock in use (`clock 100000 kHz`), spin p50 2.5 us /
p99 115 us / **max 1.3 ms** against the 2000 ms soft budget, and **0** soft/hard warnings.  4B
`Qwen3.5-Q8_0` 3-GPU `-sm tensor` same-seed greedy **byte-identical** to r58.  `llama-bench` 2-GPU
`-sm tensor` **no regression** (table above).  `scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** (0.000707 /
98.755 %, the exact r58 values).  **Forced soft-timeout test:** with the soft budget temporarily set to
1 tick and the check decimation to 1 (so every AR soft-times-out while the hard cap stays at 20 s), the
4B `-sm tensor` greedy continuation is **byte-identical** to the no-timeout reference, and the soft
warnings fire.  `scripts/validate-set.sh` strict 12/12, tree `59b9a7fa`; whitespace-clean.

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` §6 documents the two knobs (`GGML_CUDA_AR_SPIN_TIMEOUT_MS` was previously
undocumented); `README.md`, `MANIFESTS.md`, `BASELINE.md` and `patches/README.md` current-state headers
updated.  The issue record moves to `archive/work/issue-139-ar-spin-timeout/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`.
The memory-pressure half stays tracked separately in `wip/host-expert-master-drop/` (TODO #55; promoted in
**r111** as block 12 -- now `archive/work/host-expert-master-drop/`).

**Publish (2026-10-14).**  Delivery `main` pushed (`60d8207` -> `b766960`; `validate.yml` green on
`main` and on the tag).  Fork `rdna-boosts` refreshed from the r59 tip and force-pushed to the personal
fork (`stew675/llama.cpp`): `369a835bf` -> **`e1b2a41ed`**.  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r59` pushed; the Release

- **block 02** (`common/common.cpp`): in `common_init_result`, before the target context is created,
  read the configured draft GGUF's `<arch>.target_layers` (metadata-only `gguf_init_from_file`) and call
  `llama_model_set_embeddings_layer_inp_preset()`; the preset is cleared right after

## 261014.002 (docs, tooling) -- GHCR retention: prune old container versions on every `--push`

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json` and the r57 tag are untouched; no new release).

GHCR keeps every manifest ever pushed — a multi-arch image is an index version plus one version per
architecture, and each time a moving tag advances the manifest it left behind stays as an untagged
version — so `ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts` had grown to **942 versions** (only 18 of them the
current r57 release, 876 untagged).  A second, larger package, **`llama.cpp` (4,752 versions, Jun 21 →
Aug 28, only `buildcache-*` tags)** is a defunct leftover from before the fork renaming.

**New tooling.**  `scripts/cleanup-ghcr.py` keeps a version when it is inside `--keep-days` (default 7)
**or** carries a `*-<base>` tag for a `--keep-base`; deletes the rest; dry-run by default (`--apply`
deletes, parallel via `xargs`/`gh api`).  It retries a GitHub bulk-delete throttle `--attempts` times
and then reports `deleted=… remaining=…` as a warning — it never fails the build.  It also keeps any
untagged manifest created within an hour of a kept tagged one, so a 0-day window can never orphan a
future multi-arch index's platform children (today's images are single-manifest, so it is inert).  So
`scripts/build-containers.sh` now runs it automatically on `--push` with `--keep-days 7` and
`--keep-base $(release.json .base)` (the images just pushed can never be deleted).  `--no-cleanup` opts
out, `--keep-days N` widens the window.  Requires the `delete:packages` token scope
(`gh auth refresh -h github.com -s delete:packages`).  Docs: `CONTAINERS.md` §Registry cleanup and
`AGENTS.md`.

**Applied today.**  `llama-cpp-rdna-boosts` **942 → 120 versions** (37 tags): the current base
`097cf33d9` (r57) plus the previous base `a55e952b8` (Oct 8-12) as a one-release rollback, with the
retired ROCm lines `7.2`/`7.14`/`10.0` and the old bases (`84e76d8a2`, `ebbb18522`, `d1d3c3396`,
`790cf51aa`, `9113cc188`) gone.  The defunct `llama.cpp` package went 4,752 → 577 before GitHub's
secondary bulk-delete limit throttled it; a single `gh api -X DELETE /user/packages/container/llama.cpp`
finishes it when the limit clears, and the delivery package's remaining excess falls out of the rolling
window on the next release's `--push`.

## 261014.001 (r57) -- the `-Wshadow` cleanup was clang-only: scope it to the dangerous class on GCC, fix the two GCC-only sites, and re-confirm the container ccache

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v12-097cf33d9-r57` (base `097cf33d9`; canonical tip
`a300075f7`, net tree `8a56fb31267ecc523c423845662d76571f934a51`; 12 blocks; `validate-set.sh` green).
Three blocks amended, **no new block**:

- **block 00** (`src/CMakeLists.txt`): the `-Wshadow` added in r55 to the `llama` C++ target is now
  `-Wshadow=local` for GNU and plain `-Wshadow` for clang.  GCC's `-Wshadow` is a strict superset of
  clang's: it also reports "declaration shadows a member" (the ubiquitous `Foo(int x) : x(x) {}`
  constructor idiom) and "hides constructor".  `-Wshadow=local` keeps the class the campaign was
  created for (a local shadowing a local) and drops the member/global output; clang has no `=local`
  form.
- **block 09** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp`): the AMX buffer type's designated initializer now
  lists `get_compute_margin_pct` / `alloc_buffer_usage` / `get_compute_chunk_bytes`, which block 09
  appended to `ggml_backend_buffer_type_i` (block 11 already fixed the sibling `repack.cpp`;
  `-Wmissing-field-initializers` from `-Wextra`).
- **block 10** (`src/llama-lazy-reader.cpp`): `GGML_ASSERT(slot >= 0 && slot < n_slots)` drops the
  always-true `>= 0` half (`slot` is `size_t`; GCC `-Wtype-limits`).

**Also fixed (pre-existing):** block 09's `mmvq.cu` insertion ended with a blank line that block 10
removed, so the strict `git am` emitted `new blank line at EOF` on every r56/r57 apply.  Block 09 no
longer adds the blank and block 10 no longer removes it; the net tree is unchanged and the set now
applies with `git am --whitespace=error-all` clean (re-cut tip `a300075f7`).

**Finding: why r56's container log had 24,178 `-Wshadow` warnings.**  The local gate build forces clang
(`~/bin/build-llama-rocm-714` passes `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++`), but the
container leaves CMake to pick the image default, which is **GCC 13.3** (`The CXX compiler
identification is GNU 13.3.0`).  So the r55 cleanup (0 `-Wshadow` on clang) never saw GCC's wider set.
The 24,178 lines collapse to **815 unique sites in 197 files**: 24,062 "shadows a member", 76 "hides
constructor", and only 10 non-member sites (lambda-parameter / lambda-body shadows in
`llama-model.cpp`, `llama-moe-cache.cpp`, `llama-quant.cpp`, `llama-vocab.cpp`, `step35.cpp`), which
clang only reports under `-Wshadow-all`.  Every one is upstream idiom; there is **no remaining clang
`-Wshadow` site**.  Extractor: `/tmp/shadow-report.sh` (collapses the per-TU repeats).

**Finding: the container ccache is correct; the log's ~50 % was a cumulative counter.**  The r56 log's
`ccache -s` reads like a per-build miss rate, but the cache store outlives a release, so it is a
*lifetime* average; `ccache -z` before a build settles it: a **no-change container rebuild measures
844 calls / 843 hits (99.88 %) / 1 miss**, ~2 min.  `full`/`light`/`server` already share the one
`build` stage (the r56 log has exactly **2** cmake builds and 358 HIP objects per line, not 3x).  The
~30 min/line a release pays is the genuine recompile when a **common HIP header** changes: r56 touched
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/hip.h`, which every HIP TU includes, so all 358 `.cu` objects (x5 arches)
missed on both lines.  r57 touches no HIP header, so its container build is HIP-half hits + the
`llama` C++ relink.  The Dockerfile now runs `ccache -z` before the build so each image's log reports
its own rate.

**Gates.**  Build `all` green (clang, **0** warnings).  4B `Qwen3.5-Q8_0` 3-GPU same-seed greedy
**byte-identical to r56**.  `validate-set.sh` strict 12/12, tree `8a56fb31`.  The GCC-side fix is
verified by the r57 container build itself (a clean `[7.14.1/full]` log with 0 `-Wshadow` from the
`llama` target).

**Publish (2026-10-14).**  Delivery `main` pushed (`c523184`, force-with-lease once to land the
whitespace-clean re-cut; `validate.yml` green).  Fork `rdna-boosts` refreshed from a clean `097cf33d9`
checkout via `apply-all.sh` (strict, tree `8a56fb31267ecc523c423845662d76571f934a51`) and force-pushed:
`3cf0bd8ae` -> **`37549516d`**.  Tag `v12-097cf33d9-r57` pushed; the Release workflow attached the four
assets (run 38548369525, 15 s).

Container images built and pushed locally (`scripts/build-containers.sh --rocm "7.14.1 10.1" --push
--prune`): **15** GHCR tags, whole run **~7 min** for both lines (r56 was ~1 h).  With `ccache -z` the
per-build rates are visible: **7.14.1 798/844 hits (94.55 %, only the 46 `llama`-target TUs the
`-Wshadow` flag change invalidated)** and **10.1 844/844 (100 %)**; the whole r57 log has **0**
`-Wshadow` / `-Wmissing-field-initializers` / `-Wtype-limits` warnings.  The contrast with r56 is the
point: r56 changed `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/hip.h`, which every HIP TU includes, so all 358 `.cu`
objects (x5 arches) legitimately recompiled on both lines.  **ccache was never misconfigured** — the old
`ccache -s` was a *lifetime* counter (a ~50 % average over many releases) that read like a per-build
miss; a no-change container rebuild measures 843/844 hits.  A release that avoids a ubiquitous HIP
header is ~1 min/line; one that touches `hip.h`/`common.cuh` is ~30 min/line.

## 261013.006 (docs, campaign closure) -- close `moe-topk-fusion`: the fused router already fires at prefill widths on r55 (no code change)

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` untouched; no release).
TODO item **5(a)** ("MoE topk fusion adoption") is **dropped**, and `wip/moe-topk-fusion/` moves to
`archive/work/moe-topk-fusion/` with a `RESOLUTION.md`.

The campaign proposed pinning the MoE router logits (`ggml_set_output`) so the fused `topk_moe` router
could fire at prefill widths, where the address-overlap guard (`ggml_cuda_check_fusion_memory_ranges`,
`is_topk_moe`) was refusing it because the norm output aliased the just-freed `ffn_moe_logits` buffer
(~0.5 % prefill), at the cost of ~188 MB.  Two things settle it:

1. **The numerics fork is gone** (2026-09-13, item 19 / `GREEDY-PURITY.md` §31): the fused router is
   bit-identical to the generic chain it elides.
2. **The alias does not occur on r55.**  Instrumented r55 and read the guard outcome directly: the
   fusion fires at every width and **zero** refusals appear, on **both** the maintainer's devices:
   - **gfx1201 (3x R9700)**, Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS: fires at `n_tokens = 2048`; pin on/off identical;
     pp2048 **1575.7 vs 1563.8 t/s** with `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_TOPK_MOE_FUSION=1`.
   - **gfx1151 (Strix Halo, the discovery's own device)**, Flash-Next IQ4_NL (`-b 2048 -ub 2048
     -c 16384`): fires at `n_tokens = 1, 2, 4, 42, 1160, 2044, 2048`; `LLAMA_MOE_TOPK_PIN_LOGITS=1`
     gives a byte-identical fired set; pp2048 **1030.1 vs 1018.0 t/s**.

   The mechanism is unchanged (`TOPK_MOE_ROWS_PER_BLOCK = 8`); the r48-era allocation plan that produced
   the reuse changed during r51-r55.  Nothing was promoted, and no release was cut.

**Artefacts.**  `archive/work/moe-topk-fusion/{README.md,RESOLUTION.md,topk-moe-diagnostics.patch}`
(the temporary trace + env-gated pin used for the investigation, reverted from both `~/llama.cpp`
checkouts); `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` and `TODO.md` updated.

regenerated `patches/` and `release.json`.

- **TODO #15 (`wip/wshadow-cleanup` -> `archive/work/wshadow-cleanup/`) -> block 00.**  All **139**
  `-Wshadow` sites in `src/` fixed (46 "shadows a local variable", 92 "shadows a field", 1 "modifies
  constructor parameter that shadows a field"): the shadowing declarations were renamed (`_l`) across
  35 files, and `-Wshadow` is now enabled on the `llama` C++ target (`src/CMakeLists.txt`, gated on
  `LLAMA_ALL_WARNINGS`).  **138/139 sites are upstream base code**, so they land in block 00 ("prepare
  the upstream base"); the one feature-introduced site (`llama-kv-cache.cpp`
  `const int64_t n_stream = cell_pos->ne[1];`, block 05) lands in block 05.  The cleanup caught two
  real upstream bugs: a **duplicated nested `seq_id` loop** in `llama-batch.cpp` (collapsed), and
  `llama-memory-recurrent.cpp`'s `n_rs_seq = 0;` zeroing the constructor *parameter* instead of the
  *member*, so an empty memory module never actually disabled rollback snapshots -- fixed to
  `this->n_rs_seq = 0;`.
- **block 05 `swizzle_bytes` fix.**  Upstream `2ca15f540` (#29612) renamed `swizzle_bytes` to
  `swizzle` *before* the base, but block 05 re-introduced 3 calls.  On AMD they sit in a discarded
  `if constexpr` (compiled via the C++20 extension); on the swizzled NVIDIA path they would have
  failed to instantiate.  The three sites now use the current `swizzle<stride_tile>(tile_KV, ...)`
  (identical to the base), which also removes the `-Wc++20-extensions` warnings.  AMD never swizzles
  (`ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_swizzled()` requires `TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE`), so the change is
  performance-neutral on AMD.

  `calc_rows_per_block_weight` for `q5_1`/`iq4_xs` at n=2..8 (gfx1201, m=4096 k=14336): `q5_1` **one row
  is 6.6-7.1 % faster at n=2..4** while two rows stay ahead from n=5 (up to +16 % at n=8), so the rule
  is now width-dependent (`ncols_dst <= 4 ? 1 : 2`); `iq4_xs` showed **no win** (the campaign's dip did
  not reproduce) and is unchanged.

  r38 3-GPU MTP deficit is gone on r54: 3-GPU MTP **74.3 t/s** vs 3-GPU plain **55.2** (**+34.6 %**)

that own their concerns; the third was closed as a measured no-go; the fourth (host-expert master
drop) is deferred to its own session.  The fork chain was rebuilt with `git rebase -i --autosquash`
(the two fixups amended blocks 09 and 11, no message change), then `make-patches.sh` / `make-release.sh`
regenerated `patches/` and `release.json`.

- **TODO #58 (`wip/dflash-meta-split` -> `archive/work/dflash-meta-split/`) -> block 11.**  The DFlash2
  `-sm tensor` abort was root-caused: the selector (`src/models/dflash.cpp:538`, called at `:888`) runs
  `ggml_top_k` over the draft logits, which `-sm tensor` vocab-splits (axis 0), and the Meta per-row
  handler (`ggml-backend-meta.cpp:707`) cannot reduce across a split axis.  `src/llama.cpp` now rejects
  a DFlash2 drafter with a selector under `-sm tensor` with a clean `use -sm layer` message (was a
  SIGABRT at load).  The real fix (a Meta distributed top-k / split-to-mirrored gather) is re-seeded as
  `wip/dflash-meta-split-impl/`.
- **Segmented host-resident expert upload (`wip/meta-segmented-expert-upload` ->
  `archive/work/meta-segmented-expert-upload/`) -> block 09.**  `ggml_backend_meta_set_tensor_async`'s
  whole-tensor accumulate fallback (PR #22466, for the loader's chunked upload) **silently dropped**
  the scheduler's partial per-op upload of a pruned `ffn_gate_up_exps` group; the sync segmented setter
  then asserted on the `copy_experts` `min(expert_size,512)` MMQ tail pad.  The fix: zero-size uploads
  are a no-op, row-aligned segmented ranges go to the sync setter (tail pad placed flat per device),
  and mid-row loader chunks still accumulate.  The gemma4 host-expert `-sm tensor` rejection (and its
  helper) is removed, so gemma4 MoE + `-ncmoe`/`-cmoe` + `-sm tensor` now loads and generates.  **Known
  cost:** the synchronous per-op segmented upload puts that config at ~9 t/s; the async/per-row-1-D-set
  optimization is re-seeded as `wip/meta-segmented-upload-async/` (the config was previously rejected,
  so no working config regresses).
- **`ssm_alpha` + `ssm_beta` fusion (item 5(b), `archive/work/ssm-alpha-beta-fusion/`): CLOSED.**
  Re-measured on r53/gfx1201 (1.43x on the pair at N=8192, bit-identical here) but only ~0.3-0.6 %
  prefill and the two MMs remain non-adjacent in the DFS graph; below the adoption bar.

## 261013.001 (r51) -- V2.0: the 16-block set re-cut as a 12-block set (block-boundary re-org + self-contained refactor)

**Delivery change: `release.json` now names a 12-block set at base `097cf33d9`, release
`v12-097cf33d9-r51`, net tree `48cf3e8107a3e58e3bc5c10a9b5087f73a88d1f1` (the previous release was the
16-block `v16-097cf33d9-r50`, tree `f102245dfb116f02f6b3f572df7fb413a5c65cf8`).**  The applied tree is
**behaviour-preserving but not tree-identical**: Phase 1 redistributed each concern into its owning
block, and Phase 2 moved each concern into a self-contained function/file so a future upstream re-base
collides with a small call point rather than a rewritten shared function.  All same-seed gates are
byte-identical to r50.

**The 12 blocks.**  `v12` is a clean break in numbering:

| # | subject | concern |
|---|---|---|
| 00 | foundation | band-uniformity, Meta-wrapper, allocator fixes (old-00 + old-05 + old-07 + old-09a + the old-06 readback + old-15 W4) |
| 01 | hybrid HIP all-reduce (RDNA4-gated) | old-12 |
| 02 | adaptive MTP draft depth | old-01 |
| 03 | chunked gated-delta-net prefill | old-02 |
| 04 | BF16 KV cache + native-BF16 FA | old-03 |
| 05 | FA band / native quantized K-V / derived kq mask | old-04 FA + old-15 FA |

## 261011.017 (r49) -- mmap host-memory reclaim (block 06) + Q1_0 perm port and `cpy-batch` idiom (block 15); three campaigns promoted

**Delivery change.**  `release.json` is now `v16-a55e952b8-r49` (base `a55e952b8`, canonical tip
`f0a74f4cc`, net tree `45ba5da24f872c5f9aa1b70b85470b5eb4d98395`; `validate-set.sh` green, 16/16 strict
`git am`).  Three `wip/` campaigns were promoted and their records moved to `archive/work/` with
resolution banners (no stubs): `host-memory-reclaim/` -> **block 06**, `q1-0-byte-perm/` and
`gdn-conv-device-idiom/` -> **block 15**.  `TODO.md` #54 and #32 are closed.

**Block 06 -- the mmap host-memory reclaim.**  The loader used to fault the whole model file in up front
(`MAP_POPULATE` / `POSIX_MADV_WILLNEED` with `prefetch = -1`) and unmapped it only at the end of the
load, so a `-ncmoe` load held the full model mapping **and** the pinned `ROCm_Host` expert master at the
same time.  The reclaim skips the up-front full-file prefetch (`init_mappings`) and unmaps each tensor's
mapping range right after `ggml_backend_tensor_set` copies it to its device buffer (`load_all_data`).
The **exact** mmap-backed ranges (host-pointer / `buffer_from_host_ptr` buffers) are recorded before any
load (`mark_mmap_used`, called from `llama_model_base::load_tensors`), so the release never touches a
range a host-pointer tensor points into: a tied embedding (`token_embd` == `output`) is loaded twice
from the same range (once mmap-backed, once copied to a device), and unmapping it left the host copy
dangling (SIGSEGV in a CPU `GET_ROWS`).  The end-of-load cleanup now unmaps the exact **complement** of
those ranges, and `unmap_fragment` is idempotent (it munmaps only the still-mapped intersections, so a
per-tensor release and the final cleanup cannot double-unmap).  `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` is **not**
usable here: the ROCm runtime re-faults those pages on the next pageable H2D copy (reproduced in
isolation), so the range is munmapped.  `LLAMA_LOAD_RELEASE_MMAP=0` restores the pre-r49 behaviour; the
release is skipped under `--load-mode mlock`/`--mlock`, `--check-tensors` and lazy tensors.
`mmaps_used` changed from a per-file min/max pair to a list of exact ranges.

Measured (gfx1201, 2x R9700, `llama-bench -p 16 -n 0`), peak `VmRSS` / `RssFile`, reclaim off -> on:

| model | config | off | on |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-IQ4_NL (100 GB, 176.9B A3B) | `-ncmoe 40` | 122.5 / 68.2 GiB | **55.4 / 0.7 GiB** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M | `-ncmoe 40` | 40.7 / 21.8 GiB | **19.8 / 0.6 GiB** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M | `-ncmoe 0` | 22.0 / 21.8 GiB | **0.67 / 0.40 GiB** |

The on peak equals `--load-mode none` (55.8 GiB / 0.26 GiB) on the 100 GB model, so the host-memory
reason the field preferred `--load-mode none` is gone.  Warm-load cost ~1 s (this model), ~1.2 s (warm
35B).  Same-seed and `-sm tensor` coherence r48 == r49 byte-identical; the 35B `--spec-type draft-mtp`
`-n 2000` text is r48 == r49 byte-identical (175.2 vs 174.9 t/s).

**Finding (not fixed here): `--host-experts pool` does not reduce host RSS.**  It keeps the full pinned
`ROCm_Host` master (the source logs *"Phase 2b; full pinned master kept"*); measured `RssShmem` is
identical with and without the pool (18.7 GiB on 35B-A3B `-ncmoe 40`; 54.1 GiB on Flash-Next IQ4_NL
`-ncmoe 40`).  The r49 peak is therefore dominated by that master.  Re-seeded as the separate campaign
`wip/host-expert-master-drop/` (`TODO #55`, promoted in **r111**: `archive/work/host-expert-master-drop/`);
it is the strongest lever for issue #139.  `ENVIRONMENT.md`
§1.2.1 now says so.

**Block 15 -- Q1_0 `__byte_perm` -> `v_perm_b32` (TODO #54).**  New `ggml_cuda_byte_perm(x, y, s)` (HIP:
expand the four selector nibbles to selector bytes and use `__builtin_amdgcn_perm`; otherwise
`__byte_perm`) replaces HIP's private-memory `__byte_perm` at all 24 Q1_0 sites in
`vec_dot_q1_0_q8_1` and `ggml_cuda_mmq_load_tiles_q1_0`.  Bit-identical: exact over 16.7M randomized
GPU cases (0 mismatches; selectors with bit 3 and high bits exercised) and
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT -b ROCm0` **1304/1304** with every `q1_0` width.  No Q1_0 model locally, so
no speed claim.  Upstream candidate `upstream/UPSTREAM-PR-q1-0-amd-perm.*` (applies clean to `a55e952b8`).

**Block 15 -- `cpy-batch.cu` device idiom (TODO #32).**  `ggml_cuda_cpy_batch` now asks
`ggml_cuda_get_device()` like `gdn-conv.cu` instead of `ctx.device`; a no-op on the current graph (the
device is set before `ggml_cuda_try_fuse` runs).

**Validation (r49, gfx1201).**  `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (fresh-tarball strict apply and tree
match).  Prefill-logit KLD gate: mean KLD **0.000707** / same-top-p **98.755 %** (limit 0.005 / 98 %).
`MUL_MAT_ID` **931/931**; q1_0 `MUL_MAT` **1304/1304**.  4B `-sm tensor` coherence r48 == r49
byte-identical.  35B-A3B `--spec-type draft-mtp -n 2000 --reasoning off` text r48 == r49 byte-identical.

**Issue #139 (contribution, @briansp2020).**  His field report: the amdgpu driver stops all of a
process's GPU queues whenever the kernel migrates/reclaims a `hipHostMalloc`/`hipHostRegister` page, and
a stop over the AR spin budget leaves a timed-out call unreduced.  The r49 reclaim gives back up to
~67 GiB of mmap on the 100 GB model, which should lower overall memory pressure (and thus the queue
stops) even though the pinned master is unchanged.  A reply was posted on the issue asking him to
exercise r49 and report whether the stops/timeouts drop.

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `LLAMA_LOAD_RELEASE_MMAP` (§4) and a pool-does-not-reduce-RSS note
(§1.2.1); `TODO.md` current state -> r49, #54/#32 closed, #55 added; `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` rows updated
(promoted rows removed, `host-expert-master-drop/` added); `patches/README.md` current-release blockquote
and a dated r49 amendment; `upstream/README.md` row + `.md`/`.patch`; the three campaign records under
`archive/work/`.

**`fingon` validation (gfx1100, 30.5 GiB RAM, single RX 7900 XTX).**  The 35B-A3B Q4_K_M `-ncmoe 40`
case, same r49 binary, reclaim on vs off (`memwatch.sh`, 2 s samples):

| arm | peak `VmRSS` | peak `RssFile` | `RssShmem` | swap | wall | pp256 `avg_ts` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| on (r49 default) | 19.6 GiB | 0.33 GiB | 18.7 GiB | 0 | 19 s | 363.2 |
| off (`LLAMA_LOAD_RELEASE_MMAP=0`) | 29.5 GiB | 21.8 GiB | 18.7 GiB | 111 MiB | 25 s | 351.5 |

The legacy arm reaches the 30.5 GiB box limit, starts swapping and churns page cache (kswapd); the r49
arm stays at ~19.6 GiB with no swap, so the reclaim both fits the box and is faster there.  This is the
seed phenomenon from the archived `host-memory-footprint` campaign, fixed.

**Tagging.**  Container images and the `rdna-boosts` fork-branch refresh are the remaining release steps,
per the Pushing policy.

## 261011.016 (docs, campaign closure) -- close `strata-amd-kernels` as refuted; seed `q1-0-byte-perm` (#54)

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` untouched; `~/llama.cpp` tree clean).
The maintainer's call on the `strata-amd-kernels` (TODO #35) review: *"Close as refuted"*, don't keep the THP
probes (*"no point adding something that provides no benefit"*), and re-seed the one residual as a new campaign.

**K0 — full source diff against Strata's AMD decode kernels (r48).**  Six candidates, classified:

- **`#262` packed byte ops — already delivered.**  Strata's `#262` (`__byte_perm` → `v_perm_b32`; SWAR
  `__vsub4`/`__vsubss4`/`__vcmpne4`; Strata `87fbc000`, `600d7307`) is already in our tree from two sources:
  upstream base `a55e952b8` ships the AMD `__builtin_amdgcn_perm` arm in `vecdotq.cuh::get_int_from_table_16`
  and `vec_dot_q2_0_q8_1`, and the SWAR packed-byte helpers in `vendors/hip.h`; our blocks add
  `apply_ksigns` (`vecdotq.cuh:119`) and `mmb.cu`'s `mmb_pack2`/`mmb_pack2_so`.
- **`router_top10` — no delta.**  Our MoE router is upstream's fused `topk_moe_cuda`: warp-shuffle, float,
  no FP64 and no per-selection barrier.  Strata's win was removing *their* serial FP64/barrier router.
- **`fused_gr` LDS carveout — RDNA-inapplicable.**  Strata only added a `hip_compat` `#define`; AMD LDS is
  dedicated, so `hipFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout` is an ignored hint.
- **arena THP — the one survivor; measured and refuted (K1).**  The pinned host arena *is* a host-side
  gap: ROCr backs `hipHostMalloc`/`cudaHostAlloc` with a **shmem** mapping and, with this host's
  `shmem_enabled=never`, it lands on **4 KiB pages** (`ShmemPmdMapped 0` of 4 GiB); `MADV_COLLAPSE`
  collapses it to 100 % 2 MiB.  But the GPU never sees it: a bench reading the same buffer over UVA gives
  **identical** bandwidth with the buffer 4 KiB-backed vs 100 % 2 MiB-backed (sequential 2048 MiB =
  **13.49 GiB/s both**; random-page scatter 1024 MiB = **0.85 GiB/s both**; `PmdMapped` verified 0 % vs
  100 % per run).  The amdgpu GMMU page tables for a KFD userptr mapping are built at registration (ROCr
  pins inside `hipHostMalloc`), so a later host-side collapse cannot change what the GPU walks.
- **`#646` IQ-grid staging — no actionable delta.**  Strata's finding is that *staging* the IQ grids is
  slower for the single-matrix mmvq; we never stage them (`static const __device__` grids, `ggml-common.h:493`).
- **`verify` zero-doorbell / sub-warp packing — not a kernel candidate.**  `cfd3b722` is a CUDA commit in
  Strata's own host↔GPU window protocol; our blocks 11/06/13 solve it independently.

**Closed as refuted.**  `wip/strata-amd-kernels/` moved to `archive/work/strata-amd-kernels/` (resolution
banner; the two probes were discarded, their method and numbers recorded in the archive), the `wip/` entry
deleted with no stub, `TODO #35` removed, and `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` updated.  Nothing was ported; no delivery
change.  The only residual — `Q1_0` still calling HIP's private-memory `__byte_perm`
(`vecdotq.cuh:833-844`, `mmq-load-tiles.cuh:50-61`) while every other i-quant lookup uses
`__builtin_amdgcn_perm` — was **re-seeded as the new campaign `wip/q1-0-byte-perm/` (TODO #54): small,
mechanical, bit-identical by construction, no speed claim (no Q1_0 model locally; the gate is the
`test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` CPU oracle), and `upstream/`-shaped.**

## 261011.013 (containers) -- r48 images built+pushed locally; ccache added to the image build

**No delivery change** (`patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch` untouched).  Follow-up to
`261011.008`/`261011.009`: the first full local release-container build, plus the compiler cache the
host build has used since `260918.007`.

**r48 images.**  `scripts/build-containers.sh --rocm "7.14.1 10.1" --push` built and pushed all **15
tags** from the canonical r48 tree: `server-/light-/full-rocm-<7.14.1|10.1>` (plus the immutable
`-a55e952b8` variants), `rocm-7.14.1`, `rocm-10.1`, and `latest` (now 10.1).  GHCR carries the
7.14.1/10.1 lines; the old `rocm-7.14`/`rocm-10.0` images are stale and are not rebuilt.

**Measured (16 cores; `gfx1100;gfx1150;gfx1151;gfx1200;gfx1201`; pre-ccache).**  Per-target wall times:
`7.14.1/full` **34m33s**, `10.1/full` **31m17s**; `light`/`server` reuse the shared `build` stage in
4-12 s each.  Total wall for both lines including pushes: **~72 min** (the tag-push CI matrix needed
~5 h and repeatedly hit its 6 h timeout).

**ccache in the image build.**  `.devops/rdna-rocm.Dockerfile` now installs the upstream static ccache
**4.12.3** (the host-validated version, not Ubuntu's older package), sets `CCACHE_DIR=/root/.ccache` +
`CCACHE_MAXSIZE=20G`, adds `-DCMAKE_{HIP,C,CXX}_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache` mirroring
`~/bin/build-llama-rocm-714`, and mounts `/root/.ccache` as a build cache-mount (never an image layer,
so the published images are unchanged).  Measured single-arch (`gfx1201`, `light`): cold compile
**10m01s** -> `--no-cache` rebuild replayed from cache in **1m28s**, 835/836 direct hits.  The cache
persists across builds; `podman system prune` clears it.  A release whose sources mostly match the
previous one therefore recompiles only the delta.

**Cleanup policy.**  `scripts/build-containers.sh --push --prune` removes the locally built images and
dangling build layers after a successful push, **keeping the ROCm base images and the ccache store**
(do not re-pull the ~20 GB base images every release).  A bare `podman system prune -a` is the wrong
tool here.
