## 261011.008 (docs, local containers) -- release containers are built and pushed locally; WORKLOG adopts YYMMDD.VVV dated headers

**No release.**  The delivery (`patches/`, `release.json`, `rdna-boosts-all.patch`) is untouched.

**What changed.**  The ROCm container images are now built and pushed from the maintainer's box by
`scripts/build-containers.sh` instead of by the tag-driven GitHub Actions matrix.  The CI job took
~5 h for two ROCm lines and a failed/timed-out run wrote no registry cache, so every retry started
cold; the local build is minutes-to-tens-of-minutes and fails with a usable log.

- `scripts/build-containers.sh` reads `release.json`, materialises the canonical patched tree
  (`release.json.tip`, asserting `tree`), writes the build-context `.dockerignore`
  (`.devops/dockerignore`), builds `full`/`light`/`server` per ROCm line with the CI matrix's build
  args and tags, and (`--push`) pushes to `ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (new) keeps the cheap tag-triggered GitHub Release (patch set +
  `SHA256SUMS`, ~1 min); `.github/workflows/docker-ghcr.yml` is now a manual `workflow_dispatch`
  fallback only (no tag/schedule trigger).  `validate.yml` is unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the local image build as part of tagging a release; `CONTAINERS.md` is
  rewritten for the local path.

**WORKLOG date format.**  Dated headers now use `YYMMDD.VVV` (e.g. `261011.005 (r47)`), where `VVV` is
a per-local-date, monotonically increasing 3-digit sequence number in file order.  The date is *only*
a date -- it is not a version; the revision is the explicit `(rNN)` tag.  This replaces the old
`YYYY-MM-DD` headers, several of which had drifted into the future (entries labelled
`2026-10-12`..`2026-10-17`); those nine were reconciled to the real release dates from the delivery
repo's commit history (`r41`/`r42` -> 2026-10-10, `r43`..`r48` and the beta entry -> 2026-10-11).

**Known caveat (not guessed).**  The early a55e952b8 block still has dates that do not reconcile:
`r1`-`r8` are dated `2026-10-05` while `r9`-`r11` (later revisions) are dated `2026-10-04`, and the
fork holds no per-revision release commits for `r1`-`r39`, so their true dates cannot be derived from
the available history.  They are left as recorded and flagged for a separate audit.

## 261011.007 (beta) -- issue #138: FA prefill staging arena preallocation candidate in `beta/`

**No release.  The delivery is untouched** (`patches/`, `release.json` and `rdna-boosts-all.patch`
unchanged).  This records a beta candidate only.

**The issue (issue #138, @DanoPTT).**  The per-stream F16 FA prefill staging arena
(`fattn_stage_try_get`, block 15) grows in 1.25x steps by allocating the new arena and then
`cudaFree`-ing the old one.  On Windows/WDDM a freed allocation stays committed against the process, so
a 119k-token q8_0 prefill leaves ~2.65 GiB dead VRAM (final arena ~530 MiB, cumulative ladder ~5x),
and a near-limit card then spills to shared memory (pp 793 -> 255 t/s, MTP acceptance 65% -> 41%).  On
Linux/KFD the freed steps are returned and reused, so the symptom does not reproduce; the reporter
re-verified the code path on r47, and it is byte-identical in r48 (block 15 unchanged r47 -> r48).

**The candidate (`beta/fa-stage-prealloc/`).**  Patch sha256
`f1a0f0b1c87dc77e6bce796af94b63262c109dce5a8a93d09685d262137d7f2a`, cut against the r48 tree
`3b9f403544169544f312bd24e4de31a554bf189d`, applied tree
`24fdc3c7f641e7b37a0d4b0a6d4024622bde94ce`; `git apply` and `git am` clean on a fresh
`apply-all.sh` checkout.  This is the reporter's fix adapted to r48 (Option A): `launch_fattn` passes
the F16 size of the K/V view roots as a hint (per-operand capped by `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_MAX_MB`; an
unbounded cap passes no hint) and the arena allocates it once.  The hint is tried only while
`optional_alloc_within_free_cap` allows it (the r39 G4 slab guard) and falls back to the existing
growth step on a refusal or a `cudaMalloc` failure, so an oversized hint cannot cost more than the
pre-change path.  `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_PREALLOC=0` restores the ladder (A/B / bisect).

**Validation on Linux (gfx1201, ROCm 7.14, r48 + patch, `build-rocm-hybrid` at `0fb51947d`).**  Golden
coherence (f16 KV, 3-GPU `-sm tensor`) `1c5d32ac537d` unchanged; q8_0-KV coherence A/B (31k prompt,
`PREALLOC=0` vs default) byte-identical (`ab8e156cca11`); arena A/B by prefill-logit KLD (4B, q8_0 KV,
ctx 16384, 16 chunks, `--ab PREALLOC=0`) mean KLD **0.000000** / same-top-p **99.997%**; the standard
prefill-logit gate (27B Q8_0, f16 KV) PASS at mean KLD **0.000707** / **98.755%**, unchanged from base;
pp16384 A/B on 27B Q5_K_M with q8_0 KV **1108.94 ± 0.92** (ladder) vs **1108.03 ± 0.61** (prealloc)
t/s, within noise; `GGML_CUDA_FA_STAGE_MAX_MB=0`, `PREALLOC=0` and `MAX_MB=1` all produce identical
greedy output.  The reporter's Windows symptom cannot be reproduced on Linux by construction, so the
next step is their re-test with `beta/fa-stage-prealloc/BETA-TESTING.md`; a confirmation then decides
the owning block and the fold.

**`beta/` is reintroduced.**  It was removed in 2026-09-25 (r8) after `mmb-general` was integrated
(`8ea6151`).  The directory is the external-validation holding area for promotion candidates that
cannot sit in `wip/` because they edit a file a block owns: one sub-directory per candidate with a
`README.md`, a `BETA-TESTING.md` and a patch cut against the current tree, never applied by
`apply-all.sh`.  `beta/README.md` records the conventions; the `AGENTS.md` layout row and the WIP rule
are updated to match.

## 261011.006 (r48) -- fix the `--load-mode none` + `-sm tensor` startup GPU fault (issue #137); close the #38 tracker

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r48`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`0bc12586413e7fe4547916dc3ed43453b3eb09b8`, net tree
`3b9f403544169544f312bd24e4de31a554bf189d`); **16 blocks** (00-15); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).  The fix folds into **block 06** (the
loader + Meta-wrapper owner, and the first block that touches either file); block 15 no longer touches
`meta_set_tensor_async`, so its old `TODO #43` tail hunk is subsumed.

**The bug (issue #137).**  On 2x R9700 gfx1201, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_NL with
`-sm tensor -ncmoe 48 --load-mode none --lazy-mode off --fit off` + MTP n3, the load died roughly 1 run
in 10 with `Memory access fault ... Page not present or supervisor privilege`.  The kernel journal is
unambiguous about the client: `amdgpu ... [gfxhub] page fault ... Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd)`,
walking a pageable heap address.  The copy engine DMA-read pageable anonymous host memory.

**Root cause.**  Under `-sm tensor` the device weights live in the **Meta** buffer, and the Meta device's
capabilities are placeholders (`host_buffer = false`, `events = false`, `// TODO replace placeholders`)
ANDed with the simple devices, so they can never be true.  `llama_model_loader::upload_backend` then
never engaged (`D load_all_data: device Meta() does not support async, host buffers or events`), and the
loader fell back to a pageable `std::vector<no_init<uint8_t>> read_buf` with a raw async H2D from it.
`--load-mode auto`/`mmap` sources from the file-backed mapping (stable page cache) and `-sm layer` uses
per-device buffers with a real `upload_backend`, which is why both were stable and only
`--load-mode none` + `-sm tensor` faulted.

**The fix (block 06).**  Adapted from upstream **PR #22466** ("ggml-backend-meta : async pinned upload
for `-sm tensor` model load"; open and mergeable upstream, unmerged since 2026-09-04, and **not** among
the 183 upstream commits since our base).  The Meta device now reports `host_buffer`/`events` (ANDed with
the simple devices), proxies the device event iface (`event_new`/`free`/`synchronize`) and the backend
`event_record`/`event_wait` to each simple backend, and `ggml_backend_meta_set_tensor_async` handles the
loader's chunked ranges (partial head/tail rows) and multi-segment/partial layouts (an accumulator that
delegates to the synchronous segmented handler).  That subsumes the previous `TODO #43` per-device tail
guard.  Delivery-specific addition: because the delivery made `ROCm_Host` **per device**,
`ggml_backend_dev_host_buffer_type(Meta)` is null, so `upload_backend` now falls back to a real device's
pinned host buft for its staging ring.  (Loosening `get_host_buffer_type` instead was tried and rejected:
it leaks into `make_cpu_buft_list` and moves the 27.8 GiB PLE into pinned `ROCm_Host`, restoring the
whole-model 92.6 GiB pin.)

**Validation (gfx1201).**  The loader logs `using async uploads for device Meta(), buffer type Meta(),
backend Meta(ROCm0,ROCm1)`; the buffer layout is unchanged (`CPU 27806.97`, `Meta() 1789.79`,
`ROCm_Host 64800.00` MiB).  Prefill-logit gate **PASS** (mean KLD **0.000707**, same-top-p **98.755 %**,
identical to the recorded base).  `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID` **931/931**.  Width purity on the dense
27B Q8_0, 2-GPU `-sm tensor`, `--load-mode mlock`: `--spec-type none == draft-mtp
--spec-draft-n-max 7` **byte-identical** (`c0f0edeac619`, `-n 1024`, `prompts/prose-rdna-boosts.txt`).
Dense 4B Q8_0 coherence: `-sm tensor == -sm layer == 1 GPU`, and byte-identical to the unpatched build
(`b065f37593b3`).  The field config: **10/10** loads clean, coherent output, `////` = 0 over a 512-token
code run.  (The field config's greedy text is not run-to-run deterministic -- pre-existing `TODO.md` #50,
the global fusion guard vs per-table slab eviction -- so text hashing is not a gate there; the dense 4B
and the prefill-logit gate cover the numerics.  The fault is a ~1-in-10 race that also did not reproduce
on the unpatched build across 7 runs, so the close is evidence-based, not statistical; reopen if it
recurs.)

**Tracker.**  The historical `TODO #38` (host-resident expert load page fault under `--load-mode none`)
is now genuinely closed; this was its last known reproducer.  The campaign record moves from
`wip/load-mode-none-meta-upload/` to `archive/work/load-mode-none-meta-upload/`.

## 261011.005 (r47) -- fix the `--fit off` slab blackout (issue #136) and make the CE all-reduce fail-soft; close #135

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r47`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`6daf815693704a214246bea7b60523ddff00a171`, net tree
`0099dd85130db65cbfbcfd738abfc57566bffe6f`); **16 blocks** (00-15); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).  No new block; the fixes fold into the
owner blocks and block 15 is re-cut on top of blocks 06/12.  The predecessor r46 tree (`a6ca8905`) is
the reference for every A/B below.

**Root cause (issue #136, proven with gdb in the campaign and reproduced here).**  A host-expert MoE run
(`-ncmoe`/`-cmoe` > 0) with `--fit off` never armed the movable-boundary slab: `moe_cache_preflight()`
opened with `if (!g_enabled) return false;`, and `g_enabled`/`g_auto` are set only by `parse_env()`, which
ran only from `moe_cache_init()` (backend init).  `--fit off` skips the fit probe load, so the driver
preflight (`common/common.cpp` -> `llama_model_moe_cache_preflight`, before `llama_init_from_model`) saw
`g_enabled == 0`, returned early, and left `g_slab_armed` false.  The cache then auto-enabled during
`llama_init_from_model` and ran its arena on a raw `cudaMalloc` outside the slab -- the pre-slab crash
mode.  Repro on the r46 build: `--fit off` logged no `SLAB_INIT` yet `MoE expert cache (auto): arena
18662 MiB`; without `--fit off` both `SLAB_INIT` lines appeared.

**Block 06 (items A/B/D/F).**  (A) A new `ensure_env()` (guarded by a function-local static) parses the
environment once, called from the top of `moe_cache_preflight()` and from `moe_cache_init()`; the slab is
now armed whenever the cache is enabled, independent of `--fit`.  `g_init_done` keeps its device-
bookkeeping meaning rather than being reused for the env guard.  (B) `ggml_cuda_slab_configured()` (the
env kill-switch, ignoring `g_slab_armed`) backs a one-time WARN in `alloc_all_locked()` when the cache is
enabled, tables exist, and the slab is not armed.  (D) `ggml_cuda_device_malloc()` now guards the
fail-soft arena yield on `ggml_cuda_slab_enabled()` -- the predicate that chose the arena backing --
instead of the failing device's `ggml_cuda_slab_active()`, so a device whose slab failed to initialise
cannot churn the cache; `moe_cache_shrink_step(int device)` is device-scoped and no longer disables the
whole cache when the failing device has nothing to free.  (F) A slab that is armed but cannot be
**created** (no VMM, bad chunk geometry, `cudaMemGetInfo` failure, or too little free VRAM for the
reserve) now records a decline reason, refuses to retry, logs one ERROR naming the cause and the
workarounds, and disables the cache to STREAM from the host; if it were ever detected after
`moe_cache_is_sized()` it `GGML_ABORT`s instead of running inconsistently.  A raw arena is never built
silently.

**Block 12 (items C/E).**  (C) The copy-engine (`GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=ce`) all-reduce scratch no longer
grows with bare `CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc)` (the only device allocation outside the fail-soft choke point,
and the site of the #136 abort: `hipMalloc(&comm_ctx->ce_tmp2[i], need)`).  All three per-rank buffers
now allocate through `ggml_cuda_device_malloc`; a partial attempt is retired to `ce_old` (freed at
teardown, never mid-run) and `return false` lets the dispatcher fall back to the internal pipeline.  The
fallback is sticky after the first failed grow.  New opt-in budget `GGML_CUDA_AR_CE_SCRATCH_MIB`
(default 0 = unlimited) refuses an oversized scratch before allocating.  CE stays opt-in.  (E) No code
change: issue #135's gfx11 `s_wait_storecnt` guard already landed in r46; re-verified by compiling
`allreduce-hip.cu` for gfx1100/gfx1150/gfx1151/gfx1200/gfx1201 (all clean), and the maintainer also
built r46 on gfx1100 (`ssh fingon`) without error.

**Validation (gfx1201).**  The 4-way flag matrix (none / `--fit off` / `--load-mode none` / both) shows
`SLAB_INIT dev=0` and `dev=1` in **all four rows** (previously absent on `--fit off`).  With an MTP draft
the line reads `aux=4.00 GiB reserve=8.00 GiB`.  Coherence (same-seed `llama-cli`, `-sm tensor`) is
identical to the r46 base.  The MTP rule-0 gate (`-sm tensor`, 27B Q8_0, `-n 3000`, four axes) has
identical acceptance and byte-identical generated text vs r46; the host-expert MoE + slab MTP row
(`-sm tensor -ncmoe 40`, 35B-A3B Q4_K_M) has identical acceptance (0.64122) and identical output.
Prefill-logit gate: mean KLD **0.000707**, same-top-p **98.755 %** (PASS).  CE vs hybrid/internal output
byte-identical; a forced fallback (`GGML_CUDA_AR_CE_SCRATCH_MIB=1`) logs one WARN and degrades to
`internal` coherently.  The #136 field repro (arena resident after decode, then a **68 216-token**
prefill, `-sm tensor -ncmoe 48 --fit off -ub 6144 -c 204800`, q8_0 KV, MTP n3, `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=ce`)
completes with `SLAB_INIT` on both devices, 530.9 t/s prompt, and 0 OOM / 0 aborts / 0 stand-downs / 0
`////`.  A forced slab decline (`GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RESERVE_MIB=40000`) errors and streams cleanly; the
`GGML_CUDA_SLAB=0` plain path is unchanged.

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `GGML_CUDA_AR_CE_SCRATCH_MIB` and the r47 slab invariant; the
current-state headers of `README.md`, `patches/README.md`, `MANIFESTS.md` and `BASELINE.md` move to r47;
`release.json` is regenerated.  The campaign moves from `wip/slab-arming-and-ce-failsafe/` to
`archive/work/slab-arming-and-ce-failsafe/` (promoted), and `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` drops it.  Issues #136
and #135 are closed.

## 261011.004 (r46) -- block 16 folded back into 0000-0015; the RDNA4 band-WMMA GQA cap (issue #133, block 15)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r46`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`2e19a9d398f5cbc16b6f549c244133d276c19e13`, net tree
`a6ca8905f3ce5eb9ac7bf67ff8863a0b43419293`); **16 blocks** (00-15); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).  The net tree is the r45 tree plus the
#133 changes (only `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh` and `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp` differ), so
r45's validation carries; the fold only moves the patch boundary.

**Packaging -- block 16 folded thematically.**  The r45 block 16 (the six contributor PRs) is
distributed instead of carried as a 17th block, restoring the 0000-0015 set:
- **block 06** (general system-operations bucket): the `llama_kv_cache::seq_rm` used-range scan, the
  layer-uniform expert-cache re-arm, and the opt-in async graph-input uploads
  (`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=1`) + legacy-pool cache cap (`GGML_CUDA_POOL_CACHE_MB`).
- **block 12** (hybrid all-reduce): the small-message AR block count (`GGML_CUDA_AR_SMALL_BLOCKS=8`
  restores) and the opt-in 2-device P2P path (`GGML_CUDA_AR_P2P=1`).
- **block 15** (campaign/attention memory): the GDN state-gather skip
  (`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_STATE_GATHER=0`, with the `rs_s_copy` / split-copy `OUTPUT` flags), the AVX2 S2
  exact top-k prefilter, the gfx1201 grid-stall pad (`GGML_CUDA_GRID_STALL_PAD=0`, mmvf/mmvq), and
  issue #133.
The distribution follows code ownership: the r45 block-16 hunks were cut against the block-15 tree, and
the GDN decoder (`beta_sigmoid`) and mmvq decode-grid (`GGML_MMVQ_RDNA4_DECODE_GRID`) work they extend
were introduced by block 15, so those pieces belong to block 15; only the host-side/system and AR
pieces had an earlier home.

**Issue #133 (block 15) -- the decode/verify band folds GQA 12.**  `ggml_cuda_fattn_band_wmma_applies`
required `gqa_ratio <= 8`, so the qwen4exp geometry (head 256, 24 q / 2 kv = GQA 12) fell to
`flash_attn_tile<256,256,1,4>` (ncols2 = 4 -> 3 KV passes per KV head) for n_q <= 8.  The band already
loads a partial final `ncols2 = 8` group and masks its unused columns on the Q load and the dst write,
so the fix only raises the cap: `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA_GQA_MAX`, default **12** (`<= 8` restores the
old whole-group fold; `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA=0` still disables the band wholesale).  A new
`test-backend-ops` CPU-oracle matrix covers head-256/GQA-12 at nb 1/3/5/8, kv 512/4096 and
f16/bf16/q8_0.  The parked `wip/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/` note that "GSQ qwen4exp GQA12 is
excluded from the band" is updated: it is now banded, so that campaign's probe must be re-derived on
this build.

**Validation (gfx1201).**  Kernel trace: the baseline decode runs `flash_attn_tile`, the fix runs
`flash_attn_ext_f16` (band) + `flash_attn_stream_k_fixup_uniform`.  `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT`
**6358/6358 OK** (the new gqa-12 cases pass on both the band and the tile build); width purity
`--spec-type none == draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 7` **byte-identical** at 100K depth on 2 and 3 GPUs;
`Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0` coherence identical; prefill-logit **mean KLD 0.000707 / same-top-p 98.755 % (PASS)**.
Perf (Flash-Next GSQ-IQ3_XXS + shared Q8_0 MTP head, 100K-token prompt, 128 greedy, `n-max 3`, q8_0
KV): 2x R9700 MTP **73.4 -> 99.9 t/s (+36 %)**; 3x R9700 **70.0 -> 77.6 (+11 %)**; short context
**-3 %** (the band's wider tile wastes query columns at n_q = 1 -- accepted: the short case costs little
wall time and cannot be depth-gated without breaking the W = 1..8 width-purity invariant).

**CI fix (same release).**  The `docker-ghcr.yml` container matrix builds `AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100;
gfx1150;gfx1151;gfx1200;gfx1201` with `GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`; the r45 P2P all-reduce (block 12, folded
from block 16 / PR #129) contains `asm volatile("s_wait_storecnt 0x0")`, which clang rejects on gfx11
and gfx9 (`instruction not supported on this GPU`), so every r45 build failed at `allreduce-hip.cu`
(in addition to the r43 `moe_cache_set_host_pool`/`_set_host_source` `GGML_BACKEND_DL` linker failure,
already fixed by r44 #130 in block 15).  The asm is now behind `#if defined(RDNA4)` and every other
target uses the full `__threadfence_system()` fence with the lite mode compiled out (`p2p_lite =
false`, so the reader takes the volatile/fenced path); verified by compiling `allreduce-hip.cu` for
gfx1100, gfx1150, gfx1151, gfx1200 and gfx1201.  No gfx1201 behavior change (the RDNA4 branch is
unchanged).

**Docs.**  `ENVIRONMENT.md` gains `GGML_HIP_FA_BAND_WMMA_GQA_MAX` and re-homes the former block-16
variables to blocks 06/12/15; `patches/README.md`, `README.md`, `MANIFESTS.md`, `BASELINE.md`,
`TODO.md` and the current-state headers move to r46 / 16 blocks.

## 261011.003 (r45) -- block 16: the contributor decode/latency PRs (#124, #125, #126, #128, #129, #132)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r45`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-16 tip
`f92e5284bf19847c9fc33ac60cf4ef5562c2136b`, net tree
`064c72ae60c2153a525d4681df1e19aad516f08c`); **17 blocks** (00-16); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(strict 17/17 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).  New **block 16** carries the six
contributor WIP campaigns, all promoted and archived under `archive/work/<campaign>/RESOLUTION.md`.

**#124 (GDN state-gather skip, block 16).** In the one-sequence `<= 16`-token decode/verify band the
CUDA graph now skips each GDN layer's `GET_ROWS` recurrent-state gather; the sequential kernel reads
`s0` straight from the cache row (a plain copy, so bit-identical).  Default-on kill-switch
`GGML_CUDA_FUSE_GDN_STATE_GATHER=0`.  Two non-CUDA-backend riders keep the row ids alive:
`rs_s_copy` is flagged `OUTPUT` in `src/llama-graph.cpp`, and the scheduler keeps that flag on a
single split-input copy (`n_copies == 1`) in `ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp`.  `@DanoPTT`'s r38 Windows
concurrent-sequence report is the documented unified-KV/attention-offset non-determinism
(`wip/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/`, issue #134), not the skip; the maintainer confirmed the
non-determinism sources were resolved by the earlier campaigns.

**#125 (decode host-side, block 16).** `0002` `llama_kv_cache::seq_rm` scans only
`[used_min(), used_max_p1())`; `0003` adds an AVX2 block-max + NaN prefilter to the S2 exact top-k
fast path (runtime AVX2 check, scalar fallback; `_WIN32` uses `IsProcessorFeaturePresent`, the
`@DanoPTT` link fix); both always on.  `0001` async graph-input uploads (per-device 16 MiB pinned
ring, done-event ordering, `<= 1 MiB` COMPUTE-buffer writes) is **opt-in**
`GGML_CUDA_ASYNC_INPUT=1`.

**#126 (expert-cache re-arm, block 16).** `0001` makes `moe_cache_rearm` re-arm every allocated table
of a stood-down layer together, so a layer partially taken by slab chunks comes back slot-uniform.
`0002`/`0003` are **not applicable**: they fix the pipelined used-list readback and the device
`expert -> slot` map that r40's DEVMAP removal deleted.

**#128 (grid-stall pad, block 16).** `ggml_cuda_grid_stall_pad()` detects a launch whose block count
is a multiple of 256 (work-item count a multiple of 65536) and adds one returning block to
`mul_mat_vec_f` / `mul_mat_vec_q_ksplit` / `mul_mat_vec_q_moe`; bit-identical, default-on
`GGML_CUDA_GRID_STALL_PAD=0`; HIP-only, and removable once AMD fixes ROCm/legacy-rocm-build#6689.

**#129 (all-reduce small-message latency, block 16).** `0001` launches 4 blocks (not 8) for small
decode/verify messages (`GGML_CUDA_AR_SMALL_BLOCKS`, `GGML_CUDA_AR_SMALL_BYTES`), default-on.  `0002`
is the opt-in 2-device P2P push all-reduce with lightweight fences (`GGML_CUDA_AR_P2P=1`,
`GGML_CUDA_AR_P2P_LITE`).

**#132 (legacy-pool cache cap, block 16).** Opt-in `GGML_CUDA_POOL_CACHE_MB=N` frees the legacy
HIP/CUDA pool's cached bytes before a new device allocation once they exceed N MiB; unset/0 keeps
today's behaviour.  Reported win is at ~256K context; not reproduced at 64K here (peak dominated by
weights), kept opt-in.

## 261011.002 (r44) -- Windows host-pool portability (issue #130, block 15) + per-sequence rollback guard (issue #131, block 02)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r44`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`4b2874db93409c622502d73f371d2e6709914b96`, net tree `fb348f69badfab0bb2a284c97eaed84117ea57d9`);
**16 blocks**; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).
No new block: the guard folds into **block 02** and the portability fix + warning cleanup fold into
**block 15**.  `patches/` was regenerated from a canonical fork rebuilt at the base
(`scripts/apply-all.sh`) -- do not hand-edit.

**#131 (rollback-boundary diagnostic, block 02).** `llama_memory_recurrent`'s `seq_rm: rollback crossed a
batch boundary` guard compared a sequence's rollback against whichever sequence's ubatch was prepared
**last** (a single global `last_ubatch_nseq_tokens`/`last_ubatch_pos_last`), while the rollback state is
per sequence.  It now tracks the last-batch token count and position **per sequence** (only the sequences
present in the last ubatch are updated; a fully removed sequence is reset) and guards on the rolling-back
sequence's own value; the warning message reports that sequence's own count/pos.  Not a numerics change.
The report itself is **not reproducible** on the reporter's model class on the current tree: dense
Qwen3.8-27B Q5_K, `-np 2 --kv-unified -c 180224 -b 6144 -ub 512`, `--spec-type draft-mtp`, 106 partial
rollbacks and 0 warnings (`--no-kv-unified` likewise).  Issue #131 is closed as not reproducible, with a
reopen offered on evidence.  The remaining "large prefill as the last prepared batch before a rollback"
ordering is parked in the new campaign `wip/rs-rollback-boundary/`.

**#130 (Windows portability, block 15).** The bounded host pool (`moe-expert-cache.cu`) used POSIX file
I/O (`open`/`fstat`/`pread`/`posix_memalign`/`O_DIRECT`/`st_blksize`) with only the **headers** guarded, so
the Windows HIP build did not compile, and `src/llama-model-loader.cpp` forward-declared
`moe_cache_set_host_pool`/`moe_cache_set_host_source` as ggml-cuda symbols, so `llama.dll` did not link
(a Windows DLL, and a `GGML_BACKEND_DL` build, only export `GGML_API`).  The file calls now go through
four helpers (`pool_open_file`/`pool_fd_align`/`pool_pread`/`pool_aligned_alloc`) plus a `pool_ssize_t`
typedef; on Windows `pool_open_file` returns -1, the pool marks itself failed, and a miss is served from
the pinned master.  The two entry points now go through the device API
(`ggml_backend_dev_moe_cache_set_host_pool`/`_set_host_source`), so libllama no longer references a
ggml-cuda symbol.  The POSIX path is unchanged.  Reported by @DanoPTT (#130).

**Warning cleanup (block 15).** A clean build is now warning-free: the CPU, RPC and meta device-iface
initializers set every appended callback explicitly (the pre-existing `slab_narrow2_floor` misses and the
new host-pool fields).  Before this, a fresh build emitted three `-Wmissing-field-initializers` warnings.

**Validation (gfx1201).** Coherence `1c5d32ac537d` (Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0, seed 42) unchanged; prefill-logit
mean KLD **0.000707 / same-top-p 98.755 %** (PASS, identical to base); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green
(16/16 strict `git am`, tree `fb348f69...`); a clean build emits **0 warnings**; the host-pool path
smoke-tested (`35B-A3B Q4_K_M`, `--host-experts pool -ncmoe 40`: runs, logs `host_experts_mode=POOL`).
## 261011.001 (r43) -- block 06: the multi-ubatch logits readback is ordered (TODO #52 part B)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r43`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`0399ba3fe4f338c0e3a63ce927f398ad0271b05a`, net tree `73d1d92578eda70179b4fca62d9d4d61ead9fe4f`);
16 blocks; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).
Amends **block 06** (`src/llama-context.cpp`) only; `patches/` was regenerated from a canonical fork
rebuilt at the base (`scripts/apply-all.sh`) -- **do not hand-edit**.

**The bug (job B of the #52 follow-ups; the held batching change).** The held multi-token batching change
(`archive/work/moe-verify-fusions/held-B-multi-seq-ubatch.patch`, one sequence per ubatch) is **correct**
-- the recurrent-state probe is bit-identical solo vs co-batch for K=1/4/16/32. It appeared to break
`llama-perplexity` at `n_seq >= 4` (PPL 8.51 -> 2097) only because of a **logits-readback ordering
hazard**: `llama_context::decode` issued each ubatch's device->host logits copy **asynchronously** into
the pinned output buffer while the *next* ubatch's graph reused the same device tensor. On ROCm the
pinned async D2H copy is not ordered against the following compute, so an earlier ubatch's host rows
received a later ubatch's data (measured: host rows `[seq0, seq2, seq3, seq3]` instead of
`[seq0, seq1, seq2, seq3]`; `out_ids`/`output_ids` were correct -- it is the copy, not the mapping).
Forcing the output buffer pageable (`GGML_NO_PINNED_OUTPUT`) also fixes it, which isolates the pinned
async copy as the trigger.

**The fix.** After the per-ubatch readbacks, synchronize the backends that own the tensors just read --
but only when another ubatch follows (`if (!mctx->next()) break;` before the sync), so a single-ubatch
decode pays nothing. `GGML_READBACK_SYNC=0` is the A/B kill-switch. Because the next ubatch overwrites
the same device tensor, the serialization is semantically required on a correct stream; it recovers
ordering, it is not new work.

**Validation (gfx1201).** With the fix: perplexity `8.5100` (was 2097.75; B off 8.5100);
`test-recurrent-state-multiseq`/`test-multiseq-same` bit-identical solo vs co-batch; coherence
`1c5d32ac537d`; prefill-logit KLD **0.000707 / same-top-p 98.755 %** (PASS, identical to base);
`llama-batched-bench -npp 16 -ntg 32 -npl 1,4,8` batched TG unchanged (the only cost is ~2 % PP on the
multi-sequence all-output prefill path); `scripts/validate-set.sh` green.

**Not in this release (TODO #52 part C).** The residual server non-determinism under `--kv-unified` is a
separate, upstream-inherent defect, now root-caused: a sequence's **attention result depends on the
physical offset of its KV cells** in the unified stream, modulo the FA reduction tile (quantum 64).
`--no-kv-unified` is green; it reproduces on stock upstream, on two model files, with all experts on GPU,
with layer and tensor split, and with the expert cache off. New campaign:
`wip/kv-cell-offset-nondeterminism/` (handover + cold-start prompt). The closed predecessor campaign
(parts A/B and the fused-verify work) is `archive/work/moe-verify-fusions/`.

## 261010.004 (r42) -- block 02: the multi-sequence GDN kernel choice is shape-consistent (TODO #52, part 1)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r42`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`a3c13e9ca76717d8dd9b6020fca2b35bcd2c46b6`, net tree `eafc03875b2c894bda7d8081d362b234a55a9c54`);
16 blocks; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green. Amends **block 02** (`gated_delta_net.cu`) only.

**The bug (found while investigating issue #134 / TODO #52).** The GDN dispatch
(`ggml_cuda_op_gated_delta_net_impl`) took the **whole-batch chunked** kernel for `n_seqs > 1 && K == 1`
**unconditionally**, while the same sequence decoded alone with `n_tokens <= GDN_CHUNKED_MIN_TOKENS` took
the **sequential** kernel. The two kernels are not bit-identical, so on any path with `n_rs_seq == 0`
(`--spec-type none`, or `GGML_FORCE_N_RS_SEQ=0`) a sequence's logits depended on the sequences that
happened to share its ubatch. The minimal two-sequence probe
(`wip/moe-verify-fusions/tools/test-recurrent-state-multiseq.cpp`) shows the co-batched arm diverging
from the solo arm at the `GATED_DELTA_NET` op, and `GGML_CUDA_GDN_CHUNKED=0` restoring bit-identity.

**The fix.** The `n_seqs > 1` branch now uses the same `n_tokens > GDN_CHUNKED_MIN_TOKENS` gate as the
single-sequence branch, so the kernel choice depends only on `(n_tokens, K, n_rs_batch)` and not on how
many sequences share the ubatch. Large multi-sequence prefills keep the chunked path (both arms chunk,
so the choice stays shape-consistent). No new environment variable; no perf impact on the single-sequence
decode path (`n_tokens == 1` never reaches the block).

**Validation (gfx1201).** `test-recurrent-state-depth` unchanged (130 baseline failures, phase A 1..7
PASS); the probe is bit-identical solo vs co-batch for K=1/4/16/32 on Qwen3.5-4B and the Flash-Next GSQ
target; coherence `1c5d32ac537d`; prefill-logit KLD 0.000707 / same-top-p 98.755 % (PASS);
`scripts/validate-set.sh` green.

**Not in this release (the rest of #52, tracked as C).** A second, batching-level component remains: with
no cross-sequence ubatching at all, cache off, and this fix, the server plain gate is still not
byte-reproducible, so a unified-KV/attention state dependence is involved. A companion batching change
(force one sequence per ubatch for multi-token batches) makes the probe shapes consistent and is
**decode-cost-free** (batched-bench TG unchanged, prefill faster), but it breaks `llama-perplexity` at
`n_seq >= 4` (PPL 8.51 -> 2097), so it was **held** rather than shipped. Handover:
`wip/moe-verify-fusions/HANDOVER-multiseq-bc.md`.

## 261010.003 (r41) -- block 12: the hybrid NCCL init is EAGER again; `-sm tensor -ncmoe` is MTP-pure (TODO #53)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r41`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`a89ffa2735d2141293ed5472beab6746a47fbbf7`, net tree `46c4ce7a6a00aa6c6931c5a89faf847dde19fd34`);
16 blocks; `scripts/validate-set.sh` green (strict 16/16 `git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).
Amends **block 12** to bring `ncclCommInitAll` up **eagerly** in the hybrid path, reverting r34's lazy
deferral, because the **mid-run** init is what made `-sm tensor -ncmoe` non-deterministic.  `patches/` was
regenerated from a canonical fork rebuilt at the base (`scripts/apply-all.sh`) -- **do not hand-edit**.

**Root cause (TODO #53): the internal all-reduce was innocent.**  The handover had root-caused the 35B-A3B
`qwen35moe` field impurity to the internal host-staged AR.  The decisive instrument (`GGML_AR3_DBG`,
dumping the pre-AR local partial and the post-AR output per device and checking `out == local0 + local1`)
shows the AR is **bit-exact**: 0 mismatches on 2400/2400 `none`-arm and 1680/1680 `n3`-arm decode ARs
(F32 wire).  What differs between the diverging and pure configurations is the AR **input** -- the first
main-request decode AR input is `b2ee7f62b406c328` under the shipped (lazy) hybrid and `86cb27d83b28eba1`
under both eager hybrid and pure RCCL, while the AR output is the exact sum in all three.  So the AR is
downstream of the divergence.

The trigger is **block 12's lazy NCCL init** (r34).  Forcing hybrid to init NCCL eagerly (an otherwise
byte-identical build) reproduces pure RCCL **bit-for-bit**.  Isolation: routing the small tensors to RCCL's
`ncclFloat` branch while keeping the pipeline allocated (`GGML_WIP_AR_NOINTERNAL`) stays **impure**, and
freeing the pipeline's CE scratch, enabling peer access eagerly, holding a dummy VRAM reservation,
draining the comm streams before the lazy init and `GGML_CUDA_SLAB=0` all fail to restore purity.  Only
removing the mid-run init does: RCCL's init side effects perturb the layout/state, which flips a near-tie
in the upstream split compute.  Iterating RCCL's init mid-forward is exactly what r34 introduced to avoid
`ncclCommInitAll`'s decode-only slowdown of the internal pipeline (2x R9700 78 -> 46 t/s, 3x 67 -> 22).

**The fix.**  `ggml_backend_cuda_comm_init_hybrid` now calls `ggml_backend_cuda_comm_init_nccl` eagerly;
the `nccl_lazy`/`nccl_tried` fields and the dispatch-time lazy block are removed (the `ce` path no longer
clears a flag).  The dispatch still routes small tensors to the internal pipeline, so `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE`
semantics are unchanged; the only behavioural difference is *when* RCCL comes up.  On any run with a
prefill -- i.e. every expert-cache run -- RCCL was initialised during the prefill anyway, so the target
path is perf-neutral.

**The §8 fallback would not have worked.**  "Route the GDN/MTP small-tensor ARs through RCCL" makes no
difference (the `NOINTERNAL` result above); `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=nccl` is pure only because it disables
the lazy init, not because smalls go to RCCL.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| 35B-A3B Q8_0 `-sm tensor -ncmoe 99` short field (`none` vs `n1`/`n3`/`n7`) | **None / None / None** (pure) |
| 35B-A3B Q8_0 long field, **auto cache** `none` vs `n3` | **None** (pure) |
| 35B-A3B Q8_0 `-sm layer` `none` vs `n3` | **None** (pure) |

| 35B-A3B Q8_0 long field, auto cache, plain (2000 tok) | prefill **3526** t/s, decode **83.5** t/s |

MTP/plain are within run-to-run noise of the eager reference measured during the investigation

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r40`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip

rebuilt at the base (`scripts/apply-all.sh`) -- **do not hand-edit**.

**The removal is an amendment to block 06, not a later "remove" block.**  Block 06 used to create the whole
device-remap machinery (the `moe_cache_*` slot map, `moe_cache_promote_host`, `moe_cache_policy_flush`,
`moe_cache_get_slot`, the prefill tally, and the `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_DEVMAP`/`_DEVPOLICY`/`_DEVPOLICY_SPLIT`/
`_KSLOT`/`_DEV_EAGER` knobs).  It is stripped at block 06 against block 06's own content; the KSLOT hunks
are dropped from block 13; and the devmap leftovers (the level-4 validator, `CACHE_STANDDOWN_*`,
`CACHE_REDIR_DEBUG`, the in-place staging globals, the dead `slot_dev`/`g_promote_calls`/`g_remap_launches`/
`MOE_HOST_POOL_POLICY` state) are gone.  Every block 00-15 is now free of the device-remap symbols:
`grep -E 'DEVMAP|g_devmap|KSLOT|g_kslot|DEVPOLICY|g_devpolicy|slot_dev|used_dev|DEV_EAGER'` over `ggml/`
`src/` `common/` is empty at every block.  The eager host-routing path (materialized remap) is the sole
`-sm tensor` split policy.

**Non-devmap WIP fixes kept** (hard-won, folded into blocks 06/15): the **per-table fusion guard**
(`moe_cache_table_serves`, the issue **#50** repair -- block 06 no longer carries the global
`moe_cache_has_arena()` guard after this fold), the **narrow-2 slab** MTP-draft COMPUTE-aliasing fix, the
**`-ncmoe` host-expert offload** option, the level-3 slot-content validator, the `MOE_EXPERT_CACHE_ADMIT`/
`_TOUCH`/`_COLD_UVA` knobs, `GGML_CUDA_CACHE_GEOM_DEBUG` and the `test-logits-width-probe` changes.

budget sweep and the `n_rs_seq` 0-vs-3 A/B pure -- a layout-sensitive hipBLASLt solution flip (issue #67 /
ROCm/rocm-libraries#12126).  Disabling hipBLASLt costs ~12-17 % prefill on gfx1201/ROCm 7.14 and ROCm
10.1.0 does not fix it.  Paying that to keep a ~14 % decode path smaller than the prefill loss is not worth
it.  Detail: `wip/moe-verify-fusions/FINDINGS-devmap-removal.md`; the fold procedure:

## 261010.001 (r39) -- PROMOTION: the H2D staging ring moves INSIDE the movable-boundary slab (block 06 + block 15)

**Release `v16-a55e952b8-r39`** (base `a55e952b8`, canonical block-15 tip
`795ea7185f4c1d131725bbc8f4d10d4ce85cbb17`, net tree
`cc124b21e72fdc314936960f0e52394e02fd6c8c`; `n_blocks` 16; `validate-set.sh` green -- strict 16/16
`git am`, reconstructed tree == `release.json`).  Promotes `archive/work/slab-ring-region/` (TODO #49).  `patches/`
was regenerated from a canonical fork rebuilt at the base (`scripts/apply-all.sh`) -- **do not hand-edit**.

**What was folded:**

* **block 06 (the slab side)** -- the ring becomes a work-region sub-region in the
  `0 -> narrow -> RB -> wide -> arena` ordering: a fixed always-resident narrow (decode/verify) floor at
  base 0, the ring above it, the transient wide (prefill) view above that, and the arena always above the
  work.  `work_alloc` returns two stable bases, `work_needs` stores each view's boundary contribution, and
  the context pins the narrow floor with a `split_only` size-only narrow reserve (plus the compute-chunk
  formula so the pinned size matches the real allocation).  New optional device hooks
  `slab_ring_set` / `slab_narrow_floor` through the backend iface; the `moe_cache_evict_slab_range` /
  `rearm` helpers; the `--fit` h2d-bound lockstep (`ggml_backend_cuda_h2d_stage_bound` returns 0 when the
  slab is active so the ring is not reserved twice).
* **block 15 (the staging side)** -- `h2d_stage_buffer` serves a slot from the slab's reserved ring region
  first (stable VA, no `cudaFree`, no G4 cap) with the `cudaMalloc` fallback; `h2d_stage_region_bytes`
  (capped by `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB`, default 6144, against the merged host-tensor estimate); the
  `h2d_stage_slab` / `h2d_stage_max_req` fields; and the guarded `h2d_stage_free`.

**Field §5.5 (gfx1201, 2x R9700, `--fit on`, 31 482-token prose, 1000 MTP tokens).**  The point of the
campaign: r38's G4 default refused ~990 MiB of ring growth and cost **~16 % prefill**.

| arm | prefill | decode | accept | NaN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| r38 (G4 default 50 %, ring refused) | 767-769 | 61.8-62.0 | 1.0 | 0 |
| **r39, `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB=2560`** | **945.5-946.8** | 61.2-61.4 | 1.0 | **0** |
| **r39, default (6144)** | **992.2** | 61.1 | 1.0 | **0** |

The ring is reclaimed on the prefill->decode drop (boundary back to the narrow floor), the arena returns
to the 39993.8 MiB / 61.7 % baseline, and the expert cache re-sizes to 337/295 slots like r38.

**Gates on the promoted tree (gfx1201):** dense `Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0` `-sm tensor` golden **`1c5d32ac537d`**;
`scripts/gate-prefill-logits.sh` **PASS** mean KLD **0.000707**, same-top-p **98.755 %**;

is **global** (`moe_cache_has_arena()`) while the slab's eviction is **per table** -- the code's own
`OPEN 2` -- so an arena change toggles the fusions mid-run and the greedy output depends on eviction timing
(no corruption: 0 NaN, 0 `////`, prefill logits bit-identical; PR #27301's alloc dependencies were tested
and **excluded**).  Fusions stay **default-ON** (`ENVIRONMENT.md` §7 records the ~9-10 % prefill / ~6 %
decode cost of a full disable and the re-enable recipe).  `TODO.md` **#51**: 3-GPU MTP decode is **2.6x
SLOWER** than plain decode (19.5-21.4 vs 52.2 t/s), reproduced on **clean r38**, so it is orthogonal to
this change.

**P2 (FA prefill staging arena) and P3 (retire G4) are CLOSED as not-beneficial.**  The 2-GPU field config
never refuses the FA staging, and on `fingon` allowing it is *slower* (r38 §15.8: 2502.2 t/s refused vs
2315.1 allowed).  The G4 cap is the adaptive mechanism doing its job, so it stays at the default 50 %.

**Reserve-side:** `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_HEADROOM_MIB` keeps its **4096** default.  3072 was trialled (the ring no
longer spends ~1 GiB of it; +8.5 % decode step rate on the `--fit on` field config) and **rejected**: on
the §2.2 wide-prefill config (`--fit off`, IQ4_XS, `-c 204800`) 4096 is clean (312 t/s, 0 corruption) while
3072 dies in `hipblaslt.cpp:164`.  The env var (a MiB value, not a switch) stays the documented per-user
knob.

**Committed:** `patches/0000-0015` + `rdna-boosts-all.patch` regenerated; `release.json` refreshed
(`v16-a55e952b8-r39`); `ENVIRONMENT.md` catalogues `GGML_CUDA_SLAB_RING_MIB`; `TODO.md` #49 closed, #50/#51
opened; `wip/CAMPAIGNS.md` updated.  The fork's `rdna-boosts` branch is refreshed at release time per
`AGENTS.md`.
